……しかし、祖父さまの場合は、ちょっと焼いたくらいじゃ誤魔化せない、ちゃんとした証があったってことか…。
contexts.WH: ......Come to think of it, I think I've heard about some country where it's believed that people with polydactyly should be treated as gods and revered...
contexts.MG:
If Grandfather hadn't disliked his position as the Head so much, this sixth toe probably would've been pretty lucky for him.
...Come to think of it, I've heard about some country where it's believed people with polydactyly should be treated as gods and revered...
This is beside the point, but it's fairly common in mystery novels for a corpse to be burned to hide its identity.
...But I guess that in Grandfather's case, just toasting him wouldn't be enough...
And, ...Grandfather's body was not simply burnt.
contexts.UP:
it would be Grandfather, because of the auspicious sign of his birth.
If Grandfather thought being the head was not a bad gig, this sixth toe must have been pretty lucky for him.
......Come to think of it, I think I've heard about some country where it's believed that people with polydactyly should be treated as gods and revered...
This is beside the point, but it's fairly common in mystery novels for a corpse to be burned to hide whose body it is.

findings.sourceReading: 神さまの使い means a divine messenger or emissary, not the deity itself.
findings.alternative: Both preserve vague recalled reverence. The role and the descriptive belief versus prescriptive treatment nevertheless change; no external cultural truth is asserted.

findings.description: Genji proposes that weak flames may mean prolonged burning and gradual smell accumulation. WH says the body must have begun burning long ago.

炉から漏れ出した臭いが室内に少しずつ充満し、あふれ出して階段を登ってきたのではないかという。

しかもそいつはマスターキーのようなものを持ち歩いている可能性も高い。
…何しろ、今の屋敷内は戸締りがされていることになっている。
にもかかわらず、犯人はこうして屋敷内を自由に闊歩しているのだから。

findings.description: Battler proposes that a person staged their death with a substitute corpse, remains hidden and commits the crimes. WH sequences hiding after committing the crime.

contexts.japanese:
例えば、最初に殺された６人は顔面を酷く破壊されていた。
……面影を確認できる遺体もあったが、例えばウチのクソ親父辺りなんかは、
綺麗にお面でも剥がすかのように、きっちりと顔面を失わされていた…。
俺たちは服装と状況だけで遺体を特定したに過ぎない…。
予め身代わりの死体を用意し、自らを死んだと偽装してどこかに隠れ潜んでいて犯行に及んでいるとか…？
…そんな馬鹿なと思うが、それでも不可能なトリックじゃない。
contexts.japanesePC: 予め身代わりの死体を用意し、自らを死んだと偽装してどこかに隠れ潜んでいて犯行に及んでいるとか…？

had lost his entire face, as though the whole thing had been neatly peeled off...
We only figured out which body was which by their clothes and surroundings...

次々に魔女の存在を認めていくという“痛快”なことでもある…。
……だから、上機嫌だってのか…？

……この一連の不可解な事件は全て、魔女が確かに存在する証。
人間には困難な何かが起こる度に、俺たちはベアトリーチェという魔女の存在を信じなければならなくなる。
それは真里亞にとって、…かつて頑なにその存在を否定し続けた親族たちが、
次々に魔女の存在を認めていくという“痛快”なことでもある…。
……だから、上機嫌だってのか…？
contexts.WH: To Maria, who obstinately believes in the witch, ......this series of unsolvable crimes is proof that the witch actually exists.
contexts.MG:
To Maria, who obstinately believes in the witch,
......this series of unsolvable crimes is proof that the witch actually exists.
Every time something occurs that would be difficult for a human, it becomes a little harder for the rest of us to not believe in Beatrice.
It must be an "intense pleasure" for Maria to see her relatives, who once firmly denied the witch's existence,
start acknowledging that witch's existence one by one...
......Is that why she's in high spirits...?
contexts.UP:
To her, with her obstinate belief in witches,
......this series of unsolvable crimes is proof that witches actually exist.
Every time something occurs that would be difficult for a human, it becomes a little harder for the rest of us to not believe in that witch called Beatrice.
It must be an "intense pleasure" for Maria...to see her relatives, who once firmly denied the witch's existence,
start acknowledging her existence one by one...
......Is that why she's in high spirits...?
contexts.note: Both retain unsolvable crimes instead of inexplicable incidents; Maria viewpoint is preserved but characterization becomes categorical unsolvability.

findings.description: Battler tentatively excludes Maria herself as the nineteenth person after invoking her alibi. WH instead denies existence of any nineteenth person.

contexts.japanese:
……真里亞は１９人目の魔女に会っている。
それは本当に１９人目なのか、それとも１８人の誰かに、そうだと言えと吹き込まれたのか。
ひとつだけ確かなのは、真里亞は俺たちとずっと一緒にいて、常にアリバイがあるし、不審な行動も一切ない。
……ベアトリーチェのメッセンジャーにされ、心酔しているだけで、決して１９人目ではない。
………………はず。

findings.description: Battler wonders whether Jessica was present to see Kanon die. WH says she probably cared for him until death, adding an extended caregiving role and strengthening possibility.

contexts.WH: "...I agree strongly with Natsuhi oba-san.  ......Tonight, we can put off searching for the culprit.  Instead, it would be better to think of where we can barricade ourselves in."
contexts.MG:
"...At any rate, this is no time to quarrel.
...Now that we are certain the culprit can enter and leave the mansion at will and strike out of nowhere,
we must give our undivided attention to surviving until tomorrow."
"...I agree strongly with Aunt Natsuhi.
...We can figure out who the culprit is at our leisure tonight.
For now though, we're better off finding a place to barricade ourselves in."
As I said this, I pointed out the clock to everyone.
It was already 8:00 at night.
...We had been receiving shocks over and over again since the early morning, and our bodies and minds were both completely tired out.
...There's still a long, long time until tomorrow.
We needed to find some place to barricade ourselves in so we could rest our bodies and get even the smallest amount of relief...

findings.description: The narration acknowledges somewhat lax management resulting from exchanging keys at shift changes. WH adds probably and at times in the past, making the admission tentative and episodic.

contexts.japanese:
右代宮家は使用人の人数も少なくはない。
そのため、マスターキーは複数本あった。
また、勤務が交代する度に、それらを使用人の間でやり取りしていたため、
その辺りの管理が若干ずさんであったことを認めなければならなかった。
contexts.japanesePC: また、勤務が交代する度に、それらを使用人の間でやり取りしていたため、その辺りの管理が若干ずさんであったことを認めなければならなかった。

右代宮家は使用人の人数も少なくはない。

contexts.WH: Furthermore, every time the shifts changed, the keys were passed between servants, and we had to acknowledge that this had probably gotten a bit sloppy at times in the past.

There were many servants serving the Ushiromiya family.

右代宮家は使用人の人数も少なくはない。

右代宮家は使用人の人数も少なくはない。

findings.alternative: The key-sharing mechanism remains intact and the laxity is not severe in either version, but the evidential status changes.

findings.description: Kyrie explains that game theory is deep and requires substantial study to read moves as thoroughly as Battler imagines. WH supplies the opponent as the specific object of study.

「ぜひやってみたいっす！
それを勉強してチェス盤思考をもっと鍛えたら、どんな相手の手の内も読めるみたいで楽しいじゃないっすか」
「でもね、妄信しちゃ駄目よ。
ゲーム理論は非常に奥深く複雑な学問なの。
チェス盤思考はその上辺だけを私なりに解釈した考え方に過ぎない。
……戦人くんが想像するほどに、相手の手の内を読みきるには、相当の勉強が必要よ」
「しかも、チェス盤理論は応用の利く便利なものではあっても完璧ではない。
便利ではあっても弱点が多い」

「ぜひやってみたいっす！
それを勉強してチェス盤思考をもっと鍛えたら、どんな相手の手の内も読めるみたいで楽しいじゃないっすか」
「でもね、妄信しちゃ駄目よ。
ゲーム理論は非常に奥深く複雑な学問なの。
チェス盤思考はその上辺だけを私なりに解釈した考え方に過ぎない。
……戦人くんが想像するほどに、相手の手の内を読みきるには、相当の勉強が必要よ」
「しかも、チェス盤理論は応用の利く便利なものではあっても完璧ではない。
便利ではあっても弱点が多い」

findings.description: Battler thinks he has sometimes glimpsed the outline of whoever lies behind the case. WH says he has perceived that person’s plans many times.

contexts.japanese:
敵の立場に立っての思考。
これこそがチェス盤思考の基本。
…ということはつまり、
……自分が敵を見誤っていたら、そこから導き出される答えは全てデタラメであり、何の役にも立たないことになってしまう…。
俺はチェス盤思考で、事件の裏に潜む何者かの輪郭を、何度か捉えたような気でいる。
しかし、俺は犯人のことを何もわかっていない。
……全ては思考の迷路遊びでしかないのか。
………こんな時、霧江さんがいてくれたなら……、
もっともっと研ぎ澄まされた思考で何かに気付いてくれるだろうに……。

contexts.WH: Many times, I've thought that by using chessboard thinking, I could perceive the plans of the person hiding behind this case.
contexts.MG:
Think from your enemy's perspective.
That's the basis of chessboard thinking.
...Which means, if you misread your enemy,
...the answer you draw from this process will be complete rubbish, useless...
So far, I've used chessboard theory to guess several vague bits of information about the culprit hiding behind this case, or so I think.
However, I don't know anything about the culprit.
...Am I just playing around in a labyrinth of thought?
......If Kyrie-san were here at a time like this,
...she'd probably be able to notice something with her much, much sharper thinking ability...
contexts.UP:
Think from your enemy's perspective.
That is the basis of chessboard thinking.
...Which means that...
...if you misunderstand your enemy, any and all answers that you draw from that process will be complete rubbish, and of no use at all...
Many times, I'd thought that by using chessboard thinking, I had gotten a glimpse into the person behind these crimes.
However, I don't know anything about the culprit.
......Am I just playing in a labyrinth of thought?
.........If Kyrie‐san were here at a time like this......
she'd probably be able to notice something with her much, much sharper thinking ability......
contexts.note: MG restores tentative vague information about culprit and avoids plans/many times. UP restores glimpse of person rather than plans but retains many times for source several occasions.

findings.sourceReading: 何者かの輪郭 concerns a sketch of the hidden person or agent; it is not explicitly their plans. 何度か is several instances, not a strong many-times claim.
findings.alternative: His inability to understand the culprit remains in the following sentence, and plans can inform an outline; the claimed object of inference is still narrowed to intentions.

findings.description: Someone warns poison may have been added during the kitchen and parlor’s unattended interval. WH instead says it might have been death by poison. This removes the direct food-contamination premise for refusing dinner.

contexts.japanese:
……朱志香は最後まで祖父さまの書斎に移動することを嫌がった。
だが、結局は夏妃伯母さんが無理やり押し通して移動することになった。
もう、みんなすっかり疑心暗鬼に陥ってしまっていた。
…熊沢さんが、夕食を一度は用意したのだが、絵羽伯母さんたちの一件で一度、厨房と客間を無人にしてしまっている。
その際に毒を盛られたかもしれないと誰かが言い出した。
…そのため、俺たちは熊沢さんが腕を振るってくれた夕食に手を付けることができなくなったのだった。
………親父たち６人を殺した方法は未だ不明だが、毒殺の可能性もあった。
…確かにこれなら、大の大人６人の殺害を、たとえ犯人が１人であったとしても実行できる。
…しかもこの想像は、犯人が単独で且つ、夏妃伯母さんのライフル銃を恐れていることを想像させ、自分たちの精神安定上とても良かった。

contexts.WH: Someone had said that it might have been death by poison.
contexts.MG:
...Until the very last moment, Jessica resisted moving into Grandfather's study.
But in the end, Aunt Natsuhi persisted, and we decided to move there.
Everyone was completely wrapped in paranoia by now.
...Kumasawa-san had prepared dinner at one point, but during the time we were discovering the deaths of George-aniki's parents, both the kitchen and the parlor had been left empty.
Someone suggested that the food might've been poisoned while we were gone.
...Because of that, we were unable to even touch the food that Kumasawa-san had taken the trouble to make for us.
......The manner in which the first six were killed was still unknown, but it certainly could've been poison.
...Certainly, that would allow even a single person to carry out the murder of six large adults. ...Furthermore, this idea made it easy to imagine there being only a single culprit, one who'd be afraid of Aunt Natsuhi's rifle,
and this was very good for our emotional stability.
contexts.UP:
......Jessica never warmed to the idea of moving into Grandfather's study.
But in the end, Aunt Natsuhi persisted and we decided to move there.
Everyone was already trapped by paranoia.
...Kumasawa‐san had prepared dinner once already, but after the incident involving George‐aniki's parents, the kitchen and the parlor had become temporarily devoid of people.
Someone said that it might have been poisoned at that time.
...Because of that, we were unable to even touch the food that Kumasawa‐san had taken the trouble to make for us.
.........The manner in which the first six had been killed was still unknown, but there was a possibility that it was poison.
...And indeed, by this method, even a single person would be able to carry out the murder of six fully grown adults.
...Furthermore, this idea made it seem like there was only a single culprit, who was also afraid of Aunt Natsuhi's rifle, and this was very good for our emotional stability.
contexts.note: Both restore possible food contamination during unattended interval as reason for refusing dinner, separate from first murders poison theory.

findings.sourceReading: その際に毒を盛られた links poisoning to the just-described temporary absence, with the prepared meal as the danger.
findings.alternative: The following refusal and later canned-food choice let readers reconstruct the concern. Past deaths by poison are separately hypothesized afterward, so WH conflates two distinct arguments.

contexts.MG:
Grandfather's study. ...I'd heard rumors about it beforehand, so I wasn't that shocked.
He had done nothing more than fortify it thoroughly with his occult hobbies.
...If Grandfather's hobby had been chasing after pop idols, these walls might be buried beneath idol posters.

Even so, I couldn't help but remain dumbfounded by the smell of his creepy medicine and the sweet stench that seemed to melt my head...
When the door was closed, it automatically made a *clunk*.
...I see, this is the auto-lock that's activated whenever the door is closed...

findings.sourceReading: Her declarative assistance/employment account is distinguished from fools spreading claims of filthy hobbies; it carries no hearsay marker.
findings.alternative: These are still Natsuhi’s claims rather than independent proof, and the slander remains separately attributed. The change nonetheless weakens the knowledge she presents as an insider.

contexts.MG:
"......Kihihihihihihihihihihihihihihi.
...Haven't you ever heard of people making bets to test their fate?"
Like throwing a sandal and saying that if it lands right side up, tomorrow will be sunny.
...Or saying that tomorrow will be a good day if a coin lands heads up.
...There are many little superstitions like that.
Sometimes, when your luck is down and you get bored, and you roll the dice and get three sixes, you want to believe it's a portent of some miracle.
...When flipping a sandal, you have at worst a 50% chance.
Even if you get it right side up, it's not worth much.
...But if you carelessly roll three dice and they all come up six, you might think that's a small miracle.
"......Magic works the same way.
...You must pray earnestly for an extremely unlikely result.
...Then, the feelings from all those stored up prayers gain magical power and become incarnate.
......The magic that Grandfather was trying to perform was probably like that.

So, to reduce the chance that he himself was selected, he chose the day with the greatest number of people on the island to carry out the ceremony..."

findings.sourceReading: 限りなくありえない出目 is an extraordinarily improbable result of a chance process, not an unlimited effect. 奇跡の出目が現れた時 explicitly conditions manifestation on its appearance.
findings.alternative: The prior dice examples and following random sacrifice selection preserve probability themes, allowing reconstruction. The current explanation nevertheless loses the bridge linking accumulated prayer to a specific chance result.

findings.description: Nanjo says the epitaph indeed traces the subsequent course of events. WH merely says it goes on after that.

contexts.japanese:
「だが、夏妃さん…。
確かに、……碑文の内容は、その後をなぞっとる…」
「だ、第二の晩に、残されし者は寄り添う二人を引き裂け…。
…これは、絵羽さまたちのことを指しているのでしょうか…」
「………く、悔しいけど、…そうだと判断せざるを得ない。
…そして、母さんたちを殺した犯人は、続く“第三の晩”の言葉を手紙に書き、その場に残したんだからね」
「そ、そうだな…。
第二の晩を実行し、第三の晩をその場に残した。
…第三の晩は、まさにさっき夏妃伯母さんが読んだとおりだぜ…！！」

findings.description: Genji contrasts Kinzo’s wisdom with his own mediocre understanding. WH frames the comparison as madness to commoners such as himself.

contexts.japanese:
「……源次。
…その可能性は考えられるのですか…！」
「…………わかりません。
…お館様は時に千年の未来を見越されるほどの聡明なお方です。
しかし、凡庸な私にはそれが凶気としか映らないこともあります…」
「それって、イエスって意味だよな？！
熊沢さんはどうなんだよ？！」
「わっ、私は何も知りません…！
えぇ、知りませんとも…。
知っていたなら、今日この島にいると思いますか？
仮病でも何でも使ってお休みしていますよ、えぇ！！」
「お祖父さまの長年の友人である、南條先生のご意見は…？」
「………げ、源次さんに同じです。
…金蔵さんは凡人をはるかに超越した方だった。
そこに、ある種の人間離れした力すらも感じることはありました」
「………私にも、………金蔵さんが何を考えてこの碑文を残されたのか、……わからない…！」

contexts.MG:
"...Genji,
...is such a thing possible...?!"
"......I don't know.
...The Master is a man who sometimes has the wisdom to see a thousand years into the future.
However, there are times when that appears to be nothing more than madness to commoners such as myself..."
"Okay, should we take that for a "yes"?!
What do you say, Kumasawa-san?!"

"......I-I feel the same as Genji-san.

......Even I......don't know what Kinzo-san was thinking when he wrote that epitaph...!"

findings.sourceReading: 凡庸な私 concerns ordinary or limited ability, not the social class category of commoners.
findings.alternative: The ordinary-person sense of commoner can be inferred, and Genji remains deferential. Still, the English introduces a class framing absent from his self-assessment.

findings.description: Battler concludes that the ring had already passed into Beatrice’s hands while Kinzo was alive. WH explicitly assigns the transfer to Kinzo handing it over.

contexts.japanese:
あの手紙の時点で、祖父さまはまだ生きていた。
…しかしあの時点ですでに“当主の指輪”による封蝋はされていた。
…ということは、祖父さまの存命中にすでに指輪はベアトリーチェの手に渡っていたことになる。
………それは普通に考えるならば、
ベアトリーチェがこの怪しげな契約を実行するに当たって、祖父さまがその権利を保証したと見るべきだろう。
……つまり、祖父さまはこの手紙の内容を知っていて、許可したも同然だということだ。
つまり、謎を解かないとベアトリーチェが利子の回収を始めるぞ、
というのは、ベアトリーチェと祖父さまの連名のメッセージも同然なのだ。

contexts.WH: ...Which meant that Grandfather had handed the ring over to Beatrice while he was still alive.
contexts.MG:
When the letter was read, Grandfather was still alive.
...But at that time, it had already been sealed with wax by the Head's Ring.
...Which meant Grandfather had handed the ring over to Beatrice while he was still alive.
...If we take a straightforward approach,
maybe we should assume Beatrice is carrying out that strange contract, with Grandfather guaranteeing her that right.
...In other words, this was the same as saying Grandfather knew of and approved of the contents of that letter.
In other words, it's basically a joint message from Beatrice and Grandfather...
telling us that Beatrice will start collecting interest if we don't solve the riddle.
contexts.UP:
At the time that the letter had been read, Grandfather was still alive.
...But at that time, it had already been sealed with wax by the Head's Ring.
...Which meant that Grandfather had handed the ring over to Beatrice while he was still alive.
.........If you think about that straightforwardly,
we should probably take that to mean that Beatrice is carrying out that strange contract, and Grandfather is securing her that right.
......Simply put, it was the same as saying that Grandfather knew of and approved of the contents of that letter.
In other words, it's as though it was a joint message from Beatrice and Grandfather...
telling us that Beatrice will start collecting interest if we don't solve the riddle.
contexts.note: Both explicitly make Kinzo hand over ring rather than infer ring already in Beatrice possession during his life, adding transfer agency.

MG.translation: When the letter was read, Grandfather was still alive. ...But at that time, it had already been sealed with wax by the Head's Ring. ...Which meant Grandfather had handed the ring over to Beatrice while he was still alive.

At the time that the letter had been read, Grandfather was still alive.
...But at that time, it had already been sealed with wax by the Head's Ring. ...Which meant that Grandfather had handed the ring over to Beatrice while he was still alive.

findings.sourceReading: 手に渡っていた establishes receipt or possession without identifying how or by whose deliberate action it arrived.
findings.alternative: The next source paragraph itself infers Kinzo’s authorization, so the consensual-transfer interpretation is available. WH nevertheless prematurely converts that subsequent inference into the premise.

findings.description: Battler says only the brief opportunity while everyone gathered at the portrait is available for the envelope’s appearance. WH specifies a few seconds and says there was not enough time. The following narration repeats seconds where the source only describes a recent absence and diverted attention.

そして誰もこの部屋には入ってきていない！

findings.description: Battler says only the four suspects could have placed the letter, then separately says an unidentified person among them did. WH makes the first claim only one of the four could have, suggesting exclusive capability.

findings.description: 綺麗事 is misread as Natsuhi recognizing that she is oversimplifying. This invents self-criticism of her reasoning.

contexts.japanese:
「……………………………。
朱志香は、
…………主人と結婚してから、１２年もかけてようやく授かった、……大切な娘です。
私は、朱志香を守るためなら、どのような鬼にでもなります」
少しだけ強い語尾…。
綺麗事は充分に理解している、その上でなお、自分は鬼となってでも娘を守りたいという強い決意。
…………しかしそれは、罪の意識に苛むからゆえのもの。
contexts.japanesePC: 綺麗事は充分に理解している、その上でなお、自分は鬼となってでも娘を守りたいという強い決意。

私は、朱志香を守るためなら、どのような鬼にでもなります」
少しだけ強い語尾…。
綺麗事は充分に理解している、その上でなお、自分は鬼となってでも娘を守りたいという強い決意。
…………しかしそれは、罪の意識に苛むからゆえのもの。
contexts.WH: She realized very well that she was oversimplifying, but even so, she was strongly resolved to protect her daughter even if she had to become a demon.
contexts.MG:
".........
You are...
...my precious daughter, ...the one I finally received a whole twelve years after I married my husband.
I would become the worst kind of demon to protect you."
That was some pretty strong language at the end there...
She realized very well that her words were an idealized view of what a mother should be, but even so, she was strongly resolved to protect her daughter, even if she had to become a demon.
......But that was her guilty conscience tormenting her.
contexts.UP:
".................................
Jessica,
.........you are my precious daughter, ......the daughter I was finally blessed with a whole twelve years after I married my husband.
I would become the worst kind of demon to protect you."
That was some pretty strong language at the end there...
She realized very well that these were only words, but even so, she was strongly resolved to protect her daughter even if she had to become a demon.
............But that was because she was tormented by guilt.
contexts.note: MG retains self-criticism that own maternal words idealized. UP removes idealized maternal view but still says these were only words, attributing critique of her own statement rather than understanding others platitudes and choosing protection despite them.

findings.sourceReading: Battler understands her forceful ending as a resolve to protect her daughter even as a demon despite fully understanding the morally attractive sentiments being urged on her.
findings.alternative: The general conflict between maternal protection and moral qualms remains clear, and guilt follows immediately. Neither supplies the invented admission of oversimplification.

findings.sourceReading: Battler finds a three-branched candlestick that looks as though it would be used in a suspicious ritual and takes it as a weapon.
findings.alternative: The surrounding occult study and the retained three-pronged shape still suggest the setting. This is a local loss of the explicit ritual association, not a lost weapon dimension or solution clue.

findings.description: The passive 引きずり出されている applied to 俺たち becomes “had thrown them out.” The source’s second stage of the trap is replaced by a repetition of its first stage.

contexts.japanese:
ライフル銃を構え、引き金に指を掛ける夏妃伯母さんを中心に、
俺たちは背中を寄せ合うようにしながら、周囲を警戒しつつ一塊になって移動する……。
さっきの不和を目論むという魔法陣が、まるでその魔力で成したように。
…俺たちは分裂し、しかもその上、危険地帯へ引きずり出されている。
……ということはつまり、今この瞬間、犯人のシナリオに乗っかっているということになる。
…ここからは突然何が起きてもおかしくない異空間なのだ…。

findings.sourceReading: The discord circle seems to have worked: the group has split, and now they themselves have additionally been dragged out into dangerous territory.
findings.alternative: Rows 38697–38698 correctly say they were lured out of their safe room, so the English reader can reconstruct the event. The present sentence nonetheless changes the causal summary and who is now endangered.

findings.description: The simile adds a graduation ceremony where the source describes being ordered to sing in a school lesson or similar setting.

………それはまるで、学校の授業などで、歌うことを命じられて歌うような、無機質な歌い方。
…歌っている歌は、誰もが学校で一度は歌ったことがあるに違いない平凡な民謡。
……しかし、それを、なぜ、こんな深夜に、ひとりで、一生懸命に、ずっと、どうして…？！

findings.sourceReading: Maria sings mechanically, like someone singing because a school class requires it, rather than spontaneously from good spirits.
findings.alternative: A graduation ceremony can also involve compulsory singing and retains the mechanical-performance comparison. It still supplies an unsupported ceremonial occasion and its associations.

findings.sourceReading: They had been in this room throughout the time since that morning; horrors occurring elsewhere had encouraged an unfounded belief that it was safe.
findings.alternative: Their excursions mean the Japanese itself is a rhetorical generalization rather than literal continuous occupancy. Rows 38938–38939 later correctly say they spent almost the entire day there, limiting the harm.

findings.sourceReading: With a nervous laugh, Battler says he would like to say “actually, I don’t want to,” then steels himself and imagines striking back with the candlestick.
findings.alternative: His laugh and the following resolve still show him coping with danger. Nevertheless, the translated line makes him boast that he would never back out rather than admit his wish to do so.

findings.description: 冗談も休み休み言いやがれ is rendered “Calmly joking at a time like this,” treating an idiomatic rebuke as an observation about the manner and timing of a joke.

findings.description: 一喜一憂 is reduced to rejoicing, dropping the alternating delight and concern in the reactions that absorb George’s attention.

contexts.japanese:
文字通りデレデレする僕の眼中に、世界最大の水族館の大水槽はもはや映らない。
紗音が魚たちと戯れて一喜一憂する姿を映し続けるのみだ。
contexts.japanesePC: 紗音が魚たちと戯れて一喜一憂する姿を映し続けるのみだ。
contexts.japanesePS3:
文字通りデレデレする僕の眼中に、世界最大の水族館の大水槽はもはや映らない。
紗音が魚たちと戯れて一喜一憂する姿を映し続けるのみだ。
contexts.WH: Instead, I see Shannon rejoicing and playing with the fish.
contexts.MG:
I'm so entranced that I barely notice that massive tank in the world's largest aquarium anymore.
Instead, all I see are the expressions flitting across Shannon's face as she plays with the fish.
contexts.UP:
I was so entranced that I no longer even noticed the big tank of the world's largest aquarium.
Instead, I saw only Shannon happily playing with the fish, all her changing emotions showing on her face.
contexts.note: MG flitting expressions and UP changing emotions restore variation, but neither explicitly preserves paired delight/concern in 一喜一憂; UP happily retains positive framing. Original WH rejoicing wording is not copied into these witness excerpts.

MG.japanese: 古風な言い方で喩えるなら、これこそまさに薔薇色の日々…。文字通りデレデレする僕の眼中に、世界最大の水族館の大水槽はもはや映らない。紗音が魚たちと戯れて一喜一憂する姿を映し続けるのみだ。
MG.translation: To use an old-fashioned phrase, these really are rose-colored days I'm living in... I'm so entranced that I barely notice that massive tank in the world's largest aquarium anymore. Instead, all I see are the expressions flitting across Shannon's face as she plays with the fish.

UP.japanese: 古風な言い方で喩えるなら、これこそまさに薔薇色の日々…。文字通りデレデレする僕の眼中に、世界最大の水族館の大水槽はもはや映らない。紗音が魚たちと戯れて一喜一憂する姿を映し続けるのみだ。
UP.translation: To use an old‐fashioned phrase, these would be truly rose‐colored days... I was so entranced that I no longer even noticed the big tank of the world's largest aquarium. Instead, I saw only Shannon happily playing with the fish, all her changing emotions showing on her face.

findings.sourceReading: George sees only Shannon as she interacts with the fish and reacts with delight or concern to each little thing.
findings.alternative: The scene already shows her enthusiasm and embarrassment, and this is an affectionate use of a stock idiom rather than proof of deep unhappiness. Still, “rejoicing” makes the observed reactions uniformly positive.

findings.description: 自分ひとりの価値観しか持てない becomes “stick to their own view,” turning an inability to possess more than one’s own perspective into language of adhering to it.

contexts.japanese:
人間というのは、どんなに見聞を広めようとも、所詮は自分ひとりの価値観しか持てない。
だからこそ、異なる価値観を持つ人間と交流することはこんなにも面白いのかもしれない。
contexts.japanesePC: 人間というのは、どんなに見聞を広めようとも、所詮は自分ひとりの価値観しか持てない。だからこそ、異なる価値観を持つ人間と交流することはこんなにも面白いのかもしれない。
contexts.japanesePS3:
人間というのは、どんなに見聞を広めようとも、所詮は自分ひとりの価値観しか持てない。
だからこそ、異なる価値観を持つ人間と交流することはこんなにも面白いのかもしれない。
contexts.WH: No matter how far humans broaden their experiences, they stick to their own view of the world in the end.  Maybe that's why it's so interesting to mingle with people who have a different worldview.
contexts.MG:
No matter how far humans broaden their experiences, they always end up viewing the world through the lense of their own values.
Maybe that's why it's so interesting to interact with people who have different worldviews.
contexts.UP:
No matter how far humans broaden their experiences, in the end, they can only hold a single personal worldview.
Maybe that's why it's so interesting to interact with someone who has a different worldview.
contexts.note: MG viewing through own-values lens preserves single-perspective limitation; UP explicitly only a single personal worldview. Neither says stubbornly stick to views.

MG.japanese: 人間というのは、どんなに見聞を広めようとも、所詮は自分ひとりの価値観しか持てない。だからこそ、異なる価値観を持つ人間と交流することはこんなにも面白いのかもしれない。
MG.translation: No matter how far humans broaden their experiences, they always end up viewing the world through the lense of their own values. Maybe that's why it's so interesting to interact with people who have different worldviews.

UP.japanese: 人間というのは、どんなに見聞を広めようとも、所詮は自分ひとりの価値観しか持てない。だからこそ、異なる価値観を持つ人間と交流することはこんなにも面白いのかもしれない。
UP.translation: No matter how far humans broaden their experiences, in the end, they can only hold a single personal worldview. Maybe that's why it's so interesting to interact with someone who has a different worldview.

findings.sourceReading: However much experience a person gains, they can ultimately possess only their own individual value framework; exchange with someone whose framework differs is therefore interesting.
findings.alternative: “Stick to” may loosely express persistence rather than stubborn refusal, and the next sentence retains the value of different perspectives. The source nonetheless describes a limit of individual subjectivity, not a choice to adhere to beliefs.

findings.description: 白い目で見る becomes staring with “blank eyes,” losing the idiom’s disapproval or contempt.

contexts.japanese:
傍から見ていたなら、僕たちは何と微笑ましく、そして何と恥ずかしい二人なのだろう。
しかし二人になってみて初めてわかる。
僕たちにとってはこのやり取りが全てで、世界なのだ。
だから世界の外側の人がどんなに白い目で見たって、僕たちは気付かない。
……なるほど、カップルがＴＰＯを弁えずにイチャつきたがる心情を、この歳にしてようやく理解する。
contexts.japanesePC: だから世界の外側の人がどんなに白い目で見たって、僕たちは気付かない。
contexts.japanesePS3:
傍から見ていたなら、僕たちは何と微笑ましく、そして何と恥ずかしい二人なのだろう。
しかし二人になってみて初めてわかる。
僕たちにとってはこのやり取りが全てで、世界なのだ。
だから世界の外側の人がどんなに白い目で見たって、僕たちは気付かない。
……なるほど、カップルがＴＰＯを弁えずにイチャつきたがる心情を、この歳にしてようやく理解する。
contexts.WH: That's why no matter how much everyone else stared at us with blank eyes, we wouldn't have noticed it.
contexts.MG:
To anyone watching us, we might seem like an incredibly charming and embarrassing couple.
But it's only after becoming a couple that you realize.
To us, this exchange of words is everything, our entire world.
That's why no matter how much everyone else stares at us with blank expressions, we never notice.
......Indeed, at this age, I finally understand the feelings of couples who want to endlessly flirt without any regard for their surroundings.
contexts.UP:
To anyone watching us, we might have seemed like a pretty humorous—and above all embarrassing—couple.

MG.japanese: 彼女の肩を抱き寄せる。華奢な体が、強引に抱き寄せられて、まるで人形のように僕の胸に飛び込んだ。その頭を抱え込みながら、二人して水平線を見る。

findings.sourceReading: Her slender body is forcefully drawn close and consequently comes into his chest like a doll.
findings.alternative: The English explicitly retains his forceful embrace and its doll simile, so the physical cause is inferable. Nevertheless “while she dived” suggests concurrent action rather than the result of being pulled.

findings.description: 今は気付けない becomes “then, I hadn’t realized,” moving the expressed temporal perspective into retrospective awareness.

contexts.japanese:

……新しい苦悩の日々の始まりだと、今は気付けない……。

……それは甘く蕩けるような蜜の日々だけれども、
……新しい苦悩の日々の始まりだと、今は気付けない……。

contexts.MG:

...but at the time, I didn't realize that they'd be the start of a new kind of suffering...

MG.translation: So I decided to choose the path of knowing love...and tried to become a person. ...Those days were like sweet honey, ...but at the time, I didn't realize that they'd be the start of a new kind of suffering...

UP.translation: And so I learned of love, and decided to choose to become a person. ......Those days were like sweetly melting honey, ......but then, I hadn't realized that they were the beginning of days filled with a new kind of suffering......

findings.sourceReading: At this moment of choosing love and personhood, Shannon cannot recognize that the honey-sweet days also begin new suffering.
findings.alternative: The entire sequence is introduced as a recollection, and past English can be a natural narrative adjustment. However, the source shifts into the choice’s present and explicitly says “now”; the English replaces that situated ignorance with a later-looking report.

findings.alternative: “It” in the English may still refer to the old appearance from preceding sentences. Nevertheless the explicit “since ... offered” recasts the reason and drops the contrasting “rather” that applies to that appearance.

findings.description: The repeated temptation to bite the fruit of knowledge becomes “take a bite of true wisdom,” and having already eaten that fruit becomes tasting “that truth.”

contexts.japanesePS3:

あるいは、私はもうその実を口にしてしまっているのかもしれない。

findings.alternative: The earlier English retains the fruit and the following Adam/Eve and fig-leaf reference keeps Eden recognizable. This is a local loss of the exact recurring object and an added characterization of its contents as true wisdom or truth.

findings.description: A singular trial that is simultaneously small and large becomes “the small and large trials.”

contexts.japanesePC: これは自分に課す、きっと小さくて大きな試練。
contexts.japanesePS3: これは自分に課す、きっと小さくて大きな試練。

contexts.UP: These are surely the small and large trials I must impose on myself.

MG.japanese:
さぁ、勇気を。そして私を家具から解放しよう。
そして新たな苦しみを受け入れることで、人間となろう。

Jessica was still at the age where tests and entrance exams are pretty nerve-racking.
Recently, she'd clashed often with her mother, who was enthusiastic about her education.
contexts.UP:
Jessica was still at that unpredictable age with exams right around the corner.
Recently, she had clashed often with her mother, who was enthusiastic about her education.
contexts.note: MG nerve-racking entrance exams restores nervousness. UP unpredictable age removes novice error but substitutes unpredictability and leaves exams generic.

MG.japanese:
朱志香だって、受験を控えたナーバスな年頃だ。
最近は教育熱心な母親と激突することが多かった。
MG.translation: Jessica was still at the age where tests and entrance exams are pretty nerve-racking. Recently, she'd clashed often with her mother, who was enthusiastic about her education.

UP.japanese:
朱志香だって、受験を控えたナーバスな年頃だ。
最近は教育熱心な母親と激突することが多かった。
UP.translation:
Jessica was still at that unpredictable age with exams right around the corner.
Recently, she had clashed often with her mother, who was enthusiastic about her education.

findings.sourceReading: Jessica too is at a sensitive, nervous age with entrance examinations approaching, explaining the frequent clashes with her education-minded mother.
findings.alternative: Both versions connect her conflict to studying and age. However, the English attributes lack of experience where the Japanese gives emotional strain before an approaching examination.

findings.description: 身内の恥 is rendered “some shame to herself,” dropping the explicit family referent in Natsuhi’s reason for her emotional outburst.

contexts.japanese:
紗音に非があったわけではないが、
身内の恥を見られたような気持ちになり、つい夏妃は感情的な言葉をぶつけてしまう。
…右代宮家ではよくあること。
しかし、そう思って割り切れるほど紗音はたくましくはないようだった。
contexts.japanesePC: 紗音に非があったわけではないが、身内の恥を見られたような気持ちになり、つい夏妃は感情的な言葉をぶつけてしまう。

contexts.MG:
Shannon hadn't actually done anything wrong,
but Natsuhi, who felt like something shameful to herself had been shown, lashed out at her emotionally.

but Natsuhi, who felt like some shame to herself had been shown, lashed out at her emotionally.
...This was something that often happened in the Ushiromiya family.
But it seemed that Shannon wasn't strong‐willed enough to accept it that way.
contexts.note: Both shame to herself omit family embarrassment as stated cause of Natsuhi outburst.

findings.sourceReading: Though Shannon did nothing wrong, Natsuhi feels that a family embarrassment has been witnessed and impulsively lashes out at her.
findings.alternative: The immediately preceding dispute is between Natsuhi and her daughter, so a reader can infer the family embarrassment. Personal shame may coexist with it, but the source specifically names shame within the family.

findings.description: “You couldn’t have complemented it as graceful” uses complemented in place of complimented or praised.

contexts.japanese:
震える指は、カチャカチャと食器を鳴らしてしまい、お世辞にも優雅とは言えない。
それを気の毒に思えば気の毒に思うほど、場は沈黙し、
夏妃はそれにイラついているように見え、さらに紗音を萎縮させる…。
contexts.japanesePC: 震える指は、カチャカチャと食器を鳴らしてしまい、お世辞にも優雅とは言えない。
contexts.japanesePS3:
震える指は、カチャカチャと食器を鳴らしてしまい、お世辞にも優雅とは言えない。
それを気の毒に思えば気の毒に思うほど、場は沈黙し、
夏妃はそれにイラついているように見え、さらに紗音を萎縮させる…。
contexts.WH: Her shaking fingers made the utensils clang, and you couldn't have complemented it as graceful.
contexts.MG:
Her shaking fingers made the utensils clang, and you couldn't have called it graceful, not even just to be polite.
The more pitiful she appeared, the greater the silence grew,
the more irritated Natsuhi looked, and the more Shannon cowered...
contexts.UP:
Her shaking fingers made the porcelain clatter, and you couldn't have called it graceful, not even as an empty compliment.
The more pitiful everyone thought that was, the greater the silence grew,
the more irritated Natsuhi looked, and the more Shannon cowered...
contexts.note: Both remove complemented error and clearly express impossibility of honestly calling service graceful.

MG.japanese: 震える指は、カチャカチャと食器を鳴らしてしまい、お世辞にも優雅とは言えない。それを気の毒に思えば気の毒に思うほど、場は沈黙し、夏妃はそれにイラついているように見え、さらに紗音を萎縮させる…。
MG.translation: Her shaking fingers made the utensils clang, and you couldn't have called it graceful, not even just to be polite. The more pitiful she appeared, the greater the silence grew, the more irritated Natsuhi looked, and the more Shannon cowered...

UP.japanese: 震える指は、カチャカチャと食器を鳴らしてしまい、お世辞にも優雅とは言えない。それを気の毒に思えば気の毒に思うほど、場は沈黙し、夏妃はそれにイラついているように見え、さらに紗音を萎縮させる…。
UP.translation: Her shaking fingers made the porcelain clatter, and you couldn't have called it graceful, not even as an empty compliment. The more pitiful everyone thought that was, the greater the silence grew, the more irritated Natsuhi looked, and the more Shannon cowered...

findings.sourceReading: Her trembling fingers rattle the tableware; even flattering description could not call the service graceful.
findings.alternative: The intended meaning is obvious in context. The substituted word is nevertheless an English lexical error, with no change to the scene’s events.

findings.description: 今更ノコノコと客間には戻れず becomes merely “still hadn’t returned,” while nonchalance is assigned to her time-killing.

contexts.japanese:
紗音と朱志香の姿は薔薇庭園にあった。
母親と口喧嘩をしてしまった朱志香は、今更ノコノコと客間には戻れず、こうして時間を潰しているのである。
contexts.japanesePC: 母親と口喧嘩をしてしまった朱志香は、今更ノコノコと客間には戻れず、こうして時間を潰しているのである。
contexts.japanesePS3:
紗音と朱志香の姿は薔薇庭園にあった。
母親と口喧嘩をしてしまった朱志香は、今更ノコノコと客間には戻れず、こうして時間を潰しているのである。
contexts.WH: Jessica, who had gotten into a fight with her mother, still hadn't returned to the parlor, and was nonchalantly killing time like this.
contexts.MG:
Shannon and Jessica were in the rose garden.
Jessica still hadn't returned to the parlor after getting into a fight with her mother and was nonchalantly killing time here.
contexts.UP:
Shannon and Jessica could be seen in the rose garden.
Jessica, having gotten into a fight with her mother, now felt unable to simply nonchalantly wander back into the parlor, and so found herself here, killing time.
contexts.note: MG nonchalantly killing time retains displaced adverb and mere nonreturn; UP restores inability to wander back nonchalantly after argument.

MG.japanese: 紗音と朱志香の姿は薔薇庭園にあった。母親と口喧嘩をしてしまった朱志香は、今更ノコノコと客間には戻れず、こうして時間を潰しているのである。
MG.translation: Shannon and Jessica were in the rose garden. Jessica still hadn't returned to the parlor after getting into a fight with her mother and was nonchalantly killing time here.

UP.japanese: 紗音と朱志香の姿は薔薇庭園にあった。母親と口喧嘩をしてしまった朱志香は、今更ノコノコと客間には戻れず、こうして時間を潰しているのである。
UP.translation: Shannon and Jessica could be seen in the rose garden. Jessica, having gotten into a fight with her mother, now felt unable to simply nonchalantly wander back into the parlor, and so found herself here, killing time.

findings.sourceReading: After arguing with her mother, Jessica cannot now simply come sheepishly back into the parlor, so she is passing time in the garden.
findings.alternative: She may outwardly pass time casually and the English retains her argument with her mother. But it removes the inability arising from awkwardness or pride that explains remaining outside.

findings.description: すぐにピンとくる becomes “had struck back,” replacing the immediate intuitive realization that explains Jessica’s teasing question with retaliatory action.

contexts.japanese:
「そ、そんなことありません…。
…とっても素敵な方だと思います」
「んー…？！
……ひょっとして紗音、譲治兄さんに惚れたぁ？」
紗音が珍しく、ちょっぴり強い口調で朱志香の言葉を遮ったので、朱志香はすぐにピンとくる。
「いえっ、…そういうことはない、かと……」
contexts.japanesePC: 紗音が珍しく、ちょっぴり強い口調で朱志香の言葉を遮ったので、朱志香はすぐにピンとくる。

contexts.WH: Shannon had uncharacteristically refuted Jessica's words forcefully, so Jessica had struck back.
contexts.MG:

"Hmmmm...?!

findings.sourceReading: Shannon unusually interrupts Jessica’s criticism with a slightly forceful defense, so Jessica immediately catches on to her attraction to George.
findings.alternative: Jessica’s actual question about being in love lets a reader reconstruct the insight. “Struck back” may describe teasing in response, but the source specifically supplies recognition, not retaliation.

findings.description: 浮いた話 becomes “anything bad,” moving from George’s little-discussed love life to a broad claim about his reputation.

contexts.japanese:
「そういや、譲治兄さんって、あまり浮いた話を聞いたことないし。
あれ？
確か、家庭的な子がタイプだとか前に聞いたかな？
そりゃいいぜ、紗音ぴったりじゃん！」
contexts.japanesePC: 「そういや、譲治兄さんって、あまり浮いた話を聞いたことないし。あれ？　確か以前、家庭的な子がタイプだとか前に聞いたかな？
contexts.japanesePS3:
「そういや、譲治兄さんって、あまり浮いた話を聞いたことないし。
あれ？
確か、家庭的な子がタイプだとか前に聞いたかな？
そりゃいいぜ、紗音ぴったりじゃん！」
contexts.WH: "Come to think of it, I almost never hear anything bad about George nii-san.  Huh?  I think I remember hearing him say that family-oriented girls were his type, didn't I?

findings.sourceReading: Jessica says she rarely hears romantic gossip about George, then recalls his preferred type of girl and finds Shannon a good match.
findings.alternative: Romantic gossip can sometimes be scandalous, but this context supplies no misconduct. The retained next sentence keeps the matchmaking topic clear without restoring the specific lack of romantic news.

findings.description: 持たざる者 becomes “those who didn’t keep it,” replacing lack of means with apparent failure to retain something.

contexts.japanese:
金蔵は莫大な資産を持っていて、それを息子たちに貸し与えていた。
もちろん、生活に困窮したからと貸す金ではない。
…その借りた莫大な金を使い、どのように事業を拡大するか。
どれほどの利子を付けて、いつまでに返済できるのか。
持たざる者の借金とは違う。
攻める者の借金なのである。
contexts.japanesePC: 持たざる者の借金とは違う。攻める者の借金なのである。
contexts.japanesePS3:
金蔵は莫大な資産を持っていて、それを息子たちに貸し与えていた。
もちろん、生活に困窮したからと貸す金ではない。
…その借りた莫大な金を使い、どのように事業を拡大するか。
どれほどの利子を付けて、いつまでに返済できるのか。
持たざる者の借金とは違う。
攻める者の借金なのである。
contexts.WH: This wasn't a loan for those who didn't keep it.  It was a loan for those who were on the offense.
contexts.MG:
Kinzo had vast resources, and he lent those out to his children.
Of course, they didn't borrow money because they were living in poverty.
...How would they expand their businesses with the vast sums they wanted to borrow?
How much interest would be attached, and how long would they have to repay it?
This wasn't the sort of loan designed for the poor.
It was a loan for those who were on the offensive.
contexts.UP:
Kinzo had vast resources, and he lent those out to his children.
Of course, this was not money to lend because they had gotten themselves into financial trouble.
...How would they expand their business, using the vast amount of money that they borrowed?
How much interest would be attached, and how soon could it be repaid?
This wasn't a loan for the have‐nots.
It was a loan for those who were on the offense.
contexts.note: Both lack-of-means poor/have-nots correctly restore distinction from failure to retain wealth.

攻める者の借金なのである。

findings.description: 大きなお金の動く緊張の強いられる会合 becomes a situation in which nervousness forces them to move money, reversing the causal relation.

contexts.japanese:
だからこうして、六軒島に親族が訪れて、金蔵に事業説明を行なう光景はたまにあることだった。
親たちにとっては、大きなお金の動く緊張の強いられる会合かもしれない。
でも、六軒島という孤島に住む朱志香にとって、そんな機会は、いとこたちと会うことができる貴重なものでもあった。
contexts.japanesePC: 親たちにとっては、大きなお金の動く緊張の強いられる会合かもしれない。
contexts.japanesePS3:
だからこうして、六軒島に親族が訪れて、金蔵に事業説明を行なう光景はたまにあることだった。
親たちにとっては、大きなお金の動く緊張の強いられる会合かもしれない。
でも、六軒島という孤島に住む朱志香にとって、そんな機会は、いとこたちと会うことができる貴重なものでもあった。
contexts.WH: To the parents, it might be a situation where they were forced by nervousness to move a lot of money.
contexts.MG:
So Rokkenjima would sometimes play host to this spectacle, where relatives visited and described their businesses to Kinzo.
To the parents, these meetings burdened them with the strain of having to move a vast amount of money.
But to Jessica, who lived on this isolated island called Rokkenjima, it was a precious opportunity to meet up with her cousins.
contexts.UP:
So there was occasionally this spectacle where relatives visited Rokkenjima and explained their business to Kinzo.
To the parents, it may well have been a meeting concerning the movement of large sums of money, forcing immense stress upon them.
But to Jessica, who lived on this isolated island called Rokkenjima, it was a precious opportunity to meet up with her cousins.
contexts.note: MG restores money-related strain but makes meeting strain concern having to move funds, rather than large funds at stake imposing tension. UP explicitly preserves money movement causing stress and JP tentative may.

MG.japanese: 親たちにとっては、大きなお金の動く緊張の強いられる会合かもしれない。でも、六軒島という孤島に住む朱志香にとって、そんな機会は、いとこたちと会うことができる貴重なものでもあった。

findings.sourceReading: For the parents, this may be a meeting involving large sums and therefore compelling tension; for Jessica it is a chance to see her cousins.
findings.alternative: The context establishes business lending and a tense meeting, so the intended meaning is partly recoverable. It does not support nervousness as the force causing financial movement.

contexts.WH: "It's natural to be prudent when lending money.  Of course, my father will use what he borrows to expand his business, and he came with a plan that could be refused.  Everything else is left up to the presentation.
contexts.MG:
"It's natural to be prudent when lending money.
Of course, my father will use what he borrows to expand his business, and he came with a plan that promises a solid probability of repayment.
Everything else is left up to the presentation.
contexts.UP:
"It's natural to be prudent when lending money.
Of course, my father has come with a plan by which he can expand his business with what he borrows, and which he can definitely repay.
Everything else will be up to the presentation."
contexts.note: Both restore repayment plan, not rejected plan. MG solid probability slightly weakens assurance relative to UP definitely repay but core business/repayment relation restored.

MG.japanese: 「お金を貸す時、慎重になるのは当然のことだよ。もちろんうちの父さんも、借り入れた分で事業を拡大し、しっかり返却できるプランを持って訪れてる。あとはプレゼンテーション次第ってところだろうね」
MG.translation: "It's natural to be prudent when lending money. Of course, my father will use what he borrows to expand his business, and he came with a plan that promises a solid probability of repayment. Everything else is left up to the presentation.

UP.japanese: 「お金を貸す時、慎重になるのは当然のことだよ。もちろんうちの父さんも、借り入れた分で事業を拡大し、しっかり返却できるプランを持って訪れてる。あとはプレゼンテーション次第ってところだろうね」
UP.translation: "It's natural to be prudent when lending money. Of course, my father has come with a plan by which he can expand his business with what he borrows, and which he can definitely repay. Everything else will be up to the presentation."

findings.sourceReading: George says his father arrived with a plan to expand the business using the loan and reliably repay it; the presentation is what remains.
findings.alternative: A lender may of course refuse a plan, and the surrounding lines explain scrutiny. But this possibility is not what George asserts here and does not replace the repayment component.

findings.description: 正座をさせる becomes telling Krauss to sit up straight, reducing a compelled kneeling posture to a generic posture correction. The several witnessed occasions are also strengthened to often.

…紗音も何度か、金蔵が蔵臼に、平手で打ったり、正座をさせているところを見たことがある。
……いい歳にもなってそれを強いられるのは、相当の屈辱のはずだ。
そのような現場に居合わせてしまわないよう、気を利かすのもこの右代宮家では、使用人の立派な務めだ。
…もっとも、その意味では、居合わせてしまった紗音はつまり、ミスしているわけだが。

contexts.WH: ...Shannon herself had often seen Kinzo slap Krauss and tell him to sit up straight.
contexts.MG:
As Shannon hung her head, she thought back on a scene familiar to those who worked in the mansion.
Even Krauss, who acted haughtily towards his siblings, was still treated like a child by Kinzo.
...Shannon herself had often seen Kinzo slap Krauss and tell him to sit up straight.
......It was probably very embarrassing to be coerced like that at his age.
Taking care to avoid being present at times like that...was one of the important responsibilities held by the servants working here.
...However, the fact that Shannon had ended up witnessing such a scene...meant that she'd messed up at least once in the past.
contexts.UP:
As Shannon hung her head, she thought back on those scenes she had grown used to seeing while working in the mansion.
Even Krauss, who acted haughtily towards his siblings, was still treated like a child by Kinzo.
...Shannon herself had often seen Kinzo slapping Krauss, or making him sit in seiza‐style.
......It was probably deeply humiliating to have that forced upon him at his age.
In the Ushiromiya family, taking care not to be present when this happened was one of the great tasks of the servants.
...Of course, that did mean that Shannon had been making mistakes by being witness to it.
contexts.note: MG sit up straight remains wrong posture; UP restores seiza. Both often retain excessive frequency where JP says witnessed several times.

findings.sourceReading: Shannon has on several occasions seen Kinzo slap Krauss or make him sit in seiza, illustrating humiliating treatment of an adult as a child.
findings.alternative: The slapping and explicit embarrassment remain, preserving the larger abusive dynamic. Still, ordinary upright sitting does not communicate the source’s specific imposed posture and disciplinary association.

findings.sourceReading: Shannon starts to say that women aware of his real charm are surely nearby, then retreats to saying there are many. The narrator explains that she likely intended to say someone was close by.
findings.alternative: The English narrator explicitly restores “one really close,” preserving the self-directed implication. This limits the defect to her audible false start and the shift from existing recognition to future recognition.

contexts.MG:

"Shouldn't marriage meetings be done at a more mature age...?!

findings.description: The person made to forget the scolding becomes “me” in Shannon’s narration instead of Natsuhi.

contexts.japanese:
もしここに譲治さまがいてくれたなら。
さりげなく私を助けてくれただろうか。
わざと空気が読めないかのように陽気に現れ、話題をひらりと逸らし、夏妃に叱責していたことすら忘れさせてしまうに違いない…。
contexts.japanesePC: わざと空気が読めないかのように陽気に現れ、話題をひらりと逸らし、夏妃に叱責していたことすら忘れさせてしまうに違いない…。
contexts.japanesePS3:
もしここに譲治さまがいてくれたなら。
さりげなく私を助けてくれただろうか。

contexts.WH: I'm sure he would show up cheerfully, intentionally acting like he doesn't know what's going on, nimbly change the subject, and make me forget I was ever rebuked by Natsuhi...
contexts.MG:
If only George-sama were here.
Would he casually step in and save me?
Surely he'd show up cheerfully, intentionally acting like he didn't know what was going on, nimbly change the subject, and make me forget I'd ever been rebuked by Natsuhi...
contexts.UP:
If only George‐sama had been here,
perhaps he would have casually stepped in and saved me.
I'm sure he would show up cheerfully, intentionally acting like he doesn't know what's going on, nimbly change the subject, and make me forget I was ever reprimanded by Natsuhi...
contexts.note: Both make Shannon forget being rebuked, rather than Natsuhi forget having scolded.

MG.japanese:
もしここに譲治さまがいてくれたなら。
さりげなく私を助けてくれただろうか。わざと空気が読めないかのように陽気に現れ、話題をひらりと逸らし、夏妃に叱責していたことすら忘れさせてしまうに違いない…。
MG.translation: If only George-sama were here. Would he casually step in and save me? Surely he'd show up cheerfully, intentionally acting like he didn't know what was going on, nimbly change the subject, and make me forget I'd ever been rebuked by Natsuhi...

UP.japanese:
もしここに譲治さまがいてくれたなら。
さりげなく私を助けてくれただろうか。わざと空気が読めないかのように陽気に現れ、話題をひらりと逸らし、夏妃に叱責していたことすら忘れさせてしまうに違いない…。
UP.translation:
If only George‐sama had been here,
perhaps he would have casually stepped in and saved me. I'm sure he would show up cheerfully, intentionally acting like he doesn't know what's going on, nimbly change the subject, and make me forget I was ever reprimanded by Natsuhi...

findings.sourceReading: Shannon imagines George cheerfully appearing, pretending not to read the atmosphere, and deftly changing the subject so thoroughly that Natsuhi forgets the scolding itself.
findings.alternative: The embedded Japanese has awkward 夏妃に where the semantic subject would ordinarily use が, but the ongoing-scolding scene and earlier atmosphere rescue support distraction of the scolder. Relieving Shannon’s memory is a plausible consequence, not the described intervention. Confidence is limited to this contextual reading, not a claim of pristine retail wording.

findings.description: 素直ではない becomes “dishonest,” suggesting deceit rather than the familiar guarded or contrary manner of his sulky response.

素直ではない嘉音らしい態度だが、…私には少しだけ嬉しかった。
私の代わりに、怒ってくれたから。

「…………ふん」
嘉音は不貞腐れたようにそっぽを向く。
素直ではない嘉音らしい態度だが、…私には少しだけ嬉しかった。
私の代わりに、怒ってくれたから。
contexts.WH: It was a dishonest reaction, very like Kanon, ...but I was a little happy.
contexts.MG:
"......Hmph."
Kanon turned away as though sulking.
It was a reaction that hid his true feelings, which was very like Kanon, ...but I was a little happy.
He was getting mad for my sake.

"............Hmph."
Kanon faced away, acting sulky.
It was a dishonest reaction, very like Kanon‐kun, ...but I was a little happy.
He got angry in my place.
contexts.note: MG hides true feelings restores guarded/sulky sense; UP dishonest retains deceit implication.

MG.japanese: 嘉音は不貞腐れたようにそっぽを向く。素直ではない嘉音らしい態度だが、…私には少しだけ嬉しかった。私の代わりに、怒ってくれたから。
MG.translation: Kanon turned away as though sulking. It was a reaction that hid his true feelings, which was very like Kanon, ...but I was a little happy. He was getting mad for my sake.

UP.japanese: 嘉音は不貞腐れたようにそっぽを向く。素直ではない嘉音らしい態度だが、…私には少しだけ嬉しかった。私の代わりに、怒ってくれたから。
UP.translation: Kanon faced away, acting sulky. It was a dishonest reaction, very like Kanon‐kun, ...but I was a little happy. He got angry in my place.

findings.sourceReading: His turning away is typical of Kanon’s difficulty being straightforward or openly receptive; Shannon is nevertheless happy he is angry on her behalf.
findings.alternative: Dishonest can be used broadly for not openly expressing feelings, and the sulking remains clear. It ordinarily carries a stronger claim of deceit than this source description.

findings.description: 自分を顧みない becomes “didn’t reflect on himself,” misreading disregard for self as a failure of introspection.

contexts.japanese:

…時折、彼は自分を顧みない。
強く断らなくては、彼は自分の仕事を疎かにしてでも私を手伝ってしまうのだ…。
嘉音は、自分の厚意を退けられたことを少しだけ悲しく思ったが、
それが結果的に余計に彼女を苦しめることにもなると理解し、ひとつ小さなため息をつく。

Shannon knew Kanon's character well.  ...Sometimes, he didn't reflect on himself.

UP.translation:
Shannon knew Kanon's character well.
...Sometimes, he didn't reflect on himself. If I don't refuse forcefully, he will help me even if it means neglecting his own job...

findings.sourceReading: Shannon knows that Kanon sometimes fails to consider himself: unless she refuses firmly, he will help her even at the expense of his own work and risk punishment.
findings.alternative: The retained next sentence and her preceding warning restore the specific risk to his duties. The trait stated as their explanation nevertheless changes from self-neglect to lack of reflection.

findings.sourceReading: After reacting to a heart having been given to furniture, the witch says that “that one” too sometimes does amusing things. The source leaves the agent unnamed here.

findings.description: 西暦紀元 becomes “the start of the modern era,” replacing the Christian-era calendar origin in the identification of the unnamed man. The earlier 紀元前 similarly becomes before the modern era.

contexts.japanese:
「人間は世界を構成する元素について、紀元前の昔から探求を続けてきた。
古代ギリシャ人たちは風火水土の４つで世界の説明を試みたという」
「その後も数千年かけて人間たちは、その４つに様々な元素を加え、
五大、六大、七大、八大、十二大と、様々な解釈で世界を説明しようとしたが、
唯一の真実である“一なる元素”を説明することはできなかった」
「………しかし、星の導きによって現れたひとりの男が、ついにこの、世界を構成する一なる元素を説明した。
何かわかるか……？」
「…………ぇ、
………ぁ、
………だ、
………だ、誰………」
紗音は恐る恐る振り返る…。
そこには、……“い”た。
幻覚などではなく、現実として。
それが白昼の幻でないことを、落雷のコントラストがはっきりと示した。
「……それは『愛』よ。
くっくくくくくくく！」
肖像画の魔女は、優雅に黄金の煙管を咥え、くすりと笑った。
…人類の思考が迷走し、もっとも単純な答えから遠のいていった無知を笑った。
「その男は世界の全てを愛で説明した。
それこそが一なる元素。
男は最小の数で世界の構成を説明しきったのだ」
「……何とも単純明快にして豪快爽快愉快痛快。
…やがてその男の生まれた年は、西暦紀元と呼ばれるようになったがな。

contexts.WH: ......How simple and clear, how splendid, exhilarating, pleasant and thrilling.  ...The year that man was finally born was called the start of the modern era.  ......*cackle*cackle*!"
contexts.MG:
"Humans have continually searched for the elements that make up the world, since before the modern era.
It is said that in ancient times, the Greeks tried explaining the world with the four elements of wind, fire, water, and earth.
And after that, over several millennia, humans added several elements to those four,
trying to explain the world with several interpretations such as the five elements, the six elements, the seven elements, the eight elements, and the twelve elements,

Know what it is...?"

findings.sourceReading: The witch says that the year of this man’s birth eventually came to be called the beginning of the Christian/common-era reckoning, linking her star-guided man and love teaching to that calendar reference.
findings.alternative: The star, birth, and love imagery still support the implied figure. Modern era can loosely suggest contemporary calendar use, but it conventionally denotes a historical period rather than the source’s calendar epoch. The historical assertion is audited as the witch’s speech, not independently endorsed.

findings.description: 想い人 becomes “a pair of people with feelings for each other,” adding reciprocity to the offered union.

contexts.japanese:
「そなたを想い人と添い遂げさせてやっても良いと言っている。
……本来ならば、それに見合うだけの対価を要求するところだが」
「…くっくっく、妾は機嫌が良い。
それに、そなたは妾への礼を欠かさず、今日までよく尽くした。
それへの褒美としてやっても良い」
「…………ほ、…………本当ですか……」
本当なら、紗音はこの現実感を欠く客人に呆然として言葉など発せられたわけもない。
……しかし、まるですでに魔女の術中に囚われてしまったかのように。
…紗音は魔女の問い掛けに答えてしまう。
「妾の魔法に掛かれば、想い人と結ばれるように取り計らうなど、造作もない」
contexts.japanesePC: 「妾の魔法に掛かれば、想い人と結ばれるように取り計らうなど、造作もない。」
contexts.japanesePS3:
「そなたを想い人と添い遂げさせてやっても良いと言っている。
……本来ならば、それに見合うだけの対価を要求するところだが」
「…くっくっく、妾は機嫌が良い。

……しかし、まるですでに魔女の術中に囚われてしまったかのように。
…紗音は魔女の問い掛けに答えてしまう。
「妾の魔法に掛かれば、想い人と結ばれるように取り計らうなど、造作もない」
contexts.WH: "If I use magic, it is no trouble at all to arrange for a pair of people with feelings for each other to be joined."
contexts.MG:
"I am offering to bring you and the one you love together.
...Normally, I would demand something of equal value in return."
"...*cackle* However, I am in a good mood.
And you have never failed to pay your respects to me in the past.
That is something worth rewarding."
"......I-Is that true......?"
Normally, Shannon would've been shocked and struck dumb by this seemingly impossible guest.
......However, almost as though she was already under the witch's spell,
...Shannon responded.
"With my magic, it would be no trouble at all to arrange for you to be joined with the one you love."
contexts.UP:
"I am offering to bring you and the one you love together.
......Normally, I would demand something of equal value in return."
"...*cackle*, I am in a good mood.
And you have never failed to pay your respects to me in the past.
That is something worth rewarding."
"............Do, ............do you really mean it......?"
Normally, Shannon would have been shocked by this guest who lacked realism, and wouldn't have been able to speak.
......However, as though she had already been caught in the witch's trap,
...Shannon responded to the witch.
"With my magic, it is no trouble at all to arrange for a pair of people with feelings for each other to be joined."
contexts.note: MG uses the one you love in both offers. UP corrects row 796 but retains a pair with feelings for each other in row 805, adding established reciprocity.

MG.japanese: 「妾の魔法に掛かれば、想い人と結ばれるように取り計らうなど、造作もない」
MG.translation: "With my magic, it would be no trouble at all to arrange for you to be joined with the one you love."

UP.japanese: 「妾の魔法に掛かれば、想い人と結ばれるように取り計らうなど、造作もない」
UP.translation: "With my magic, it is no trouble at all to arrange for a pair of people with feelings for each other to be joined."

findings.sourceReading: Beatrice says arranging for Shannon to be united with the person she loves is trivial for her magic.
findings.alternative: The intended romantic outcome may include reciprocal affection, and previous dialogue has shown George appreciating Shannon. But this offer does not stipulate or establish that both already have feelings for each other.

findings.description: 最後の理性で踏み止まる becomes “gave up on her last bit of common sense,” directly reversing the stated action. The near-spoken verification also becomes “Yes, that’s true.”

…思わずそう口にしてしまいそうな自分を、紗音は最後の理性で踏み止まる。
魔女は、魔女だ。
禍々しい存在なのだ。
魔女ベアトリーチェが、自分の心の隙間をついて、私を虜にしようとしているに違いないのだ……。
小さい頃から、何度も絵本のおとぎ話で警告されてきた誘惑が、今まさに私の前にあった。

contexts.WH: Yes, that's true.  ...Shannon, who almost said that without thinking, gave up on her last bit of common sense.
contexts.MG:
"Yes, of course."
...Shannon almost said that without thinking, but held back with her last bit of common sense.
After all, this is a witch.
A sinister being.
The witch Beatrice is clearly trying to slip in through the cracks in my heart and take me prisoner......
That sort of temptation, which so many fairy tale picture books warned me about when I was young, is right in front of me now.
contexts.UP:
You do mean it, don't you...
...Those words almost escaped Shannon's lips, but she held herself back, with her final reserves of reason.
A witch is a witch.
A sinister being.
The witch Beatrice is clearly trying to slip in through the cracks in my heart and take me prisoner......
That sort of temptation, which so many fairy tale picture books had warned me about when I was young, was right in front of me now.
contexts.note: Both restore holding back with remaining reason. MG still changes the near-spoken verification into Yes, of course; row 807 explicitly makes it almost spoken despite quotation marks. UP restores the verification and restraint.

findings.description: 不気味な錯覚 becomes a creepy hallucination, giving a sensory-unreality label to her unsettling impression about the bargain.

contexts.japanese:

鏡は恐らく魔女を縛るためのもの。
…なれば、鏡は魔女のために割られるべきもののはず。
……なのにそれがまるで、紗音のために割らなければならないような気がする。
何かの前提が摩り替えられている気がする…。

contexts.WH: Shannon was trapped by a creepy hallucination.
contexts.MG:
Shannon felt overwhelmed by an eerie illusion.
The mirror probably existed for the purpose of restraining the witch.

It felt like some premise had been switched...

findings.sourceReading: Shannon is seized by an uncanny mistaken impression: what ought to be breaking the mirror for the witch seems to become something she must do for herself, as though a premise has been substituted.
findings.alternative: Hallucination can be used loosely for an unreal impression, and the following explanation retains the actual thought. Here the source is immediately unpacked as a conceptual shift in the bargain, not a report of a new sensory perception.

findings.description: 今宵は退散しよう becomes “now, let us disperse,” omitting tonight and including the listeners in a group action.

contexts.japanese:

敵意の眼差しは心地よくあるが、美容にはちと悪いのでな？
くっくくくくく…」
「消えろ…！！
お前が何者か知らないが、お前は紗音を脅かしている！
二度と現れるな！！」
嘉音のその言葉は、魔女をひどく不快にさせたようだった。
「……言葉を選ばぬか下賎め。
…妾は敬う者に寛大だが、敬わぬ者には残酷であるぞ…？」
魔女が笑顔のまま、表情を歪ませ始める…。
そして、人の五感では形容できぬ何かの圧迫感が、徐々に部屋を満たしていく…。
それが何か理解できなくても、恐ろしいものであることはすぐに理解できた…。
海で泳ぐ時、その下の海中に巨大な何かが横切ったなら、正体を知るより早く陸に逃れたくなるはず。
…それと同じこと！
「お、……おやめ下さいベアトリーチェさま！！
嘉音くんはまだ子どもなんです。
言葉遣いについては謝ります！」
「………………………」
「……………………ッ」
体を張って紗音の前に立ちはだかる嘉音。
…その額に緊迫の汗が浮かぶ。
その時、確かに魔女は嘉音の命運を握っていた。
…指一本必要ない。
自らの微笑みをひとつ歪めるだけで、その命運を握り潰してしまえるほど簡単に、その命運を握っていた…。
嘉音にもそれがわかっているのだ。
だから汗が浮かぶ。
足が竦む…。
しかし、ベアトリーチェはふっと緊張感を解き、笑った。
「………良かろう。
そなたが求めるなら特別に許そう。
…嘉音とやら。
彼女に免じて今宵は許してつかわす。
感謝するがよいぞ。
さて、今宵はこれで退散する」

contexts.MG:

*cackle*cackle*cackle*..."
"Disappear...!!

Even though they couldn't comprehend what it was, they immediately realized it to be something terrifying...
If you were swimming in the ocean, and something large went by in the water beneath you, you would want to escape to the land even before you learned what it was.
...This was the same as that!
contexts.note: MG retains could not be noticed; UP restores could not be described. Both retain immediate terror and ocean analogy.

MG.japanese: 魔女が笑顔のまま、表情を歪ませ始める…。そして、人の五感では形容できぬ何かの圧迫感が、徐々に部屋を満たしていく…。それが何か理解できなくても、恐ろしいものであることはすぐに理解できた…。
MG.translation: While she still smiled, the witch's face began to twist itself... Then, an oppressive feeling that couldn't be noticed with any of the five senses gradually filled the room... Even though they couldn't understand it, they immediately realized it was something terrifying...

UP.japanese: 魔女が笑顔のまま、表情を歪ませ始める…。そして、人の五感では形容できぬ何かの圧迫感が、徐々に部屋を満たしていく…。それが何か理解できなくても、恐ろしいものであることはすぐに理解できた…。
UP.translation: While she still smiled, the witch's expression began to warp... And an oppressive feeling that couldn't be described with any of the five senses gradually filled the room... Even though they couldn't comprehend what it was, they immediately realized it to be something terrifying...

findings.sourceReading: A pressure impossible to characterize through the human senses gradually fills the room; they immediately recognize its terror even though they cannot understand what it is.
findings.alternative: The English still calls it a feeling and immediately describes their response, so an unusual sensed experience is inferable. It nevertheless expressly denies sensory notice rather than adequate characterization.

findings.description: 体を張って becomes “his body outstretched,” supplying bodily extension in place of personal risk or bodily protection.

contexts.japanese:
体を張って紗音の前に立ちはだかる嘉音。
…その額に緊迫の汗が浮かぶ。
その時、確かに魔女は嘉音の命運を握っていた。
…指一本必要ない。
自らの微笑みをひとつ歪めるだけで、その命運を握り潰してしまえるほど簡単に、その命運を握っていた…。
嘉音にもそれがわかっているのだ。
だから汗が浮かぶ。
足が竦む…。

だから汗が浮かぶ。

contexts.WH: Kanon blocked the way to Shannon, his body outstretched.  ...There was tense sweat on his forehead.
contexts.MG:
Kanon placed his body between the witch and Shannon.
...There was tense sweat on his forehead.
At that time, the witch certainly held Kanon's fate in the palm of her hand.
...She didn't even need to lift a finger.
She held a grasp on his fate so tight that a single twist of her smile could easily crush it...
Kanon understood that as well.
So he started sweating.
His knees felt weak...
contexts.UP:
Kanon blocked the way to Shannon at the risk of his life.
...There was tense sweat on his forehead.
In that moment, the witch certainly had Kanon's fate in her clutches.
...She didn't even need to move a finger.
She had Kanon's fate so readily in her grasp that she could crush it completely with a single twist of her own smile...
Kanon also understood that.
Which is why he was sweating,
and his knees felt weak...
contexts.note: MG placing his body between them with nearby lethal threat conveys bodily protection and risk without invented extension. UP explicitly states risk of life.

findings.description: 出会いが水族館をきっかけにした becomes “used the aquarium as an excuse to get together,” inventing purposeful pretext in place of an originating occasion.

contexts.japanese:
紗音と譲治が旅行先を沖縄に選んだのは、巨大な水族館があったからだった。
それは、彼らの出会いが水族館をきっかけにしたものだったからだ。
水族館で始まった縁だから、初めてのお泊り旅行の行き先も水族館というちょっと記念的な意味もあったに違いない。

contexts.WH: And they had used the aquarium as an excuse to get together.
contexts.MG:
Shannon and George had chosen to go to Okinawa because there was a huge aquarium there.
They did this because an aquarium had given them the opportunity to start going out.
Since their relationship had started at an aquarium, having their first overnight trip also be to an aquarium must have held some commemorative value.
contexts.UP:
Shannon and George had chosen to go to Okinawa because there was a huge aquarium there.
That was because their first meeting had revolved around an aquarium.
Since they had started at an aquarium, having their first overnight trip also be to an aquarium must have held some commemorative value.
contexts.note: Both remove purposeful aquarium pretext and restore an originating occasion. UP first meeting creates a different continuity issue, recorded separately below.

MG.japanese: 紗音と譲治が旅行先を沖縄に選んだのは、巨大な水族館があったからだった。それは、彼らの出会いが水族館をきっかけにしたものだったからだ。水族館で始まった縁だから、初めてのお泊り旅行の行き先も水族館というちょっと記念的な意味もあったに違いない。

findings.sourceReading: They chose Okinawa’s huge aquarium because their relationship began through an aquarium, giving the first overnight aquarium trip commemorative significance.
findings.alternative: The next English sentence explicitly restores that their relationship started at an aquarium. Using one as an excuse can also fit a date, but does not translate the narrator’s given reason here.

findings.description: てきめん becomes “instantaneous,” converting the claimed effectiveness of the witch’s magic into an absolute timing assertion.

contexts.japanese:
「当然よ、妾の魔法はてきめんである。
…そなたにはまるで、二人が出会うのは予め決められた運命であったかのように感じているかも知れぬ。
だがそれは間違いよ、ゆめゆめ運命だなどと思うでないぞ」
「……そ、……それはわかってます」
魔女は念を押す。
２つのことを、念を押す。
譲治との縁は、本来なら絶対にありえなかった運命。
……そして、それを捻じ曲げるほどに、魔女の力が強大であると。

contexts.WH: "Naturally, my magic is instantaneous.  Maybe you feel that your meeting was a predetermined fate.  But that isn't correct, don't think this has anything to do with fate."
contexts.MG:
"Naturally. The effects of my magic are immediate.
Perhaps you feel your meeting was a predetermined fate.
However, that is a mistake. Don't even think fate has anything to do with it."
"......I-I understand that."
The witch was calling attention to something.
Two things, actually.
First, that Shannon's relationship with George was a fate that'd be absolutely impossible under normal circumstances.
...Second, that the power of the witch was great enough to overturn that fact.
contexts.UP:
"Naturally; my magic is instantaneous.
...You may even be feeling as if your meeting was a predetermined fate.
But that isn't correct; don't think for a moment this has anything to do with fate."
"......I, ......I understand that."

findings.sourceReading: The witch says her magic is strikingly effective, then insists the relationship was not naturally predetermined but made possible by her power.
findings.alternative: てきめん can suggest a prompt or conspicuous effect, and instantaneous can be hyperbole. The source does not nonetheless specify zero delay, and the surrounding statement is about efficacy and altered fate.

"Hmph.

findings.description: 少し厳しい口調 and 非常に厳しく are rendered as speaking seriously and seeming extremely serious, weakening the contrast between gentle Shannon and unusually stern reproach.

contexts.japanese:
紗音が珍しく、少し厳しい口調で言う。
…それは、彼女をよく知る嘉音にとっては、非常に厳しく感じられるのだろう。
紗音の口調に比べれば過剰なくらい嘉音は驚き、閉口する。
「確かにベアトリーチェさまは、人間とは違う。
恐ろしい力を持っているし、恐れ敬わなければならない存在だと思う。
…でも、人間とは違うからといって、それだけを理由に忌み嫌うのはとても失礼なことだと思うの」
「…………姉さんの言いたいことはわかるよ。
…姉さんはあいつにあのブローチをもらってから変わった。
まるで魔女の虜だよ。
譲治さまとの仲を取り持ってもらって、頭が上がらないんだ」
「…そんなことを言わないで」
「あいつは人間じゃない。
何を考えてるかわからない。
だから気を許しちゃ駄目なんだ。
………そして、人間じゃないのは僕らも同じだよ。
姉さん」
嘉音の言葉が厳しくなる。
contexts.japanesePC: 紗音が珍しく、少し厳しい口調で言う。

contexts.WH: Shannon spoke seriously, which was unusual for her.
contexts.MG:
There was a touch of sternness in Shannon's voice, which was unusual for her.
...To Kanon, who knew her well, she must've sounded extremely stern.
Kanon, looking excessively surprised considering Shannon's tone, fell silent.
"It's true that Beatrice-sama is different from humans.
She has a terrifying power, so I think it's right for us to fear and respect her.
...Still, I think it's incredibly rude to despise her just because she isn't human."
"......I understand what you're trying to say, Nee-san.
...You've changed ever since she gave you that brooch.
It's like you're her prisoner.
She brought you and George-sama together, and now you're indebted to her."
"...Don't say things like that."
"That thing isn't human.
We don't know what she's thinking.
So you mustn't trust her.
......And we aren't humans either,
Nee-san."
Kanon's words grew more serious.
contexts.UP:
Shannon spoke seriously, which was unusual for her.
...To Kanon, who knew her well, it must have seemed extremely serious.
Kanon showed almost excessive surprise at Shannon's style of speech, and remained silent.
"It's true that Beatrice‐sama is different from humans.
She has a terrifying power, so I think she is to be feared and respected.
...But I think it's really rude to loathe her just for the single reason that she's different from a human."
"............I know what you're trying to say, Nee‐san.
...You've changed since she gave you that brooch.
It's like you're the witch's prisoner.
She mediated your relationship with George‐sama, and now you're indebted to her."
"...Don't say things like that."
"She isn't human.
We don't know what she's thinking.
You mustn't trust her.
.........And we aren't humans either,
Nee‐san."
Kanon's words became more serious.
contexts.note: MG restores Shannon sternness at 445–446 but retains Kanon more serious at 461. UP retains serious for both speakers rather than stern/harsh reproach.

MG.japanese:
紗音が珍しく、少し厳しい口調で言う。
…それは、彼女をよく知る嘉音にとっては、非常に厳しく感じられるのだろう。紗音の口調に比べれば過剰なくらい嘉音は驚き、閉口する。
MG.translation: There was a touch of sternness in Shannon's voice, which was unusual for her. ...To Kanon, who knew her well, she must've sounded extremely stern. Kanon, looking excessively surprised considering Shannon's tone, fell silent.

UP.japanese:
紗音が珍しく、少し厳しい口調で言う。
…それは、彼女をよく知る嘉音にとっては、非常に厳しく感じられるのだろう。紗音の口調に比べれば過剰なくらい嘉音は驚き、閉口する。
UP.translation:
Shannon spoke seriously, which was unusual for her.
...To Kanon, who knew her well, it must have seemed extremely serious. Kanon showed almost excessive surprise at Shannon's style of speech, and remained silent.

findings.sourceReading: She speaks a little sternly; to Kanon, who knows her, it must feel very stern.
findings.alternative: Serious speech can carry reprimand in this context, and Kanon’s startled silence preserves its impact. The specific harshness, however, becomes general seriousness.

MG.japanese: 嘉音の批判は、いつの間にか紗音と魔女の交流から焦点をずらしているようだった。…紗音もすぐにそれを察する。

UP.japanese: 嘉音の批判は、いつの間にか紗音と魔女の交流から焦点をずらしているようだった。…紗音もすぐにそれを察する。

findings.sourceReading: During this conversation, Kanon’s criticism has imperceptibly moved from her association with the witch to her own status and entitlement to love. Shannon quickly notices that change of target.
findings.alternative: The preceding dialogue still lets readers infer the new target. But から attaches to the focus being left behind, not a date when criticism changed; “suddenly started meeting” also moves いつの間にか onto an unsupported event.

findings.description: 自分が家具であることを苦悩した日々の洗礼 attributes the metaphorical baptism or ordeal to the days spent agonizing over being furniture. “After being baptized as furniture in his days of suffering” instead makes furniture the status conferred by baptism.

contexts.japanese:
嘉音は吐き捨てるように、…だけれども弱々しくそう言い、そっぽを向く。
それは多分、諦め。
……自分が家具であることを苦悩した日々の洗礼が、彼の心を頑なに閉ざしてしまった…。
contexts.japanesePC: ……自分が家具であることを苦悩した日々の洗礼が、彼の心を頑なに閉ざしてしまった…。
contexts.japanesePS3:
嘉音は吐き捨てるように、…だけれども弱々しくそう言い、そっぽを向く。
それは多分、諦め。
……自分が家具であることを苦悩した日々の洗礼が、彼の心を頑なに閉ざしてしまった…。
contexts.WH: ......After being baptized as furniture in his days of suffering, his heart was firmly sealed...
contexts.MG:
Kanon spat those words out, ...but did so weakly and turned away.
He was probably giving up.
...After all the suffering he'd undergone during those days he'd lived as furniture, his heart was firmly sealed...
contexts.UP:
Kanon spat that out, ...but weakly, and turned away.
That was probably...resignation.
......The baptism of days upon days of suffering being furniture had firmly sealed his heart...
contexts.note: MG ordeal of suffering and UP baptism of days of suffering both make the days the hardening ordeal, rather than a baptism conferring furniture status.

MG.japanese: 嘉音は吐き捨てるように、…だけれども弱々しくそう言い、そっぽを向く。それは多分、諦め。……自分が家具であることを苦悩した日々の洗礼が、彼の心を頑なに閉ざしてしまった…。
MG.translation: Kanon spat those words out, ...but did so weakly and turned away. He was probably giving up. ...After all the suffering he'd undergone during those days he'd lived as furniture, his heart was firmly sealed...

UP.japanese: 嘉音は吐き捨てるように、…だけれども弱々しくそう言い、そっぽを向く。それは多分、諦め。……自分が家具であることを苦悩した日々の洗礼が、彼の心を頑なに閉ざしてしまった…。
UP.translation: Kanon spat that out, ...but weakly, and turned away. That was probably...resignation. ......The baptism of days upon days of suffering being furniture had firmly sealed his heart...

findings.sourceReading: The ordeal of days spent suffering over his furniture status has stubbornly closed his heart; the preceding 諦め frames his weak denial as resignation.
findings.alternative: The English preserves suffering and a sealed heart, and baptism remains metaphorical in context. The objection concerns the relation within the metaphor, not a claim that readers must infer an actual rite.

contexts.japanese:
金蔵が書斎を出ることは珍しかった。
……しかし、だからといって、彼の高尚な研究が中断されているわけではない。
気分を変えるために書斎を出たのだろうが、
その頭の中をいっぱいに占めているものは、書斎の中のそれと何も変わらない。
contexts.japanesePC: 気分を変えるために書斎を出たのだろうが、その頭の中をいっぱいに占めているものは、書斎の中のそれと何も変わらない。

その頭の中をいっぱいに占めているものは、書斎の中のそれと何も変わらない。

嘉音は咄嗟に、魔女が何か良からぬ陰謀で金蔵に害を為そうとしているに違いないと考え、

…その気持ちは霧散した。
なぜなら、ベアトリーチェの表情は、

contexts.WH: At once, Kanon, thinking that the witch must be plotting to do Kinzo some harm, quickly ran back to Kinzo, trying to become a shield himself.
contexts.MG:
At once, thinking that the witch must be plotting to do Kinzo some harm,
Kanon dashed back to Kinzo and tried to form a shield with his body.
But when he saw the expression on the witch's face,
...that emotion of his vanished.
Because Beatrice's expression was...
...sorrowful...
...or maybe pitying.
contexts.UP:
At once, Kanon, thinking that the witch must be plotting to do Kinzo some harm,
quickly ran back to Kinzo, trying to become a shield himself.

...sorrow,

MG.japanese: 嘉音は咄嗟に、魔女が何か良からぬ陰謀で金蔵に害を為そうとしているに違いないと考え、急ぎ金蔵の元へ駆け戻り、自らを楯にしようと思った。
MG.translation: At once, thinking that the witch must be plotting to do Kinzo some harm, Kanon dashed back to Kinzo and tried to form a shield with his body.

UP.japanese: 嘉音は咄嗟に、魔女が何か良からぬ陰謀で金蔵に害を為そうとしているに違いないと考え、急ぎ金蔵の元へ駆け戻り、自らを楯にしようと思った。
UP.translation: At once, Kanon, thinking that the witch must be plotting to do Kinzo some harm, quickly ran back to Kinzo, trying to become a shield himself.

findings.sourceReading: Seeing the witch, he thinks of hurrying back to shield Kinzo; seeing her expression dispels that impulse.
findings.alternative: Japanese sequential phrasing can momentarily suggest movement, and English preserves his protective aim and its disappearance. But the sentence’s governing 思った presents the proposed action as thought, while English explicitly narrates a completed return.
