findings.description: 何とか持つかも becomes I might be able to do something. Nanjo’s conditional prognosis concerns the patient holding on, not his own ability to intervene.

contexts.japanese: は、肺まで届いてなければ何とか持つかも……。
contexts.japanesePC: 「……これは……酷い…。何か槍のようなもので刺されたようです。は、肺まで届いてなければ何とか持つかも……。とにかく、止血を……！」
contexts.japanesePS3: は、肺まで届いてなければ何とか持つかも……。
contexts.WH: "......This is......horrible...  It appears that he has been stabbed with something like a spear.  I, If it hasn't reached the lungs, I might be able to do something......  Anyway, stop the bleeding......!"
contexts.MG: I-If it hasn't reached the lungs, I might be able to do something...
contexts.UP: I‐if it hasn't reached the lungs, I might be able to do something......
contexts.note: Both retain I might be able to do something instead of saying Kanon might hold on if the wound has not reached his lungs.

MG.japanese: 「……これは……酷い…。何か槍のようなもので刺されたようです。は、肺まで届いてなければ何とか持つかも……。とにかく、止血を……！」
MG.translation: "...This is...horrible... He appears to have been stabbed by something like a spear. I-If it hasn't reached the lungs, I might be able to do something... At any rate, we must stop the bleeding...!"

UP.japanese: 「……これは……酷い…。何か槍のようなもので刺されたようです。は、肺まで届いてなければ何とか持つかも……。とにかく、止血を……！」
UP.translation: "......This is......horrible... It appears that he has been stabbed with something like a spear. I‐if it hasn't reached the lungs, I might be able to do something...... Anyway, stop the bleeding......!"

findings.sourceReading: If the injury has not reached the lungs, Kanon may somehow hold out; Nanjo then calls for stopping the bleeding.
findings.alternative: Medical intervention could be implied by hope of holding out, and the bleeding instruction remains. The English nevertheless changes the subject and type of uncertainty from endurance to the doctor’s possible action.

findings.description: 眼前で朱志香がその手にかけられるのを見たとでも言うよう becomes like he was seeing Jessica being harmed right before his eyes. The source frames the voice as if he had witnessed her being killed by that person; English substitutes ongoing seeing and generic harm.

contexts.japanese: …まるで、自分の眼前で朱志香がその手にかけられるのを見たとでも言うような呪わしい声だった。
contexts.japanesePC: …まるで、自分の眼前で朱志香がその手にかけられるのを見たとでも言うような呪わしい声だった。
contexts.japanesePS3: …まるで、自分の眼前で朱志香がその手にかけられるのを見たとでも言うような呪わしい声だった。
contexts.WH: ...His hate-filled voice made it seem like he was seeing Jessica being harmed right before his eyes.
contexts.MG: ...His hate-filled voice made it seem like he was seeing Jessica being harmed right before his eyes.
contexts.UP: ...His hate‐filled voice made it seem like he had seen Jessica being harmed right before his eyes.
contexts.note: MG retains seeing and harmed. UP restores completed witnessing with had seen but still reduces being killed by that person to being harmed.

MG.japanese:
なおも恨めしそうに叫ぶ嘉音…。
…まるで、自分の眼前で朱志香がその手にかけられるのを見たとでも言うような呪わしい声だった。
MG.translation: Kanon screamed even more hatefully... ...His hate-filled voice made it seem like he was seeing Jessica being harmed right before his eyes.

UP.japanese:
なおも恨めしそうに叫ぶ嘉音…。
…まるで、自分の眼前で朱志香がその手にかけられるのを見たとでも言うような呪わしい声だった。
UP.translation:
Kanon screamed even more hatefully...
...His hate‐filled voice made it seem like he had seen Jessica being harmed right before his eyes.

findings.sourceReading: The voice sounds as though he had personally watched Jessica being killed at Rosa’s hands.
findings.alternative: Seeing could evoke reliving an event, and the immediately preceding accusation and following discussion of killing supply the death context. The Japanese still makes the apparent prior eyewitness experience and the killer’s agency more explicit.

findings.description: この風雨の中では全て失われているだろう becomes she would probably lose it all in this wind and rain. The passive resulting condition becomes her prospective loss.

contexts.japanese: 薔薇庭園を探せば見付かるかもしれないが、この風雨の中では全て失われているだろう…。
contexts.japanesePC: 薔薇庭園を探せば見付かるかもしれないが、この風雨の中では全て失われているだろう…。
contexts.japanesePS3: 薔薇庭園を探せば見付かるかもしれないが、この風雨の中では全て失われているだろう…。
contexts.WH: She might find it if she searched the rose garden, but she would probably lose it all in this wind and rain...
contexts.MG: She might find it if she searched the rose garden, but they'd probably all been lost in this wind and rain...
contexts.UP: She might find some if she searched the rose garden, but they would probably have all been lost in this wind and rain...
contexts.note: Both editions say the sought items have probably already been lost in the wind and rain rather than predicting Shannon will lose them.

MG.japanese: 紗音は駆けて行く。どこへ？……屋敷内では掃除が行き届いているから、簡単には見つけられないだろう。薔薇庭園を探せば見付かるかもしれないが、この風雨の中では全て失われているだろう…。
MG.translation: Shannon ran. To where? ...The inside of the mansion had been scrupulously cleaned, so it probably wouldn't be easy to find. She might find it if she searched the rose garden, but they'd probably all been lost in this wind and rain...

UP.japanese: 紗音は駆けて行く。どこへ？……屋敷内では掃除が行き届いているから、簡単には見つけられないだろう。薔薇庭園を探せば見付かるかもしれないが、この風雨の中では全て失われているだろう…。
UP.translation: Shannon ran. To where? ......The inside of the mansion had been scrupulously cleaned, so they probably wouldn't be easy to find. She might find some if she searched the rose garden, but they would probably have all been lost in this wind and rain...

findings.sourceReading: The sought material might be found in the rose garden, but all of it would probably already have been lost amid the wind and rain, prompting her to consider the less-clean boiler room.
findings.alternative: Lose can imply weather dispersal, and both versions make the garden unattractive. English explicitly assigns the future loss to her, shifting the problem from existing availability to what happens after finding it.

findings.description: didn’t let his eyes off Kanon is not the intended idiom for maintaining observation.

contexts.japanese: 南條はそれをあまりよい傾向だと思っていないらしく、一時も目を離さなかった。
contexts.japanesePC: 南條はそれをあまりよい傾向だと思っていないらしく、一時も目を離さなかった。
contexts.japanesePS3: 南條はそれをあまりよい傾向だと思っていないらしく、一時も目を離さなかった。
contexts.WH: Nanjo apparently didn't think of this as that great of a trend, and didn't let his eyes off Kanon for a second.
contexts.MG: Nanjo apparently didn't view this as a very good sign, ...and he didn't let his eyes off Kanon for a second.
contexts.UP: Nanjo apparently didn't think of this as that great of a trend, and didn't let his eyes off Kanon for a second.
contexts.note: Both retain didn't let his eyes off Kanon rather than didn't take his eyes off Kanon.

MG.japanese: 何かの薬が土壇場で効いてくれたのだろうか、それともとうとう嘉音は痛みを感じることすら失われてしまったのか。…嘉音はとりあえず苦痛に喘ぐことだけはなくなった。南條はそれをあまりよい傾向だと思っていないらしく、一時も目を離さなかった。
MG.translation: Did some medicine take effect at the brink of death, or was Kanon finally beyond feeling pain? ...For the time being, at least Kanon's painful gasping had subsided. Nanjo apparently didn't view this as a very good sign, ...and he didn't let his eyes off Kanon for a second.

UP.japanese: 何かの薬が土壇場で効いてくれたのだろうか、それともとうとう嘉音は痛みを感じることすら失われてしまったのか。…嘉音はとりあえず苦痛に喘ぐことだけはなくなった。南條はそれをあまりよい傾向だと思っていないらしく、一時も目を離さなかった。
UP.translation: Had some medicine taken effect at the brink of death, or had Kanon finally stopped even feeling pain? ...For the time being, Kanon had at least gotten over his painful gasping. Nanjo apparently didn't think of this as that great of a trend, and didn't let his eyes off Kanon for a second.

findings.sourceReading: Nanjo never took his eyes off Kanon.
findings.alternative: The intended meaning is readily understood, but let his eyes off is a malformed rendering of the observation idiom.

findings.description: こちらから仕掛けるべき becomes we should wage war from here. Gohda proposes initiating action, immediately specifying taking the gun under a pretext.

contexts.japanese:
源次さん、こちらから仕掛けるべきです。
せめて銃さえ理由をこじつけて奪えば、何とかなるかも…！」
contexts.japanesePC: 源次さん、こちらから仕掛けるべきです。せめて銃さえ理由をこじつけて奪えば、何とかなるかも…！」
contexts.japanesePS3:
源次さん、こちらから仕掛けるべきです。
せめて銃さえ理由をこじつけて奪えば、何とかなるかも…！」
contexts.WH: Genji-san, we should wage war from here.  If we can at least steal the gun under some pretext, things might work out...!"
contexts.MG:
Genji-san, we should take action first.
If we can at least steal the gun under some pretext, it might work out...!"
contexts.UP:
Genji‐san, we should be the ones to make the first move.
If we can at least take the gun from her under some pretext, things might work out...!"
contexts.note: MG says take action first and UP says make the first move; both restore Gohda's proposal to initiate action before specifying the gun.

MG.japanese: 「しかし、明日までは長い…！　どんな手を打ってくるか想像もつきませんよ！　源次さん、こちらから仕掛けるべきです。せめて銃さえ理由をこじつけて奪えば、何とかなるかも…！」
MG.translation: "But tomorrow is still a long way off...! We can't even imagine what strategies she might use! Genji-san, we should take action first. If we can at least steal the gun under some pretext, it might work out...!"

UP.japanese: 「しかし、明日までは長い…！　どんな手を打ってくるか想像もつきませんよ！　源次さん、こちらから仕掛けるべきです。せめて銃さえ理由をこじつけて奪えば、何とかなるかも…！」
UP.translation: "But there is still much time before tomorrow comes...! We can't even imagine what strategy she will use! Genji‐san, we should be the ones to make the first move. If we can at least take the gun from her under some pretext, things might work out...!"

findings.sourceReading: They should act first, at least inventing a reason to take away the gun.
findings.alternative: They have discussed a possible group assault, so adversarial action is in context. Wage war inflates the scope of his proposal, while from here mistakes direction of initiative for a location.

findings.description: 朗々と喋る becomes talking brightly. The source highlights strong clear vocal production, not specifically a cheerful manner.

contexts.japanese:
それまで、静かに眠っていると思っていた嘉音が、急に朗々と喋る。
まるでさっきからずっと起きていて、急に口を開いたかのようだった。
その様子がしっかりしていたので、南條は少しだけほっとするが、傷の深さを考えると、どうしてもある不気味さが拭えなかった。
contexts.japanesePC: それまで、静かに眠っていると思っていた嘉音が、急に朗々と喋る。
contexts.japanesePS3:
それまで、静かに眠っていると思っていた嘉音が、急に朗々と喋る。
まるでさっきからずっと起きていて、急に口を開いたかのようだった。
その様子がしっかりしていたので、南條は少しだけほっとするが、傷の深さを考えると、どうしてもある不気味さが拭えなかった。
contexts.WH: Kanon, who they thought had been sleeping quietly, suddenly started talking brightly.
contexts.MG:
Kanon, who they'd thought was sleeping quietly, suddenly started talking brightly.
Almost as though he'd been awake this whole time and had suddenly opened his mouth.
Kanon looked firm and steady, which relieved Nanjo a bit, but considering the depth of that wound, he couldn't wipe away a certain creepy feeling.
contexts.UP:
Kanon, who they thought had been sleeping quietly, suddenly started talking brightly.
Almost like he had been awake the whole time and had suddenly opened his mouth.
He looked firm and steady, and Nanjo was slightly relieved, but thinking of the deepness of that wound, he just couldn't wipe away a certain creepy feeling.
contexts.note: Both retain talking brightly even though the surrounding effect is eerie lucidity rather than cheerfulness.

MG.japanese: それまで、静かに眠っていると思っていた嘉音が、急に朗々と喋る。まるでさっきからずっと起きていて、急に口を開いたかのようだった。その様子がしっかりしていたので、南條は少しだけほっとするが、傷の深さを考えると、どうしてもある不気味さが拭えなかった。
MG.translation: Kanon, who they'd thought was sleeping quietly, suddenly started talking brightly. Almost as though he'd been awake this whole time and had suddenly opened his mouth. Kanon looked firm and steady, which relieved Nanjo a bit, but considering the depth of that wound, he couldn't wipe away a certain creepy feeling.

UP.japanese: それまで、静かに眠っていると思っていた嘉音が、急に朗々と喋る。まるでさっきからずっと起きていて、急に口を開いたかのようだった。その様子がしっかりしていたので、南條は少しだけほっとするが、傷の深さを考えると、どうしてもある不気味さが拭えなかった。
UP.translation: Kanon, who they thought had been sleeping quietly, suddenly started talking brightly. Almost like he had been awake the whole time and had suddenly opened his mouth. He looked firm and steady, and Nanjo was slightly relieved, but thinking of the deepness of that wound, he just couldn't wipe away a certain creepy feeling.

findings.sourceReading: He abruptly speaks in a clear ringing voice despite having seemed asleep.
findings.alternative: Bright can describe vocal tone, and the next sentence retains abrupt apparent wakefulness. Talking brightly nevertheless commonly suggests cheerfulness rather than the unexpected vocal strength the source specifies.

findings.description: 意識を失って当然だ becomes It wouldn’t have been unexpected if ... . The source presents loss of consciousness as the expected outcome, not merely a possible outcome that would not surprise.

contexts.japanese:
嘉音の出血量なら意識を失って当然だ。
なのにこんなにもはっきりとした意識を保てるなんて。
contexts.japanesePC: 嘉音の出血量なら意識を失って当然だ。
contexts.japanesePS3:
嘉音の出血量なら意識を失って当然だ。
なのにこんなにもはっきりとした意識を保てるなんて。
contexts.WH: It wouldn't have been unexpected if Kanon had lost consciousness after losing so much blood.
contexts.MG:
After losing so much blood, Kanon might easily have lost consciousness.
And yet, somehow, he was still intensely aware of his surroundings.
contexts.UP:
Kanon should have been expected to fall unconscious after losing so much blood.
And yet somehow, he had preserved his awareness so clearly.
contexts.note: MG's might easily have lost consciousness remains a possibility rather than the medically expected outcome. UP says Kanon should have been expected to fall unconscious.

MG.japanese:
……彼は医者だからわかる。嘉音の出血量なら意識を失って当然だ。
なのにこんなにもはっきりとした意識を保てるなんて。……若さ？　それとも執念？
…時に人の生命力は常識を超えることもあるし……。
MG.translation: ...He knew because he was a doctor. After losing so much blood, Kanon might easily have lost consciousness. And yet, somehow, he was still intensely aware of his surroundings. ...Was it youth? Or was it tenacity? ...Sometimes, the power of human life surpassed common knowledge...

UP.japanese:
……彼は医者だからわかる。嘉音の出血量なら意識を失って当然だ。
なのにこんなにもはっきりとした意識を保てるなんて。……若さ？　それとも執念？
…時に人の生命力は常識を超えることもあるし……。
UP.translation:
......He knew because he was a doctor. Kanon should have been expected to fall unconscious after losing so much blood.
And yet somehow, he had preserved his awareness so clearly. ......Youth? Or tenacity?
...Sometimes the power of human life did surpass common knowledge......

findings.sourceReading: Given that much blood loss, unconsciousness should follow; continued clear awareness is anomalous to Nanjo.
findings.alternative: Wouldn’t have been unexpected can serve as understated expectation, and the following contrast preserves the anomaly. It is nevertheless weaker than 当然 and lets continued consciousness sound less contrary to the expectation.

findings.description: 確実に肺にすら届いているはず becomes had certainly reached as far as his lungs. The source retains はず, marking a strong inference about the injury.

contexts.japanese:
止血の時、患部に何か異物があってはいけないと、
血の湧き出す穴をピンセットで少しだけまさぐったが、そのあまりの深さに驚いた。
…傷は確実に肺にすら届いているはずなのだ。
contexts.japanesePC: …傷は確実に肺にすら届いているはずなのだ。
contexts.japanesePS3:
止血の時、患部に何か異物があってはいけないと、
血の湧き出す穴をピンセットで少しだけまさぐったが、そのあまりの深さに驚いた。
…傷は確実に肺にすら届いているはずなのだ。
contexts.WH: ...The wound had certainly reached as far as his lungs.
contexts.MG:
While stopping the bleeding, Nanjo had groped around a bit inside the bleeding hole with tweezers, making sure there were no foreign objects inside the affected area,
and the great depth of the wound had shocked him.
...It had certainly reached as far as his lungs.
contexts.UP:

Nanjo had groped around a bit inside the bleeding hole with tweezers, and the great depth of the wound had surprised him.
...The wound had certainly reached as far as his lungs.

MG.japanese:
止血の時、患部に何か異物があってはいけないと、血の湧き出す穴をピンセットで少しだけまさぐったが、そのあまりの深さに驚いた。…傷は確実に肺にすら届いているはずなのだ。……なのに、…なのに…。
……いや、でも、生きているのはとにかく幸いなことで…。
MG.translation: While stopping the bleeding, Nanjo had groped around a bit inside the bleeding hole with tweezers, making sure there were no foreign objects inside the affected area, and the great depth of the wound had shocked him. ...It had certainly reached as far as his lungs. ...And yet, ...and yet... ...No, but...the fact that he's still alive is wonderful...

UP.japanese:
止血の時、患部に何か異物があってはいけないと、血の湧き出す穴をピンセットで少しだけまさぐったが、そのあまりの深さに驚いた。…傷は確実に肺にすら届いているはずなのだ。……なのに、…なのに…。
……いや、でも、生きているのはとにかく幸いなことで…。
UP.translation:
When they had stopped the bleeding, to make sure there were no foreign objects inside the affected area, Nanjo had groped around a bit inside the bleeding hole with tweezers, and the great depth of the wound had surprised him. ...The wound had certainly reached as far as his lungs. ......And yet, ...and yet...

findings.sourceReading: The butterflies fade into nothing as though dissolving into water—or rather into the air.
findings.alternative: English preserves their fading into nothingness, and evaporating gives a disappearance image. It nevertheless reverses the comparison’s subject and changes dissolution into evaporation of the surrounding medium.

findings.description: 白昼夢と溶け込んで becomes melt away like a daydream. Blending the remembered experience with a waking dream becomes a simile for its disappearance.

contexts.japanese:
そして、それは紗音も同じに見えた。
ほんの少し気を許せば、ついさっき見たばかりのことが、すぐに白昼夢と溶け込んでしまって、
自分が何を見たのかも思い出せなくなってしまう。
……そんな風に見えた。
contexts.japanesePC: ほんの少し気を許せば、ついさっき見たばかりのことが、すぐに白昼夢と溶け込んでしまって、自分が何を見たのかも思い出せなくなってしまう。
contexts.japanesePS3:
そして、それは紗音も同じに見えた。
ほんの少し気を許せば、ついさっき見たばかりのことが、すぐに白昼夢と溶け込んでしまって、
自分が何を見たのかも思い出せなくなってしまう。
……そんな風に見えた。
contexts.WH: If she let her guard down, what she had seen just a short while ago would quickly melt away like a daydream, and she wouldn't be able to remember what she saw.
contexts.MG:
And Shannon looked the same way.
If she let her guard down, what she'd seen just a short while ago would quickly melt away like a daydream,
and she wouldn't be able to remember anything.
...That's what she looked like.
contexts.UP:
And Shannon looked the same way.
If she let her guard down, what she had seen just a short while ago would quickly melt away like a daydream,
and she wouldn't even be able to remember what she saw.
......That's what she looked like.
contexts.note: Both retain the memory melting away like a daydream rather than blending into one.

MG.japanese: そして、それは紗音も同じに見えた。ほんの少し気を許せば、ついさっき見たばかりのことが、すぐに白昼夢と溶け込んでしまって、自分が何を見たのかも思い出せなくなってしまう。……そんな風に見えた。
MG.translation: And Shannon looked the same way. If she let her guard down, what she'd seen just a short while ago would quickly melt away like a daydream, and she wouldn't be able to remember anything. ...That's what she looked like.

UP.japanese: そして、それは紗音も同じに見えた。ほんの少し気を許せば、ついさっき見たばかりのことが、すぐに白昼夢と溶け込んでしまって、自分が何を見たのかも思い出せなくなってしまう。……そんな風に見えた。

findings.sourceReading: Battler thinks Shannon looks liable to let what she just saw merge with a daydream and become impossible to recall.
findings.alternative: Both versions preserve unstable memory, inability to recall, and Battler’s explicit impression qualifier. The source specifically blurs experience and dream rather than merely comparing fading memories to dreams.

contexts.note: MG says Rosa's first conclusion was correct; UP retains the original claim that it had been correct from the beginning. Both validate it rather than say the favorable interpretation amounts to the same meaning.

MG.japanese: …彼らの言っていることを、好意的に解釈すると、……それは楼座叔母さんが最初に断じているのと同じ意味になる。

findings.sourceReading: Interpreted favorably, their testimony amounts to what Rosa initially asserted.
findings.alternative: The English keeps the conditional interpretation and remains Battler’s reasoning, not an omniscient verdict. His following reconstruction supports Rosa’s reading, but the source sentence itself describes agreement rather than correctness.

findings.description: トリックがあるということなのか becomes Kanon-kun had used some trick. The question shifts from whether such a means exists to whether Kanon used it; just as Rosa oba-san thought also supplies an explicit attribution absent here.

contexts.japanese:
つまりそれは、……嘉音くんが現れたということだ。
彼らがどんなに混乱し、言葉を濁そうとも、つまりはそういうことになる。
やはり嘉音くんがあの部屋を施錠したまま抜け出すトリックがあるということなのか？！
いや、今そんなことはどうでもいい。
contexts.japanesePC: やはり嘉音くんがあの部屋を施錠したまま抜け出すトリックがあるということなのか？！　いや、今そんなことはどうでもいい。
contexts.japanesePS3:
つまりそれは、……嘉音くんが現れたということだ。
彼らがどんなに混乱し、言葉を濁そうとも、つまりはそういうことになる。
やはり嘉音くんがあの部屋を施錠したまま抜け出すトリックがあるということなのか？！
いや、今そんなことはどうでもいい。
contexts.WH: So just as Rosa oba-san thought, Kanon-kun had used some trick to escape that room while it was locked?!  No, that doesn't matter anymore.
contexts.MG:
In other words, that means...Kanon-kun did appear.
No matter how confused they are, no matter how they muddle their words, that's what it means in the end.
So, does that mean that, after all, Kanon-kun used some trick to escape that room even though it was locked?!
No, that doesn't matter anymore.
contexts.UP:
In other words, this meant......Kanon‐kun had appeared.
No matter how confused they were, no matter how they muddled their words, that's what it meant in the end.
So had Kanon‐kun indeed used some trick to escape that room while it was locked?!
No, that doesn't matter anymore.
contexts.note: Both remove the earlier added attribution to Rosa but retain the shift from whether an escape trick exists to whether Kanon used one.

MG.japanese: やはり嘉音くんがあの部屋を施錠したまま抜け出すトリックがあるということなのか？！　いや、今そんなことはどうでもいい。南條先生と熊沢さんが殺されたことの方が重要な問題だ。
MG.translation: So, does that mean that, after all, Kanon-kun used some trick to escape that room even though it was locked?! No, that doesn't matter anymore. The real problem is that Doctor Nanjo and Kumasawa-san were killed.

UP.japanese: やはり嘉音くんがあの部屋を施錠したまま抜け出すトリックがあるということなのか？！　いや、今そんなことはどうでもいい。南條先生と熊沢さんが殺されたことの方が重要な問題だ。
UP.translation: So had Kanon‐kun indeed used some trick to escape that room while it was locked?! No, that doesn't matter anymore. The real problem is that Doctor Nanjo and Kumasawa‐san were killed.

findings.sourceReading: Does this mean there really is a trick by which Kanon could escape with the room still locked?
findings.alternative: Both are excited rhetorical questions within Battler’s tentative reconstruction, and the next sentence dismisses the issue for now. The English nevertheless moves a step from possible mechanism to its employment.

まるで壊れた玩具で遊んでいるような感覚。

findings.description: それ resumes the apparent invisible wall, which repels the impostor while leaving red ripples. The loci left a bright red ripple on the wall attributes the ripple to the trajectories instead, though it then repelled him.

contexts.japanese:

それは真っ赤な軌跡の波紋を残しながら、……偽者を弾く。
……違う、弾いたんじゃない、砕いた。

......No, it didn't repel him, it smashed him.
contexts.note: MG makes the wall repel the impostor while leaving the ripple. UP removes the old loci attribution but grammatically lets a ripple trail become the subject of it repelled, leaving the defensive agent unstable.

MG.japanese: 偽者の嘉音が紫の軌跡を何条も描きながら、確かに紗音に襲い掛かったはずだった…。しかし、紗音に飛び掛った時、……紗音の前に、何か見えない壁が出来たように感じた。それは真っ赤な軌跡の波紋を残しながら、……偽者を弾く。……違う、弾いたんじゃない、砕いた。……黄金の粉にして、欠片にして、ばらばらにして弾き返した…！

But when he flew at Shannon, ......it felt like some kind of invisible wall had been set up in front of her. findings.sourceReading: The wall leaves a ripple of bright-red traces as it repels, then actually shatters, the impostor.
findings.alternative: An impact can cause a wall to ripple, and the next clauses still make the barrier repel and shatter him. The source sentence does not assign the red trace to the attacking trajectories.

you're just hiding what you don't want to see by covering it with a veil do you stiiill not understand that's why you're furniture you fuuuuuurniture,"
"see see see see see it's chipping awaaaaaaaaay crackcrunchsmacksnap how thin how shameful,
compared to your frail resistance Parmigiano‐Reggiano would take muuch more effort to shaaaaaaaaaaaaaave
hiiyahhaaahahaah!!"
The golden windstorm that covered the room gradually shaved away the walls of the column that protected Shannon and George.

findings.description: 不可避であるならば is conditional. Since the fate that awaited him was unavoidable states unavoidability as a premise.

contexts.japanese:

源次にとって、自分を待ち受ける運命が不可避であるならば、
その瞬間まで勤めを整然と果たすことがきっと美徳であったに違いない。
彼の心の奥底をうかがい知ることは、彼が自ら語らぬ限り、永遠に不可能だろう……。

せいぜい廊下を回り、窓の戸締りを確認するくらいだ。

抜けて倒れていた。

杭のようなものであることを理解する。

杭のようなものであることを理解する。
contexts.WH: So, by looking that one that had fallen over, for the first time, I realized that it wasn't a knife, but something like a stake.
contexts.MG:

but the one that had been thrust into Kumasawa-san's ankle might have been a little shallower.

だから、その倒れたものを見て初めて俺は、これがナイフではなく、杭のようなものであることを理解する。全長は多分、３０ｃｍあるかないか。
青銅とか鉄とか、そういう類のもので出来ているのだろう。手に触れずとも重みのあるものであることがわかる。
握りと、円錐部分で構成されていて、明らかに刺すための武器として作られたものだとわかる。
MG.translation: So, by looking at the one that had fallen over, for the first time, I realized that it wasn't a knife, but something like a stake. Its full length was probably about 30 centimeters. It was composed of a grip and a cone-shaped part, and it was obviously made to be a piercing weapon.

contexts.japanese:

……あれだけ深々と胸に刺されたら、一体どこまで至ってしまうのか。
…想像しただけで自分の胸が痛んだ。
「…胸をえぐれは、第五の晩だったか」

contexts.WH: ...Just imagining it would cause anyone's chest to hurt.
contexts.MG:
Right in the center of his chest, almost as though it had been stuck there to finish off a vampire, was one of those demon stakes from before.
...Exactly how far could it have reached after being stuck that deeply into his chest?
...Just imagining it would make anyone's chest hurt.
"...Wasn't gouging the chest...the fifth twilight?"
contexts.UP:
One of those demon stakes had been rammed right into the center of his chest, almost as though it had been stuck there to finish off a vampire.
......Exactly how far would it have reached after being stuck that deeply into his chest?
...My own chest hurt just imagining it.
"...Gouge the chest was the fifth twilight?"
contexts.note: MG generalizes the pain to anyone's chest. UP says My own chest hurt, preserving Battler's actual response.

MG.japanese: しかし、それより最初に目に入るのは、………部屋を入ってすぐのところにうつ伏せに倒れている郷田さんの遺体だった…。胸のど真ん中に、まるで吸血鬼に止めでも刺すみたいに、例の悪魔の杭がぶち込まれていた。……あれだけ深々と胸に刺されたら、一体どこまで至ってしまうのか。…想像しただけで自分の胸が痛んだ。
MG.translation: But the very first thing that caught our eyes... ...was Gohda-san's corpse lying facedown right in front of the door... Right in the center of his chest, almost as though it had been stuck there to finish off a vampire, was one of those demon stakes from before. ...Exactly how far could it have reached after being stuck that deeply into his chest? ...Just imagining it would make anyone's chest hurt.

UP.japanese: しかし、それより最初に目に入るのは、………部屋を入ってすぐのところにうつ伏せに倒れている郷田さんの遺体だった…。胸のど真ん中に、まるで吸血鬼に止めでも刺すみたいに、例の悪魔の杭がぶち込まれていた。……あれだけ深々と胸に刺されたら、一体どこまで至ってしまうのか。…想像しただけで自分の胸が痛んだ。
UP.translation: But the thing that caught the eye before that... ......was Gohda‐san's body lying facedown right in front of the door... One of those demon stakes had been rammed right into the center of his chest, almost as though it had been stuck there to finish off a vampire. ......Exactly how far would it have reached after being stuck that deeply into his chest? ...My own chest hurt just imagining it.

findings.sourceReading: Merely imagining the penetration makes his own chest hurt.
findings.alternative: Anyone’s chest can rhetorically include the speaker, and his horror is clear. The explicit felt reaction and subject are nevertheless changed.

findings.description: 額 specifies the forehead; head removes that anatomical precision.

contexts.japanese:
こんなことしてはいけないとわかっているのに、…彼女の顔をあげ、それを確認する。
……そして、自分の想像が完全に的中していることを、確認した。
紗音ちゃんの額にはぽっかりと穴が空き、そこから中身がどろりと溢れてくる。
それどころか、…その中身まで、…見えてしまう。
それを見て、俺はようやくしてはいけないことをしたことに気付いた。
contexts.japanesePC: 紗音ちゃんの額にはぽっかりと穴が空き、そこから中身がどろりと溢れてくる。

contexts.WH: There was a gaping hole in Shannon-chan's head, and her insides were dripping out.
contexts.MG:
Even though I knew it was wrong, ...I lifted her head...and checked.
...And, I confirmed that my guess had been right on the mark.
There was a gaping hole in Shannon-chan's head, and the insides were dripping out.
Not only that, ...but you could even see...inside her.
After seeing that, I finally realized I was doing something wrong.
contexts.UP:
Even though I knew what I was doing was wrong, ...I lifted her head, and checked.
......And confirmed that my guess was right on the mark.
There was a gaping hole in Shannon‐chan's forehead, and her insides were dripping out.
Not only that, ...you could even see...inside her.

contexts.note: MG retains a hole in Shannon's head. UP correctly specifies her forehead.

MG.japanese: 紗音ちゃんの額にはぽっかりと穴が空き、そこから中身がどろりと溢れてくる。それどころか、…その中身まで、…見えてしまう。それを見て、俺はようやくしてはいけないことをしたことに気付いた。慌てて目を背けたところで、今さら何の意味もなかっただろうが。
MG.translation: There was a gaping hole in Shannon-chan's head, and the insides were dripping out. Not only that, ...but you could even see...inside her. After seeing that, I finally realized I was doing something wrong. I immediately averted my eyes, but by now, it was probably pointless.

UP.japanese: 紗音ちゃんの額にはぽっかりと穴が空き、そこから中身がどろりと溢れてくる。それどころか、…その中身まで、…見えてしまう。それを見て、俺はようやくしてはいけないことをしたことに気付いた。慌てて目を背けたところで、今さら何の意味もなかっただろうが。
UP.translation: There was a gaping hole in Shannon‐chan's forehead, and her insides were dripping out. Not only that, ...you could even see...inside her. After seeing that, I finally noticed that what I was doing was wrong. I immediately averted my eyes, but by now, it was probably pointless.

findings.sourceReading: With Maria he will definitely be safe, she insists, so he should not fear.

findings.description: 死んでいる者だけが正しくて contrasts the dead as blameless or in the right with living wolves. Only the dead were safe shifts to safety.

contexts.japanese:

もう、何が何だかわからない。
……死んでいる者だけが正しくて、生きている者が全て狼だと言うなら、
……あとに残るは、俺に楼座叔母さんに真里亞、それに源次さん。
……そして、祖父さまと、気配すら見せない１９人目の来客、ベアトリーチェだけ。
contexts.japanesePC: ……死んでいる者だけが正しくて、生きている者が全て狼だと言うなら、……あとに残るは、俺に楼座叔母さんに真里亞、それに源次さん。

I don't have a clue what's going on anymore. ......If only the dead are safe, and everyone alive is a wolf, ......then all that's left is me, Auntie Rosa, Maria, and Genji‐san. ......Only those, Grandfather, and that 19th person—the guest who I hadn't even sensed— Beatrice.

findings.sourceReading: If only the dead count as in the right and every living person is a wolf, the remaining suspects are the six survivors or presumed survivors.
findings.alternative: Safe can occasionally mean safe to trust, which fits the earlier trust discourse. Here the bare were safe also naturally means free from danger, and no to trust qualification specifies the source’s innocence contrast.

findings.sourceReading: Rosa distinguishes her observations about table access from Battler’s asserted discovery.
findings.alternative: In ordinary conversation the English may still imply the approach occurred, and both versions single him out. The formal evidential scope nonetheless makes the approach an assertion rather than the observed action supporting hers.

金蔵。覚えている……？
私としていた、まだ途中だったチェスの譜面……。
MG.translation: Kinzo, do you remember...? That game of chess you played with me, which is still ongoing...?

UP.japanese:
金蔵。覚えている……？
私としていた、まだ途中だったチェスの譜面……。

The board position of our chess game, which we never finished......?

findings.sourceReading: Beatrice asks whether he remembers their unfinished chess game’s moves or position.
findings.alternative: Score can describe both music and games, but musical piece resolves the ambiguity in the wrong domain. The following reconstruction clarifies chess.

MG.japanese: 家具を、山羊の貴族たちが見下ろしている。彼らは実は待っていた。シャンパンを飲むためにはまずコルクを抜かなければならないように、宴に供された贄を口にする前に、ある、たったひとつのソレを待っていた。もちろんソレを家具は知らない。…でも、勝手に口にするのだ。コルクを抜けば必ず、ポンと音がするように、彼も必ず口にするのだ。
MG.translation: The goat nobles looked down upon the furniture. Actually, they had been waiting. Just like how one must remove the cork in order to drink champagne, they had to wait for one thing before partaking of the offering served at this banquet. Of course, the furniture didn't know about this thing. ...But it came out of his mouth all by itself. Just like the unavoidable pop of a cork, it inevitably came out of his mouth.

UP.japanese: 家具を、山羊の貴族たちが見下ろしている。彼らは実は待っていた。シャンパンを飲むためにはまずコルクを抜かなければならないように、宴に供された贄を口にする前に、ある、たったひとつのソレを待っていた。もちろんソレを家具は知らない。…でも、勝手に口にするのだ。コルクを抜けば必ず、ポンと音がするように、彼も必ず口にするのだ。
UP.translation: The goat nobles looked down upon the furniture. They were, in fact, waiting. Just like how one must remove the cork in order to drink champagne, before bringing the offering served at the banquet to their mouths, they were waiting for just one of those. Of course, the furniture didn't know what that was. ...But it would come out of his mouth all by itself. In the same way there is always a pop when the cork is removed, it too would certainly leave his mouth.

findings.sourceReading: The guests wait for one thing before eating: his involuntary scream, revealed as the signal.
findings.alternative: The eventual scream revelation allows recovery; no inability to solve a mystery is established.

findings.description: 一瞬だけ qualifies Rosa’s thought of abandoning her daughter. For just an instant, Rosa was ashamed instead limits her shame. 大地を蹴り戻して also describes pushing off to reverse direction, not waiting until her feet touch the ground.

contexts.japanesePC: 楼座は一瞬だけ、娘を見捨てて駆け去ることを考えたことを恥じ、大地を蹴り戻して瞬時に逆走する。

MG.translation: Maria fell down. For just an instant, Rosa was ashamed by thoughts of abandoning her daughter and running away, and at the instant her feet touched ground, she ran back. The goat head that had sprinted over to get the first bite... grabbed hold of the back of Rosa's own child's hair and pulled...!!

UP.translation: Maria tripped over. Rosa, ashamed that for just an instant she had entertained thoughts of abandoning her daughter and running away, kicked back against the ground and instantly reversed direction. As Rosa's own child tried to stand, the goat‐head that had sprinted over to get the first bite grabbed a fistful of her hair and pulled her up from the back...!!

findings.sourceReading: Ashamed that she had even briefly considered abandoning Maria, Rosa pushes off and immediately runs back.
findings.alternative: The English retains shame, the abandonment thought and rapid return, but attaches the brief duration to the wrong mental event.

バースデープレゼントに買ってあげて、……その夜にしか遊んであげなくて。
「うんッ、遊ぼうね、一緒に！！！
約束するッ！！！」
contexts.WH: She had bought that as a birthday present, ......and then hadn't played it for Maria after that night.
contexts.MG:
And then we'll play together!
Play with the "Wolves and Sheep Puzzle"!!
Mama hasn't solved more than one of the puzzles, but I've solved them all.
So I'll be the riddle-giver!!"
She had bought it as a birthday present...and then hadn't played it with Maria after that first night.
"Yes, we'll play together!!!
I promise!!!"
contexts.UP:
"And then we'll play together!
Play with the "Wolves and Sheep Puzzle"!!
You still haven't solved more than one question, Mama, but I solved them all.
So I'll be the questioner!!"
She had bought that as a birthday present, ......and then hadn't played it with Maria after that night.
"Yes, let's play, together!!!
I promise!!!"
contexts.note: Both editions say Rosa had not played the puzzle with Maria after the first night, restoring shared play.

MG.japanese: バースデープレゼントに買ってあげて、……その夜にしか遊んであげなくて。
MG.translation: She had bought it as a birthday present...and then hadn't played it with Maria after that first night.

UP.japanese: バースデープレゼントに買ってあげて、……その夜にしか遊んであげなくて。
UP.translation: She had bought that as a birthday present, ......and then hadn't played it with Maria after that night.

findings.sourceReading: Rosa bought the puzzle for Maria’s birthday and only played with her that night.
findings.alternative: The surrounding promises to play together make the intended shared activity recoverable.

findings.description: ため息が堪えられない describes being unable to suppress a sigh of admiration. A forced deep breath substitutes a different response.

contexts.japanese: 幼い私が見ても、その美しさにため息が堪えられないほどに。
contexts.japanesePC: 幼い私が見ても、その美しさにため息が堪えられないほどに。
contexts.japanesePS3: 幼い私が見ても、その美しさにため息が堪えられないほどに。
contexts.WH: Even as young as I was, it still forced me to take a deep breath when I witnessed its beauty.
contexts.MG: Even as young as I was, it still forced me to take a deep breath when I witnessed its beauty.
contexts.UP: Even as young as I was, it still forced me to take a deep breath when I witnessed its beauty.
contexts.note: Both editions retain “forced me to take a deep breath,” substituting breathing for an irrepressible sigh of admiration.

MG.japanese: それは、とてもとても美しくて、価値と歴史のある素晴らしい壷でした。幼い私が見ても、その美しさにため息が堪えられないほどに。
MG.translation: The vase was very beautiful, rich with history and value. Even as young as I was, it still forced me to take a deep breath when I witnessed its beauty.

UP.japanese: それは、とてもとても美しくて、価値と歴史のある素晴らしい壷でした。幼い私が見ても、その美しさにため息が堪えられないほどに。
UP.translation: The vase was very, very beautiful, rich with history and value. Even as young as I was, it still forced me to take a deep breath when I witnessed its beauty.

findings.sourceReading: Even the young narrator cannot help sighing at the vase’s beauty.
findings.alternative: Both suggest being affected by beauty, but a deep inhalation does not express the involuntary admiring sigh.

findings.description: もっともお気に入りのコレクションのひとつ identifies one of Grandfather’s most treasured collectibles. The English attaches favorite to the collection as a whole instead.

contexts.japanese: もちろんそれは、お祖父さまにとってもっともお気に入りのコレクションのひとつ。
contexts.japanesePC: もちろんそれは、お祖父さまにとってもっともお気に入りのコレクションのひとつ。
contexts.japanesePS3: もちろんそれは、お祖父さまにとってもっともお気に入りのコレクションのひとつ。
contexts.WH: Of course, that was a member of Grandfather's favorite collection.
contexts.MG: Of course, it was a member of Grandfather's favorite collection.
contexts.UP: Of course, it was one of Grandfather's favorite collection pieces.
contexts.note: MG retains “member of Grandfather’s favorite collection.” UP restores one of his favorite collection pieces.

MG.japanese: もちろんそれは、お祖父さまにとってもっともお気に入りのコレクションのひとつ。その儚き美しさが、間違って欠けてしまうようなことがないように、私には絶対触れてはならないと日頃から厳命されていました。
MG.translation: Of course, it was a member of Grandfather's favorite collection. So that I didn't accidentally destroy its fragile beauty, I was always given strict orders never to touch it.

UP.japanese: もちろんそれは、お祖父さまにとってもっともお気に入りのコレクションのひとつ。その儚き美しさが、間違って欠けてしまうようなことがないように、私には絶対触れてはならないと日頃から厳命されていました。
UP.translation: Of course, it was one of Grandfather's favorite collection pieces. So that I didn't accidentally destroy its fragile beauty, I was always strictly ordered never to touch it.

findings.sourceReading: The vase is among Grandfather’s most treasured collection pieces.
findings.alternative: English collection can loosely include the favorite items; the item-specific emphasis is nevertheless weakened.

MangaGamer uses the accepted MangaGamer-based Witch Hunt backport, and Umineko Project uses its repository English; both are compared with maintained PS3-derived Japanese. The MangaGamer and PS3 witnesses are not independently certified retail extractions.

findings.description: 軽やかに見えながら物言わぬ重厚感 contrasts apparent lightness with silent gravitas. Just glancing at it gave it an indescribable sense of dignity drops that contrast and makes the glance confer dignity.

contexts.japanese: このような透き通るようで、だけれども気品があって、軽やかに見えながら物言わぬ重厚感があり。
contexts.japanesePC: このような透き通るようで、だけれども気品があって、軽やかに見えながら物言わぬ重厚感があり。
contexts.japanesePS3: このような透き通るようで、だけれども気品があって、軽やかに見えながら物言わぬ重厚感があり。
contexts.WH: It was transparent and yet so elegant that just glancing at it gave it an indescribable sense of dignity.
contexts.MG: It looked light...and yet so elegant that just glancing at it gave it an indescribable sense of dignity.
contexts.UP: You could almost see right through it, and yet it was so elegant; it appeared so weightless, and yet it had an indescribable presence.
contexts.note: MG retains the lost transparency/lightness contrast and makes the glance confer dignity. UP restores the visual contrasts and weighty presence.

MG.japanese: ……でも、だから触れてみたかったのです。このような透き通るようで、だけれども気品があって、軽やかに見えながら物言わぬ重厚感があり。…そんな壷に触れたなら、どんな手触りなのか、試してみたかったのです。
MG.translation: ...But that just made me want to touch it. It looked light...and yet so elegant that just glancing at it gave it an indescribable sense of dignity. ...I wanted to see what it felt like to touch a vase like that.

UP.japanese: ……でも、だから触れてみたかったのです。このような透き通るようで、だけれども気品があって、軽やかに見えながら物言わぬ重厚感があり。…そんな壷に触れたなら、どんな手触りなのか、試してみたかったのです。
UP.translation: ......But that just made me want to touch it. You could almost see right through it, and yet it was so elegant; it appeared so weightless, and yet it had an indescribable presence. ...I wanted to see what it felt like to touch a vase like that.

findings.sourceReading: The vase seems translucent yet refined, light yet silently imposing.
findings.alternative: Dignity captures part of 重厚感, but not its tension with lightness or its silent quality.
findings.sourceNote: Original Witch Hunt is compared with the original-PC Japanese embedded in the historical patches. MangaGamer uses the accepted MangaGamer-based Witch Hunt backport, and Umineko Project uses its repository English; both are compared with maintained PS3-derived Japanese. The MangaGamer and PS3 witnesses are not independently certified retail extractions.

findings.description: 触れてはならぬものだからこそ explains this degree of beauty by its being something one must not touch. Because something this beautiful should not be touched reverses the explanatory relation.

contexts.japanese: これほどの美しさは、触れてはならぬものだからこそ。
contexts.japanesePC: これほどの美しさは、触れてはならぬものだからこそ。
contexts.japanesePS3: これほどの美しさは、触れてはならぬものだからこそ。
contexts.WH: Because something this beautiful shouldn't be touched.
contexts.MG: Something this beautiful should never be touched.
contexts.UP: This much beauty arises precisely because it must never be touched.
contexts.note: MG retains the reversed relation, saying the vase must not be touched because it is beautiful. UP says its beauty arises precisely because it must not be touched.

MG.japanese: しかし、…それはお祖父さまが言われた通り、触れてはならないものだったのです。これほどの美しさは、触れてはならぬものだからこそ。触れれば壊れるほどに儚いものにしか宿らぬ美しさ。
MG.translation: However, ...just as Grandfather had said, it was a thing that shouldn't be touched. Something this beautiful should never be touched. Such beauty can only dwell in something so easily broken.

UP.japanese: しかし、…それはお祖父さまが言われた通り、触れてはならないものだったのです。これほどの美しさは、触れてはならぬものだからこそ。触れれば壊れるほどに儚いものにしか宿らぬ美しさ。
UP.translation: However, ...just as Grandfather had said, it was something that must not be touched. This much beauty arises precisely because it must never be touched. It was a beauty that could only dwell in something so fragile it would break at a touch.

findings.sourceReading: It has such beauty precisely because it is something forbidden to the touch, a beauty dwelling only in extreme fragility.
findings.alternative: The next line retains fragility and supports the same prohibition, but the immediate causal relation is reversed.
findings.sourceNote: Original Witch Hunt is compared with the original-PC Japanese embedded in the historical patches. MangaGamer uses the accepted MangaGamer-based Witch Hunt backport, and Umineko Project uses its repository English; both are compared with maintained PS3-derived Japanese. The MangaGamer and PS3 witnesses are not independently certified retail extractions.

findings.description: 黄金の燐粉で幻想的に輝きながら describes butterflies glowing fantastically with golden scale dust. Glowing dots shone detaches the dust from them and substitutes dots for powder.

contexts.japanese: 黄金の燐粉で幻想的に輝きながら、その美しき蝶が一匹、二匹と集まります。
contexts.japanesePC: 黄金の燐粉で幻想的に輝きながら、その美しき蝶が一匹、二匹と集まります。
contexts.japanesePS3: 黄金の燐粉で幻想的に輝きながら、その美しき蝶が一匹、二匹と集まります。
contexts.WH: As mysteriously glowing golden dots shone, the beautiful butterflies began to gather, one at a time.
contexts.MG: As mysteriously glowing golden dots shone in the air, the butterflies began to gather, one at a time.
contexts.UP: The beautiful butterflies began to gather, one at a time, glittering fantastically with glowing golden powder.
contexts.note: MG retains detached glowing dots. UP restores the butterflies glittering with golden powder.

MG.japanese:
黄金の燐粉で幻想的に輝きながら、その美しき蝶が一匹、二匹と集まります。あぁ、ベアトリーチェです。
頼もしき黄金の魔女、ベアトリーチェが来てくれたのです。
MG.translation: As mysteriously glowing golden dots shone in the air, the butterflies began to gather, one at a time. Oh, it's Beatrice. Beatrice, that reliable Golden Witch, had arrived.

UP.japanese:
黄金の燐粉で幻想的に輝きながら、その美しき蝶が一匹、二匹と集まります。あぁ、ベアトリーチェです。
頼もしき黄金の魔女、ベアトリーチェが来てくれたのです。
UP.translation:
The beautiful butterflies began to gather, one at a time, glittering fantastically with glowing golden powder. Oh, it's Beatrice.
That reliable Golden Witch, Beatrice had arrived.

findings.sourceReading: The beautiful butterflies gather, shining fantastically with golden scale dust.
findings.alternative: Dots could evoke tiny particles, but their relation to the butterfly surface is lost.

MangaGamer uses the accepted MangaGamer-based Witch Hunt backport, and Umineko Project uses its repository English; both are compared with maintained PS3-derived Japanese. findings.description: Became a group. and there, became the witch’s form separates a lowercase conjunction with a period and leaves the transformation clause without a workable subject.

contexts.japanese: 蝶が次々と集まって群れとなると、そこには彼女の姿が…。
contexts.japanesePC: 蝶が次々と集まって群となると、そこには彼女の姿が…。
contexts.japanesePS3: 蝶が次々と集まって群れとなると、そこには彼女の姿が…。
contexts.WH: The butterflies gathered one after another and became a group. and there, became the witch's form...
contexts.MG: The butterflies kept gathering until they formed a cloud, ...and then she was there...
contexts.UP: The butterflies gathered one after another, grouped together, and there, became her form...
contexts.note: MG replaces the broken clause with a cloud forming and Beatrice appearing. UP makes the gathered butterflies the subject of becoming her form; its punctuation remains awkward, but the original sentence-fragment failure is repaired.

MG.japanese:
蝶が次々と集まって群れとなると、そこには彼女の姿が…。彼女はいつだって私の味方。
私が困っていると、いつだって現れて助けてくれるのです。
MG.translation: The butterflies kept gathering until they formed a cloud, ...and then she was there... She was always there for me. Whenever I was in trouble, she'd always appear and save me.

UP.japanese:
蝶が次々と集まって群れとなると、そこには彼女の姿が…。彼女はいつだって私の味方。
私が困っていると、いつだって現れて助けてくれるのです。
UP.translation:
The butterflies gathered one after another, grouped together, and there, became her form... She was always on my side.
Whenever I was in trouble, she would always appear and help me.

findings.sourceReading: As butterflies gather into a swarm, her figure appears there.
findings.alternative: The transformation is recoverable, but the English sentence is malformed.
findings.sourceNote: Original Witch Hunt is compared with the original-PC Japanese embedded in the historical patches. MangaGamer uses the accepted MangaGamer-based Witch Hunt backport, and Umineko Project uses its repository English; both are compared with maintained PS3-derived Japanese. findings.description: 一度言い聞かせたこと refers to something he has already instructed the child about. Failed to follow something he said even once relocates once onto the disobedience.

contexts.japanese: そして、一度言い聞かせたことが守られなかった時は、地獄の堕天使も震え上がるほどに怒りくるうのです。
contexts.japanesePC: そして、一度言い聞かせたことが守られなかった時は、地獄の堕天使も震え上がるほどに怒り狂うのです。
contexts.japanesePS3: そして、一度言い聞かせたことが守られなかった時は、地獄の堕天使も震え上がるほどに怒りくるうのです。
contexts.WH: And when you failed to follow something he said even once, he would become so mad, with a rage that would make even the fallen angels in hell quiver.
contexts.MG: And when you failed to follow something he said even once, he would become so mad, with a rage that would make even the fallen angels in hell quiver.
contexts.UP: And once he told you something, if you failed to follow it, he would become mad with a rage that would make even the fallen angels in hell quiver.
contexts.note: MG retains “failed ... even once,” attaching once to disobedience. UP restores the condition as failing an instruction already given.

MG.japanese: お祖父さまはとても恐ろしい方です。そして、一度言い聞かせたことが守られなかった時は、地獄の堕天使も震え上がるほどに怒りくるうのです。私はそれを骨身に染みてよく知っていましたから、こうして震えながら涙を零すしかないのです…。
MG.translation: Grandfather was a very frightening person. And when you failed to follow something he said even once, he would become so mad, with a rage that would make even the fallen angels in hell quiver. Since I knew that down to my bones, I couldn't do anything but tremble and cry...

UP.japanese: お祖父さまはとても恐ろしい方です。そして、一度言い聞かせたことが守られなかった時は、地獄の堕天使も震え上がるほどに怒りくるうのです。私はそれを骨身に染みてよく知っていましたから、こうして震えながら涙を零すしかないのです…。
UP.translation: Grandfather was a very frightening person. And once he told you something, if you failed to follow it, he would become mad with a rage that would make even the fallen angels in hell quiver. I was intimately familiar with that, which is why I couldn't do anything but shake like this and cry...

findings.sourceReading: Kinzo rages when an instruction he has already given is not followed.
findings.alternative: Both describe intolerant anger; the threshold shifts from prior instruction to even a single failure.
findings.sourceNote: Original Witch Hunt is compared with the original-PC Japanese embedded in the historical patches. MangaGamer uses the accepted MangaGamer-based Witch Hunt backport, and Umineko Project uses its repository English; both are compared with maintained PS3-derived Japanese. The MangaGamer and PS3 witnesses are not independently certified retail extractions.

findings.description: 折檻 denotes punitive chastisement, stronger than being scolded. The earlier English punishment at 83107 shows that the threatened consequence was not consistently limited to verbal reprimand.

contexts.japanese:
「零してしまった姫様の涙を掬う魔法は持ち合わせておりませんが、
姫様がお館様から折檻を受けなくて済むようにする魔法なら、何とかなるかもしれません」
contexts.japanesePC: 「零してしまった姫様の涙を掬う魔法は持ち合わせておりませんが、姫様がお館様から折檻を受けなくて済むようにする魔法なら、何とかなるかもしれません。」
contexts.japanesePS3:
「零してしまった姫様の涙を掬う魔法は持ち合わせておりませんが、
姫様がお館様から折檻を受けなくて済むようにする魔法なら、何とかなるかもしれません」
contexts.WH: "I hold no magic to scoop up your fallen tears, princess, but if you want magic that will make it possible for you to avoid being scolded by the Master, I might be able to do something."
contexts.MG:
"I possess no magic that can scoop up your fallen tears, princess,
but if you need magic that will prevent the Master from scolding you, I might be able to manage something."
contexts.UP:
"I hold no magic to scoop up your fallen tears, princess,
but if you want magic that will make it possible for you to avoid being scolded by the Master, I might be able to do something."
contexts.note: Both editions reduce 折檻 to being scolded, despite translating the same threatened consequence as punishment at row 41.

MG.japanese: 「零してしまった姫様の涙を掬う魔法は持ち合わせておりませんが、姫様がお館様から折檻を受けなくて済むようにする魔法なら、何とかなるかもしれません」
MG.translation: "I possess no magic that can scoop up your fallen tears, princess, but if you need magic that will prevent the Master from scolding you, I might be able to manage something."

UP.japanese: 「零してしまった姫様の涙を掬う魔法は持ち合わせておりませんが、姫様がお館様から折檻を受けなくて済むようにする魔法なら、何とかなるかもしれません」
UP.translation: "I hold no magic to scoop up your fallen tears, princess, but if you want magic that will make it possible for you to avoid being scolded by the Master, I might be able to do something."

findings.sourceReading: Beatrice may provide magic that spares the princess Kinzo’s punishment.
findings.alternative: The scene also uses 叱る and later お叱り, so scolding is part of the threat; it nevertheless softens this specifically stronger term.
findings.sourceNote: Original Witch Hunt is compared with the original-PC Japanese embedded in the historical patches. MangaGamer uses the accepted MangaGamer-based Witch Hunt backport, and Umineko Project uses its repository English; both are compared with maintained PS3-derived Japanese. The MangaGamer and PS3 witnesses are not independently certified retail extractions.

findings.description: 無限の魔力が備わる says endless magical power is acquired at that level. Considered to be an Endless Witch substitutes a title or classification for the attainment, and supplies the title before the next Japanese reveal.

contexts.japanese:
その境地に達した時、無限の魔力が備わるでしょう。
それこそが、魔女の達するべき無限の境地。
私たちはその魔女を、最大の敬いをもってこう呼びます」
「無限の魔女…」
contexts.japanesePC: 「えぇ。その境地に達した時、無限の魔力が備わるでしょう。それこそが、魔女の達するべき無限の境地。私たちはその魔女を、最大の敬いをもってこう呼びます。」
contexts.japanesePS3:
その境地に達した時、無限の魔力が備わるでしょう。
それこそが、魔女の達するべき無限の境地。
私たちはその魔女を、最大の敬いをもってこう呼びます」
「無限の魔女…」
contexts.WH: "Yes.  When one reaches that level they are considered to be an Endless Witch.  That is the endless level that all witches should reach.  We respect those witches the most and call them this."
contexts.MG:
When one reaches that level, they are considered to be an Endless Witch.
That is the endless level that all witches ought to reach.
We offer the utmost respect to those witches and call them by that title."
"An Endless Witch..."
contexts.UP:
When one reaches that level, they are possessed of endless magical power.
That is the endless level that all witches should strive to reach.
As a sign of the highest respect to those witches, we call them..."
"An Endless Witch..."
contexts.note: MG prematurely substitutes the Endless Witch title for acquiring endless magical power. UP restores the power attainment and leaves the title reveal to the following lines.

MG.japanese: 「えぇ。その境地に達した時、無限の魔力が備わるでしょう。それこそが、魔女の達するべき無限の境地。私たちはその魔女を、最大の敬いをもってこう呼びます」
MG.translation: "Yes. When one reaches that level, they are considered to be an Endless Witch. That is the endless level that all witches ought to reach. We offer the utmost respect to those witches and call them by that title."

UP.japanese: 「えぇ。その境地に達した時、無限の魔力が備わるでしょう。それこそが、魔女の達するべき無限の境地。私たちはその魔女を、最大の敬いをもってこう呼びます」
UP.translation: "Yes. When one reaches that level, they are possessed of endless magical power. That is the endless level that all witches should strive to reach. As a sign of the highest respect to those witches, we call them..."

findings.sourceReading: Upon reaching the level of repeated restoration, a witch possesses endless magic; the honorific name is then introduced.
findings.alternative: Later explanation preserves endless restoration and the title, so this is a local mechanism-to-classification change and timing shift, not an unsolvability finding.
findings.sourceNote: Original Witch Hunt is compared with the original-PC Japanese embedded in the historical patches. MangaGamer uses the accepted MangaGamer-based Witch Hunt backport, and Umineko Project uses its repository English; both are compared with maintained PS3-derived Japanese. The MangaGamer and PS3 witnesses are not independently certified retail extractions.

findings.description: 有難味を感じる means appreciating the worth of what she has attained. Feel valued changes her gratitude or appreciation into receiving validation.

contexts.japanese:
「…たまには有難味を感じねば、少々勿体無いというものよ。
……くっくくくくく」
contexts.japanesePC: …たまには有難味を感じねば、少々勿体無いというものよ。……くっくくくくく。」
contexts.japanesePS3:
「…たまには有難味を感じねば、少々勿体無いというものよ。
……くっくくくくく」
contexts.WH: ...It's a little bit of a waste if I don't feel valued every once in a while.  ......*cackle*cackle*cackle*."
contexts.MG:
...It'd be a bit of a waste if I never got a chance to appreciate it.
...*cackle*cackle*cackle*."
contexts.UP:

「……あほやなぁ…。

findings.description: 大学院 means graduate school. College changes the educational stage of Eva’s rejected ambition; this repeats at 84153 and 84280.

contexts.japanese:
この腹立たしい言葉は、私が大学院を希望したが父に拒否され、失意の私に兄が吐いた暴言だ。
私は、自分が右代宮家の長女として相応しい品格と教養を身につける上で、大学院進学は必要なものだと訴えた。

findings.description: いつ理解したのだろう asks when she came to understand. I probably understood that drops the temporal question and instead qualifies whether she understood at all.

contexts.japanese:
それを、私はいつ理解したのだろう。
……少女時代にはもう、理解していたのかもしれない。
…でも、それを本当の意味で受け容れるには、成人を待たなければならなかった。
contexts.japanesePC: それを、私はいつ理解したのだろう。
contexts.japanesePS3:
それを、私はいつ理解したのだろう。
……少女時代にはもう、理解していたのかもしれない。
…でも、それを本当の意味で受け容れるには、成人を待たなければならなかった。
contexts.WH: I probably understood that.
contexts.MG:
When was it that I came to understand that?
...It may have been as early as my childhood years.
...But, I was going to have to wait until I grew up before I could truly accept it.
contexts.UP:
I wonder when it was that I understood that.
......I probably understood ever since I was a young girl.
...But to truly accept it, I had to wait until I had grown up.
contexts.note: Both editions first ask when Eva understood and then suggest childhood as a possibility, preserving the temporal question.

MG.japanese:
それを、私はいつ理解したのだろう。
……少女時代にはもう、理解していたのかもしれない。…でも、それを本当の意味で受け容れるには、成人を待たなければならなかった。
MG.translation: When was it that I came to understand that? ...It may have been as early as my childhood years. ...But, I was going to have to wait until I grew up before I could truly accept it.

UP.japanese:
それを、私はいつ理解したのだろう。
……少女時代にはもう、理解していたのかもしれない。…でも、それを本当の意味で受け容れるには、成人を待たなければならなかった。

I wonder when it was that I understood that.
......I probably understood ever since I was a young girl. ...But to truly accept it, I had to wait until I had grown up.

findings.sourceReading: She wonders when she understood her father’s view, perhaps already in girlhood, though acceptance waited until adulthood.

findings.description: 女を養う means provide for or support women, not cultivate them.

contexts.japanese:
女は男に仕えるために存在する。
そして男は女を養うために存在する。
女の仕事は、男の背中を守り、家庭を守って子を育てることだ」
contexts.japanesePC: 「それを認めるのはエレガントではないが、お前の勘違いを正すには、少々毒のある言葉も必要かと思うよ。だから言い切ろう。女は男に仕えるために存在する。そして男は女を養うために存在する。女の仕事は、男の背中を守り、家庭を守って子を育てることだ。
contexts.japanesePS3:
女は男に仕えるために存在する。
そして男は女を養うために存在する。
女の仕事は、男の背中を守り、家庭を守って子を育てることだ」
contexts.WH: "It isn't elegant to accept that, but in order to correct your mistake, I think that a few unpleasant words are necessary.  So let me say it plainly.  Women exist to serve men.  And men exist to cultivate women.  A woman's job is to protect a man's back, to protect their house and raise their children.
contexts.MG:
Women exist to serve men.
And men exist to provide for women.
A woman's job is to protect a man's back, to protect his house and raise his children."
contexts.UP:
Women exist to serve men.
And men exist to cultivate women.
A woman's job is to protect a man's back, to protect their house and raise their children."
contexts.note: MG restores men providing for women. UP retains “cultivate women,” changing financial support into cultivation.

MG.japanese: 「それを認めるのはエレガントではないが、お前の勘違いを正すには、少々毒のある言葉も必要かと思うよ。だから言い切ろう。女は男に仕えるために存在する。そして男は女を養うために存在する。女の仕事は、男の背中を守り、家庭を守って子を育てることだ」
MG.translation: "It isn't elegant to say it out loud, but I think a few unpleasant words are necessary in order to correct your mistake. So let me say it plainly. Women exist to serve men. And men exist to provide for women. A woman's job is to protect a man's back, to protect his house and raise his children."

UP.japanese: 「それを認めるのはエレガントではないが、お前の勘違いを正すには、少々毒のある言葉も必要かと思うよ。だから言い切ろう。女は男に仕えるために存在する。そして男は女を養うために存在する。女の仕事は、男の背中を守り、家庭を守って子を育てることだ」
UP.translation: "It isn't elegant to admit that, but in order to correct your mistake, I think that a few unpleasant words are necessary. So let me say it plainly. Women exist to serve men. And men exist to cultivate women. A woman's job is to protect a man's back, to protect their house and raise their children."

findings.sourceReading: Krauss asserts that women exist to serve men and men to provide for women.
findings.alternative: Cultivate might loosely imply care, but introduces development rather than the stated reciprocal provision.

MG.japanese: 父には到底及ばなくても、金融や経済に学識を深め、いつでもその手伝いができるよう自分を研磨してきたはずだった。……しかし、それが父に認められることはついになかった。父にとって、女は男を支えるものでしかなく、それ以上であることを許さなかったからだ。
MG.translation: Even if I couldn't quite reach Father's level, I deepened my knowledge in economics and finance, trying to improve myself so I could be of use to him at any time. ...However, in the end, Father never acknowledged my efforts. To Father, a woman was only meant to support a man, and nothing further than that was permissable.

UP.japanese: 父には到底及ばなくても、金融や経済に学識を深め、いつでもその手伝いができるよう自分を研磨してきたはずだった。……しかし、それが父に認められることはついになかった。父にとって、女は男を支えるものでしかなく、それ以上であることを許さなかったからだ。
UP.translation: Even if I was far from reaching Father's level, I deepened my knowledge in economics and finance, and tried to improve myself so that I could help out with that at any time. ......However, in the end, there never came a time when Father acknowledged that. findings.description: 私の心に入った傷の裂け目 describes the fissure of a wound in her heart. The fate that went into my heart invents fate as the agent and loses the wound noun until the next sewing image.

その傷の縫い方を、“彼女”は教えてくれた…。

その傷の縫い方を、“彼女”は教えてくれた…。

「お父様は、少なくとも“今”は、女に当主を継がせないと言っている。

お父様が決めた以上、それを破棄出来るのもお父様」

findings.description: 三度読み直してから口にすべきかどうか考える instructs deciding whether to speak after rereading. Read it three times before you say it out loud removes the decision and presumes eventual speech.

じゃねぇと、きっと後悔するからな…」

findings.description: 聞きだそうとする素振り describes George feigning an attempt to draw the embarrassing remarks from Shannon in order to tease Battler. Warming up for when Shannon would tell him changes the staged interrogation into preparation for a future disclosure.

contexts.japanese:
しばらくの間、譲治の兄貴は、紗音ちゃんから俺の恥ずかしい失言を聞きだそうとする素振りをして、俺をからかうのだった。
譲治の兄貴は、紗音ちゃんとつるむ様にしてふざけているわけだが、
……何というか、とても気さくでフランクな感じだった。
彼は、いとこ相手にならフランクだが、使用人たちには節度ある紳士的態度で接していたはずだ。
…それを思うと、何だかちょっぴり馴れ馴れしいようにも感じ、わずかな違和感を覚えた。

急にまともな言葉で話すように努力し始めたらその、そういう気概みたいなもんでドキっと来ちまう男もいるかもなぁ」
「そ、そうなんだ…？
そうか……、
……うん…」
朱志香は、急に神妙な言葉遣いになったかと思うと、ほんのりと頬を染めている。
…なるほど、告白は空振りしたが、どうやら諦めちゃいないらしい。
contexts.WH: As Jessica thought about suddenly speaking meekly, she blushed faintly.
contexts.MG:
"I-I-Is it really...
...Is the way I speak...
really that bad?"
"...Hmm?
Well, umm, how you talk isn't everything, but when people like you, who usually have a rough style of speech,
suddenly start working hard to talk more normally... well, there are guys out there whose heart'll skip a beat when they see how determined you are."
"I-Is that really true...?
I see,
...yeah..."
Jessica suddenly started talking more meekly, and then her face instantly went slightly red.
...I see, even though her confession didn't go well, it looks like she still hasn't given up.
contexts.UP:
"I‐i‐is it really...
......Is the way I speak...
...really that bad?"
"...Hmm?
Well, uhh, how you talk isn't everything, but if someone like you, who usually talks badly,
suddenly started making an effort to talk nicely, umm, that takes courage, and that might really get some guys' hearts thumping, maybe."
"R‐really...?
I see......
......Yeah..."
Jessica had suddenly started speaking meekly, and was faintly blushing.
...I see, even though her confession didn't go well, it looks like she still hasn't given up.

findings.description: この使用人風情が and 泥棒猫 are imagined insults: lowly servant and romantic thief or homewrecker. As though a servant was the same as a cat who had snuck in substitutes a literal comparison and loses both direct class contempt and romantic theft.

この使用人風情がー、泥棒猫ーと絶叫するだろう。

……この６年ですっかり成長し、青春を謳歌しているいとこたちとの出会いは、本当に新鮮。

findings.description: The wording “can escape barefooted” turns the idiom of alarm into an ability to escape, weakening Ronove’s teasing praise.

UP.japanese: 譲治の兄貴は、そんな親たちを理解してやってほしいと弁護する。…理屈ではわかる。金の話はどんなに汚くとも、目を閉じれば済む問題ではない。しかしそれでも、ああもあからさまにカネの亡者に成り下がれるものなのか…。
UP.translation: George‐aniki pleaded on behalf of our parents, saying that he wanted us to understand them. ...I understood his reasoning. No matter how filthy this talk of money was, it wouldn't go away if you just closed your eyes to it. But even so, how could they so blatantly degenerate into such money‐grubbing demons...

findings.sourceReading: カネの亡者 means people consumed by greed for money; Battler deplores how overtly the adults have become such people.
findings.alternative: The inheritance dispute concerns eventual death, but 亡者 here forms the money-grubber idiom, not a reference to a deceased person’s property.

findings.description: WH says Eva left Krauss dumbfounded by ending the conversation, and Eva asks who is ending it. Inability to conduct a reasonable exchange becomes an act of termination.

findings.description: WH says distant days and embellished, losing the gray/color contrast linking oppressive life to the meeting.

contexts.japanese:
関東大震災でお家が傾き、金蔵は望まずして右代宮家の当主に担ぎ出された。
しかし、当初の金蔵は、それを傀儡にしようという親戚の長老たちの強い影響下にあり、操り人形も同然だった。
自分では何も決めることが許されず、婚姻の相手すらも拒めなかった…。
……金蔵の黄金伝説は、そんな灰色の日々に、
黄金の魔女ベアトリーチェに出会うことにより、急にドラマチックなものに彩られていく。
それはつまり、
…金蔵が本当に愛する女性に出会った、
ということなのかもしれない。
contexts.japanesePC: ……金蔵の黄金伝説は、そんな灰色の日々に、黄金の魔女ベアトリーチェに出会うことにより、急にドラマチックなものに彩られていく。

それはつまり、
…金蔵が本当に愛する女性に出会った、
ということなのかもしれない。
contexts.WH: ......Since the time he met that Golden Witch Beatrice in those distant days, Kinzo's Legend of the Gold was quickly embellished into something dramatic.
contexts.MG:
The family sank after the Great Kanto Earthquake, and Father was set up as the Ushiromiya Family Head against his will.
However, in the beginning, the elder relatives treated Kinzo like a dummy and influenced him powerfully, almost like he was a puppet.
He wasn't permitted to decide anything by himself, not even his marriage partner...
...Ever since he met that Golden Witch Beatrice in those distant days,
Kinzo's Legend of the Gold was quickly embellished into something dramatic.
In other words,
...it could mean...
that Kinzo really did find a woman he loved.
contexts.UP:
The family sank after the Great Kanto Earthquake, and Kinzo was set up as the Ushiromiya family head against his will.
However, in the beginning, he was influenced strongly by the elder relatives, who treated him like a puppet while they pulled the strings.
He wasn't permitted to decide anything by himself, not even his marriage partner...
......And by his meeting with the Golden Witch Beatrice in those unhappy days,
Kinzo's Legend of the Gold was quickly embellished into something dramatic.
In other words,
...it could mean...
that Kinzo met with a woman he really did love.
contexts.note: MG retains “distant days,” losing the gray or unhappy quality that supports the color contrast. UP restores “unhappy days.”

findings.description: WH says she has nothing to do with this, replacing lack of succession prospects with lack of involvement.

contexts.japanese:

…つまり、序列は楼座より１つ下ね。
とても家督争いに加われるようなレベルじゃないわ」
「そういうことか。
…魔女の碑文を解けば、序列に関係なく家督が継げる。
つまり、まったく可能性のないベアトリーチェにとってもっとも有利な条件ってわけだ」
contexts.japanesePC: 「そういうことか。…魔女の碑文を解けば、序列に関係なく家督が継げる。つまり、まったく可能性のないベアトリーチェにとってもっとも有利な条件ってわけだ。」

つまり、まったく可能性のないベアトリーチェにとってもっとも有利な条件ってわけだ」
contexts.WH: "Is that so?  ...If someone can solve the witch's riddle, they will receive the inheritance regardless of rank.  In other words, it is the most advantageous condition that Beatrice could get, since she has nothing to do with this."
contexts.MG:
"Even if that mistress was added into the family ranking system, she isn't a direct relative of Father, so she'd be inferior even to the children.
...In other words, she'd be one step below Rosa in rank.
That wouldn't be a good position to enter the battle for the Headship from."
"I see, so that's it.
...If someone can solve the witch's riddle, they'll get the Headship regardless of rank.
In other words, it's the most advantageous condition Beatrice could possibly get, since she's got no chance otherwise."
contexts.UP:
"Even if that mistress obtained a rank within the Ushiromiya family, since she is not a direct relative of Father, she would be inferior to even the children.
...In other words, she would be right below Rosa in rank.
That's not a good position to join the battle for the headship."
"So that's it.
...If someone can solve the witch's riddle, they will receive the headship regardless of rank.
In other words, it is the most advantageous condition that Beatrice could get, since she had no chance whatsoever."
contexts.note: Both editions restore that Beatrice has no chance of succession otherwise, rather than saying she has nothing to do with the matter.

findings.description: WH separates the game not being on even footing from some compelling force, obscuring what that force must compel.

私たちは家督を素直に譲るわけもない」
「……つまり、私たちがこのゲームに対等な条件で挑まなくてはならないという、強制力がない限り、
このゲームは成立しないのよ」

「……つまり、私たちがこのゲームに対等な条件で挑まなくてはならないという、強制力がない限り、

contexts.WH: "That's it exactly.  No matter how one-sided a game Beatrice proposes, even if she splendidly shows us the answer, there's no way that we'll obediently hand over the inheritance.  ......So as long as this game isn't on an even footing, unless they have some kind of compelling force, the game won't succeed."
contexts.MG:
No matter how Beatrice might one-sidedly propose a game like this, even if she were to spectacularly show us the answer,
there's no way we'd obediently hand over the Headship.
...In other words, unless she has a compelling force in the form of challenging us to a game with equal conditions for us all,
this won't truly count as a game."
contexts.UP:

there's no way that we'll obediently hand over the headship."

MG.japanese:
「そういうことよ。いくらベアトリーチェが一方的にこんなゲームを提案しても、そして見事その答えを示して見せたとしても。私たちは家督を素直に譲るわけもない」
「……つまり、私たちがこのゲームに対等な条件で挑まなくてはならないという、強制力がない限り、このゲームは成立しないのよ」

"That's it exactly. No matter how Beatrice might one-sidedly propose a game like this, even if she were to spectacularly show us the answer, there's no way we'd obediently hand over the Headship. 
...In other words, unless she has a compelling force in the form of challenging us to a game with equal conditions for us all, this won't truly count as a game."

UP.japanese:
「そういうことよ。いくらベアトリーチェが一方的にこんなゲームを提案しても、そして見事その答えを示して見せたとしても。私たちは家督を素直に譲るわけもない」
「……つまり、私たちがこのゲームに対等な条件で挑まなくてはならないという、強制力がない限り、このゲームは成立しないのよ」
UP.translation:
"That's it exactly. No matter how one‐sided a game Beatrice proposes, and even if she splendidly shows us the answer, there's no way that we'll obediently hand over the headship."
"......In other words, unless there is something that forcibly compels us to play this game under fair conditions, this game won't function as a game."

findings.sourceReading: The game cannot function without leverage obliging the family to participate on equal terms, including accepting defeat.
findings.alternative: The surrounding loser-payment clarification helps, but the source makes compulsory equal participation the object of the leverage, not an independent condition.

"That is correct.

You can directly prove that "this box is the winner = this box has a cookie in it".
However, if the box you open is empty, then the reverse, Hempel's Raven, is satisfied.
In other words 'this box does not have a cookie in it = this box isn't the winner."

"And that means, as long as we accept the premise that there are no more than two boxes,
the contrapositive shows that the other box is automatically the winner."
contexts.note: Both editions preserve the staged inference: the opened box is shown not to be the winner, then the fixed two-box premise establishes that the other box wins.

findings.description: WH says a little part of his heart splits, replacing the supports he relies on with an emotional wound.

contexts.japanese:
ベアトリーチェの赤は、まさに伝家の宝刀。
ヤツが赤で語ったことは証拠も反論の余地もなく、それが真実となって確定してしまう。
それらは俺を何度も叩き斬り、わずかな心の拠り所をいつも真っ二つにしてきた。
だが、迂闊に使えばそれは俺に真相を探る情報とされてしまうこともある。

contexts.WH: Until now she had used that to severely wound me, and each time a little part of my heart would split in half.
contexts.MG:
Beatrice's red was her true trump card.
When that person speaks in red, it's definitely the truth, and no amount of proof or counterarguments can change that.
Until now, she's used that to severely wound me, and each time, the tiny foundations supporting my heart get split in half.
However, if she uses it carelessly, then I can also gleam a little information about the truth.
contexts.UP:
Beatrice's red was truly her secret weapon, her treasured blade.
The things she spoke in red would become solidified as the truth, and no amount of evidence or counterarguments could change them.
They had cut me down to size many times now, rending in two any supports my heart had to lean on.
However, if she used it carelessly, then I could also find a little information about the truth.

Don't be afraid of the red.
Keep her cornered, so that she'll have no choice but to refute me with the red...!
contexts.UP:
The more she recklessly flourishes that red, the more chances I'll have to strike back.

contexts.note: Both editions restore Battler cornering Beatrice so she is forced to answer in red, rather than preventing a red reply.

MG.japanese:
赤に怯えるな。
むしろ、赤で反論せざるを得ないよう、追い詰めろ……！ヤツがどんなに高圧に赤を語ろうとも、……そう、その赤こそは、ヤツの傷口より噴出す血潮も同じなのだ。
MG.translation: Don't be afraid of the red. Keep her cornered, so that she'll have no choice but to refute me with the red...! No matter how oppressively she speaks in red, ...that's right, that red itself is the same as fresh blood leaking from her wounds.

UP.japanese:
赤に怯えるな。
むしろ、赤で反論せざるを得ないよう、追い詰めろ……！ヤツがどんなに高圧に赤を語ろうとも、……そう、その赤こそは、ヤツの傷口より噴出す血潮も同じなのだ。
UP.translation:
Don't be afraid of the red.
Keep the pressure on, so that she is forced to refute with the red......! No matter how oppressively she speaks in red, ......yes, that red itself is the same as fresh blood spurting from her wounds.

findings.sourceReading: Battler tells himself to corner her so she has no choice but to counter in red.
findings.alternative: He hopes her red will fail to defeat him, but 反論せざるを得ない explicitly means she must reply, consistent with his strategy of extracting information.

findings.description: WH says she probably planned to smile back, making the performed smile itself merely intended.

contexts.japanese:

ベアトは笑いを返し、余裕をアピールしたつもりだったろうが、……額に浮かぶ汗を隠せない。

contexts.WH: Beato probably planned to smile back and appear relaxed, ......but she couldn't hide the sweat building up on her forehead.
contexts.MG:
Ronove, who was supposed to be her ally, roguishly rushed her into making her next move.
Beato probably thought she'd managed to smile back and appear confident, ...but she couldn't hide the sweat building up on her forehead.

contexts.note: MG says Beatrice probably thought she had managed to smile back, making the smile itself uncertain. UP restores the actual smile followed by her probable intention.

MG.japanese: 味方のはずのロノウェが、主に悪戯っぽく次の手を急かす。ベアトは笑いを返し、余裕をアピールしたつもりだったろうが、……額に浮かぶ汗を隠せない。格下の相手を鼻であしらってやろうという余裕は、今や完全に失われていた。
MG.translation: Ronove, who was supposed to be her ally, roguishly rushed her into making her next move. Beato probably thought she'd managed to smile back and appear confident, ...but she couldn't hide the sweat building up on her forehead. By now, she had completely lost the confident feeling that had allowed her to turn her nose up at her worthless opponent.

findings.sourceReading: Beatrice smiles back, presumably intending to project composure, but cannot hide her sweat.
findings.alternative: The uncertainty concerns her intended display of composure, not whether she smiled.

私は一瞬、ぐるりと回って、元のお屋敷に戻ってきてしまったのではないかと思ったわ。
確かに、私たちが森へ入らないように、お屋敷でも柵はあった。

findings.description: WH makes both alternatives explanations of an impression and attributes difficult walking to her child’s legs.

その柵は高さに負けないくらい、とてもとても長くて、いつまで経っても角を迎えなかった。
相当広大な範囲を囲んでいたのかもしれないし、
…あるいは子どもの足だし、森は歩きにくかったからそういう印象を持ったのかもしれないわ。

contexts.WH: "There was definitely something she was worried about.  ......I remember that when I noticed that it didn't seem like something I could resolve just by talking to her, I was also really sad.
contexts.MG:
"......I'd already introduced myself, so I asked about her.
...When I did, the atmosphere quickly grew depressing.
...How should I put it... She seemed to grow listless and lonely.
...It was that same expression I saw on her face in the beginning."
"Well, she was his hidden mistress, after all.
If she just walked around wherever she liked, Mom might've found her.
...I'll bet she was practically under house arrest."
"Even though she had beautiful clothes, a beautiful mansion, and a garden, she must've felt pretty cramped.
I'll bet she had it rough.
......And then?"
"She was definitely worried about something.
...I remember feeling really sad myself,
when I realized it wasn't something I could do anything about by talking to her."
"......She seemed to forget I was even there.
...She gazed vaguely off into the distance...and was silent for a long, long time.
...I thought I must've said something wrong,
...but it didn't seem to be the type of atmosphere where I could apologize,
...so I remained silent too for a long, long time, until she remembered I was there..."

findings.alternative: Both versions suggest talking would not help, but the source specifically frames disclosure by Beatrice to Rosa; WH reverses the conversational direction and centers Rosa’s ability to resolve it.

contexts.MG:
"......Are there really no wolves beyond the fence?"

findings.description: WH moves the extraordinary degree from the required courage to the first step, calling the step unspeakable.

いつかは外へ出なくてはならないと気付き始めていた。
でも、外の世界のことを知らない彼女にとって、
外へ踏み出す第一歩は想像を絶する勇気が必要だったに違いない…。
その上で、彼女は決意した。
外へ出たいと、きっと生まれて初めてに違いない決意を、口にしたのだ。

外へ出たいと、きっと生まれて初めてに違いない決意を、口にしたのだ。
contexts.WH: But, since she didn't know about the outside world, she must have needed the courage to take that unspeakable first step outside...
contexts.MG:
She was starting to realize that she couldn't stay there forever.
She was starting to realize that she had to go outside someday.
But, since she didn't know about the outside world,
she must have needed courage to take that unspeakable first step outside...
And despite that, she had made her decision.
She'd voiced her decision to go outside, a decision she was probably making for the first time in her life.
contexts.UP:

She was starting to realize that she had to go outside sometime.
But, since she didn't know about the outside world,

contexts.note: MG retains “unspeakable first step,” moving the extraordinary degree away from the courage. UP restores an unimaginable amount of courage.

While I had been imprisoned in a cage of flesh, I had completely lost my memory as a witch.
However, thanks to Rosa, if you could say that...
Thanks to my accidental but fortunate death, I had now finally brought myself together......
"......Rosa.
You are probably regretting that you brought about my death.
But as for me, I could even thank you.
*cackle*cackle*...!"
contexts.note: MG restores that Beatrice regained herself. UP retains “brought myself together,” suggesting composure rather than recovered identity.

MG.translation: While being imprisoned in a cage of flesh, I completely lost my memory as a witch. However, thanks to Rosa, if you could say that... ...Thanks to my accidental death, I'd now finally regained my self...

UP.translation: While I had been imprisoned in a cage of flesh, I had completely lost my memory as a witch. However, thanks to Rosa, if you could say that... Thanks to my accidental but fortunate death, I had now finally brought myself together......

findings.sourceReading: Through being able to die accidentally, she has finally regained herself, including her witch memories and identity.
findings.alternative: Bringing oneself together can suggest composure or consolidation, but the preceding restored memories and cage-induced loss establish recovering identity, not merely emotional composure.

findings.description: WH makes Kinzo repay what he borrowed instead of Beatrice planning to repay him for his treatment of her.

contexts.japanese:
とにかく、ゆっくり時間を掛けて養生し、元の力を取り戻そう。
……これまでの借りを、金蔵にどう返してやるかを思案しながら。
ひらりと宙を舞いながら、もう一度だけ海岸を見下ろす。

とにかく、ゆっくり時間を掛けて養生し、元の力を取り戻そう。

findings.sourceReading: She considers how to pay Kinzo back for everything he has done to her.
findings.alternative: 借りを返す may describe debt repayment, but 金蔵に marks the recipient and 返してやる expresses her retaliatory agency; their captivity history and subsequent revenge thoughts fix the sense.

UP.japanese: 「くっくっくっく。蝶に姿を変え、森に紛れた妾を探し出すことなど、もはや金蔵には不可能なこと。……だが、金蔵も指をくわえているわけではなかった。しかし、妾を捕らえる方法はすぐに用意は出来ぬ」

findings.sourceReading: Kinzo did not sit idly by, though a capture method could not be prepared immediately.
findings.alternative: He might also be undismayed, but 指をくわえている is an idiom of watching helplessly or idly; his immediate countermeasures explain the contrast.
