contexts.WH: The measure of time that counted to 24 had returned to 0, and had begun to count back again...
contexts.MG:
On the antique clock with the intricate design that had been sitting on his desk,
the two overlapping hands tilted to the right and began to slide.
The measure of time that counted up to 24...had returned to 0...and had begun to count back again...
"...Measuring time is a brutal thing.
It drags itself all the way to 24 over the course of a day, and then returns back to 0.
...It certainly did count to 23:59.
However, is it ever able to reach 24:00?
...If you conclude that it returns to 0:00 again without reaching 24, how futile it must all be."
contexts.UP:
On the antique clock with an intricate design that was sitting on his desk,
the two overlapping hands had begun to tilt to the right, and separate from one another.
The passage of time that had counted to 24 had returned to 0, and begun to start counting again...
"......The passage of time is a brutal thing.
It drags itself all the way to 24 over the course of a day, and then returns back to 0.
......It surely managed to count to 23:59.
However, was it ever able to reach 24:00?
......If you believe that it returns to 0:00 again without reaching it, how futile it seems."
contexts.note: MG retains “count back again,” suggesting reverse counting. UP restores renewed counting, despite its separate redundant construction.

UP.translation: It would depend on how he defined the result most favorable to him, but if he demanded the best result in a strict sense, it would be the same as a simple roulette of luck, where he sought an arithmetic miracle. ......However, to Kinzo, who made miracles of numbers the basis of his magical power, this could become very much like a magic ritual.

findings.sourceReading: He seeks an arithmetic miracle in a roulette of luck.

contexts.MG:
...Or rather, those servants called furniture were supposed to be like that.
Just like how desks and closets go unnoticed by members of the family,
these servants also held it as a great virtue to just suddenly be there whenever they were needed.

but compared to Kanon and Genji...well, you could say she was a little more boisterous...

findings.sourceReading: Like unnoticed furniture, servants should appear unobtrusively when the household needs them; this is their greatest virtue.
findings.alternative: They can be recovered as the family grammatically, but the main-clause servants subject and needed to construction instead attach necessity to the servants; the source has household members needing their service.

findings.description: WH writes that is really was a strong lock, colliding present and past verb forms.

contexts.japanese:
鍵穴にそれを刺し、重い手応えで捻る。
……一見、それは確かに厳重な施錠を示した。
しかし、結界が破られているということは、
魔力ある者にとって、この扉はすでに開きっぱなしと同じ意味だ…。
ゴトリと重い音がして、人間にとっても、扉が開かれたことを示す。
contexts.japanesePC: ……一見、それは確かに厳重な施錠を示した。
contexts.japanesePS3:
鍵穴にそれを刺し、重い手応えで捻る。
……一見、それは確かに厳重な施錠を示した。
しかし、結界が破られているということは、
魔力ある者にとって、この扉はすでに開きっぱなしと同じ意味だ…。
ゴトリと重い音がして、人間にとっても、扉が開かれたことを示す。
contexts.WH: ......At first glance, it looked like that meant that is really was a strong lock.
contexts.MG:
He stuck it in the key hole and turned it heavily.
...At first glance, that seemed to prove that it was a sturdy lock.
However, now that the barrier had been destroyed,
this door might as well have been left open, from the viewpoint of anyone with magical power.
The heavy sound just now meant that the door had now been opened even for humans.
contexts.UP:
He stuck it in the keyhole, and turned it heavily.
......At a glance, that would have indicated that it really was a strong lock.
However, the fact that the barrier had been destroyed...
meant that this door had long been wide open for anyone with magical power...
The lock made a heavy sound, indicating that the door had been opened to humans as well.
contexts.note: Both editions repair WH’s “is was” collision in the lock sentence.

MG.japanese:
源次は懐より、黄金の鍵を取り出す。
金蔵が持つ以外に、唯一存在する書斎の鍵だ。鍵穴にそれを刺し、重い手応えで捻る。
……一見、それは確かに厳重な施錠を示した。
MG.translation: Genji pulled a gold key out of his pocket. It was the only key to the study that existed, other than the one Kinzo held. He stuck it in the key hole and turned it heavily. ...At first glance, that seemed to prove that it was a sturdy lock.

Genji pulled a gold key out of his pocket.
It was the only key to the study that existed, other than the one Kinzo held. He stuck it in the keyhole, and turned it heavily.
......At a glance, that would have indicated that it really was a strong lock.

findings.sourceReading: The heavy turn seemingly indicates securely locked status.
findings.alternative: The intended meaning is easy to recover, but is was is ungrammatical.

findings.description: WH adds or a fraud to Kanon’s explanation of how furniture changes according to its master.

contexts.japanese:
「嘉音くんとは、会うのは初めてになりますね。
……私は、ベアトリーチェさまの家具頭を任されております、ロノウェと申します。
……源次さんの古い馴染みですよ。
あなたと同じに、私も家具です。
仕える主は異なりますが」
嘉音の表情からは決して緊張の色は消えない。
……家具は仕える主が違えば、やさしくも残酷にも如何様にでもなる。
…彼が嫌悪するベアトリーチェに仕える家具だと名乗ったならば、
彼もまた嫌悪すべき存在に違いないのだ…。
contexts.japanesePC: ……家具は仕える主が違えば、やさしくも残酷にも如何様にでもなる。
contexts.japanesePS3:
「嘉音くんとは、会うのは初めてになりますね。
……私は、ベアトリーチェさまの家具頭を任されております、ロノウェと申します。
……源次さんの古い馴染みですよ。
あなたと同じに、私も家具です。
仕える主は異なりますが」
嘉音の表情からは決して緊張の色は消えない。
……家具は仕える主が違えば、やさしくも残酷にも如何様にでもなる。
…彼が嫌悪するベアトリーチェに仕える家具だと名乗ったならば、
彼もまた嫌悪すべき存在に違いないのだ…。
contexts.WH: ......If furniture served a different master, they could be kind or brutal or a fraud.
contexts.MG:
"This will be our first meeting, Kanon-kun.
...I, Ronove, have been entrusted with the position of Beatrice-sama's head furniture.
...I am an old friend of Genji-san's,
and I am also furniture, just like you.
Although the master I serve is different."
The tense color didn't disappear from Kanon's face in the slightest.
...Depending on the master furniture served, they might be kind or brutal or anything else.
...If this person claimed to be furniture serving the hated Beatrice,
then he must be despicable as well...
contexts.UP:
"This will be the first time I have met you, Kanon‐kun.
......I have been entrusted with the position of Beatrice‐sama's head furniture. My name is Ronove.
......I am an old friend of Genji‐san's.
I am also furniture, just like you.
Although the master I serve is different."
The color of tension didn't disappear from Kanon's expression in the slightest.
......Serving under a different master, furniture could become kind, brutal, or anything else as desired.
...If he called himself furniture serving the hated Beatrice,
then surely he was a despicable being as well...
contexts.note: Both editions restore that furniture can become kind, cruel, or anything else depending on its master, without inventing fraud.

findings.sourceReading: Depending on their master, furniture can become kind, cruel, or behave in any manner.
findings.alternative: 如何様に is read as in any way here, with にでもなる; reading it as fraud confuses that construction with いかさま and adds a specific deception allegation.

findings.description: WH says his reaction differed from what he anticipated and therefore made them laugh.

contexts.japanese:
ベアトリーチェはニコリと、あるいはニヤリと微笑む。
嘉音は乱暴に視線を逸らし、あからさまな不快感を示した。
…その仕草は、彼の思惑とは異なり、魔女とその執事を笑わせた。
contexts.japanesePC: …その仕草は、彼の思惑とは異なり、魔女とその執事を笑わせた。
contexts.japanesePS3:
ベアトリーチェはニコリと、あるいはニヤリと微笑む。
嘉音は乱暴に視線を逸らし、あからさまな不快感を示した。
…その仕草は、彼の思惑とは異なり、魔女とその執事を笑わせた。
contexts.WH: ...His reaction was so different from what he had anticipated that it made the witch and her butler laugh.
contexts.MG:
Beatrice grinned.
Kanon violently averted his gaze, obviously unhappy.
...His reaction was so different from what he wanted to do that it made the witch and her butler laugh.

Kanon violently averted his gaze, obviously disturbed.
...His reaction was so different from what he had obviously intended that it made the witch and her butler laugh.

金蔵の１人に、あといくつを加えたら６人になるのか。……この屋敷で５人という数字は、彼らにとって真っ先に使用人の人数を想起させた…。
MG.translation: Their instincts were good enough to spot her meaning instantly... Six sacrifices were required for the first twilight. After Kinzo, how many more would you need to add up to six? ...In this mansion, the number five instantly made them think of the number of servants here...

勘のいい彼らはすぐに察した…。第一の晩に必要な生贄は６人。

They instinctively figured it out immediately... Six sacrifices were required for the first twilight.

findings.sourceReading: They quickly infer the implication, and five brings to mind the number of servants.

findings.sourceReading: For Kanon, the evil ritual itself is not something he can now do much about; surviving and obtaining his wish matter more.
findings.alternative: 今更どうこう can imply setting a matter aside as no longer relevant, so the English captures a shift of priority. Couldn’t care less nevertheless asserts total emotional indifference, stronger than the source’s pragmatic dismissal and the next sentence’s comparative importance.

findings.description: WH says there had never been anything on Rokkenjima outside the Ushiromiya family. It adds never and substitutes anything for the household occupancy premise.

だから戸締りやその確認には、それほど意味があるわけではない。

MG.japanese:
郷田は、夜の見回りをしていた。そもそも、六軒島には右代宮家以外は存在しない。
だから戸締りやその確認には、それほど意味があるわけではない。しかし、夏妃がそれを無用心だと咎めて以来、夜回りは使用人たちの日課に組み込まれた。
MG.translation: Gohda was doing the nighttime rounds. Rokkenjima had always been empty, except for the Ushiromiya Family household. So, checking that the doors and windows were all closed had no real purpose. However, ever since the time Natsuhi had condemned such an attitude as being careless, the nighttime rounds had become part of the servants' daily routine.

UP.japanese:
郷田は、夜の見回りをしていた。そもそも、六軒島には右代宮家以外は存在しない。
だから戸締りやその確認には、それほど意味があるわけではない。しかし、夏妃がそれを無用心だと咎めて以来、夜回りは使用人たちの日課に組み込まれた。
UP.translation:
Gohda was doing the nighttime rounds. There had never been anything on Rokkenjima outside the Ushiromiya family.
So checking that the doors and windows were all closed had no real purpose. However, ever since Natsuhi had scolded them saying that this was careless, the nighttime rounds had become part of the servants' daily routine.

findings.sourceReading: The Ushiromiya household is the only presence on the island, which makes checking locks seem of limited practical value.
findings.alternative: Outside the family can denote the household, including its servants; the issue is the added unrestricted historical never and broad anything, not a demand to exclude servants.

findings.description: WH supplies people who thought they were alone in the mansion as the circumstance of the ghost stories.

というような話は、自然と起こったものだった。
contexts.japanesePC: だから時折、誰もいないはずの屋敷内に、不気味な音や人影が…、というような話は、自然と起こったものだった。
contexts.japanesePS3:
だから時折、誰もいないはずの屋敷内に、不気味な音や人影が…、
というような話は、自然と起こったものだった。
contexts.WH: Because of that, it was only natural that some people would say that, when they thought they were alone in the mansion..., they would hear a strange sound or see the shadow of a person.

MG.japanese: ……そもそも、夏妃が夜回りを命じたのは、時折起こった、魔女騒動のせいだった。この島に出入りする者なら誰もが知る、森の魔女ベアトリーチェの伝説。それはこの島独自の怪談として根付いていた。だから時折、誰もいないはずの屋敷内に、不気味な音や人影が…、というような話は、自然と起こったものだった。
MG.translation: ...In the first place, Natsuhi had ordered this because of the occasional witch disturbances. Everyone who came and left this island knew about the legend of Beatrice, the witch of the forest. It had become established as this island's characteristic ghost story. Because of that, it was only natural that some people would claim that, when they thought they were alone in the mansion, ...they would hear a strange sound or see the shadow of a person.

UP.japanese: ……そもそも、夏妃が夜回りを命じたのは、時折起こった、魔女騒動のせいだった。この島に出入りする者なら誰もが知る、森の魔女ベアトリーチェの伝説。それはこの島独自の怪談として根付いていた。だから時折、誰もいないはずの屋敷内に、不気味な音や人影が…、というような話は、自然と起こったものだった。
UP.translation: ......The reason that Natsuhi had ordered this was the occasional disturbances of the witch. Everyone who visited this island knew about the legend of Beatrice, the witch of the forest. This had become established as this island's characteristic ghost story. Because of that, it was only natural that some people would occasionally say that, when they thought they were alone in the mansion, ...they had heard strange sounds, or seen the shadow of a person.

findings.sourceReading: Stories arose about eerie sounds or figures inside the mansion where no one was supposed to be.
findings.alternative: A witness can observe an apparently empty part of the mansion while elsewhere inside it; English alone in the mansion instead assigns witnesses a belief about the occupancy of the entire building.

MG.japanese: 郷田は今頃になって、自分が小心者であったことを自覚する。……ならばなぜ、蓋が鳴っていたのかという疑問ももちろん湧いたが、…ちょっとした角度とかの問題、などと抽象的に考え、深くは悩まないことにした。
MG.translation: By now, Gohda realized that he had been a coward. ...So, while he still had some doubts as to what had caused the lid to make that sound, ...he figured it wasn't a big problem, and decided not to worry about it too much.

UP.japanese: 郷田は今頃になって、自分が小心者であったことを自覚する。……ならばなぜ、蓋が鳴っていたのかという疑問ももちろん湧いたが、…ちょっとした角度とかの問題、などと抽象的に考え、深くは悩まないことにした。
UP.translation: By now, Gohda realized that he had been a coward. ......So while he still had some doubts about what had caused the lid to make that sound, ...he explained it away abstractly as some quirk of positioning or something, and decided not to worry about it too much.

findings.sourceReading: He wonders why the lid rattled but vaguely supposes some minor issue with its angle or the like, choosing not to dwell on it.
findings.alternative: The explanation is deliberately vague and is not an established scientific cause; nevertheless the source gives a candidate physical explanation, whereas English gives only reassurance.

findings.description: The sister interprets the unmoving Kumasawa as having resigned herself to her fate; WH instead has the sister announce I’m ready.

おいおい、見つけた見つけた、薔薇庭園だよ。
こいつ、傘も差さずに何をぼんやり？
観念したんだよ、いただきいただき、いっただきぃ！
ノロマなあんたたちはぼんやり見てればいいのよ！

ノロマなあんたたちはぼんやり見てればいいのよ！
contexts.WH: I'm ready, all mine all mine all mi-ne!  You blockheads can just sit there and watch!

But she wasn't in the mansion either, right?

ノロマなあんたたちはぼんやり見てればいいのよ！だから駄目ぇえええぇ、今度は私がもらうのぉおおおおぉおお！！
MG.translation: She's already given up, all mine, all mine, all miiine! You blockheads can just sit there and watch! I told you, nooooooo, this one's miiiiiiiiiiiiine!!

UP.translation:
She's given herself up, all mine all mine all miiine!
You slowpokes can just sit there and watch! I told you, nooooooo, this one's miiiiiiiiiiiiine!!

findings.sourceReading: She has given up / accepted her fate, so I’ll take her.
findings.alternative: 観念した can stand without an expressed subject, but the immediately preceding question about Kumasawa standing motionless establishes the interpreted subject; readiness by the attacker does not convey resignation.

findings.description: The English assigns burst and disappeared to she, after making the golden light passive wrapping.

contexts.japanese:
薔薇の園から一匹二匹と現れた黄金の蝶たちが、次第に熊沢の周りに集まり始める…。
そして黄金の輝きとなって彼女を包んだ後、弾けて消えると、そこには熊沢の姿はなかった。
…代わりにそこにあったのは、………ベアトリーチェにかつて、無限の魔女の道を説き、
生涯でただひとり、師匠と呼んだ、もう一人の黄金の魔女の姿だった。
contexts.japanesePC: そして黄金の輝きとなって彼女を包んだ後、弾けて消えると、そこには熊沢の姿はなかった。
contexts.japanesePS3:
薔薇の園から一匹二匹と現れた黄金の蝶たちが、次第に熊沢の周りに集まり始める…。
そして黄金の輝きとなって彼女を包んだ後、弾けて消えると、そこには熊沢の姿はなかった。
…代わりにそこにあったのは、………ベアトリーチェにかつて、無限の魔女の道を説き、

contexts.WH: Then, after she was wrapped in a golden sparkle, she burst and disappeared, and Kumasawa's form was no longer there.
contexts.MG:
Gold butterflies appeared in ones and twos from the garden of roses and began to gather around Kumasawa...
Then, after she was wrapped in a golden sparkle, she burst and disappeared, and Kumasawa's form was no longer there.
...Instead, there was another Golden Witch, ......the one who once taught the path of an Endless Witch to Beatrice,
and the only person Beatrice ever called Teacher.
contexts.UP:
Gold butterflies appeared in ones and twos from the garden of roses and began to gather around Kumasawa...
And after becoming a golden radiance and enveloping her, they burst and disappeared—and Kumasawa's form was no longer there.
...Instead, there was another Golden Witch, .........the one who had, in the past, explained to Beatrice the path of an Endless Witch,
the only person Beatrice had called Master in her entire life.
contexts.note: MG assigns bursting and disappearing to Kumasawa; UP restores the golden butterflies as the things that envelop, burst, and vanish.

MG.japanese: 薔薇の園から一匹二匹と現れた黄金の蝶たちが、次第に熊沢の周りに集まり始める…。そして黄金の輝きとなって彼女を包んだ後、弾けて消えると、そこには熊沢の姿はなかった。…代わりにそこにあったのは、………ベアトリーチェにかつて、無限の魔女の道を説き、生涯でただひとり、師匠と呼んだ、もう一人の黄金の魔女の姿だった。
MG.translation: Gold butterflies appeared in ones and twos from the garden of roses and began to gather around Kumasawa... Then, after she was wrapped in a golden sparkle, she burst and disappeared, and Kumasawa's form was no longer there. ...Instead, there was another Golden Witch, ......the one who once taught the path of an Endless Witch to Beatrice, and the only person Beatrice ever called Teacher.

UP.japanese: 薔薇の園から一匹二匹と現れた黄金の蝶たちが、次第に熊沢の周りに集まり始める…。そして黄金の輝きとなって彼女を包んだ後、弾けて消えると、そこには熊沢の姿はなかった。…代わりにそこにあったのは、………ベアトリーチェにかつて、無限の魔女の道を説き、生涯でただひとり、師匠と呼んだ、もう一人の黄金の魔女の姿だった。
UP.translation: Gold butterflies appeared in ones and twos from the garden of roses and began to gather around Kumasawa... And after becoming a golden radiance and enveloping her, they burst and disappeared—and Kumasawa's form was no longer there. ...Instead, there was another Golden Witch, .........the one who had, in the past, explained to Beatrice the path of an Endless Witch, the only person Beatrice had called Master in her entire life.

findings.sourceReading: The gathered butterflies become golden radiance, envelop her, and burst/disappear, revealing another form where Kumasawa had stood.
findings.alternative: The Japanese permits omitted subjects, but the preceding butterflies are the agents of becoming light and enveloping her, and the succeeding disappearance of Kumasawa’s form is stated separately. English explicitly makes her the bursting subject.

findings.sourceReading: All the guilt belongs to the master, including what the furniture does in her service.
findings.alternative: Her crimes can be understood broadly as crimes perpetrated under her authority, especially after the furniture clause; nevertheless the explicit Japanese universal burden is replaced with a possessive restriction.

findings.description: WH replaces the conditional 粗相があるようならば with It seems there has been a mistake, so and turns the resulting threat into a request.

箒星の訪れよりも久しい再会です。
もてなしてもらいましょうか。
………粗相があるようならば、我が名と無限の魔女の称号。
……返してもらいますよ？」
contexts.japanesePC: ………粗相があるようならば、我が名と無限の魔女の称号。……返してもらいますよ？」

「そうですね。

もてなしてもらいましょうか。
………粗相があるようならば、我が名と無限の魔女の称号。
……返してもらいますよ？」
contexts.WH: .........It seems there has been a mistake, ......so will you give back my name and the title of Endless Witch?"
contexts.MG:
"Let's see.

Perhaps I will accept your hospitality.
......And if it seems a mistake has been made,

contexts.note: Both editions restore a conditional threat: if Beatrice commits a blunder, the teacher will take back her name and title.

findings.sourceReading: If there is any lapse in your hospitality/performance, I will have you return my name and the title of Endless Witch.
findings.alternative: The teacher has already condemned Beatrice’s conduct, but this clause explicitly sets a condition in the hospitality challenge; the following license-renewal joke confirms the prospective examination framing.

"Come on, Eva.

...The library was next to the servant room.
Father always owned a vast book collection,
but ever since he started to become engrossed with his occult hobby, that collection grew even larger,
so that the normal books suitable for a normal study had been forced out as his study overflowed.
This so-called library was mostly used as a storage room for those normal books.
They were all thick, like complete encyclopedias for intellectuals,
but that was very convenient for me, now that I was investigating something.

contexts.japanese:
天井の高さはたっぷりあったため、息苦しさはない。
むしろ、冷たい風が吹き上げてくるような気がして、その不気味さに霊気さえ感じた…。
銃を構え、慎重に先をうかがいながら、……私は階段を下りていく……。
壁や階段、灯りは皆、かなり古臭い。
…この島に屋敷が建てられた当時に作られたものなのは、疑いようもないかもしれない。
天井にはひびが入り、雨水が壁を伝って、さらさらと流れ落ちている。
その水は階段脇に設けられた側溝に落ちて、地下の闇へ静かに早く流れていく。
早く先へ進めと私を急かすかのようだった…。
階段は何度か折り返した。
どの程度を降りたかわからないが、地下１階よりはもっと深く降りたと思う。
するとやがて、…………無骨な金属製の扉が姿を現した。

contexts.MG:

On the contrary, it felt as though a cool breeze was blowing upwards, and that creepiness seemed to form a sort of aura...
As I readied my gun and carefully stared forwards, ...I descended the stairs...
The walls, the stairs, the lights...all of them were very old-fashioned.
...It was easy to suspect that this had been built back when the mansion had been constructed on this island.
There were cracks in the ceiling, and water clung to the walls, constantly dripping down.
That water fell into a gutter that had been set up alongside the stairs, then quickly and silently flowed into the underground darkness.
As though it was telling me to go faster...
The staircase kept turning back on itself.
I don't know how far down I've gone, but I think it's much deeper than one floor.
Eventually, ......a rough, metal door showed itself.

...no, timidly kept my gun raised, and searched the interior.
And......in the center of the room, I found it.
"...............Eee—..............."
My gasp came out strangely, as though a bunny was being choked.
...I mean, ......after finding something like this,
...no one would have any words other than that stupid voice...
"It's here......
......I‐......it's really here.........
......Father's......gold......!!"
On the opposite side of the canopy bed, it was piled up in a massive heap...
contexts.note: MG restores the gold being farther inside at the back of the room; UP retains “in the center.”

MG.japanese: 私はそんな部屋に度肝を抜かれながらも、慎重に、…いや、臆病に銃を構えながら室内を探るのだった。そして、……部屋の奥に、それを見つける。
MG.translation: Even though I was completely shocked by this room, I carefully... no, timidly searched the interior with my gun raised. And, ...at the back of the room, I found it.

UP.japanese: 私はそんな部屋に度肝を抜かれながらも、慎重に、…いや、臆病に銃を構えながら室内を探るのだった。そして、……部屋の奥に、それを見つける。
UP.translation: Although I was dumbfounded by this room, I cautiously, ...no, timidly kept my gun raised, and searched the interior. And......in the center of the room, I found it.

findings.sourceReading: And in the rear of the room she finds it.
findings.alternative: 奥 can mean the inner portion rather than a precisely measured back wall, but does not specify the center. Later bed-relative description may restore placement.

おめでとう、私。
おめでとう、右代宮絵羽。
…私たちの悲しい半生は、今ここに全ての念願が叶って昇華されたわ。
「あなたのお陰よ…。
あなたの魔法があったから、このチャンスに恵まれた。

だから、私の魔法の力だけじゃない。
私たちの勝利よ。
だからこそ、おめでとう。
“私たち”。
「ありがとう、私…。
ありがとう、右代宮絵羽…。
……今日まで挫けなくて良かった。
悲しみに溺れ、足掻くことを忘れなくて良かった…」

contexts.japanese:
俺はそれを遠目に見ながら、
少しだけ照れたような表情で笑みを浮かべている新生ベアトリーチェを見る。
……初めは戸惑っていた彼女の表情には、
ようやく自覚できてきた喜びが溢れているようだった。
その表情には、黄金を前に惑乱した笑い声を上げたような凶気は一切ない。
ただただ、喜びを噛み締める初々しさがあるだけだった。

……しかし、あの無邪気な笑顔を見ていると、
…今だけは祝福したいような、そんな気持ちにさせられる。

contexts.WH: Since I denied witches, I couldn't put on a joyful expression at this witch succession ceremony and accept her...
contexts.MG:
As I stared from the distance,
I looked at the newly born Beatrice, who had a slightly embarrassed smile on her face.
...Her expression, which had been lost and confused at first,
seemed to be full of the happiness that she was finally starting to recognize.
That expression didn't look at all like someone laughing insanely while standing before the gold.
There was just the innocence of a person basking in their own joy.
As a person who denied the existence of witches, I couldn't view this witch succession ceremony with a joyful expression and accept her...
...However, when I looked at that innocent smile,
I felt like I wanted to offer my blessings, just for that moment.
contexts.UP:
As I stared from the distance,
I looked at the Beatrice given new life, who had a slightly embarrassed smile on her face.
......Her expression, which had been hesitant at first,
seemed to be full of a happiness that she had finally become aware of.
In that expression, there wasn't a trace of the madness that had led her to that insane laugh before the gold.
There was only the innocence of relishing her joy.
Since I deny witches, I couldn't accept her as she showed that joyful expression at her witch succession ceremony...
......However, as I watched that innocent smile,
...it made me feel like I wanted to celebrate her, just for now.
contexts.note: MG makes the joyful expression belong to Battler viewing the ceremony; UP restores it as Eva’s expression that he cannot accept.

findings.description: WH omits the corridor destination and changes a movement out into it to running around the second floor.

contexts.japanese:
するとその時、２階で、どたどたどたっという慌しい足音が聞こえた。
ゲストハウスは安っぽい建物ではないので、普通の足音なら聞こえるわけもない。
踵で地団太を踏むような、そんな音だった。
すると間髪入れずに、２階廊下へ走り出たらしい音と、
真里亞のうーうーうーと連呼する不機嫌そうな声が聞こえてきた。
楼座は髪を振り乱しながら頭を抱え、声なき声で苦悶の唸りをあげる…。
大人たちはその仕草にさりげなく背を向け、気付かぬフリをしてやるのだった。
ドタドタドタと賑やかな音が２階から降りてきてロビーに飛び込んでくる。
泣きじゃくる真里亞と、それに付いてきた子どもたち、そして南條だった。
…つまり、真里亞の大騒ぎのせいで、２階の全員が降りてきてしまったというわけだ。

contexts.WH: And in a flash, in addition to the sound which seemed to be caused by her running around the second floor, they could hear Maria calling uu-uu-uu- over and over again, sounding displeased.
contexts.MG:
At that moment, they heard the sound of wild footsteps coming from the second floor.
The guesthouse wasn't a cheap building, so they wouldn't normally have heard the sound of footsteps.
It was like the sound of someone stamping their feet in frustration.
And an instant later, accompanied by what seemed to be the sound of her running out into the second floor hallway,
they could hear Maria calling uu-uu-uu- over and over again, sounding displeased.
Rosa grabbed her head, her hair flying, and she voicelessly moaned in anguish...
The adults conscientiously turned their backs to her, pretending not to notice.
The noisy clamor came down from the second floor and flew into the lobby.
It was Maria, who was sobbing, along with the other children and Nanjo.
...In other words, they had all come downstairs because of Maria's tantrum.

they could hear Maria calling "uu‐uu‐uu" over and over again, sounding displeased.
Rosa grabbed her head, ruffled up her hair, and voicelessly moaned in anguish...
The adults conscientiously turned their backs to her, pretending not to notice.

contexts.japanese:
楼座たちが表に出た時に比べると、再び風は強くなっていた。
留弗夫たち３人は、傘をささず、銃や折り畳んだ台車を抱え、小走りに薔薇庭園を駆け抜けていく。
もしも雨も風の音もしない静寂だったなら、３人は耳を澄まし慎重に行動したかもしれない。
しかしこの雨では、近くに不審者が潜んでいたとしても、その気配を気取ることは困難だ。
それならばむしろ、危険地帯を駆け抜けた方が良いだろうという留弗夫の提案だった。
……相手が銃で武装している可能性があるならば、
固まってゆっくり歩くのは的にしてくれと言っているようなものだ。
迅速な行動はおそらく正しい判断だろう。

contexts.MG:
Compared to the time Rosa and Maria had gone outside, the winds were much stronger.
Rudolf's group of three people jogged through the rose garden without umbrellas, holding their guns and a folded cart.
If everything had been still and quiet, without the wind and the rain, they would probably have kept their ears open and moved with caution.
But in this rain, even if some suspicious person was hiding nearby, it would be difficult to notice them.
Because of that, it had been Rudolf's plan to instead dash through the dangerous area.
...If there was a chance that their opponent was equipped with a gun,
then walking slowly with their guard up would only make them targets.
Taking swift action was probably the correct choice.

Compared to the time Rosa and Maria had gone outside, the winds had picked up once again.
Rudolf's group of three people jogged through the rose garden without umbrellas, holding their guns and a folded cart.
If everything had been still and quiet, without the wind and the rain, they would probably have kept their ears open and moved with caution.
But in this rain, even if some suspicious person was hiding nearby, it would be difficult to notice them.
Because of that, it had been Rudolf's plan to instead dash through the dangerous area.
......If there was a chance that their opponent was equipped with a gun,
then walking slowly with their guard up would only make them a target.
It was probably correct to decide on swift action.

彼女の暴論は、無限の魔女としては極めて正論。

findings.description: WH says the furniture gloomily bore the brunt of her dissatisfaction, rather than that she found the restraining furniture annoying and her own dissatisfaction peaked.

contexts.japanese:
魔女の表情が邪悪な笑みで歪む。
その表情を恐れながらも、ルシファーが現れて進言する。
「お、…恐れながらっ。
…先代さまよりそのような残酷行為は慎むようにと…、」
魔女がぎょろりと恐ろしい目で睨みつけると、ルシファーは閉口する。
…不満なのだ。
自らの持つ力と、自らの持つ残酷さを存分に解放できないことが退屈なのだ。
……それを自重しろという先代の家具は鬱陶しく、彼女の不満は頂点だった。
contexts.japanesePC: ……それを自重しろという先代の家具は鬱陶しく、彼女の不満は頂点だった。
contexts.japanesePS3:
魔女の表情が邪悪な笑みで歪む。
その表情を恐れながらも、ルシファーが現れて進言する。
「お、…恐れながらっ。
…先代さまよりそのような残酷行為は慎むようにと…、」
魔女がぎょろりと恐ろしい目で睨みつけると、ルシファーは閉口する。
…不満なのだ。
自らの持つ力と、自らの持つ残酷さを存分に解放できないことが退屈なのだ。
……それを自重しろという先代の家具は鬱陶しく、彼女の不満は頂点だった。
contexts.WH: ......And this furniture of the predecessor, who was telling her to act with prudence, gloomily bore the brunt of her dissatisfaction.
contexts.MG:
The witch's expression twisted into an evil smile.
Even though she feared that expression, Lucifer appeared and spoke.
"F-Forgive my presumption,
...but the Predecessor-sama asked that you avoid brutal actions of that sort..."
When the witch stared at her with those terrifying eyes, Lucifer was struck dumb.
...She was frustrated.
It was so boring, not being able to let her own power and cruelty run wild.
...This annoying furniture of the Predecessor kept telling her to show restraint, bringing her irritation to a peak.
contexts.UP:
The witch's expression twisted with an evil smile.
Even though she feared that expression, Lucifer appeared and spoke.
"M‐...my apologies.
...The Predecessor said to avoid brutal actions of that—"
When the witch stared at her with those terrifying eyes, Lucifer was struck dumb.
...She was unsatisfied.
She was bored, of not being able to let her own power and her own cruelty run wild.
......Irritated by her predecessor's furniture telling her to act with restraint, her discontent was at its peak.
contexts.note: Both restore the witch’s irritation with the restraining furniture and her own discontent reaching a peak.

MG.japanese: …不満なのだ。自らの持つ力と、自らの持つ残酷さを存分に解放できないことが退屈なのだ。……それを自重しろという先代の家具は鬱陶しく、彼女の不満は頂点だった。
MG.translation: ...She was frustrated. It was so boring, not being able to let her own power and cruelty run wild. ...This annoying furniture of the Predecessor kept telling her to show restraint, bringing her irritation to a peak.

UP.translation: ...She was unsatisfied. She was bored, of not being able to let her own power and her own cruelty run wild. ......Irritated by her predecessor's furniture telling her to act with restraint, her discontent was at its peak.

findings.sourceReading: The predecessor’s furniture telling her to restrain herself was irritating, and her dissatisfaction reached its height.
findings.alternative: Her glare silences Lucifer and supports the idea of bearing the brunt, but this sentence assigns annoyance and culmination to the witch, not gloom to the furniture.

UP.translation: "That's right. I am me in my youth, who was always living in the heart of your wife, Ushiromiya Eva. ...And I'm a witch. .........Eva became an adult by forgetting me. So she can't use magic."

findings.sourceReading: She is the girlhood version of Eva who lived within his wife’s heart.
findings.alternative: The intended younger-self meaning is recoverable, but youthful me or girlhood self would be grammatical.

目を覚まさんかい、このアホンダラが…ッ！！」

findings.description: Jessica’s statement about every form of separation becomes a statement about how one says farewell.

「……別れはどんな形でも、いつも悲しいさ」
「…でもそれが、例えば老いであるとか、何かの時間であるとか、
…予め約束されていて、いつか訪れる別れであるとわかっているものは、
…その悲しみを、長い時間を掛けて予め薄めておくことができる。
……それを許されないから、…突然の不幸は、悲しいんだろうよ…」
contexts.japanesePC: 「……別れはどんな形でも、いつも悲しいさ。

「……別れはどんな形でも、いつも悲しいさ」

…予め約束されていて、いつか訪れる別れであるとわかっているものは、

contexts.WH: "......No matter how you say your farewell, it's always sad.
contexts.MG:
His question probably hadn't been directed at anyone, but Jessica answered.
"...It's always sad when you have to say goodbye.
...But when the person's old or there's some time,
...when you know beforehand that it's coming, sooner or later,
that sadness gets spread out over a long period of time.
...When misfortune comes suddenly, it's sad...because you don't even get that time..."
contexts.UP:
He probably hadn't been asking anyone, but Jessica answered.
"......Partings are always sad, no matter what they're like."
"...But, when, for example, the person is old, or there's some time it's going to happen,
...when it's expected in advance, and you know it's a farewell that must come sooner or later,
...you can spend a long time softening the blow of that sadness.
......Sudden misfortune is probably sad...because you aren't allowed even that..."
contexts.note: MG retains saying goodbye rather than every form of separation; UP restores partings no matter their form.

頭の中で、死者を蘇らすいくつかの魔法的手段を思案する。
……かつては容易に出来たはずの魔法も、今の魔力では難しくなっている。
思いついては舌を打つ、を数度繰り返す。
その末、……ようやく、ひとつの魔法を思いつく。
しかしそれは、彼女ひとりでは使えない魔法。
力の弱い魔女が使う、他者の助けを借りる魔法だ。
…かつて、ベアトはそういう類の魔法を見下していた。
なので、それ以外に可能な魔法はないのかと、必死に思案してみたのだが、
………結局、思いつかず、肩を落として自嘲する。

contexts.WH: Inside her head, she thought about several magical steps she could take to revive the dead.
contexts.MG:
Inside her head, she thought about several magical steps she could take to revive the dead.
...Even magic that should have been easy in the past would be difficult with her current power.
She thought of something, then clicked her tongue, then did so again, over and over.
In the end, ...she finally thought of a single spell.
But that was a spell that she couldn't use by herself.
It was a spell that witches with weak power used, one that relied on the aid of others.
...In the past, Beato had looked down upon that type of magic.
Therefore, she frantically tried to search for any conceivable alternative,
......but in the end, she couldn't think of one and slumped over in self-derision.
contexts.UP:
Inside her head, she thought about several magical methods for reviving the dead.
......Even magic that she could do easily in the past would be difficult with her current magic power.
She thought of something, then clicked her tongue, and repeated this several times.
In the end, ......she finally thought of a single spell.
But that was a spell that she couldn't use by herself.
It was a spell that witches with weak power used, that relied on the aid of others.
...In the past, Beato had looked down upon that type of magic.
Therefore, she frantically tried to think if there wasn't any other possible spell,
.........but in the end, she couldn't think of one, and slumped over in self‐derision.
contexts.note: MG retains magical steps rather than alternatives; UP restores several methods and the search for an alternative.

MG.japanese: 頭の中で、死者を蘇らすいくつかの魔法的手段を思案する。……かつては容易に出来たはずの魔法も、今の魔力では難しくなっている。思いついては舌を打つ、を数度繰り返す。
MG.translation: Inside her head, she thought about several magical steps she could take to revive the dead. ...Even magic that should have been easy in the past would be difficult with her current power. She thought of something, then clicked her tongue, then did so again, over and over.

UP.japanese: 頭の中で、死者を蘇らすいくつかの魔法的手段を思案する。……かつては容易に出来たはずの魔法も、今の魔力では難しくなっている。思いついては舌を打つ、を数度繰り返す。
UP.translation: Inside her head, she thought about several magical methods for reviving the dead. ......Even magic that she could do easily in the past would be difficult with her current magic power. She thought of something, then clicked her tongue, and repeated this several times.

findings.sourceReading: いくつかの魔法的手段 refers to alternative means, rejected one by one before she chooses one spell.
findings.alternative: Steps could loosely mean actions she might take, but commonly implies components of a procedure rather than competing options.

findings.description: WH makes his feelings change into magic and retrieve Shannon’s soul, where Beato says George can convert those feelings and bring her back.

contexts.japanese:
「…だが、今の妾にはその隙間より紗音の魂を連れ出せるほどの力はない。
………しかし、紗音のことを強く想うそなたなら、
その想いを魔力に変えて、彼女の魂を必ずや連れ戻せるだろう」
「……どうだ。
妾を手伝うか…？」
contexts.japanesePC: …だが、今の妾にはその隙間より紗音の魂を連れ出せるほどの力はない。………しかし、紗音のことを強く想うそなたなら、その想いを魔力に変えて、彼女の魂を必ずや連れ戻せるだろう。

その想いを魔力に変えて、彼女の魂を必ずや連れ戻せるだろう」
「……どうだ。
妾を手伝うか…？」
contexts.WH: ...But as I am now, I do not have the power to bring Shannon's soul up through that gap.  .........However, if it were you, who has strong feelings for Shannon, those feelings should change into magic and bring her soul out without fail.
contexts.MG:
"...But as I am now, I do not have the power to bring Shannon's soul up through that gap.
......However, you have strong feelings for Shannon,
and those feelings will surely become magic that can bring her soul out without fail."
"...What do you say?
Will you help me...?"

"...But as I am now, I do not have the power to bring Shannon's soul up through that gap.
.........However, if it were you, who has strong feelings for Shannon,
you should be able to change those feelings into magic, and bring her soul out without fail."
"......What do you say?
Will you help me...?"
contexts.note: MG makes the feelings themselves become retrieving magic; UP restores George converting those feelings and bringing back the soul.

MG.translation: "...But as I am now, I do not have the power to bring Shannon's soul up through that gap. ......However, you have strong feelings for Shannon, and those feelings will surely become magic that can bring her soul out without fail."

UP.japanese: 「…だが、今の妾にはその隙間より紗音の魂を連れ出せるほどの力はない。………しかし、紗音のことを強く想うそなたなら、その想いを魔力に変えて、彼女の魂を必ずや連れ戻せるだろう」
UP.translation: "...But as I am now, I do not have the power to bring Shannon's soul up through that gap. .........However, if it were you, who has strong feelings for Shannon, you should be able to change those feelings into magic, and bring her soul out without fail."

findings.sourceReading: そなたなら、その想いを魔力に変えて…連れ戻せる assigns conversion and retrieval to George.
findings.alternative: The immediately following request for his help preserves his necessary participation; autonomous feelings may be figurative shorthand. The explicit procedure nevertheless loses his agency.

contexts.japanese:
……そして黄金の煙管で、鎧戸が閉ざす窓を軽く叩いた。

そして音もなく窓をすうっと開いた。
その向こうの鎧戸もまったく同じ。
留め金が、同じく音もなく外れて、すぅっと静かに開いた。

そのせいで譲治は、しばらくの間、
外への入り口が開かれたことを夢か幻のように感じてしまい、実感することができなかった。

contexts.japanese:

UP.japanese: 譲治の、想い人の死を悲しむ力は、……それまでの彼の一生懸命だった人生と、紗音との温かな時間、そして将来を誓い合った夢の大きさから生まれるのだ。
UP.translation: George's power to feel sorrow for the death of his loved one......arose from the way he had tried his hardest throughout his life, from the warm time spent together with Shannon, and from the size of their shared dream, promising each other their futures.

findings.sourceReading: 譲治の…死を悲しむ力は…人生と…時間、そして…夢の大きさから生まれる gives the lived experiences and promised future as origins of his grief’s power.
findings.alternative: The prior sentence supplies power as an antecedent and the broad interpretation remains close, but adding sadness as a separate cause breaks the explicit explanation of where sadness itself derives its strength.

findings.description: WH drops こともある from Beato’s question about witches being inferior to humans.

contexts.japanese:

……死の山さえ越えられぬ有限のニンゲンに、劣ることもあるというのか……」
魔女は、今こそ認める。
命の価値を理解できない魔女には宿せない魔力を、彼は持ち得ている。

命の価値を理解できない魔女には宿せない魔力を、彼は持ち得ている。
contexts.WH: ".........Is an Endless Witch, who can do as she wants even with life and death, ......inferior to a limited human who can't even surpass the mountain of death......?"

inferior to a limited Human who can't even surpass the mountain of death...?"

......is inferior to a finite Humanhuman, for whom even death's mountain is impossible to cross......?"
Now, the witch acknowledged it.
He was able to hold a magical power that could not reside in witches who didn't understand the value of a life.
contexts.note: MG retains general inferiority; UP restores there are times when.

MG.japanese: 「………生死すら自在にする無限の魔女が、……死の山さえ越えられぬ有限のニンゲンに、劣ることもあるというのか……」

findings.description: The vase’s beauty makes the child unable to suppress a sigh; WH says it forced a deep breath.

contexts.japanese:
それは、とてもとても美しくて、価値と歴史のある素晴らしい壷でした。
幼い私が見ても、その美しさにため息が堪えられないほどに。
……でも、だから触れてみたかったのです。
contexts.japanesePC:
幼い私が見ても、その美しさにため息が堪えられないほどに。
……でも、だから触れてみたかったのです。

幼い私が見ても、その美しさにため息が堪えられないほどに。

MG.japanese: それは、とてもとても美しくて、価値と歴史のある素晴らしい壷でした。幼い私が見ても、その美しさにため息が堪えられないほどに。……でも、だから触れてみたかったのです。
MG.translation: The vase was very beautiful, rich with history and value. Even as young as I was, it still forced me to take a deep breath when I witnessed its beauty. ...But that just made me want to touch it.

UP.translation: The vase was very, very beautiful, rich with history and value. Even as young as I was, it still forced me to take a deep breath when I witnessed its beauty. ......But that just made me want to touch it.

findings.sourceReading: ため息が堪えられない conveys involuntary sighing at beauty, followed by the wish to touch.
findings.alternative: A deep breath can accompany wonder, but is a different gesture from a sigh and loses the inability to contain it.

findings.description: WH says Grandfather and those who saw his grief cried, where the child anticipates that they will surely cry.

contexts.japanese:
お祖父さまも、大切な壷が失われたことを、きっと泣くでしょう。
それを見て、お祖父さまを大切に思う人たちもみんな、きっと泣くでしょう。
たったひとつの命が失われただけで、世界中はこんなにも悲しみに染まるのです。
……その恐ろしさに、私はさらに泣きました。
contexts.japanesePC:
お祖父さまも、大切な壷が失われたことを、きっと泣くでしょう。

それを見て、お祖父さまを大切に思う人たちもみんな、きっと泣くでしょう。
たったひとつの命が失われただけで、世界中はこんなにも悲しみに染まるのです。
……その恐ろしさに、私はさらに泣きました。
contexts.WH:
I'm sure that Grandfather also cried at the loss of his precious vase.
I'm sure that all of the people who valued Grandfather and saw him like that cried.
contexts.MG:
I'm sure Grandfather will also cry at the loss of his precious vase.
I'm sure that all the people who love Grandfather and see him like that will cry.
With the loss of a single life, the whole world can be filled with so much sadness.
...I cried even more at how terrible that was.
contexts.UP:
I was sure that Grandfather would also cry at the loss of his precious vase.
I was sure that all of the people who thought fondly of Grandfather would cry too, when they saw him like that.
By just the loss of a single life, the whole world would be filled with so much sadness.
......I cried even more at how terrible that would be.
contexts.note: Both restore anticipated crying, using future will or remembered would rather than completed crying.

MG.japanese: お祖父さまも、大切な壷が失われたことを、きっと泣くでしょう。それを見て、お祖父さまを大切に思う人たちもみんな、きっと泣くでしょう。たったひとつの命が失われただけで、世界中はこんなにも悲しみに染まるのです。……その恐ろしさに、私はさらに泣きました。
MG.translation: I'm sure Grandfather will also cry at the loss of his precious vase. I'm sure that all the people who love Grandfather and see him like that will cry. With the loss of a single life, the whole world can be filled with so much sadness. ...I cried even more at how terrible that was.

UP.japanese: お祖父さまも、大切な壷が失われたことを、きっと泣くでしょう。それを見て、お祖父さまを大切に思う人たちもみんな、きっと泣くでしょう。たったひとつの命が失われただけで、世界中はこんなにも悲しみに染まるのです。……その恐ろしさに、私はさらに泣きました。
UP.translation: I was sure that Grandfather would also cry at the loss of his precious vase. I was sure that all of the people who thought fondly of Grandfather would cry too, when they saw him like that. By just the loss of a single life, the whole world would be filled with so much sadness. ......I cried even more at how terrible that would be.

findings.sourceReading: きっと泣くでしょう projects the consequences of the broken vase, with others expected to cry upon seeing Grandfather grieve.
findings.alternative: A recollection can report past events with uncertainty, but the source’s local progression describes imagined future grief before the restoring intervention rather than reporting that it occurred.

………次第に、輝きを取り戻していく。
そして、………その瞳が動き、…譲治の姿を認める。

…幸い、朱志香は立ち上がってくれた。
悲しみに一区切りがついたのだろう。
……しかし、代わりに浮かべている形相はまるで鬼のそれだ。
「…私がこの手でぶっ殺して、……必ず仇を取ってやる………。

悪ぃが早い者勝ちだぜ」
「…あぁ、…そうだな…。
……ぶっ殺してやろうぜッ！」
俺の言葉に、ようやく朱志香は自らの気持ちを共感してもらえたことを感じたのだろう。
物騒な表情ではあるが、少しだけ朱志香が正気に戻るのを感じた。

findings.description: WH turns Battler’s approximate hourly victim rate into they probably were not killed with the speed of a single person.

contexts.japanese:

…そりゃあもうすげぇ勢いでだ。

…それこそ、時速１人くらいのスピードで殺されてるんじゃねぇだろうか。

……それまで、まだ１２時間以上もたっぷりあるんだぞ。
…あと、魔女の生贄が何人いてくれりゃ、俺たちは生き残れるってんだ…。
俺たち４人じゃ、１時間に１人で、…４時間しかもたない。
今夜の２４時だって、もはや迎えられるかわからないのだ…。

Jessica was rolling around on the floor, covering both her eyes.
Auntie Eva and Doctor Nanjo were looking down at her, shocked...
"A‐are you alright, Jessica‐san...?!
Jessica‐san...!!"
"UuuAaaaAAAaaaaHHHaHHHhhh,
oww, owwww, ow...
uuuaa{0a{0a{0a{0a{0a{0a{0a{0a{0a{0a{0a{0a{0a{0aaggghhh...!"
"I‐......it isn't my fault...
Th‐......this happened because you came at me even after I told you to stop...!"
"H‐...hey, hey, what the hell happened, what's going on...?!"
Jessica had grabbed at Auntie Eva, and it had turned into a scuffle...
They had then...started fighting over the gun Auntie Eva had been holding?
And some movement or other caused the trigger to be pulled...?
I didn't know the details, about whether the bullet had grazed her, or whether she had been burned by the discharge,
but whatever the case, Jessica was covering both of her eyes, screaming in pain, and rolling around on the floor.

南條は応急手当を行ない、患部をガーゼで覆って包帯で巻いた。

傷が痛んだり疼いたりするでしょうが、絶対に掻いたり揉んだりしてはなりませんぞ。
明日になったらすぐに、眼科の先生のところへ行きましょう」

contexts.MG:

自然と睨みつけるような仕草になり、目を圧迫するため、傷を痛ませた。
朱志香もその内、喋れば喋るほど傷が痛むことに気付き、
絵羽への疑いを解いたかどうかは別にして、とりあえず落ち着きを取り戻すのだった…。

contexts.WH: So for now, Jessica-san, you should devote yourself to resting your body and keeping your eyes safe.  ...Of course, if you wrinkle your forehead too much, it will do nothing good for the beauty of your eyes."
contexts.MG:
"So for now, Jessica-san, you should devote yourself to resting your body and keeping your eyes safe.
...Of course, if you wrinkle your forehead too much, it will do nothing good for your eyes, not to mention your beauty."
When Jessica's abuse of Eva had reached a crescendo,
she actually had started glaring instinctively, and the pressure on her eyes had hurt her.
Jessica herself realized that the more she talked, the more the wound would hurt,
and regardless of whether she'd overcome her suspicions of Eva, she regained her composure for the time being...

Indeed, when Jessica had grown agitated in her verbal abuse of Eva,
she had naturally started glaring, and the pressure on her eyes hurt her.
Jessica herself soon realized that the more she talked, the more the wound would hurt,
and regardless of whether she had overcome her suspicions of Eva, she regained her composure for the time being...
contexts.note: Both separately identify harm to the eyes and to appearance rather than beauty of the eyes.

MG.translation: Jessica was now less fearful about the fact that she was blinded, and more frightened that the police would carry Kanon's body away while she still couldn't see, and that she would have to say her final farewell without being able to look at his face.

UP.japanese: 今の朱志香には、失明するかもしれない恐れよりも、目が見えない内に嘉音の死体が警察に運び出され、その顔を見ることもできず、お別れすることになるかもしれない方を恐れていた。
UP.translation: Jessica was now less fearful about the fact that she might go blind, and more frightened that the police would carry Kanon's corpse away while she still couldn't see, and that she would have to say her final farewell without being able to see his face.

findings.sourceReading: 失明するかもしれない恐れ contrasts possible blindness with the more pressing fear of never seeing Kanon’s face before removal of his body.
findings.alternative: She currently cannot see and the bandages completely block vision, but possible loss of sight is distinct from that present obstruction; the source maintains prognostic uncertainty.

findings.sourceReading: たった今、生命を脅かされている is an ongoing present threat inferred from his frightened voice.
findings.alternative: Must have been can be an inference about the immediately present situation, but just a second ago explicitly moves its temporal reference backwards.

findings.description: WH substitutes a candy jar and candy for things like confectionery tins and bottles stacked on the shelf.

contexts.japanese:
何とか逃れようと、手探りで辺りを探る。
しかし、よく知るはずの部屋は、目が見えなくなっただけで、暗黒の密室も同然だ。
棚か何かにぶつかってしまい、その上に積んであった菓子缶や瓶のようなものが降ってきて、彼女の頭にぶつかる。
…今の彼女には、それを防ぐために頭を守ることすらおぼつかない。
…視界を失うだけで、人はここまで無力なのかと痛感する。
もちろん、そんなことに感心している暇はない。
彼女はとにかく這い回って、その場を逃げ出そうとするのだが、
よくわからないモノに次々にぶつかり、色々なモノが降ってきてはぶつかって、
まるで部屋全体が生きていて、彼女を逃がすまいと意地悪をしているように感じるのだった。

まるで部屋全体が生きていて、彼女を逃がすまいと意地悪をしているように感じるのだった。
contexts.WH: She ran into a shelf or something, and something like a candy jar and candy fell down, hitting her on the head.
contexts.MG:
She searched around with her hands, trying to find some way to escape.
But even though she should have known this room well, just being unable to see made it like a closed room of darkness.
She ran into a shelf or something, and things like a candy jars and bottles fell down, hitting her on the head.
...As she was now, it would've been tough for her to even guard her head to block it.
...She was painfully aware of how powerless humans become just by losing their sense of sight.
Of course, she had no time to be impressed by this fact.
She crawled around at random, trying to escape from that place,
but she kept bumping into things that she didn't understand, getting hit by various falling objects,
and it felt like the entire room was alive, bullying her and refusing to let her escape.
contexts.UP:
She searched around with her hands, trying to find some way to escape.
But even though she knew this room well, just being unable to see made it like a locked room of darkness.
She bumped into some shelves or something, and some tins of sweets and bottles and things fell down from them, hitting her on the head.
...As she was now, even protecting her head to block them wasn't working out.
...She was becoming painfully aware of how very powerless humans become just by losing their sense of sight.
Of course, she had no time to appreciate that.
She crawled around, as best as she could, trying to escape that place,
but she kept bumping into things that she didn't understand, getting hit by various falling objects,
and it felt to her like the entire room was alive, bullying her and refusing to let her escape.
contexts.note: MG restores bottles and removes loose candy but retains jars rather than confectionery tins. UP restores tins of sweets and bottles.

She ran into a shelf or something, and things like a candy jars and bottles fell down, hitting her on the head.

findings.sourceReading: 菓子缶や瓶のようなもの names hard containers falling and striking her head, with uncertainty about precise objects.
findings.alternative: A jar is a type of bottle-like container and may contain candy, but the second falling item candy replaces the separately specified tin or bottle-like objects.

findings.description: WH has the successor poke the heart with a fingernail rather than nudge it with her toe.

contexts.japanese: 残酷なる魔女は、爪先でベアトリーチェの心臓を小突く。
contexts.japanesePC: 残酷なる魔女は、爪先でベアトリーチェの心臓を小突く。
contexts.japanesePS3: 残酷なる魔女は、爪先でベアトリーチェの心臓を小突く。
contexts.WH: The cruel witch poked Beatrice's heart with her fingernail.
contexts.MG: The cruel witch poked Beatrice's heart with her fingernail.
contexts.UP: The merciless witch poked Beatrice's heart with her fingernail.
contexts.note: Both retain fingernail instead of toe.

MG.japanese:
残酷なる魔女は、爪先でベアトリーチェの心臓を小突く。ベアトリーチェはその挑発に返す言葉など何もない。……だが、…言葉の代わりに、表情をひとつ返した。
……それは、残酷なる魔女にとってのみ屈辱的に見えた。口を緩やかに曲げて、……笑っていたからだ。
MG.translation: The cruel witch poked Beatrice's heart with her fingernail. Beatrice had no words with which to respond to that provocation. ...However, ...instead of words, she returned a single expression. ...It felt humiliating only to the cruel witch. Because she had gently curved her mouth...and smiled.

UP.japanese:
残酷なる魔女は、爪先でベアトリーチェの心臓を小突く。ベアトリーチェはその挑発に返す言葉など何もない。……だが、…言葉の代わりに、表情をひとつ返した。
……それは、残酷なる魔女にとってのみ屈辱的に見えた。口を緩やかに曲げて、……笑っていたからだ。
UP.translation:
The merciless witch poked Beatrice's heart with her fingernail. Beatrice had no words with which to respond to that provocation. ......However, ...instead of words, she returned a single expression.
......It looked insulting only to the cruel witch. Because she had gently curved her mouth, ......and smiled.

findings.sourceReading: 爪先 is the toe or tip of the foot; 小突く describes nudging the fallen heart.
findings.alternative: The word contains 爪, but the compound denotes the foot tip and the floor-level heart makes the action coherent.

findings.description: WH says when that was blocked by resistance where Japanese describes trying to stop the warhead with resistance.

contexts.japanese:
黄金弓の弾頭は、相互浸食によって如何なる魔法装甲をも貫通する。
対魔法抵抗力でそれを防ごうとした場合、８桁あっても貫通は免れない。
contexts.japanesePC: 対魔法抵抗力でそれを防ごうとした場合、８桁あっても貫通は免れない。
contexts.japanesePS3:
黄金弓の弾頭は、相互浸食によって如何なる魔法装甲をも貫通する。
対魔法抵抗力でそれを防ごうとした場合、８桁あっても貫通は免れない。
contexts.WH: When that was blocked by anti-magic resistance power, even something with eight digits wouldn't escape penetration.
contexts.MG:
Golden bow warheads could penetrate any magical armor through reciprocal corrosion.
When one tried to block them with anti-magic resistance power, even eight digits were not sufficient to prevent their penetration.
contexts.UP:
The warheads of the golden bows could penetrate any magical armor with their mutual corrosion.
When attempting to block that using the anti‐magic resistance stat, even something with eight digits wouldn't escape penetration.
contexts.note: Both restore attempting to block rather than successful blocking.

MG.japanese: 黄金弓の弾頭は、相互浸食によって如何なる魔法装甲をも貫通する。対魔法抵抗力でそれを防ごうとした場合、８桁あっても貫通は免れない。…ちなみに、神話に出てくる著名な神々の抵抗力でも、９桁に達する者はそう多くない。その為、それを計るには９桁あれば常識的に考えほとんどの数値は表示できる。…その９桁を、戦人は全て９で埋めてしまう……。
MG.translation: Golden bow warheads could penetrate any magical armor through reciprocal corrosion. When one tried to block them with anti-magic resistance power, even eight digits were not sufficient to prevent their penetration. ...By the way, even famous gods that appear in myths rarely reach as high as nine digits. For that reason, nine digits were enough to measure pretty much all sensible values. ...Battler had buried all 9 of those digits with nines...

UP.japanese: 黄金弓の弾頭は、相互浸食によって如何なる魔法装甲をも貫通する。対魔法抵抗力でそれを防ごうとした場合、８桁あっても貫通は免れない。…ちなみに、神話に出てくる著名な神々の抵抗力でも、９桁に達する者はそう多くない。その為、それを計るには９桁あれば常識的に考えほとんどの数値は表示できる。…その９桁を、戦人は全て９で埋めてしまう……。
UP.translation: The warheads of the golden bows could penetrate any magical armor with their mutual corrosion. When attempting to block that using the anti‐magic resistance stat, even something with eight digits wouldn't escape penetration. ...Furthermore, even among the famous gods that appear in myths, there are not many who reach a resistance stat of nine digits. For that reason, nine digits were enough to measure almost all imaginable values. ...Battler had filled all nine of those digits with 9's......

findings.sourceReading: 防ごうとした場合 makes the blocking attempt hypothetical, then states eight-digit resistance still cannot avoid penetration.
findings.alternative: Blocked can loosely mean met by a defense, but its normal completed-success sense conflicts with the same English clause’s unavoidable penetration.

findings.description: WH has Beelzebub leave food out of gratitude rather than condescending pity or mercy.

contexts.japanese:
「あんた光栄に思いなさいよね！！
本当は私が全部食べるところを、お情けであんたらの分も残してあげてるんだからね！」
contexts.japanesePC: 「あんた光栄に思いなさいよね！！　本当は私が全部食べるところを、お情けであんたらの分も残してあげてるんだからね！」
contexts.japanesePS3:
「あんた光栄に思いなさいよね！！
本当は私が全部食べるところを、お情けであんたらの分も残してあげてるんだからね！」
contexts.WH: "You should be honored!!  Normally, I would have eaten all of it, but I left you some out of gratitude!"
contexts.MG:
"You should be honored!!
Normally, I would've eaten all of it, but I left you some out of gratitude!"
contexts.UP:
"You should be honored!!
Normally, I would have eaten all of it, but I left you guys some out of pity!"
contexts.note: MG retains gratitude; UP restores condescending pity.

MG.japanese: 「あんた光栄に思いなさいよね！！　本当は私が全部食べるところを、お情けであんたらの分も残してあげてるんだからね！」
MG.translation: "You should be honored!! Normally, I would've eaten all of it, but I left you some out of gratitude!"

UP.japanese: 「あんた光栄に思いなさいよね！！　本当は私が全部食べるところを、お情けであんたらの分も残してあげてるんだからね！」
UP.translation: "You should be honored!! Normally, I would have eaten all of it, but I left you guys some out of pity!"

findings.sourceReading: お情けであんたらの分も残してあげてる portrays sparing their portions as a favor from her generosity, matching the demand that they feel honored.
findings.alternative: Both imply leaving a share for others, but gratitude reverses the direction of obligation and is not the meaning of お情け.

findings.description: WH says our Jessica cannot do such a thing, replacing Natsuhi’s refusal to give her daughter to a servant’s child.

contexts.japanese:
「使用人の子となんて…！！
駄目です、うちの朱志香をやれるわけありません…！！」
contexts.japanesePC: 「使用人の子となんて…！！　駄目です、うちの朱志香がやれるわけありません…！！」
contexts.japanesePS3:
「使用人の子となんて…！！
駄目です、うちの朱志香をやれるわけありません…！！」
contexts.WH: "With a servant child...?!!  You can't, our Jessica cannot do such a thing...!!"
contexts.MG:
"With a servant child...?!!
You can't, our Jessica cannot do such a thing...!!"
contexts.UP:
"With a servant child...?!!
I forbid it, I couldn't possibly give away our Jessica to such a person...!!"
contexts.note: MG makes Jessica unable to do it; UP restores Natsuhi refusing to give her away.

MG.japanese: 「使用人の子となんて…！！　駄目です、うちの朱志香をやれるわけありません…！！」
MG.translation: "With a servant child...?!! You can't, our Jessica cannot do such a thing...!!"

UP.japanese: 「使用人の子となんて…！！　駄目です、うちの朱志香をやれるわけありません…！！」
UP.translation: "With a servant child...?!! I forbid it, I couldn't possibly give away our Jessica to such a person...!!"

findings.sourceReading: うちの朱志香がやれるわけありません uses やる for giving the family’s daughter in marriage, as shown by the proposed pairing and Krauss’s reply about choosing a partner.
findings.alternative: Both versions oppose the relationship, but the English makes Jessica the one unable to do something and loses Natsuhi’s parental disposition of her daughter.

findings.description: WH reverses Kyrie’s judgment by saying the scene proves a parent can let go of their children.

contexts.japanese:
「そうよ。
親が子離れしてない証拠ね」
contexts.japanesePC: 「そうよ。親が子離れしてない証拠ね。」
contexts.japanesePS3:
「そうよ。
親が子離れしてない証拠ね」
contexts.WH: "That's right.  It's proof that a parent can let go of their children."
contexts.MG:
"That's right.
It's proof that a parent's too attached to their child."
contexts.UP:
"Exactly.
It's proof the parent hasn't let go of their child."
contexts.note: Both restore parental failure to let go.

MG.japanese: 「そうよ。親が子離れしてない証拠ね」
MG.translation: "That's right. It's proof that a parent's too attached to their child."

UP.japanese: 「そうよ。親が子離れしてない証拠ね」
UP.translation: "Exactly. It's proof the parent hasn't let go of their child."

findings.sourceReading: 親が子離れしてない証拠 explicitly says this is evidence that the parents have not separated emotionally from their children.
findings.alternative: Rosa endorses freedom immediately before it, but Kyrie’s observation refers to the clinging parents and retains a negative predicate in Japanese.

findings.alternative: The warning makes a father running off with the girlfriend imaginable, but the final sentence is advice to the son, not a prediction about the father.

findings.description: WH has Battler and Beato turn their heads to see what is going on, instead of looking at each other in puzzlement before ascending.

contexts.japanese:
階段の踊り場の上に、祖父さまとワルギリアがいて、手招きをしている。
俺とベアトは何事かと顔を見合わせてから、二人で階段を登った。
contexts.japanesePC: 俺とベアトは何事かと顔を見合わせてから、二人で階段を登った。
contexts.japanesePS3:
階段の踊り場の上に、祖父さまとワルギリアがいて、手招きをしている。
俺とベアトは何事かと顔を見合わせてから、二人で階段を登った。
contexts.WH: After Beato and I turned our heads to see what was going on, we climbed the stairs together.
contexts.MG:
Grandfather and Virgilia were standing on the landing at the top of the staircase, beckoning to us.
Beato and I turned our heads to see what was going on, then climbed the stairs together.
contexts.UP:
Grandfather and Virgilia were standing on the landing at the top of the staircase, beckoning us.
Beato and I looked at each other quizzically, then climbed the stairs together.
contexts.note: MG changes mutual puzzlement to looking toward the event; UP restores the exchanged look.

MG.japanese: 階段の踊り場の上に、祖父さまとワルギリアがいて、手招きをしている。俺とベアトは何事かと顔を見合わせてから、二人で階段を登った。そこは、ホールから見るとまるで、とても高いステージの上のようだった。そこには小さなテーブルが用意され、そこに羊皮紙と、古風な羽ペンが用意されていた。
MG.translation: Grandfather and Virgilia were standing on the landing at the top of the staircase, beckoning to us. Beato and I turned our heads to see what was going on, then climbed the stairs together. From the hall, it looked like a very high stage. A small table had been set up there, as well as a piece of parchment and an old-fashioned quill pen.

UP.japanese: 階段の踊り場の上に、祖父さまとワルギリアがいて、手招きをしている。俺とベアトは何事かと顔を見合わせてから、二人で階段を登った。そこは、ホールから見るとまるで、とても高いステージの上のようだった。そこには小さなテーブルが用意され、そこに羊皮紙と、古風な羽ペンが用意されていた。
UP.translation: Grandfather and Virgilia were standing on the landing at the top of the staircase, beckoning us. Beato and I looked at each other quizzically, then climbed the stairs together. From the hall, it looked like a very high stage. A small table had been set up there, as well as a piece of parchment and an old‐fashioned quill pen.

findings.sourceReading: 何事かと顔を見合わせて describes an exchanged glance between the two.
findings.alternative: Both versions show uncertainty and subsequent ascent, but the mutual glance is replaced by looking to inspect the event.

contexts.japanesePC: 「頼もしいわね。……さぁ、彼らと一緒に行きましょう。六軒島へ。駒たちがもうすぐ全て揃う。……第４のゲームが幕を開けるわ。ベアトも戦人も、もう席についてる頃よ。」
contexts.japanesePS3: 駒たちがもうすぐ全て揃う。
contexts.WH: "How reliable.  ......Come, let us go with them.  To Rokkenjima.  All of the pieces are already gathered.  ......The curtain will open on the fourth game.  By this time, Beato and Battler are already seated."
contexts.MG: All of the pieces are already gathered.
contexts.UP: Soon, all of the pieces will be gathered.
contexts.note: MG pieces already gathered; UP restores imminent gathering.

MG.japanese: 「頼もしいわね。……さぁ、彼らと一緒に行きましょう。六軒島へ。駒たちがもうすぐ全て揃う。……第４のゲームが幕を開けるわ。ベアトも戦人も、もう席についてる頃よ」
MG.translation: "I'm glad to hear it. ...Come, let us go with them. To Rokkenjima. All of the pieces are already gathered. ...The curtain will open on the fourth game. By this time, Beato and Battler will already be seated."

UP.japanese: 「頼もしいわね。……さぁ、彼らと一緒に行きましょう。六軒島へ。駒たちがもうすぐ全て揃う。……第４のゲームが幕を開けるわ。ベアトも戦人も、もう席についてる頃よ」
UP.translation: "I'm glad to hear it. ......Now, let's go with them. To Rokkenjima. Soon, all of the pieces will be gathered. ......The curtain will open on the fourth game. Beato and Battler will already be seated by now."

findings.sourceReading: 駒たちがもうすぐ全て揃う uses もうすぐ for an imminent event, distinct from the following guess that Beato and Battler are already seated.
findings.alternative: The fourth game is imminent in both versions, but English moves completion of the full gathering into the past.
findings.sourceNote: Original Witch Hunt is compared with the original-PC Japanese embedded in the historical patches. MangaGamer uses the accepted MangaGamer-based Witch Hunt backport, and Umineko Project uses its repository English; both are compared with maintained PS3-derived Japanese. The MangaGamer and PS3 witnesses are not independently certified retail extractions.

findings.description: WH says she surely turned her face up, where Japanese describes her looking upward sharply or resolutely.

contexts.japanese: 縁寿は両拳を握り締めたまま、きっと天を仰ぐ。
contexts.japanesePC: 縁寿は両拳を握り締めたまま、きっと天を仰ぐ。
contexts.japanesePS3: 縁寿は両拳を握り締めたまま、きっと天を仰ぐ。
contexts.WH: As she stood there with her fists still clenched, she surely turned her face up to the heavens.
contexts.MG: As she stood there with her fists still clenched, she surely turned her face up to the heavens.
contexts.UP: As she stood there with her fists still clenched, she surely turned her face to the heavens.
contexts.note: Both retain surely rather than resolute upward look.

MG.japanese:
縁寿は両拳を握り締めたまま、きっと天を仰ぐ。
瞳の淵に溜まった涙の雫が一粒、宙に零れ落ちる。そして二人の魔女の姿は、時が動き出す時に吹く暴風に飲み込まれて瞬時に消え去った。
MG.translation: As she stood there with her fists still clenched, she surely turned her face up to the heavens. A single teardrop from the depths of her eyes dripped down into the air. And when time started moving again, the two witches' figures were swallowed up by a blowing gale and erased in an instant.

UP.japanese:
縁寿は両拳を握り締めたまま、きっと天を仰ぐ。
瞳の淵に溜まった涙の雫が一粒、宙に零れ落ちる。そして二人の魔女の姿は、時が動き出す時に吹く暴風に飲み込まれて瞬時に消え去った。
UP.translation:
As she stood there with her fists still clenched, she surely turned her face to the heavens.
A single teardrop from the depths of her eyes dripped down into the air. And when time started moving again, the two witches' figures were sucked into a blowing gale, and erased in an instant.

findings.sourceReading: きっと天を仰ぐ uses きっと for the forceful or firm manner of the gaze, alongside clenched fists.
findings.alternative: Surely can emphatically narrate an action, but here reads as certainty rather than manner and drops the resolute gesture.

findings.description: WH reports that Battler made no effort to touch the food rather than that it showed no sign of being touched.

contexts.japanese:
「……実は、膝を抱いてうずくまられて、もうだいぶになります。
何度かお声をお掛けしたのですが、お返事をされません。
お食事もお運びしたのですが、手を触れた様子もありません」
contexts.japanesePC: 「……実は、膝を抱いてうずくまられて、もうだいぶになります。何度かお声をお掛けしたのですが、お返事をされません。お食事もお運びしたのですが、手を触れた様子もありません。」
contexts.japanesePS3:
「……実は、膝を抱いてうずくまられて、もうだいぶになります。
何度かお声をお掛けしたのですが、お返事をされません。
お食事もお運びしたのですが、手を触れた様子もありません」
contexts.WH: "......In truth, he has been crouching and clutching at his knees for some time now.  I spoke to him several times, but he did not answer.  I also carried him food, but he made no effort to touch it."
contexts.MG:
"...In truth, he has been crouching and clutching at his knees for some time now.
I spoke to him several times, but he did not answer.
I also brought him some food, but he never even touched it."
contexts.UP:

I called out to him several times, but he did not answer.
I also carried him something to eat, but he does not appear to have touched it."
contexts.note: MG removes lack of effort but asserts never touched; UP restores appearance.

MG.japanese: 「……実は、膝を抱いてうずくまられて、もうだいぶになります。何度かお声をお掛けしたのですが、お返事をされません。お食事もお運びしたのですが、手を触れた様子もありません」

findings.sourceReading: 手を触れた様子もありません is an observational statement about apparent lack of contact, not a claim about effort or attempt.
findings.alternative: Untouched food can suggest no attempt to eat, but the English makes that inference explicit and loses the observational qualification in Ronove’s report.

findings.description: WH describes the flags and confetti as completely stupid and out of place, rather than creating a thoroughly celebratory atmosphere; red-and-white confetti colors also disappear.

contexts.japanese:
…威勢良く扉が開き。
某キャラメルの箱に書かれたマラソンの人みたいに、両手を高々と上げて、
馬鹿みたいに明るそうに振る舞いながら、
……ベアトが登場する。
なぜだか、万国旗やら紅白の紙吹雪が舞い散り、実におめでたい雰囲気満点だった。
……クロワッサンを取り合って床で取っ組み合いをしていた戦人たちは、争いも忘れて絶句してしまう。
contexts.japanesePC: なぜだか、万国旗やら紅白の紙吹雪が舞い散り、実におめでたい雰囲気満点だった。
contexts.japanesePS3:
…威勢良く扉が開き。
某キャラメルの箱に書かれたマラソンの人みたいに、両手を高々と上げて、
馬鹿みたいに明るそうに振る舞いながら、
……ベアトが登場する。
なぜだか、万国旗やら紅白の紙吹雪が舞い散り、実におめでたい雰囲気満点だった。
……クロワッサンを取り合って床で取っ組み合いをしていた戦人たちは、争いも忘れて絶句してしまう。
contexts.WH: For some reason, flags from around the world and confetti scattered about, looking completely stupid and out of place.
contexts.MG:
...She flung the door open.
Like a marathon runner drawn on a certain caramel box,
with her hands held high and an idiotic cheeriness,
...Beato appeared.
For some reason, flags from around the world and confetti scattered about, perfectly completing this magnificent entrance.
...Battler and Beelzebub, who had been fighting over the croissant, completely forgot about their argument, speechless.
contexts.UP:
...The door opened forcefully.
Like a marathon runner drawn on a certain caramel box,
with her hands held high and with an idiotic cheeriness,
......Beato appeared.
For some reason, countless country flags and confetti scattered everywhere, creating what was clearly intended to be the perfect party atmosphere.
......Battler and Beelzebub, who had been grappling on the floor over the croissant, completely forgot about their argument and stared at her speechless.
contexts.note: Both restore celebratory atmosphere but omit red-and-white colors.

MG.japanese: …威勢良く扉が開き。某キャラメルの箱に書かれたマラソンの人みたいに、両手を高々と上げて、馬鹿みたいに明るそうに振る舞いながら、……ベアトが登場する。なぜだか、万国旗やら紅白の紙吹雪が舞い散り、実におめでたい雰囲気満点だった。

UP.japanese: …威勢良く扉が開き。某キャラメルの箱に書かれたマラソンの人みたいに、両手を高々と上げて、馬鹿みたいに明るそうに振る舞いながら、……ベアトが登場する。なぜだか、万国旗やら紅白の紙吹雪が舞い散り、実におめでたい雰囲気満点だった。
UP.translation: ...The door opened forcefully. Like a marathon runner drawn on a certain caramel box, with her hands held high and with an idiotic cheeriness, ......Beato appeared. findings.sourceReading: おめでたい雰囲気満点 describes an abundance of festive atmosphere, with 紅白 paper confetti conventionally celebratory.
findings.alternative: おめでたい can mean foolish and preceding narration calls her cheeriness idiotic, but here the flags and red-white confetti establish a celebration; out of place adds a judgment absent from this sentence.

findings.description: WH places Battler in a futon rather than under or inside a blanket.

contexts.japanese: いえいえ、毛布の中で、膝を抱くようにぐっすりお休みでございまして。
contexts.japanesePC: 「ぷっくくくくく！！　いえいえ、毛布の中で、膝を抱くようにぐっすりお休みでございまして。お目覚めの時間をお知らせしたのですが、まるでお起きになられず。食事をしようにも、悪戯猫が迷い込んでそれどころではなかったようで。ぷっくっく、ぷーっくっくっくっく！」

findings.description: WH says people get lazy from their own certainty rather than neglecting their own verification and delegating it to others.

contexts.japanese:
「人はいきなり騙されたりはしない。
自らの確認を怠り、それを他人に委ねた時、騙される。
……他の人が渡り始めたからもう信号は青になったと思った、じゃ、事故の言い訳にはならないってこと。
contexts.japanesePC: 「人はいきなり騙されたりはしない。自らの確認を怠り、それを他人に委ねた時、騙される。……他の人が渡り始めたからもう信号は青になったと思った、じゃ、事故の言い訳にはならないってこと。わかる…？」
contexts.japanesePS3:
「人はいきなり騙されたりはしない。

……他の人が渡り始めたからもう信号は青になったと思った、じゃ、事故の言い訳にはならないってこと。
contexts.WH: "People don't just get tricked out of the blue.  They get lazy from their own certainty, and when they entrust things to other people, that's when they get tricked.  ......Saying that you thought the light had turned green just because you saw other people start crossing doesn't count as an excuse for getting into an accident. contexts.note: Both restore neglecting personal verification and delegating it.

findings.description: WH says the one further away can accurately gauge the witch instead of saying separated viewpoints allow accurate measurement.

contexts.japanese:
「さっき彼は戦うことを、あなたとの距離を詰めると表現した。
でも、ひとつの目では距離は測れない。
ふたつの目があって初めて物事は立体的に見え、その距離も測れる」
「……そして二つの視点があっても、同じ場所からでは意味がない。
離れている方が、魔女を正確に測ることが出来る」
contexts.japanesePC: 「さっき彼は戦うことを、あなたとの距離を詰めると表現した。でも、ひとつの目では距離は測れない。ふたつの目があって初めて物事は立体的に見え、その距離も測れる。……そして二つの視点があっても、同じ場所からでは意味がない。離れている方が、魔女を正確に測ることが出来る。」
contexts.japanesePS3:

離れている方が、魔女を正確に測ることが出来る」
contexts.WH: "Just now, he described fighting with you as closing the distance.  But you can't measure distance with a single eye.  Only with two eyes are things visible in three dimensions, and only then can distance be measured.  ......And even if there are two fields of vision, it's pointless if they're in the same place.  The one further away can accurately gauge the witch."
contexts.MG:
"Just now, he described fighting with you as closing the distance.
But you can't measure distance with a single eye.
Only with two eyes are things visible in three dimensions, and only then can distance be judged.
...And even when you have two fields of vision, it's pointless if they're in the same place.
You can pin down witches more accurately when they're far apart."
contexts.UP:

Only with two eyes are things visible in three dimensions, and only then can distance be measured."
"......And having two viewpoints is meaningless if they're in the same place.
You can gauge the witch more accurately if they're far apart."
contexts.note: MG plural witches makes the separated objects the targets rather than viewpoints; UP singular witch retains viewpoints as the antecedent.

MG.japanese:

findings.sourceReading: 二つの視点…同じ場所…離れている方が concerns the distance between the two perspectives, in the preceding binocular analogy.
findings.alternative: An observer farther from the other observer is separated, but the English privileges one farther-away observer and can imply distance from the witch rather than the baseline between viewpoints.

MG.japanese: 彼女らの言葉遣いや振る舞いなどは、確かにお嬢様学校らしいものだが、本質的な部分はみんな歳相応に無邪気で残酷だ。……私が、自分に掛けられた挨拶だと誤解したことが面白かったらしい。いや、その逆かもしれない。…私みたいな根暗な子に突然挨拶をされて、対応に困った、というべきか。
MG.translation: Their choice of words and manner were certainly what you'd expect from a school for rich girls, but the actual meaning was as innocent and cruel as you'd expect from kids of that age. ...It seems they found it funny that I'd mistakenly thought the greeting was directed at me. No, it might be the opposite. ...Maybe they didn't know how to react after being suddenly greeted by a gloomy, quiet kid like me.

UP.japanese: 彼女らの言葉遣いや振る舞いなどは、確かにお嬢様学校らしいものだが、本質的な部分はみんな歳相応に無邪気で残酷だ。……私が、自分に掛けられた挨拶だと誤解したことが面白かったらしい。いや、その逆かもしれない。…私みたいな根暗な子に突然挨拶をされて、対応に困った、というべきか。
UP.translation: Their choice of words and manner were certainly what you would expect of a school for rich girls, but at their core, they were as innocent and cruel as any children of that age. ......It seems they found it funny that I'd mistakenly thought the greeting had been directed at me. No, it might be the opposite. ...Maybe I should say that they didn't know what to do after being greeted by an introverted kid like me.

findings.sourceReading: 本質的な部分 contrasts their essential nature with outward speech and behavior.

findings.description: WH makes an injury’s seriousness the hospital-room status analogy instead of the severity of an illness one has contracted.

contexts.japanese: 病室では自分の掛かった病の重さがステータスになるように、ここでは生まれの高潔さがステータスとなる。
contexts.japanesePC: 病室では自分の掛かった病の重さがステータスになるように、ここでは生まれの高潔さがステータスとなる。
contexts.japanesePS3: 病室では自分の掛かった病の重さがステータスになるように、ここでは生まれの高潔さがステータスとなる。
contexts.WH: Just like how the seriousness of an injury becomes a sign of status in a hospital room, how noble a birth one had became a sign of status here.
contexts.MG: Just like how the seriousness of an injury becomes a sign of status in a hospital room, how noble a birth one had became a sign of status here.
contexts.UP: Just like how the seriousness of your injury grants you status in a hospital room, here, status is granted by the nobility of your birth.
contexts.note: Both retain injury for illness.

MG.japanese: 病室では自分の掛かった病の重さがステータスになるように、ここでは生まれの高潔さがステータスとなる。公の場に出ることが許されない存在など、汚らわしいものでしかないのだろう。そういう生徒にかかわると、自分までもが穢れてしまうとでも思っているに違いない。
MG.translation: Just like how the seriousness of an injury becomes a sign of status in a hospital room, how noble a birth one had became a sign of status here. Those girls who couldn't be acknowledged in public were probably nothing more than filth to the others. They must've thought that getting involved with such students would dirty them as well.

UP.japanese: 病室では自分の掛かった病の重さがステータスになるように、ここでは生まれの高潔さがステータスとなる。公の場に出ることが許されない存在など、汚らわしいものでしかないのだろう。そういう生徒にかかわると、自分までもが穢れてしまうとでも思っているに違いない。
UP.translation: Just like how the seriousness of your injury grants you status in a hospital room, here, status is granted by the nobility of your birth. Those who aren't permitted to go out in public are probably nothing more than filth to them. They must think that getting involved with students like that would dirty them as well.

findings.sourceReading: 自分の掛かった病の重さ refers to disease or illness, not injury.
findings.alternative: Both concern severity of medical conditions, but the source specifically invokes illness as the comparison for school birth-status ranking.

findings.description: WH narrates being kept like a pet as a past state instead of the lifetime of powerless captivity Ange realizes awaits her.

contexts.japanese:
私は絵羽伯母さんとは到底一緒に生活をすることは出来ない。
……私は生涯を、亡き息子の当てつけにされながら、飼い殺される。
contexts.japanesePC: ……私は生涯を亡き息子に当てつけられながら、飼い殺される。
contexts.japanesePS3:
私は絵羽伯母さんとは到底一緒に生活をすることは出来ない。
……私は生涯を、亡き息子の当てつけにされながら、飼い殺される。
contexts.WH: ......As my life was continually compared with her dead son's, I was kept like a pet.
contexts.MG:
I couldn't possibly live together with Aunt Eva.
...I was kept like a pet, my life continually compared with her dead son's.
contexts.UP:
I couldn't possibly live together with Aunt Eva.
......I would be eternally suffocated, continually compared with her dead son.
contexts.note: UP would be restores the anticipated lifetime; suffocated is a free rendering of wasted captivity.

MG.japanese:
……しかし、それは私にとってはたまったものではない。
私は絵羽伯母さんとは到底一緒に生活をすることは出来ない。……私は生涯を、亡き息子の当てつけにされながら、飼い殺される。それを、まだ小学生の私ですら、理解した。
MG.translation: ...However, that wasn't something I could endure. I couldn't possibly live together with Aunt Eva. ...I was kept like a pet, my life continually compared with her dead son's. I understood that even when I was still in elementary school.

UP.japanese:
……しかし、それは私にとってはたまったものではない。
私は絵羽伯母さんとは到底一緒に生活をすることは出来ない。……私は生涯を、亡き息子の当てつけにされながら、飼い殺される。それを、まだ小学生の私ですら、理解した。
UP.translation:
......However, that wasn't something I could endure.
I couldn't possibly live together with Aunt Eva. ......I would be eternally suffocated, continually compared with her dead son. Even as an elementary schooler, I understood that.

findings.sourceReading: 生涯…飼い殺される describes being maintained in subjugation without a meaningful role for her whole life, followed by even elementary-school Ange understanding that prospect.
findings.alternative: Pet imagery conveys dependence and later cattle/slave imagery remains, but loses the specific wasted-life force of 飼い殺し and its prospective lifetime scope.
