findings.description: WH says I had stolen the inheritance rather than describing Eva’s resentment that her son’s intended succession would be taken from him by Ange succeeding.

contexts.japanese:
……最愛の息子を失った怒りと悲しみと、息子が継ぐはずだった家督を私に奪われることになる恨み辛み。
そしてそんな感情を私にぶつけて発散できる黒い喜び。
……そんな、負の感情のありったけをぶつけられた。
contexts.japanesePC: ……最愛の息子を失った怒りと悲しみと、息子が継ぐはずだった家督を私に奪われることになる恨み辛み。そしてそんな感情を私にぶつけて発散できる黒い喜び。
contexts.japanesePS3:
……最愛の息子を失った怒りと悲しみと、息子が継ぐはずだった家督を私に奪われることになる恨み辛み。
そしてそんな感情を私にぶつけて発散できる黒い喜び。
……そんな、負の感情のありったけをぶつけられた。
contexts.WH: ......The anger and sadness of losing her beloved son, and well as the hatred and pain that I had stolen the inheritance from the son who should have succeeded it.  And the dark pleasure at being able to let those feelings out on me.
contexts.MG:
...I saw the anger and sadness of losing her beloved son, and well as the hatred and pain from me stealing that inheritance from the son who should've received it.
And the dark pleasure at being able to let those feelings out on me.
...I was hit with all those negative emotions at once.
contexts.UP:
......The anger and sadness of losing her beloved son, and well as her hatred and pain towards the fact that I was going to steal the headship her son was meant to inherit.
And the dark pleasure of being able to let those feelings out on me.
......I was pummeled with all of those negative emotions at once.
contexts.note: MG removes completed had stolen but retains inheritance rather than prospective headship.

MG.japanese: 私を罰する絵羽伯母さんを何という言葉で例えればいいだろう。凶乱？　嬉々として？……最愛の息子を失った怒りと悲しみと、息子が継ぐはずだった家督を私に奪われることになる恨み辛み。そしてそんな感情を私にぶつけて発散できる黒い喜び。……そんな、負の感情のありったけをぶつけられた。
MG.translation: How should I describe what Aunt Eva was like when she punished me? In a frenzy? Gleeful? ...I saw the anger and sadness of losing her beloved son, and well as the hatred and pain from me stealing that inheritance from the son who should've received it. And the dark pleasure at being able to let those feelings out on me. ...I was hit with all those negative emotions at once.

UP.japanese: 私を罰する絵羽伯母さんを何という言葉で例えればいいだろう。凶乱？　嬉々として？……最愛の息子を失った怒りと悲しみと、息子が継ぐはずだった家督を私に奪われることになる恨み辛み。そしてそんな感情を私にぶつけて発散できる黒い喜び。……そんな、負の感情のありったけをぶつけられた。
UP.translation: How should I describe what Aunt Eva was like when she punished me? Frenzied? Gleeful? ......The anger and sadness of losing her beloved son, and well as her hatred and pain towards the fact that I was going to steal the headship her son was meant to inherit. And the dark pleasure of being able to let those feelings out on me. ......I was pummeled with all of those negative emotions at once.

findings.sourceReading: 私に奪われることになる presents a prospective passive deprivation from Eva’s viewpoint, not Ange’s completed act of theft.
findings.alternative: The source already describes resentful blame directed at Ange, but WH makes a completed active theft more explicit and changes its timing.

findings.description: WH calls classmates’ derisive laughter calm and pleasant where Japanese treats it as comparatively mild and unable to hurt her heart.

……私の心に、堪えるわけもない…。

そんな生活に比べれば、ここでのクラスメートの冷笑など涼やかなもの。
……私の心に、堪えるわけもない…。
contexts.WH: Compared to that lifestyle, the derisive laughter of my classmates here was calm and pleasant.  ......It was no match for my heart...

findings.description: WH says Maria had certainly been nine when she died rather than recalling that she was nine, if memory serves.

……だからその姿はすでに私よりも幼い。

contexts.japanesePS3:

MG.japanese: 今日は真里亞の誕生日。楼座は彼女の誕生日を、必ず素敵なレストランで過ごすようにしていた。真里亞がまだ幼稚園の頃は、近所のお友達を招いてホームパーティーをしたこともある。楼座が腕によりを掛けた、手作りの素敵なケーキやお菓子、室内のレイアウトなどをして、とても盛大に祝ったものだ。ただ、引越しの関係で、近所に友人を持たなくなってからは奮発した高級レストランがそれに変わるようになった。
MG.translation: Today was Maria's birthday. Rosa always tried to let Maria spend her birthdays at great restaurants. When Maria had been in kindergarten, they sometimes invited other kids from the neighborhood over and had a party at home. Rosa would make a wonderful cake and snacks and decorate the house herself, making it a huge celebration. But when they moved and Maria no longer had friends in the neighborhood, Rosa had started splurging at expensive restaurants instead.

findings.sourceReading: 必ず…過ごすようにしていた describes ensuring or regularly arranging that birthday practice, clarified by home parties then expensive restaurants.
findings.alternative: The reservation and past celebrations still show actual effort, but wanted weakens the established action to desire.

findings.description: WH links possible refusal of a pet to Maria treating objects as precious, instead of listing pet refusal and care for objects as separate possible contributing motives.

contexts.japanese:
楼座叔母さんにペットを飼うことを許してもらえなかったこともあるかもしれないし、
物を大切にするという気持ちもあったかもしれない。
contexts.japanesePC: 楼座叔母さんにペットを飼うことを許してもらえなかったこともあるかもしれないし、物を大切にするという気持ちもあったかもしれない。
contexts.japanesePS3:
楼座叔母さんにペットを飼うことを許してもらえなかったこともあるかもしれないし、
物を大切にするという気持ちもあったかもしれない。
contexts.WH: Maybe Rosa oba-san hadn't let her keep a pet at some point in time, so she treated objects as though they were precious.
contexts.MG:
Maybe Aunt Rosa hadn't let her keep a pet at some point in time,
so she felt like treasuring objects instead.
contexts.UP:
Maybe it was partly that Auntie Rosa hadn't let her keep a pet,
or maybe just her innate desire to treat things as though they were precious.
contexts.note: UP restores separate possible motives.

MG.japanese: 確かに、さくたろうほどにまで人格化されて愛された存在はないだろうが、真里亞お姉ちゃんにとってそれは特別なことではない。彼女は自分の持ち物をとてもよく愛し、まるで友人やよく懐いたペットのように扱った。楼座叔母さんにペットを飼うことを許してもらえなかったこともあるかもしれないし、物を大切にするという気持ちもあったかもしれない。……身近に友人を見つけなければならないほど、彼女が孤立していたこともあったかもしれない。そんな様々な事情から、彼女にとってこのようなことは特別なことではなかったのだ。
MG.translation: Of course, that wasn't anything extraordinary in Maria onee-chan's eyes, although I don't think she'd personified and loved anything quite as much as Sakutarou. She loved the things she owned very much, treating them just like friends or beloved pets. Maybe Aunt Rosa hadn't let her keep a pet at some point in time, so she felt like treasuring objects instead. ...And maybe she was so isolated that she'd been forced to find a friend nearby. Because of all that, what happened that day wasn't anything extraordinary from her perspective.

UP.japanese: 確かに、さくたろうほどにまで人格化されて愛された存在はないだろうが、真里亞お姉ちゃんにとってそれは特別なことではない。彼女は自分の持ち物をとてもよく愛し、まるで友人やよく懐いたペットのように扱った。楼座叔母さんにペットを飼うことを許してもらえなかったこともあるかもしれないし、物を大切にするという気持ちもあったかもしれない。……身近に友人を見つけなければならないほど、彼女が孤立していたこともあったかもしれない。そんな様々な事情から、彼女にとってこのようなことは特別なことではなかったのだ。
UP.translation: Of course, I don't think anything could be as personified and loved as Sakutarou was, but that wasn't anything extraordinary in Maria onee‐chan's eyes. She loved the things she owned very much, treating them just like friends or beloved pets. Maybe it was partly that Auntie Rosa hadn't let her keep a pet, or maybe just her innate desire to treat things as though they were precious. ......Maybe it was that she was so isolated, she had been forced to find friends closer to home. Because of all those various circumstances, this wasn't anything extraordinary from her perspective.

findings.sourceReading: …こともあるかもしれないし、…気持ちもあったかもしれない offers parallel possibilities; the following isolation speculation joins these various circumstances.
findings.alternative: The English retains Maybe and later various conditions, but so supplies a causal relationship and omits the second motive’s separate uncertainty.

findings.description: WH renders 口をすっぱくして as sourly saying, replacing insistent repetition with an irritable tone.

contexts.japanesePC: 楼座は眉間にしわをよせながら、それだけは絶対駄目だと口をすっぱくして伝え、電話を切るのだった。
contexts.japanesePS3: 楼座は眉間にしわをよせながら、それだけは絶対駄目だと口をすっぱくして伝え、電話を切るのだった。
contexts.WH: Rosa's forehead creased, and after sourly saying that Maria definitely must not do that, she hung up.
contexts.MG: Rosa's forehead creased, and after sourly saying that Maria definitely mustn't do that, she hung up.
contexts.UP: Rosa's forehead creased, and after sourly telling Maria that she was absolutely not to, she hung up.
contexts.note: Both retain sourly rather than insistent repeated warning.

MG.japanese: 真里亞の口調から、自分の与り知れない内に、あのぬいぐるみと一緒に買い物に出たことでもありそうな気配を察する。楼座は眉間にしわをよせながら、それだけは絶対駄目だと口をすっぱくして伝え、電話を切るのだった。
MG.translation: From Maria's manner of speech, Rosa got the feeling that Maria might've gone shopping with that stuffed animal without her knowing about it. Rosa's forehead creased, and after sourly saying that Maria definitely mustn't do that, she hung up.

UP.japanese: 真里亞の口調から、自分の与り知れない内に、あのぬいぐるみと一緒に買い物に出たことでもありそうな気配を察する。楼座は眉間にしわをよせながら、それだけは絶対駄目だと口をすっぱくして伝え、電話を切るのだった。
UP.translation: From Maria's manner of speech, Rosa got the feeling that Maria had been going shopping with that stuffed animal without her knowing about it. Rosa's forehead creased, and after sourly telling Maria that she was absolutely not to, she hung up.

findings.sourceReading: The idiom describes repeatedly or emphatically telling someone, here that taking Sakutaro out is absolutely forbidden.
findings.alternative: Rosa is visibly displeased and sourly fits that mood, but it does not express the warning’s repetition or insistence.

findings.description: WH says Mama says not to take me outside a lot, which attaches a lot to taking the toy outside instead of to how often Mama gives the prohibition.

contexts.japanese:
『ママはよく、ボクをお外に連れて行っちゃいけないって言うし。
真里亞のことをよく、もう何歳になったんだから駄目とか、そういう言い方をするし…』
contexts.japanesePC: 『ママはよく、ボクをお外に連れて行っちゃいけないって言うし。真里亞のことをよく、もう何歳になったんだから駄目とか、そういう言い方をするし…。』
contexts.japanesePS3:
『ママはよく、ボクをお外に連れて行っちゃいけないって言うし。
真里亞のことをよく、もう何歳になったんだから駄目とか、そういう言い方をするし…』
contexts.WH: 『Mama says not to take me outside a lot.  And she usually says Maria can't do it because she's too old...』
contexts.MG:
"Mama says not to take me outside a lot.
And she usually says Maria can't do it because she's too old..."
contexts.UP:
‘Mama often says not to take me outside.
And she usually words it like, no, you're too old for that now...’
contexts.note: UP restores frequency of prohibition rather than permitted outings.

MG.japanese: 『ママはよく、ボクをお外に連れて行っちゃいけないって言うし。真里亞のことをよく、もう何歳になったんだから駄目とか、そういう言い方をするし…』
MG.translation: "Mama says not to take me outside a lot. And she usually says Maria can't do it because she's too old..."

UP.japanese: 『ママはよく、ボクをお外に連れて行っちゃいけないって言うし。真里亞のことをよく、もう何歳になったんだから駄目とか、そういう言い方をするし…』
UP.translation: ‘Mama often says not to take me outside. And she usually words it like, no, you're too old for that now...’

findings.sourceReading: ママはよく…いけないって言う means Mama often says not to take me outside; it is not permission for occasional outings.
findings.alternative: An alternative reading can attach a lot to says, but its placement after outside naturally changes the prohibited quantity. The following age-based ban favors the repeated prohibition.

いっつも真里亞たちは縁寿のすぐ側にいる。
でも、縁寿の魔法が弱いから、こうして真里亞の日記を開かないと知覚できないだけ」

findings.alternative: English will always can imply a continuing state, and the later wind discussion clearly restores current proximity. The local assertion nevertheless reads as a promise of companionship rather than the premise of a perception explanation.

findings.description: WH substitutes witches for magic in Ange’s summary of Maria’s account of what fills the world.

contexts.japanese: 彼女に言わせれば、この世は魔法や霊でいっぱいらしい。
contexts.japanesePC: 彼女に言わせれば、この世は魔法や霊でいっぱいらしい。
contexts.japanesePS3: 彼女に言わせれば、この世は魔法や霊でいっぱいらしい。
contexts.WH: According to her, this world is full of witches and spirits.
contexts.MG: According to her, this world is full of magic and spirits.
contexts.UP: According to her, this world is full of magic and spirits.
contexts.note: Both restore magic and spirits.

MG.japanese: 彼女に言わせれば、この世は魔法や霊でいっぱいらしい。たとえばそれは、ちょっとしたそよ風くらいに自然で身近なものだとか。
MG.translation: According to her, this world is full of magic and spirits. And they're as natural and nearby as a light breeze.

UP.japanese: 彼女に言わせれば、この世は魔法や霊でいっぱいらしい。たとえばそれは、ちょっとしたそよ風くらいに自然で身近なものだとか。
UP.translation: According to her, this world is full of magic and spirits. As natural and nearby as a light breeze.

findings.sourceReading: 魔法や霊 means magic and spirits; 魔法 is not 魔女. The breeze analogy concerns natural nearby unseen phenomena.
findings.alternative: Witches belong to the surrounding discussion and gods/spirits appear later, but changing magic to its practitioners changes the class of entities or phenomena in the summary.

findings.description: WH repeats Maria’s merry appearance rather than the narrator’s judgment that she would look conspicuously out of place.

contexts.japanese:
そんな中、まるでハイキングのように上機嫌な真里亞はとても浮いて見えただろう。
時折すれ違う会社員が、場違いなものを見たような目で彼女の後姿をちらりと見る。
contexts.japanesePC: そんな中、まるでハイキングのように上機嫌な真里亞はとても浮いて見えただろう。
contexts.japanesePS3:
そんな中、まるでハイキングのように上機嫌な真里亞はとても浮いて見えただろう。
時折すれ違う会社員が、場違いなものを見たような目で彼女の後姿をちらりと見る。
contexts.WH: Amidst all that, Maria, who was in a good mood as though she was hiking, probably looked quite merry.
contexts.MG:
Amidst all that, Maria, who was in a good mood like someone on a hike, probably looked quite merry.
Every once in a while, passing employees would glance at her back with the eyes of someone seeing something out of place.
contexts.UP:
Amidst all that, Maria, in the best of moods as though she was hiking, probably stood out a great deal.
The occasionally passing employees glanced backwards over their shoulders at her with the eyes of someone seeing something out of place.
contexts.note: UP restores conspicuously standing out.

MG.japanese: 真里亞は、さくたろが半分顔をのぞかせたナップザックを背負って、深夜の商店街を意気揚々と歩いている。何しろこの時間だ。商店街には、シャッターを下ろすお店の店主や、家路を急いだり、あるいは千鳥足だったりする会社員ばかりだ。そんな中、まるでハイキングのように上機嫌な真里亞はとても浮いて見えただろう。
MG.translation: With her knapsack on her back and half of Sakutaro's face peeking out of it, she triumphantly walked through the shopping district late at night. Well, it was that time of day, after all. Everyone in the shopping district was either a shop owner lowering the shutters on their shops, or an employee rushing, or else staggering, on their way home. Amidst all that, Maria, who was in a good mood like someone on a hike, probably looked quite merry.

UP.japanese: 真里亞は、さくたろが半分顔をのぞかせたナップザックを背負って、深夜の商店街を意気揚々と歩いている。何しろこの時間だ。商店街には、シャッターを下ろすお店の店主や、家路を急いだり、あるいは千鳥足だったりする会社員ばかりだ。そんな中、まるでハイキングのように上機嫌な真里亞はとても浮いて見えただろう。
UP.translation: With half of Sakutaro's face peeking out of the knapsack on her back, Maria walked through the late‐night shopping district in high spirits. It was only to be expected given the time. Everyone in the shopping district was either a shop owner lowering the shutters on their shop, or an employee rushing, or else staggering, back home. Amidst all that, Maria, in the best of moods as though she was hiking, probably stood out a great deal.

findings.sourceReading: 浮いて見えただろう describes standing out incongruously among closing shops and homebound workers; good spirits already appear in 上機嫌.
findings.alternative: The next sentence retains workers seeing something out of place, so the scene still supplies the social contrast, but this sentence’s judgment is replaced.

しかし、最近、流行のコンビニエンスストアは深夜まで営業している。
母の帰宅が深夜を越えることも多い真里亞にとってはとても便利だった。

MG.translation: The supermarket had been closed for a while by this time. However, convenience stores, which had been growing in popularity lately, stayed open until midnight. It was very convenient for Maria, whose mother's return was often late.

UP.japanese: この時間にはスーパーはとっくに閉まっている。しかし、最近、流行のコンビニエンスストアは深夜まで営業している。母の帰宅が深夜を越えることも多い真里亞にとってはとても便利だった。
UP.translation: The supermarket had been closed for a while by this time. However, the recently popular convenience stores stayed open until late into the night. It was very convenient for Maria, whose mother's return was often later still.

findings.sourceReading: 深夜まで営業している specifies late-night availability, not a precise twelve-o’clock closing time.
findings.alternative: Until midnight can be colloquial for late-night service, but it supplies a specific temporal boundary not licensed by the Japanese.

findings.description: WH describes summoning Maria in a world where she does not exist rather than summoning Maria, who is no longer in this world.

findings.description: WH uses passive be shown a smile where Maria cites Ange’s ability to sometimes show a smile as evidence of magical talent.

Since you are able to be reunited with me and have a conversation, and be shown a smile every once in a while, you must have some magical talent, Ange.  Maria onee-chan guarantees it.  Uu-!"

本当に？
私がそう思い込んでるだけじゃないの…？
いや、違う。
そう思い込んでしまうから、視えないんだ。

応援？
本当に？
私がそう思い込んでるだけじゃないの…？
いや、違う。

findings.alternative: Wrong idea signals doubt generally, and later imagination/inner-voice language restores the issue, but the immediate self-generated-versus-external distinction is flattened.

UP.japanese: 広大で近代的な会議室に、縁寿と、上等なスーツを着た老紳士が二人きりでいた。プレゼンテーション用のあらゆる最新機材が準備され、それでいて上品で落ち着いた雰囲気を損なっていないその会議室は、ただそれだけで、この会議室の主である企業の格を知らしめ威圧している。

悪いことは言わない。
家出ごっこはこの辺で切り上げて、須磨寺の家に戻ったらどうだい」

findings.description: WH says Ange would inherit the family wealth after Eva’s death rather than that she has inherited it.

contexts.japanese: 絵羽伯母さんが死んだ後、右代宮家の全ての財産は私が相続している。
contexts.japanesePC: 絵羽伯母さんが死んだ後、右代宮家の全ての財産は私が相続している。
contexts.japanesePS3: 絵羽伯母さんが死んだ後、右代宮家の全ての財産は私が相続している。
contexts.WH: After Eva oba-san's death, I would inherit all of the wealth of the Ushiromiya family.
contexts.MG: When Aunt Eva died, I would inherit all the wealth of the Ushiromiya family.
contexts.UP: After Aunt Eva died, all the wealth of the Ushiromiya family was inherited by me.
contexts.note: UP restores completed inheritance.

MG.japanese: 絵羽伯母さんが死んだ後、右代宮家の全ての財産は私が相続している。それが目当てでなかったら、あんな虫唾が走るような言葉を口になんか出来るものか。
MG.translation: When Aunt Eva died, I would inherit all the wealth of the Ushiromiya family. If that wasn't what they were after, there's no way they would've been able to say such disgusting words.

UP.japanese: 絵羽伯母さんが死んだ後、右代宮家の全ての財産は私が相続している。それが目当てでなかったら、あんな虫唾が走るような言葉を口になんか出来るものか。
UP.translation: After Aunt Eva died, all the wealth of the Ushiromiya family was inherited by me. If they weren't after that, there's no way they'd have been able to say such disgusting words.

findings.sourceReading: 絵羽伯母さんが死んだ後…私が相続している states the current inherited ownership after Eva’s death; the following wealth she bears and guardian speculation use that existing position.
findings.alternative: Would could be read as future-in-the-past, and the later wealth passage restores possession, but no retrospective reporting frame requires future-in-the-past here.

findings.description: WH describes Eva letting her true intentions slip to him rather than his reputed role as the one person to whom she could reveal her real feelings.

contexts.japanese: その為、秀吉を失った後の絵羽が、唯一本音を漏らせる人物だったともされる。
contexts.japanesePC: その為、秀吉を失った後の絵羽が、唯一本音を漏らせる人物だったともされる。
contexts.japanesePS3: その為、秀吉を失った後の絵羽が、唯一本音を漏らせる人物だったともされる。
contexts.WH: For that reason, after Eva lost Hideyoshi, he had become the only person to which Eva would have let her true intentions slip.
contexts.MG: For that reason, when Eva lost Hideyoshi, he became the only person to whom Eva might have let her true intentions slip.
contexts.UP: For that reason, after Eva lost Hideyoshi, he had become the only person to whom she could reveal her true thoughts.
contexts.note: UP restores confidant role but omits reported-status qualification.

MG.japanese: その為、秀吉を失った後の絵羽が、唯一本音を漏らせる人物だったともされる。家族を失った絵羽が心を病み、縁寿に辛く当たるようになると、彼はその間の緩衝材的な役割も担ってくれたため、心が許せるほどではないが、縁寿にとっても訪ねやすい人物だった…。
MG.translation: For that reason, when Eva lost Hideyoshi, he became the only person to whom Eva might have let her true intentions slip. Whenever Eva's heart was torn by the loss of her family, whenever she took it out on Ange, he had acted as a buffer between the two, so although Ange didn't trust him, she found him a very easy person to question...

UP.japanese: その為、秀吉を失った後の絵羽が、唯一本音を漏らせる人物だったともされる。家族を失った絵羽が心を病み、縁寿に辛く当たるようになると、彼はその間の緩衝材的な役割も担ってくれたため、心が許せるほどではないが、縁寿にとっても訪ねやすい人物だった…。
UP.translation: For that reason, after Eva lost Hideyoshi, he had become the only person to whom she could reveal her true thoughts. When Eva's heart had been torn by the loss of her family, and she had taken it out on Ange, he had also acted as a buffer between the two, so although Ange didn't trust him, she too found him an easy person to pay a visit...

findings.sourceReading: 本音を漏らせる describes being able to let out honest feelings; ともされる marks this as a reported characterization of their relationship.
findings.alternative: Let slip can describe emotional disclosure, and would introduces some distance, but true intentions suggests concealed plans rather than a trusted outlet and the explicit reported-status cue disappears.

findings.description: WH calls Kinzo’s desired justification an official stance instead of a pretext for bypassing the eldest son.

contexts.japanese:
蔵臼を飛び越えて絵羽を次期当主に選ぶことの出来る建前を探していた。
その建前が、碑文の謎。

contexts.japanesePS3:
蔵臼を飛び越えて絵羽を次期当主に選ぶことの出来る建前を探していた。
その建前が、碑文の謎。
contexts.WH: searched for an official stance by which he could skip over Krauss and select Eva as the next head.
contexts.MG:
and he'd searched for an official stance by which he could skip over Krauss and select Eva as his successor.
That official stance was the riddle of the epitaph.
contexts.UP:
searched for an official stance by which he could skip over Krauss and select Eva as his successor.
That official stance was the riddle of the epitaph.
contexts.note: Both retain official stance rather than pretext.

MG.japanese: しかし自らにも頑固な金蔵は、自ら蔵臼に与えた次期当主という肩書きが邪魔で、蔵臼を飛び越えて絵羽を次期当主に選ぶことの出来る建前を探していた。その建前が、碑文の謎。
MG.translation: However, Kinzo, who was stubborn even against himself, was stymied by the title of Successor that he'd already given to Krauss, and he'd searched for an official stance by which he could skip over Krauss and select Eva as his successor. That official stance was the riddle of the epitaph.

UP.japanese: しかし自らにも頑固な金蔵は、自ら蔵臼に与えた次期当主という肩書きが邪魔で、蔵臼を飛び越えて絵羽を次期当主に選ぶことの出来る建前を探していた。その建前が、碑文の謎。
UP.translation: However, Kinzo, stubborn even to himself and obstructed by the title of successor that he had given to Krauss, searched for an official stance by which he could skip over Krauss and select Eva as his successor. That official stance was the riddle of the epitaph.

findings.sourceReading: 建前 is the publicly defensible rationale contrasted with his alleged underlying wish to select Eva; the epitaph is proposed as that pretext.
findings.alternative: Official stance can carry public-versus-private contrast, and earlier farce wording supports the theory, but it does not itself convey the instrumental excuse being sought.

findings.description: WH describes the ring as reminiscent of rich people’s dark hobbies rather than combining imposing weight with wealthy bad taste.

それは、金蔵が一時も外すことなく指にはめていたものだ。

台座の部分にダイヤがあしらわれ、重厚感と金持ち的な悪趣味さを兼ね備えている。

had diamonds adorning the pedestal, and possessed both stateliness and a sense of gaudy extravagance.

UP.japanese: 右代宮家、当主の指輪。黄金の重みがあり、片翼の紋章の入ったその指輪には、台座の部分にダイヤがあしらわれ、重厚感と金持ち的な悪趣味さを兼ね備えている。それは、金蔵が一時も外すことなく指にはめていたものだ。

findings.sourceReading: 金持ち的な悪趣味さ evaluates ostentatious or tasteless design, not sinister pastimes; the gold, crest and diamond are the objects of this judgment.
findings.alternative: 悪趣味 can concern objectionable tastes, but the design description gives no basis for hobbies or their darkness.

findings.description: WH makes Eva the most drastic person here, replacing the general observation that she can take very bold action when the stakes are critical.

あるいは、……右代宮家の財産を独り占めできるチャンスに、生涯でただ一度の殺人を犯したかもしれない。
…………だがね、俺はそうは思わない」

findings.description: WH frames the investigation as Eva’s person being clean and nothing unnatural found on her, rather than ordinary surrounding circumstances and absence of suspicious preparations.

一族を事故に見せ掛けて虐殺するような、あらゆる不自然な準備が見つけられなかったのだ。
当日は非番で難を逃れた使用人たちも、彼女を含め、全ての関係者について不自然な様子が見られなかったと証言した。

findings.alternative: English person can broadly concern conduct and clean can mean no wrongdoing, but nothing found on her explicitly narrows the next claim toward a personal search.

…私は絵羽伯母さんが大嫌いだから、彼女に利するあらゆる情報は否定するし、
中立的なあらゆる情報は悪意を以って解釈するだろう。

...I hate Aunt Eva, so I'll probably deny any information beneficial to her...
and interpret any neutral information in a negative way.

UP.japanese: それを言われると弱い。…私は絵羽伯母さんが大嫌いだから、彼女に利するあらゆる情報は否定するし、中立的なあらゆる情報は悪意を以って解釈するだろう。……つまり、私の中で、もう真実は決め付けられているのだ。にもかかわらず、なおも満たされずに探す“真実”とは一体、何物なのか…。
UP.translation: He has a point. ...I hate Aunt Eva, so I'll probably deny all information beneficial to her, and maliciously interpret all neutral information. ......In other words, inside myself, the truth is already decided. And yet I'm still unsatisfied, still searching for the "truth"—so what exactly is this "truth" I'm searching for...?

findings.sourceReading: 悪意を以って assigns ill will to Ange’s interpretive stance; it does not assert that the information itself is read as evidence of malicious intent.
findings.alternative: The English still conveys negative bias, and prior rejection of beneficial information remains, but shifts where the malice lies.

findings.description: WH says you cannot see anything from a single journalist’s viewpoint rather than that a single newspaper limits you to that viewpoint.

contexts.japanese:
ひとつの新聞だけじゃ、その記事を書いた記者の目線ひとつでしかものが見られない。
複数の新聞を読むことで初めて、立体的かつ冷静に分析が出来ることもある」
contexts.japanesePC: 新聞だってそうさ。ひとつの新聞だけじゃ、その記事を書いた記者の目線ひとつでしかものが見られない。複数の新聞を読むことで初めて、立体的かつ冷静に分析が出来ることもある。
contexts.japanesePS3:
ひとつの新聞だけじゃ、その記事を書いた記者の目線ひとつでしかものが見られない。
複数の新聞を読むことで初めて、立体的かつ冷静に分析が出来ることもある」
contexts.WH: It's the same with newspapers.  You can't see anything from the single viewpoint of a writer who made the article in a single newspaper.  Sometimes you can only process information composedly and in three dimensions when you read multiple newspapers.
contexts.MG:
You can't see anything from the single viewpoint of a writer who wrote an article in a single newspaper.
Sometimes you can only process information composedly and in three dimensions when you read multiple newspapers."
contexts.UP:
With only a single newspaper, you can only see things from the single viewpoint of the writer who wrote the article.
Sometimes it takes reading multiple papers before you can process the information rationally and in three dimensions."

MG.japanese: 「新聞だってそうさ。ひとつの新聞だけじゃ、その記事を書いた記者の目線ひとつでしかものが見られない。複数の新聞を読むことで初めて、立体的かつ冷静に分析が出来ることもある」
MG.translation: "It's the same with newspapers. You can't see anything from the single viewpoint of a writer who wrote an article in a single newspaper. Sometimes you can only process information composedly and in three dimensions when you read multiple newspapers."

UP.japanese: 「新聞だってそうさ。ひとつの新聞だけじゃ、その記事を書いた記者の目線ひとつでしかものが見られない。複数の新聞を読むことで初めて、立体的かつ冷静に分析が出来ることもある」
UP.translation: "It's the same with newspapers. With only a single newspaper, you can only see things from the single viewpoint of the writer who wrote the article. Sometimes it takes reading multiple papers before you can process the information rationally and in three dimensions."

findings.sourceReading: 記者の目線ひとつでしかものが見られない expresses only-from-one-viewpoint restriction; it allows partial sight and motivates comparative reading.
findings.alternative: The next sentence retains multiple-newspaper analysis, but cannot see anything turns limited perspective into complete absence of usable perception.

After being turned face up, the first thing I saw was...an arm stuck out right in front of my eyes.
contexts.note: UP restores being rolled over rather than falling.

MG.japanese: その黒服ごと、私たちはごろんと転がされる。仰向けにされて最初に目に入ったのは、私の目の前にずいっと突き出された腕だった。
MG.translation: Along with the black-suit guy, I fell with a *thunk*. After landing face up, the first thing I saw...was an arm stuck out right in front of my eyes.

UP.japanese: その黒服ごと、私たちはごろんと転がされる。仰向けにされて最初に目に入ったのは、私の目の前にずいっと突き出された腕だった。
UP.translation: The black‐suit and I were unceremoniously rolled over. After being turned face up, the first thing I saw was...an arm stuck out right in front of my eyes.

findings.sourceReading: 転がされる is an externally caused rolling movement, followed by 仰向けにされて describing her being turned face up, still on the ground after face-down restraint.
findings.alternative: Fell could loosely describe losing balance, but they were already pressed against asphalt; it obscures the rescue movement and its external agency.

findings.description: WH makes Ange the subject of suddenly taking off while on all fours, rather than the passenger affected by Amakusa’s abrupt acceleration.

contexts.japanese: 四つん這い状態のままで急発進されたので、私は椅子の上でしばらくの間、引っ繰り返された亀のようにジタバタしなくてはならなかった…。
contexts.japanesePC: 四つん這い状態のままで急発進されたので、私は椅子の上でしばらくの間、引っ繰り返された亀のようにジタバタしなくてはならなかった…。
contexts.japanesePS3: 四つん這い状態のままで急発進されたので、私は椅子の上でしばらくの間、引っ繰り返された亀のようにジタバタしなくてはならなかった…。
contexts.WH: Since I had suddenly taken off while still on all fours, I had to kick and struggle around on the chair for a while, like a turtle that's been flipped over...
contexts.MG: Since we suddenly accelerated while I was still on all fours, I had to kick and struggle around on the chair for a while, like a turtle that's been flipped over...
contexts.UP: Since we had suddenly taken off while I was still on all fours, I had to kick and struggle around on the seat for a while, like a turtle flipped onto its back...
contexts.note: Both restore on-all-fours state.

MG.japanese:
私はサイドブレーキを乗り越え、助手席へ潜り込む。
天草も私を押し込むようにして運転席へ乗り込んでくる。四つん這い状態のままで急発進されたので、私は椅子の上でしばらくの間、引っ繰り返された亀のようにジタバタしなくてはならなかった…。
MG.translation: I climbed over the hand brake and slid into the passenger's seat. Pushing me in, Amakusa also got into the driver's seat. Since we suddenly accelerated while I was still on all fours, I had to kick and struggle around on the chair for a while, like a turtle that's been flipped over...

UP.japanese:
私はサイドブレーキを乗り越え、助手席へ潜り込む。
天草も私を押し込むようにして運転席へ乗り込んでくる。四つん這い状態のままで急発進されたので、私は椅子の上でしばらくの間、引っ繰り返された亀のようにジタバタしなくてはならなかった…。
UP.translation:
I climbed over the hand brake and slid into the passenger's seat.
Pushing me through, Amakusa also got in and took up the driver's seat. Since we had suddenly taken off while I was still on all fours, I had to kick and struggle around on the seat for a while, like a turtle flipped onto its back...

findings.sourceReading: 急発進された is passive from Ange’s perspective after Amakusa gets into the driver’s seat; the resulting motion makes her flail like an overturned turtle.
findings.alternative: Taking off can refer colloquially to the whole car ride, but I had suddenly taken off attaches the action to Ange and obscures the driver/passenger distinction.

findings.description: WH says Amakusa took a pass at Ange, specifying romantic or sexual intent where the Japanese describes bothering or teasing her despite the no-chat instruction.

contexts.japanese: 彼はそんなのお構いなしに私にちょっかいを出してきたっけ。
contexts.japanesePC: 護衛たちは私に対し、余計なお喋りをしないように強く言われていたらしいが、彼はそんなのお構いなしに私にちょっかいを出してきたっけ。
contexts.japanesePS3: 彼はそんなのお構いなしに私にちょっかいを出してきたっけ。
contexts.WH: The guards were sternly told not to chat with me unnecessarily, but he came and took a pass at me, didn't he?
contexts.MG: but he came and took a pass at me, didn't he?
contexts.UP: but I recall that didn't stop him coming to take a pass at me.
contexts.note: Both retain taking a pass for teasing/interference.

MG.japanese: 護衛たちは私に対し、余計なお喋りをしないように強く言われていたらしいが、彼はそんなのお構いなしに私にちょっかいを出してきたっけ。その辺を特に嫌われて、絵羽伯母さんが死ぬ直前頃に解雇されたはずだ。
MG.translation: The guards were sternly told not to chat with me unnecessarily, but he came and took a pass at me, didn't he? Aunt Eva was apparently particularly put off by that...and had supposedly dismissed him shortly before she died.

UP.japanese: 護衛たちは私に対し、余計なお喋りをしないように強く言われていたらしいが、彼はそんなのお構いなしに私にちょっかいを出してきたっけ。その辺を特に嫌われて、絵羽伯母さんが死ぬ直前頃に解雇されたはずだ。
UP.translation: Apparently, the guards had been sternly told not to chat with me unnecessarily, but I recall that didn't stop him coming to take a pass at me. Aunt Eva had particularly disliked that, and I believe she dismissed him right before she died.

findings.sourceReading: ちょっかいを出す covers meddling, teasing or pestering and can in some contexts include flirting; this passage explains excessive chat and disregard for isolation rules without expressly specifying flirtation.
findings.alternative: A flirtatious reading is possible and his outward flippancy supports it, but took a pass commits to that reading rather than retaining the broader behavior.

contexts.WH: "He probably wanted to buy some gratitude from you, lady.  ......After I was fired, I got indebted to President Okonogi in various ways.  He took advantage of me here and there, and now I can't say no to him.  Hyahha!"

contexts.UP: The license plate on display was a fake.

MG.translation: "...Kasumi-sama, the escaping car was a rental. The license plate they displayed was a fake. We're clearly dealing with a pro. They'll probably abandon the car. Pursuit will be difficult. ...Should we have the police chase them?"

UP.japanese: 「……霞さま。逃走車両はレンタル。提示した免許証は偽装とのこと。明らかにプロです。恐らく車両は放棄するでしょう。追跡は困難です。……警察に追わせますか」

findings.sourceReading: 提示した免許証 refers to the presented driving-license credential; the preceding rental-car identification supplies the context of presentation.
findings.alternative: Both are evasion devices and could impede tracing, but plate falsification changes the vehicle’s visible identification rather than the renter’s recorded identity.

findings.description: WH says the bottle made things return to the occult theory rather than beginning to rewrite the earlier account retroactively as an occult/witch theory.

contexts.japanese: 「………数年後に漂着した手紙入りのワインボトル、『メッセージボトル』が、それをオカルト説という魔女説に遡って塗り替え始めた」
contexts.japanesePC: 「そう。恒星爆発の光が地球に届くまでの間の虚偽の真実が、陰謀説という人間説だったかのよう。………数年後に漂着した手紙入りのワインボトル、『メッセージボトル』が、それをオカルト説という魔女説に遡って塗り替え始めた。
contexts.japanesePS3: 「………数年後に漂着した手紙入りのワインボトル、『メッセージボトル』が、それをオカルト説という魔女説に遡って塗り替え始めた」
contexts.WH: "That's right.  The false truth that exists before the light from an exploding star reaches Earth is almost like the conspiracy theory, which is the human theory.  .........The wine bottle with a letter in it that drifted ashore several years later, the 'message bottle', painted over that theory and made things return to the occult theory, which is the witch's theory.
contexts.MG: ......The wine bottle with a letter in it that drifted ashore several years later, the "message bottle", painted over that theory and made things return to the occult theory, which is a witch's theory."
contexts.UP: ".........The wine bottle with a letter inside that drifted ashore several years later, the "message bottle", began to retroactively paint over that theory with the occult witch theory."
contexts.note: UP restores retroactive rewriting rather than returning to occult theory.

MG.japanese: 「………数年後に漂着した手紙入りのワインボトル、『メッセージボトル』が、それをオカルト説という魔女説に遡って塗り替え始めた」
MG.translation: ......The wine bottle with a letter in it that drifted ashore several years later, the "message bottle", painted over that theory and made things return to the occult theory, which is a witch's theory."

UP.japanese: 「………数年後に漂着した手紙入りのワインボトル、『メッセージボトル』が、それをオカルト説という魔女説に遡って塗り替え始めた」
UP.translation: ".........The wine bottle with a letter inside that drifted ashore several years later, the "message bottle", began to retroactively paint over that theory with the occult witch theory."

findings.sourceReading: 遡って塗り替え始めた describes retrospectively replacing the account of past events after a later discovery, directly paralleling delayed starlight revising earlier history.
findings.alternative: Painted over retains replacement, but return implies an earlier occult account being restored, whereas the proposed analogy concerns new later observation overwriting the earlier human theory.

「な？　そうやろ？　ただ、ついつい意地になってもうたんで、今さら会ってもいいなんて言えなくなってしまっただけや。そうやろ？　な？　な？」
MG.translation:
And Krauss nii-san, I know reeeal well how you're dyin' to get back at us for the things we've said...!" "If you're willin' to go so far, then you just need to let us meet with him! 
Right? Isn't that right? You just got a bit stubborn, and it felt awkward to say you'd let us see him after sayin' we couldn't all those times. Isn't that it? Right? Right?"

UP.japanese:

"Right? Isn't that right? But after all we've said, you just couldn't help gettin' stubborn, and now you're havin' trouble sayin' it's alright to see him, that's all. Isn't that it? Right? Right?"

findings.sourceReading: 蔵臼兄さんかて、本当はそこまで言うんなら、会わせてやってもいいと思っとる asserts that even Krauss really thinks he could let them meet Kinzo if they insist that much. Hideyoshi supplies a face-saving account of a concession Krauss could make.
findings.alternative: The later English stubbornness explanation preserves part of the escape route, but the first sentence assigns going so far to Krauss and substitutes an instruction for an attributed private thought.

findings.description: WH explicitly says Krauss was blown by the wind rather than presenting the cape pressure and fall through an as-if comparison.

contexts.japanese: その風圧に吹き飛ばされるかのように、蔵臼が尻餅をついてしまったとしても、何の不思議もなかった。

MG.japanese: 金蔵が振り返りながら払ったマントは、澱んだ部屋の空気を力強く一閃する。その風圧は、まさに右代宮金蔵の威厳と気迫をそのままに表していた。その風圧に吹き飛ばされるかのように、蔵臼が尻餅をついてしまったとしても、何の不思議もなかった。
MG.translation: As Kinzo turned and brushed his cape, it flashed forcefully through the room's stale air. That air pressure truly signified Ushiromiya Kinzo's majesty and willpower itself. After being blown back by that wind, it wasn't strange that Krauss landed on his butt.

UP.japanese: 金蔵が振り返りながら払ったマントは、澱んだ部屋の空気を力強く一閃する。その風圧は、まさに右代宮金蔵の威厳と気迫をそのままに表していた。その風圧に吹き飛ばされるかのように、蔵臼が尻餅をついてしまったとしても、何の不思議もなかった。
UP.translation: As Kinzo spun around and brandished his cloak, a blast of wind shook up the stale air inside the room. That air pressure expressed clearly the majesty and willpower of Ushiromiya Kinzo. It was no wonder at all that Krauss landed on his backside, as if that pressure had literally blown him to the ground.

findings.sourceReading: 風圧に吹き飛ばされるかのように qualifies the image as seeming to be blown away, while 尻餅をついてしまったとしても frames the fall as unsurprising. It does not assert that cape-generated wind physically blew him down.
findings.alternative: The narration is deliberately extravagant and the following English also uses as though for his legs, but After being blown by that wind makes this particular causal link factual.

蔵臼の爪先は宙をもがく。金蔵の隆々とした指が喉を締め上げているのだ。

findings.sourceReading: 爪先 means toes/tips of the feet; 宙をもがく depicts his dangling feet struggling as he is lifted by the collar. It does not mean clawing with his hands.
findings.alternative: Clawed at the air does not explicitly name hands, and the preceding lift still establishes suspension, but the normal English image differs and loses the feet-specific evidence.

findings.sourceReading: 魔女より得たものは何も残せぬのが初めからの約束 uses transitive 残せぬ: he cannot leave anything obtained from the witch. The contrast with passing on the Ushiromiya name is about what he can leave to successors.
findings.alternative: Would remain can be understood as remain as an inheritance in this succession context, but WH removes the explicit inability to leave and makes the agreement sound like an impersonal prediction of non-survival.

findings.description: Rosa asks whether Maria caught a cold instead of whether she is experiencing chills.

MG.japanese: 「大丈夫？　寒気とかしない？　やっぱり一度戻って着替えさせた方がいいかしら…」
MG.translation: "Are you okay? You didn't catch a cold, did you? Maybe we really should go back for now and get a change of clothes..."

UP.translation: "Are you alright? You didn't catch a chill, did you? Maybe we really should go back quickly and get a change of clothes..."

findings.sourceReading: 寒気とかしない asks about a current symptom or feeling of chill. It does not itself ask whether the child has contracted a cold. The preceding 風邪を引かないか is worry about possible illness.
findings.alternative: Chills can prompt concern about a cold, and both preserve maternal worry, but illness and the immediate symptom are distinct. WH also renders the preceding concern retrospectively as had caught a cold.

findings.sourceReading: 幸せのおすそわけ is the gift/share Maria sends her exhausted mother, explicitly motivated by the preceding wish to pass on her own happiness.
findings.alternative: Let us share can be read as inviting Mama to partake, so the broad affection remains; our happiness nevertheless makes it jointly possessed rather than explicitly something Maria gives to a tired mother.

findings.description: WH inserts every time a child plays with dolls into Beatrice’s explanation.

contexts.japanese:
ベアトリーチェが言うには、いわゆる子どもの頃のお人形遊びなどは、
本当に人形が意思を持って対話をし、自らの意思で動くことさえあるという。
contexts.japanesePC: ベアトリーチェが言うには、いわゆる子どもの頃のお人形遊びなどは、本当に人形が意思を持って対話をし、自らの意思で動くことさえあるという。

ベアトリーチェが言うには、いわゆる子どもの頃のお人形遊びなどは、
本当に人形が意思を持って対話をし、自らの意思で動くことさえあるという。
contexts.WH: According to Beatrice, every time a child plays with dolls, the dolls actually gain a will and converse with them, sometimes even moving by their own will.

the dolls actually gain a will and converse with them, sometimes even moving by their own will.

contexts.note: UP removes the universal every-time doll-play reading.

MG.japanese: ベアトリーチェが言うには、いわゆる子どもの頃のお人形遊びなどは、本当に人形が意思を持って対話をし、自らの意思で動くことさえあるという。しかし、その依り代に宿らせる力は、無垢ゆえにとても弱い。人形が喋るわけがない、動くわけがない、というニンゲンの常識の毒がわずかでも入り込むと、たちどころにそれは、物言わぬただの人形に逆戻りする……。
MG.translation: According to Beatrice, every time a child plays with dolls, the dolls actually gain a will and converse with them, sometimes even moving by their own will. However, because of their innocence, the power imbued into such a vessel is very weak. If they get struck with even a tiny bit of the toxin from a Human's common sense, which says that there's no way a doll can talk or move, they instantly revert to being non-speaking dolls...

UP.japanese: ベアトリーチェが言うには、いわゆる子どもの頃のお人形遊びなどは、本当に人形が意思を持って対話をし、自らの意思で動くことさえあるという。しかし、その依り代に宿らせる力は、無垢ゆえにとても弱い。人形が喋るわけがない、動くわけがない、というニンゲンの常識の毒がわずかでも入り込むと、たちどころにそれは、物言わぬただの人形に逆戻りする……。
UP.translation: According to Beatrice, when a child "plays with dolls", the dolls sometimes gain an actual will and converse with them, in rare cases even moving on their own. However, the power that they can imbue into such a vessel is very weak due to their innocence. If even a tiny bit of the toxin from a Humanhuman's common sense gets involved, and tells them that there's no way a doll can talk or move, it instantly reverts to being an ordinary non‐speaking doll......

findings.sourceReading: いわゆる子どもの頃のお人形遊びなど introduces familiar childhood doll play as an example. It does not state that animation occurs on every occasion; preceding explanation says spirits not uncommonly inhabit responding to innocent children.
findings.alternative: The narrator describes real dialogue according to Beatrice, but this does not license an added universal frequency. Sometimes even moving only qualifies movement, leaving English will/dialogue universal.

findings.description: WH says the magical effect could be controlled when Beatrice writes and Virgilia signs, rather than that the magic takes effect through writing and a witness signature.

contexts.japanese: ベアトリーチェが記し、ワルギリアが立会人にサインすることで効力を発揮する、魔法。
contexts.japanesePC: ベアトリーチェが記し、ワルギリアが立会人にサインすることで効力を発揮する、魔法。
contexts.japanesePS3: ベアトリーチェが記し、ワルギリアが立会人にサインすることで効力を発揮する、魔法。
contexts.WH: It was magic whose effect could be controlled if Beatrice wrote and Virgilia signed.
contexts.MG: It was magic whose effect could be controlled if Beatrice wrote and Virgilia signed.
contexts.UP: Magic, which would take effect by Beatrice writing it and Virgilia giving her signature as a witness.
contexts.note: UP restores taking effect rather than control of effect.

MG.japanese: ……それは、魔女が高位世界に対して記す宣言書のようなもの。ベアトリーチェが記し、ワルギリアが立会人にサインすることで効力を発揮する、魔法。最初は何を書いているのか理解できなかった真里亞も、途中からその書面の素晴らしき魔力を理解し、瞳を輝かせ始める…。
MG.translation: ...It was something like a written declaration made by witches to a high-order world. It was magic whose effect could be controlled if Beatrice wrote and Virgilia signed. Maria didn't understand what Beato was writing at first, but partway through, she figured out the wonderful magical power of this document, and her eyes began to sparkle...

UP.japanese: ……それは、魔女が高位世界に対して記す宣言書のようなもの。ベアトリーチェが記し、ワルギリアが立会人にサインすることで効力を発揮する、魔法。最初は何を書いているのか理解できなかった真里亞も、途中からその書面の素晴らしき魔力を理解し、瞳を輝かせ始める…。
UP.translation: ......It was something like a written proclamation made by witches to a higher‐order world. Magic, which would take effect by Beatrice writing it and Virgilia giving her signature as a witness. Maria didn't understand what Beato was doing at first, but partway through, she figured out the wonderful magic power of this document, and her eyes began to sparkle...

findings.sourceReading: ベアトリーチェが記し、ワルギリアが立会人にサインすることで効力を発揮する describes the act that makes the magic effective. It does not describe subsequent regulation/control of its effect, and expressly identifies the signer as a witness.
findings.alternative: Controlled may loosely refer to making magic work, and the later oath explicitly restores the witness role, but the local definition replaces activation with control and drops that qualification.

UP.translation: The discovery of that huge number of books at the end of the 20th century, books so valuable that dilettantes were filled with the desire to hoard them away, and their subsequent release to the public, gave the entire world a massive shock...

findings.sourceReading: 好事家たちが死蔵して独占欲を満たしたくなるほどに価値ある describes an inducement: their value makes collectors want to keep them hidden and satisfy the desire for exclusive possession. 満たしたくなる is wanting to satisfy, not inability to satisfy.
findings.alternative: Collectors can have insatiable acquisitive desires, but the source does not make that psychological claim; it explains why such valuable books would be withheld from public access.

findings.description: WH reduces the bottle’s sealing condition to the bare fact that it was sealed as a basis for the police judgment.

contexts.japanese:
「警察は現場の状況とボトルの封印状況から、捏造の可能性は低く、
事故直前の数日以内に投棄したものと判断したようです。
contexts.japanesePC: 「警察は現場の状況とボトルの封印状況から、捏造の可能性は低く、事故直前の数日以内に投棄したものと判断したようです。　また双方の筆跡は一致しました。これにより、漁師の発見したノート片の信憑性が増すこととなりました。
contexts.japanesePS3:
「警察は現場の状況とボトルの封印状況から、捏造の可能性は低く、
事故直前の数日以内に投棄したものと判断したようです。
contexts.WH: "It seems that, due to evidence from the surrounding area and the fact that the bottle was sealed, the police had decided that its likelihood of being a fabrication was low and that it had been abandoned no earlier than a few days before the accident.  And the handwriting for both matched.  This caused the credibility of the scraps of paper discovered by the fisherman to rise.
contexts.MG:
"It seems that, due to evidence from the surrounding area and the fact that the bottle had been sealed,
the police had decided that its likelihood of being a fabrication was low and that it had been abandoned no earlier than a few days before the accident.
contexts.UP:
"It seems that, due to evidence from the surrounding area and the intact state of the bottle's seal, the police had decided that its likelihood of being a hoax was low,
and that it had been cast out no earlier than a few days before the accident.
contexts.note: UP restores intact state of bottle seal.

MG.japanese: 「警察は現場の状況とボトルの封印状況から、捏造の可能性は低く、事故直前の数日以内に投棄したものと判断したようです。また双方の筆跡は一致しました。これにより、漁師の発見したノート片の信憑性が増すこととなりました」
MG.translation: "It seems that, due to evidence from the surrounding area and the fact that the bottle had been sealed, the police had decided that its likelihood of being a fabrication was low and that it had been abandoned no earlier than a few days before the accident. And the handwriting for both matched. This caused the credibility of the scraps of paper discovered by the fisherman to rise."

UP.japanese: 「警察は現場の状況とボトルの封印状況から、捏造の可能性は低く、事故直前の数日以内に投棄したものと判断したようです。また双方の筆跡は一致しました。これにより、漁師の発見したノート片の信憑性が増すこととなりました」
UP.translation: "It seems that, due to evidence from the surrounding area and the intact state of the bottle's seal, the police had decided that its likelihood of being a hoax was low, and that it had been cast out no earlier than a few days before the accident. And the handwriting for both matched. This caused the credibility of the notebook pages discovered by the fisherman to rise."

findings.sourceReading: 現場の状況とボトルの封印状況 are the circumstances at the scene and the condition/state of the bottle’s sealing. The source leaves the relevant observed condition unspecified rather than asserting that simple seal presence is the entire basis.
findings.alternative: Being sealed is one possible relevant condition and scene evidence remains, but the English selects that narrower observation instead of preserving the broader unspecified evidentiary detail.

findings.description: WH supplies attention as the motive in Ange’s speculation about the author of the witch accounts.

contexts.japanese: ……魔女幻想を生み出したい何者かの、愉快犯的犯行としか思えない。
contexts.japanesePC: ……魔女幻想を生み出したい何者かの、愉快犯的犯行としか思えない。
contexts.japanesePS3: ……魔女幻想を生み出したい何者かの、愉快犯的犯行としか思えない。
contexts.WH: ......I can only imagine that someone who wanted to give rise to an illusion of a witch carried out this crime for attention.
contexts.MG: ...It seems to me that the only possible explanation...is that someone who wanted to give rise to an illusion of a witch carried out this crime for their own enjoyment.
contexts.UP: ......I can only imagine that this was a crime committed for pleasure, by someone who wanted to create an illusion of a witch.
contexts.note: Both restore pleasure motive rather than the inherited attention motive.

MG.japanese: ……魔女幻想を生み出したい何者かの、愉快犯的犯行としか思えない。しかし、絵羽伯母さんを除く１７人もの人命が失われ、莫大な遺産と、あるいは１０ｔもの黄金さえもが闇で動いたのだ。その結末の告白が、こんな魔女の幻想だなんて、どうしても腑に落ちない。
MG.translation: ...It seems to me that the only possible explanation...is that someone who wanted to give rise to an illusion of a witch carried out this crime for their own enjoyment. However, the 17 people other than Aunt Eva lost their lives, and a vast wealth or maybe even 10 tons of gold had moved around secretly in the darkness. It doesn't feel right...for a confession occurring after all that to bring up this illusion of the witch.

UP.japanese: ……魔女幻想を生み出したい何者かの、愉快犯的犯行としか思えない。しかし、絵羽伯母さんを除く１７人もの人命が失われ、莫大な遺産と、あるいは１０ｔもの黄金さえもが闇で動いたのだ。その結末の告白が、こんな魔女の幻想だなんて、どうしても腑に落ちない。
UP.translation: ......I can only imagine that this was a crime committed for pleasure, by someone who wanted to create an illusion of a witch. But 17 people excluding Aunt Eva lost their lives, and a vast inheritance—and maybe even ten tons of gold—changed hands behind the scenes. It just doesn't make sense for the confession coming at the end of all that to be this fantasy about a witch.

findings.sourceReading: 愉快犯的犯行 describes a crime committed for amusement or the thrill of doing it. Ange can only conceive of someone seeking to generate a witch illusion doing such a thing; no particular desire for attention is specified.
findings.alternative: Seeking attention can overlap with such thrill-seeking behavior, especially for a public hoax. That plausible motive is nevertheless narrower than the motive stated here and is not established by the preceding speculation about the bottles.

findings.sourceReading: マモンを呼び出せただけで、リハビリには十分 says merely having managed to summon Mammon is sufficient for rehabilitation: it is enough practice toward regaining her ability. Ange replies that just one already counts as rehabilitation (１人だけでリハビリになっちゃうの), then elects to keep going as a pastime.
findings.alternative: Summoning is exhausting in both versions, so needing recovery afterward is plausible and later warnings about fatigue remain accurate. findings.sourceReading: 再びお役に立てる機会を賜るどころか、新しい主人の負担になる contrasts being granted another opportunity to be useful with instead becoming a burden to the new master. The disgrace is their negative effect on Ange rather than insufficient gratitude for an opportunity.
findings.alternative: Not honored at being given another chance could be read as a contrast between receiving an honor and becoming a burden. contexts.japanesePC: 私は罠に落ちかけているかもしれないと自覚しながらも、その先を促してしまう。
contexts.japanesePS3: 私は罠に落ちかけているかもしれないと自覚しながらも、その先を促してしまう。
contexts.WH: Even though I realized that I was falling into a trap, I urged her forwards.
contexts.MG: Even though I realized I was falling into a trap, I urged her forwards.
contexts.UP: Even though I realized that I could be on the verge of falling into a trap, I urged her onwards.
contexts.note: UP restores possible impending trap rather than certain present entrapment.

MG.japanese: まずい…。向こうのペースに乗せられた。…しかし私は、彼女の話に耳を傾けない限り解放されないのだ。…ならば、いずれは聞かねばならぬ話…。私は罠に落ちかけているかもしれないと自覚しながらも、その先を促してしまう。
MG.translation: Damn... I'm letting her take the initiative. ...But I won't be released until I lend an ear to her. ...So it's something I'll have to hear anyway... Even though I realized I was falling into a trap, I urged her forwards.

UP.japanese: まずい…。向こうのペースに乗せられた。…しかし私は、彼女の話に耳を傾けない限り解放されないのだ。…ならば、いずれは聞かねばならぬ話…。私は罠に落ちかけているかもしれないと自覚しながらも、その先を促してしまう。
UP.translation: Shoot... I've let her take the initiative. ...But I won't be released until I lend an ear to her story. ...So it's something I'll have to hear anyway... Even though I realized that I could be on the verge of falling into a trap, I urged her onwards.

findings.sourceReading: 罠に落ちかけているかもしれないと自覚しながらも is awareness that she may be on the verge of falling into a trap, despite which she prompts the next explanation.
findings.alternative: The surrounding text establishes loss of initiative and forced listening; actual manipulation is plausible. That context does not erase the explicit かもしれない qualification of her trap assessment.

findings.description: WH omits bringing the outcome and changes the domain of the happiest-outcome promise into an added receiving condition.

contexts.japanese: …見返りに、あなたが享受できる可能性の中で、もっとも幸せな結末を探して持ってくることを約束するわ。”
contexts.japanesePC: “あなたに、復讐のチャンスを。…見返りに、あなたが享受できる可能性の中で、もっとも幸せな結末を探して持ってくることを約束するわ。”
contexts.japanesePS3: …見返りに、あなたが享受できる可能性の中で、もっとも幸せな結末を探して持ってくることを約束するわ。”
contexts.WH: 'I'm giving you a chance for revenge.  ...In exchange, if it is possible for you to receive it, I promise to search for the happiest resolution for you.'
contexts.MG: ...In exchange, I promise to search for and bring you the happiest resolution among the possibilities you're capable of accepting.'
contexts.UP: ...In exchange, I promise to find and bring you the happiest resolution that it is possible for you to receive.
contexts.note: Both restore bounded outcomes and bringing the result; MG accepting is less exact but does not retain the canonical added conditional structure.

MG.japanese: そして、……最後にこう言ったわ。“あなたに、復讐のチャンスを。…見返りに、あなたが享受できる可能性の中で、もっとも幸せな結末を探して持ってくることを約束するわ。”
MG.translation: And, ...in the end, she said this. 'I'm giving you a chance for revenge. ...In exchange, I promise to search for and bring you the happiest resolution among the possibilities you're capable of accepting.'

UP.japanese: そして、……最後にこう言ったわ。“あなたに、復讐のチャンスを。…見返りに、あなたが享受できる可能性の中で、もっとも幸せな結末を探して持ってくることを約束するわ。”
UP.translation: And, ......in the end, she said this. ——I'm giving you a chance for revenge. ...In exchange, I promise to find and bring you the happiest resolution that it is possible for you to receive.

findings.sourceReading: あなたが享受できる可能性の中で、もっとも幸せな結末を探して持ってくることを約束する promises to search for and bring the happiest outcome among the possibilities Ange can enjoy. The bounded set of available outcomes is the basis for choosing the happiest one.
findings.alternative: Earlier recalled speech promises a search without guaranteed discovery, and the Japanese domain itself limits possible benefits. WH therefore preserves substantial uncertainty, but if it is possible for you to receive it changes the construction and omitting 持ってくる narrows the stated commitment in this separately quoted promise.

findings.description: WH changes the feared reduction of Ange’s own aims into a restriction on what her furniture existence can do.

contexts.japanese:
…お兄ちゃんの側にいられればいいだけの、
………魔女の家具に、成り下がっているのかもしれない……。
contexts.japanesePC: …お兄ちゃんの側にいられればいいだけの、………魔女の家具に、成り下がっているのかもしれない……。
contexts.japanesePS3:
…お兄ちゃんの側にいられればいいだけの、
………魔女の家具に、成り下がっているのかもしれない……。
contexts.WH: ...I might have been degraded into a witch's furniture, .........that can only be by Onii-chan's side......
contexts.MG:
...I might've been degraded into a witch's furniture,
......one that cares about nothing but being by Onii-chan's side...
contexts.UP:
...I might have degraded into a witch's furniture,
.........satisfied merely to be by Onii‐chan's side......
contexts.note: Both restore reduction to merely remaining by Onii-chan side.

MG.japanese: ……でも、もう私は違うかもしれない。…お兄ちゃんの側にいられればいいだけの、………魔女の家具に、成り下がっているのかもしれない……。
MG.translation: ...But I might be different now. ...I might've been degraded into a witch's furniture, ......one that cares about nothing but being by Onii-chan's side...

UP.japanese: ……でも、もう私は違うかもしれない。…お兄ちゃんの側にいられればいいだけの、………魔女の家具に、成り下がっているのかもしれない……。
UP.translation: ......But I might be different now. ...I might have degraded into a witch's furniture, .........satisfied merely to be by Onii‐chan's side......

findings.sourceReading: お兄ちゃんの側にいられればいいだけの describes being satisfied merely if she can remain by her brother’s side. She fears she may have sunk to furniture with only that aim, rather than the innocent sister praying for his victory. The possibility markers qualify her feared self-change.
findings.alternative: That can only be by his side overlaps with the practical limitation Lambdadelta has described. It does not express the source’s いられればいい, the minimal condition Ange might accept as sufficient, which is the emotional and moral conflict here.

findings.description: WH weakens the lethal act attributed to some sisters in the occult message bottle to an unspecified attack, then repeats that weakening in Ange’s hypothetical forgiveness.

contexts.japanese:
…彼女らの何人かは、私の家族を手に掛けてさえいるらしい。
しかし、私はそれを信じないし、彼女らにそれを詰問しても無駄なことだ。
彼女らは家具なのだから、主のリクエストに応えるだけなのだ。
もし本当に彼女らが私の家族に手を掛けていたとしても、彼女らを憎むことは出来ない。
contexts.japanesePC: ……私を不快にさせる、オカルトメッセージボトルによるならば、…彼女らの何人かは、私の家族を手に掛けてさえいるらしい。
contexts.japanesePS3:
…彼女らの何人かは、私の家族を手に掛けてさえいるらしい。
しかし、私はそれを信じないし、彼女らにそれを詰問しても無駄なことだ。
彼女らは家具なのだから、主のリクエストに応えるだけなのだ。
もし本当に彼女らが私の家族に手を掛けていたとしても、彼女らを憎むことは出来ない。
contexts.WH: ......According to the occult message bottle, which I didn't like, ...it seems that several of them even attacked my family.
contexts.MG:
...it seems that several of them even attacked my family.
But I don't believe that, and it's pointless to question them about it.
They are furniture, so they only respond to their master's requests.
Even if they really did attack my family, I can't hate them.
contexts.UP:
...it seemed that several among them even attacked my family.
But I didn't believe that, and it would be pointless to question them about it.
They're furniture, so all they do is respond to their master's requests.
Even if they really had attacked my family, I couldn't hate them.
contexts.note: Both retain attacked rather than killed family in the attributed bottle account.

MG.japanese: 彼女らは本来は、ベアトリーチェの残酷な生贄の儀式を行なうための家具だったという。……私を不快にさせる、オカルトメッセージボトルによるならば、…彼女らの何人かは、私の家族を手に掛けてさえいるらしい。
MG.translation: It's said that they were originally furniture that existed to carry out Beatrice's cruel sacrifice ceremony. ...According to the occult message bottle I hated, ...it seems that several of them even attacked my family.

UP.japanese: 彼女らは本来は、ベアトリーチェの残酷な生贄の儀式を行なうための家具だったという。……私を不快にさせる、オカルトメッセージボトルによるならば、…彼女らの何人かは、私の家族を手に掛けてさえいるらしい。
UP.translation: It's said that they were originally furniture that existed to carry out Beatrice's cruel sacrificial ritual. ......If that sickening occult message bottle was to be believed, ...it seemed that several among them even attacked my family.

findings.sourceReading: 私の家族を手に掛けてさえいる in the cruel sacrificial-ritual and lost-family context means even having killed her family members. The following conditional 私の家族に手を掛けていた maintains that alleged killing while Ange denies belief and distinguishes furniture from the commanding master.
findings.alternative: An attack can be fatal, and prior family loss makes death inferable. However, attacked does not state the lethal outcome expressed by the idiom in this context; it changes the culpable act she is willing to consider without hating the furniture.

findings.sourceReading: もっと私の原初の魔法を学んだなら addresses Ange: if she learns more of Maria’s Magic of Origins, she will be able to create friends to her taste. The next sentence contrasts that prospective capacity with creation still being difficult for Ange now.
findings.alternative: Japanese omits the learner pronoun, but 私の identifies whose magic is taught, and the address plus current-Ange limitation identify the learner. WH explicitly inserts I in both clauses, changing the instruction.

MG.japanese: 「絶対に叶うという保証を、誰かがくれたなら、きっと心も休まるでしょうにね」

UP.japanese: 「絶対に叶うという保証を、誰かがくれたなら、きっと心も休まるでしょうにね」

findings.sourceReading: 絶対に叶うという保証を、誰かがくれたなら asks for someone to give a guarantee that her wish will certainly come true. Sakutarou immediately offers to guarantee it, and she thanks him even as consolation; Maria objects to the doubting emotion.
findings.alternative: Guarantees can rest on evidence, and colloquial proof may loosely mean convincing assurance. Nonetheless, proof selects an evidential warrant absent from the source and breaks the lexical guarantee/guarantee linkage with Sakutarou’s answer.

findings.description: WH translates リュート as lute without supplying the Japanese reading that makes it an alternative answer beginning with ryu.

contexts.japanese: “リュート”の方が素敵ぃ！」

contexts.UP: {ruby:ryuuto:"Lute" would have been so much more wonderful!"
contexts.note: Both restore ryuuto reading needed for the Japanese word-chain game.

MG.japanese: 「私が一番に言いたかったのにぃ！　“リュート”の方が素敵ぃ！」

UP.translation: "I wanted to be the one to speak first! {ruby:ryuuto:"Lute" would have been so much more wonderful!"

findings.sourceReading: The players choose りゅ from うりゅー. Mammon answers 竜頭, and Leviathan says リュート would be more elegant. The written リュート begins with precisely that disputed sound, making her counterproposal immediately legible in Japanese.
findings.alternative: A reader familiar with the Japanese loanword can reconstruct ryuuto, and this is an unused alternative rather than a successful chain link. However, English lute does not begin with ryu; unlike Mammon’s ryuuzu and the subsequent gesuidou/umetatechi/chikashitsu chain, the supporting reading is absent.

findings.sourceReading: 呆れた表情 conveys appalled/exasperated disbelief at their foolish behavior. Her next remark calls this the same strange school as always and asks why their own good grades are not enough.

findings.sourceReading: Ange says there is no point in continuing to live, then repeats that she had no reason to be alive and should have gone with her family in 1986.
findings.alternative: Her coerced self-criticism supports shame as an associated feeling, and later dialogue makes her wish to die explicit. findings.description: 負い目があった becomes “Rosa was liable,” shifting an internal feeling of guilt/indebtedness to a statement of responsibility or liability.

contexts.japanese: 楼座には、真里亞のような幼い子を、ひとりで留守番させていることに負い目があったし、
contexts.japanesePC: 楼座には、真里亞のような幼い子を、ひとりで留守番させていることに負い目があったし、社会的にそれが許容されるものではないことを知っていたのだろう。
contexts.japanesePS3: 楼座には、真里亞のような幼い子を、ひとりで留守番させていることに負い目があったし、
contexts.WH: It was probably because Rosa was liable for making such a young girl like Maria watch over the house by herself, and because she knew that this was not something that would be permitted by society.
contexts.MG: It was probably because Rosa would be liable for making such a young girl like Maria watch over the house by herself,
contexts.UP: It was probably because Rosa felt guilty for making such a young girl as Maria watch over the house by herself,
contexts.note: UP restores Rosa feeling guilty instead of liability.

MG.japanese: 楼座には、真里亞のような幼い子を、ひとりで留守番させていることに負い目があったし、社会的にそれが許容されるものではないことを知っていたのだろう。だから真里亞に、大人に目を付けられないよう、買い物をする店をなるべく変えろとか、お巡りさんに話し掛けられても、挨拶以上のことはするなと吹き込んできたのだ。
MG.translation: It was probably because Rosa would be liable for making such a young girl like Maria watch over the house by herself, and because she knew that this wasn't something that would be permitted by society. So, Maria was indoctrinated into changing the stores she bought things at, so that she didn't catch the eyes of adults, and into saying no more than a greeting to policemen, even if they talked to her.

UP.japanese: 楼座には、真里亞のような幼い子を、ひとりで留守番させていることに負い目があったし、社会的にそれが許容されるものではないことを知っていたのだろう。だから真里亞に、大人に目を付けられないよう、買い物をする店をなるべく変えろとか、お巡りさんに話し掛けられても、挨拶以上のことはするなと吹き込んできたのだ。
UP.translation: It was probably because Rosa felt guilty for making such a young girl as Maria watch over the house by herself, and because she knew that this was not socially acceptable. So she had indoctrinated Maria into changing the stores she bought things at so that she didn't catch the eyes of adults, and saying no more than a greeting to policemen, even if they talked to her.

findings.sourceReading: Rosa felt guilty about leaving a child as young as Maria alone and probably knew society would not accept it; this motivates her instructions to avoid adult scrutiny.
findings.alternative: Liable can loosely mean responsible and the surrounding sentence still gives her awareness of social disapproval. Nevertheless it does not state her own guilty feeling, which is the source’s explicit characterization.

contexts.MG: "I am together with her as much as I should be!!

MG.japanese: 「なるべく一緒にいるようにしています！！　そんなこと、あなたに指図される覚えはありません…！！」
MG.translation: "I am together with her as much as I should be!! I don't need to take instructions from you for something like that...!!"

findings.sourceReading: Rosa says she tries to be with Maria as much as possible and rejects being instructed by the welfare officer.
findings.alternative: Her defensive tone plausibly implies she thinks she is doing enough, and the adjacent rejection of instructions supports that attitude. But the English makes sufficiency explicit in place of the stated attempt to maximize time.

findings.sourceReading: Rosa realizes the school knows the humiliating spectacle of her daughter bringing toys and playing alone, with those toys as her sole friends.
findings.alternative: This narration follows Rosa’s realization and may carry her harsh judgment, while the earlier school passage explicitly preserves that the toys are her only friends. Nonetheless the English makes the child rather than the displayed behavior the disgrace and introduces a hypothetical relation absent here.

MG.translation: "......Because you didn't listen to what Mama told you, I broke one of them. From now on, every time you disobey something Mama says, I'll break another one. ...Remember that!!!"

UP.japanese: 「………ママの言うことをちゃんと聞かないから、ひとつ壊れちゃったわ。今後、ママの言うことを守らない度にまたひとつ、壊すからね。……覚えておきなさいッ！！！」
UP.translation: ".........Because you didn't listen to what Mama told you, one of them broke. From now on, every time you disobey something Mama says, I'll break another one. ......Remember that!!!"

findings.sourceReading: Rosa says one has broken because Maria did not listen; she then explicitly threatens to break another whenever Maria disobeys.
findings.alternative: The preceding action makes Rosa’s physical agency indisputable, and English accurately states who broke it. But the dialogue’s first clause deflects responsibility onto Maria and the event before the second clause openly asserts Rosa’s future violence; that rhetorical distinction is lost.

findings.sourceReading: Rather than let beautiful-hearted Maria be torn apart by herself, Beatrice says the heartless mother who caused her suffering deserves to be torn apart far more.
findings.alternative: Rosa caused Maria’s pain and thus indirectly her self-destruction, so the English accusation is thematically plausible. But the preceding image explicitly identifies the tearing arms as Maria’s own; Beatrice’s decision compares two targets for that destructive force, not simply punishment for an already maternal tearing.

findings.description: あの時の幻を信じたいがために becomes “because it was hard to believe that those events were an illusion,” replacing a wish to believe with difficulty accepting a contrary interpretation.

contexts.japanese: だから、あの時の幻を信じたいがために、旅を続けている。
contexts.japanesePC: だから、あの時の幻を信じたいがために、旅を続けている。
contexts.japanesePS3: だから、あの時の幻を信じたいがために、旅を続けている。
contexts.WH: So, because it was hard to believe that those events were an illusion, I've continued on my journey.
contexts.MG: So, because it was hard to believe that those events were an illusion, I've continued on my journey.
contexts.UP: So, I'm continuing this journey because I want to believe in that illusion.

MG.japanese:
だから、あの時の幻を信じたいがために、旅を続けている。この旅で何かを変えられるなんて、本気で信じちゃいない。
……いつ旅を終わりにするかも自由。どこを終着点とするかも、自由なのだ。結局、この旅は、私の自己満足のためでしかない……。
MG.translation: So, because it was hard to believe that those events were an illusion, I've continued on my journey. I don't seriously believe that this journey will change anything. ...It's even up to me when to end this journey. It's up to me to choose where the final destination is. In the end, this journey is only for my self-satisfaction...

UP.japanese:
だから、あの時の幻を信じたいがために、旅を続けている。この旅で何かを変えられるなんて、本気で信じちゃいない。
……いつ旅を終わりにするかも自由。どこを終着点とするかも、自由なのだ。結局、この旅は、私の自己満足のためでしかない……。
UP.translation:
So, I'm continuing this journey because I want to believe in that illusion. I don't seriously believe that this journey will change anything.
......I'm even free to end it at any time. It's up to me to choose where the final destination is. In the end, this journey is only for my personal self‐satisfaction......

findings.sourceReading: Ange continues because she wants to believe the vision of that time, despite her doubt and lack of serious expectation that the journey changes anything.
findings.alternative: The preceding paragraph says stopping would mean acknowledging the witch’s message as illusion, so resistance to that acknowledgement is a plausible inference. But the English removes her explicit desire to believe and renders the motive as disbelief in the illusion explanation.

findings.sourceReading: Amakusa says self-satisfaction is perfectly fine, then explains that praise matters only if one can accept it and one need not receive praise to be content.
findings.alternative: His subsequent argument strongly supports self-acceptance, so the overall position remains. The opening statement nevertheless becomes tentative/conditional in frequency where the source is emphatic.

findings.alternative: 無欲 can carry an unselfish connotation, and Mammon’s greed context makes selfishness relevant. Here the immediately preceding reasoning defines desire as wanting what one lacks, so lack of desire rather than altruism supplies the stated inference.

findings.sourceReading: Kinzo sarcastically compares his own tens of billions with his children each having produced a grandchild instead of building comparable wealth.
findings.alternative: From Kinzo’s viewpoint these are his grandchildren, so he has gained them in a loose sense. But the source’s explicit contrast is between what he earned and what his children produced, continuing Nanjo’s defense of their accomplishments.

findings.sourceReading: Kinzo gives a clear answer to the competing interpretations of the ceremony; the following declaration supplies it.
findings.alternative: The answer is delivered with a laughing sprite and Kinzo laughs elsewhere. That staging can support a smile but does not substitute for the explicit answer in this narration.

findings.description: The English drops the specific financial action in 損切り and renders it generic fear of losing, weakening Krauss’s warning about waiting too long.

findings.sourceReading: If they fear cutting their losses, their lives may become as worthless as paper. This contrasts holding a losing position while waiting for improvement with accepting a loss to avoid total ruin.

findings.sourceReading: そこまでに至ってこそ、我が生涯を捧げるに値する愛である means only when it reaches that point is it love worthy of devoting my life to. The threshold applies to the intensity of love, not her deserving chains.
findings.alternative: The preceding beloved-witch discussion invites an application to Beatrice, but that context does not make the implicit application an explicit past declaration or shift the criterion from love to the woman.

findings.sourceReading: 刺さってる expresses something being stuck or piercing. Its omitted subject and precise referent remain unspecified; 知っている then separately states knowing. The rendering should retain that image without deciding whether it is literal pain, memory, or metaphor.
findings.alternative: Her imminent recollection makes an understanding idiom contextually plausible, but it does not preserve 刺さる and duplicates the adjoining knowing expression. The script’s translator query also signals uncertainty; it does not authorize replacing the image with a resolved interpretation.

contexts.japanese:
その落下してくる譲治の下腹部に、
狙い澄まされた蜂の一撃のような鋭いピンヒールによる後回し蹴りが打ち込まれる…！
東屋から吹き飛ばされた譲治は、薔薇の茂みに飲み込まれるかと思った瞬間。
そこに再び漆黒の穴が開き譲治を飲み込む。
すると今度はガァプの目の前の足元に漆黒の穴が開き、そこから無防備な譲治を吐き出す。
……その時にはガァプはすでに次の後回し蹴りの予備動作を終えている。
「ぐッ、……これ……は…、」
「お帰りなさい。くす！」
右側頭部。
右脇の下。
右膝側面。
まるで小さな竜巻のようにガァプはくるくると舞い踊りながら、
右足左足右足左足で連続回し蹴りを次々に叩き込む。
四連撃目は足払いとなって譲治の足を刈り取り転倒させるが、
もちろんそこに床はなく、漆黒の穴が開いていて、またしても譲治を飲み込んでしまう。
ガァプは再び小さい竜巻のように舞い踊る。
譲治もまた、再び東屋の天井より吐き出された。
「………食らって噛み締めなさい、奈落の終点が一撃。
……死ね……！！」
鋭き女王蜂の一撃は、昇る竜巻のように、天を刺す。
それは天井より落下する譲治の腹部を蹴り抜いた……。

contexts.WH: As George fell down, he was hit by a reverse roundhouse kick from a sharp stiletto heel, like a strike from a carefully aimed bee...!
contexts.MG:
As George fell down,
he was hit by a reverse roundhouse kick from a sharp stiletto heel, like a strike from a carefully aimed bee...!
The instant George, after being blown out of the arbor, thought that he'd be swallowed up by a rose bush...
Another pitch-black hole opened there and swallowed George up.
And this time, a pitch-black hole opened at Gaap's feet before her eyes, spitting a defenseless George out of it.
...At that time, Gaap had already finished the preparatory motions for the next reverse roundhouse kick.
"Ghh, ...what is...this...?"
"Welcome back. *giggle*!"
Right side of the head.
Below the right armpit.
Side of the right knee.
As Gaap danced and spun like a small cyclone,
she kept hitting him, left foot right foot left foot right foot, with successive roundhouse kicks.

George was once again spat out from the ceiling of the arbor.

The sharp strike of the queen bee pierced the heavens like a rising cyclone.
It kicked through George's lower chest as he fell from the ceiling...

MG.japanese: だからきっと。……真里亞お姉ちゃんが将来、子どもを持っても。その子どもに代々押し付けられてきた苦しみを押し付けることはないだろう。……一体、どれほどの長きにわたって受け継がれ、押し付けられてきたかわからない苦しみと悲しみの連鎖を、………真里亞お姉ちゃんの魔法は、断ち切ったのだ。
MG.translation: So I'm sure... ...If Maria onee-chan had had children in the future... UP.japanese: だからきっと。……真里亞お姉ちゃんが将来、子どもを持っても。その子どもに代々押し付けられてきた苦しみを押し付けることはないだろう。……一体、どれほどの長きにわたって受け継がれ、押し付けられてきたかわからない苦しみと悲しみの連鎖を、………真里亞お姉ちゃんの魔法は、断ち切ったのだ。

findings.sourceReading: わからない qualifies how long the chain has been inherited and imposed; it does not assign Maria a failure to understand that suffering.
findings.alternative: Who knows how long already captures the source uncertainty. The additional which she did not understand cannot be explained by that duration phrase.

findings.description: The public attacks on Eva deceased father business and character are assigned to her husband.

MG.japanese: ………………連日、ワイドショーや週刊誌が、彼女を公然と中傷した。亡父の事業も人格も、最愛の息子のことまで、否定された。彼女には、もう、何も残らなかった。痛みと悲しみを、わずかの間でも忘れるために、……泣きながら吼えるしかなかった。吼えている間だけは、わずかに解放されたからだ。だから、………黒き魔女が吼え方を教えた。
MG.translation: .........In the following days, the talk shows and magazines publicly slandered her. The truth of her husband's business and character...and even her beloved son were negated. She no longer had anything left. She could do nothing but cry and howl, ...trying to forget the pain and sadness at least for a while. After all, she could only feel a tiny bit of release, and only during the time that she howled. And so, ......the black witch taught her how to howl.

findings.alternative: The preceding paragraph mentions losing husband and son, which may explain the substitution, but cannot change the explicit father here.

findings.description: English describes how quickly black magic releases pain instead of limiting how long relief lasts.

contexts.UP: The black magic probably did release her from that suffering for just a short time.

MG.japanese: 私が憎むのは、その黒き魔女。黒き魔法は、ひと時の間だけ、確かに苦しみから解放はしただろう。……しかし。その重みを肩から下ろしてやることは決してない。それどころか、その重みを次なる犠牲者にも強いて、………世界を憎しみの重みで、いっぱいにしてしまう。
MG.translation: The one I hated...was the black witch. Black magic can probably release one from that pain for an instant. ...However, it never lifts that weight from a person's shoulders. On the contrary, it forces that weight onto further victims, ......filling the world with hatred.

UP.japanese: 私が憎むのは、その黒き魔女。黒き魔法は、ひと時の間だけ、確かに苦しみから解放はしただろう。……しかし。その重みを肩から下ろしてやることは決してない。それどころか、その重みを次なる犠牲者にも強いて、………世界を憎しみの重みで、いっぱいにしてしまう。
UP.translation: The one I hated...was the black witch. The black magic probably did release her from that suffering for just a short time. ......However, it would never lift that weight from her shoulders. To the contrary, it would force that weight on further victims, .........filling the world with the weight of hatred.

findings.sourceReading: ひと時の間だけ means only for a short time; the next sentence denies removal of the burden and the following sentence describes its transmission.
findings.alternative: In an instant could imply a brief experience informally, but its ordinary reading is speed of onset and it omits only and the duration restriction.

MG.translation: There...was the beautiful Ushiromiya family rose garden. However, the flowers on the roses were all gold. ...The nectar was also gold-colored. There, all wishes are granted, and all magic and dreams are born.

MG.japanese: ベアトは冷たく言い放つ。………かつて不敵に嘲笑って見せた彼女とはまるで別人のよう。心を閉ざし、真里亞お姉ちゃんと二人だけの世界に閉じ篭っているのだ。仲良しの真里亞お姉ちゃんといつまでも二人きりで、魔法談義をしながらお茶を飲んでいられる世界。……誰にも急かされず、何にも拒まれない。傷つけるかもしれないような誰一人すらも、彼女ら以外に存在しない世界。そう、それは二人にとって完成された、もはや小さな宇宙……。
MG.translation: Beato spoke coldly. ......She seemed like a completely different person from the boldly sneering woman she had once been. She had closed off her heart...and shut herself up in a world where she was alone with Maria onee-chan. A world where she could always be alone with a friendly Maria onee-chan, lecturing about magic while drinking tea. ...With no one to hurry them...and nothing to hold them back. A world where not a single person who might hurt them existed. Yes, to the two of them, it was a small, perfect universe...
