findings.description: もう少し楽観的な考え方に変わって来る explicitly says Natsuhi becomes more optimistic after learning relatives are also missing. English says her optimistic thinking began to change, omitting the direction and permitting reduced optimism.

contexts.japanese:
郷田ひとりだけ姿が見えないと聞いた時は、寝坊したのか、どこかで油を売っているのかと思ったが、
親族たちも含めての不在だということになると、もう少し楽観的な考え方に変わって来る。
contexts.japanesePC: 郷田ひとりだけ姿が見えないと聞いた時は、寝坊したのか、どこかで油を売っているのかと思ったが、親族たちも含めての不在だということになると、もう少し楽観的な考え方に変わって来る。
contexts.japanesePS3:
郷田ひとりだけ姿が見えないと聞いた時は、寝坊したのか、どこかで油を売っているのかと思ったが、
親族たちも含めての不在だということになると、もう少し楽観的な考え方に変わって来る。
contexts.WH: When she had heard that Gohda alone was missing, she had thought that he might have slept in or was loafing around somewhere, but once she heard that several of the relatives were also missing, her optimistic way of thinking began to change.
contexts.MG:
When she'd heard that Gohda alone was missing, she'd assumed he had slept in or was loafing around somewhere.
However, now that she'd learned that several of the relatives were also nowhere to be seen, she began to take a slightly more optimistic view.
contexts.UP:
When she had heard that Gohda alone was missing, she had thought that he might have slept in or was loafing around somewhere,
but once she heard that several of the relatives were also missing, she began to start thinking a little more optimistically.
contexts.note: Both more optimistic direction explicit.

MG.japanese: 郷田ひとりだけ姿が見えないと聞いた時は、寝坊したのか、どこかで油を売っているのかと思ったが、親族たちも含めての不在だということになると、もう少し楽観的な考え方に変わって来る。昨夜の親族会議は、下手をすると徹夜となり未だに続いているのではないか。それで、部屋の空気も澱んできたので、頭を冷やそう等ということになり、この雨の中、ぞろぞろと散歩に出ている可能性も考えられた。…頭を冷やそう、等という辺りは、実に蔵臼が好んで言いそうな言葉だった。多分、郷田も何かの世話に呼ばれ同行しているのだろう。
MG.translation: When she'd heard that Gohda alone was missing, she'd assumed he had slept in or was loafing around somewhere. However, now that she'd learned that several of the relatives were also nowhere to be seen, she began to take a slightly more optimistic view. Could last night's family conference have continued all night, up until the present moment? If so, they might have wanted to cool their heads after being shut in a stuffy room, going out for walks on their own through the rain. ...The part about "cooling their heads" really sounded like something Krauss would say. Gohda had probably been summoned to accompany them and aid them in some way.

UP.japanese: 郷田ひとりだけ姿が見えないと聞いた時は、寝坊したのか、どこかで油を売っているのかと思ったが、親族たちも含めての不在だということになると、もう少し楽観的な考え方に変わって来る。昨夜の親族会議は、下手をすると徹夜となり未だに続いているのではないか。それで、部屋の空気も澱んできたので、頭を冷やそう等ということになり、この雨の中、ぞろぞろと散歩に出ている可能性も考えられた。…頭を冷やそう、等という辺りは、実に蔵臼が好んで言いそうな言葉だった。多分、郷田も何かの世話に呼ばれ同行しているのだろう。
UP.translation: When she had heard that Gohda alone was missing, she had thought that he might have slept in or was loafing around somewhere, but once she heard that several of the relatives were also missing, she began to start thinking a little more optimistically. Last night's family conference might have continued all night, and in fact might still be going on. It would then be imaginable that they had wanted to cool off their heads after being in that stuffy room, and had all gone off on a group walk through the rain. ...The part about "cooling off their heads" really sounded like something Krauss would like to say. Probably, Gohda had been called to go with them to aid them with something.

findings.sourceReading: Her thinking shifts to something a little more optimistic.
findings.alternative: The reassuring conference/walk hypotheses that follow recover the emotional direction in context. That mitigates this local loss rather than supplying the missing comparative meaning in the sentence.

findings.description: Japanese says the facts cannot be known unless the police investigate. English substitutes until police arrive and assigns the future knowledge specifically to Nanjo. Arrival alone is not the investigative step named by the source.

contexts.japanese:
南條は医者らしく冷静に、少し見ただけでは何もわからない、
警察が調べなければわからないと繰り返すのだった。
contexts.japanesePC: 南條は医者らしく冷静に、少し見ただけでは何もわからない、警察が調べなければわからないと繰り返すのだった。
contexts.japanesePS3:
南條は医者らしく冷静に、少し見ただけでは何もわからない、
警察が調べなければわからないと繰り返すのだった。
contexts.WH: but Nanjo, in a calm doctor-like manner, kept repeating that nothing could be understood by only glancing at the scene, and that until the police arrived, he wouldn't know anything.
contexts.MG:
but the latter kept repeating in a calm, doctor-like manner that nothing could be understood by only glancing at the scene,
and that until the police arrived, they wouldn't learn anything.
contexts.UP:
but Nanjo, in a calm doctorly manner, kept repeating that nothing could be understood by only glancing at the scene,
and that until the police arrived, he wouldn't know anything.
contexts.note: Both police arriving instead of investigation.

MG.japanese: 秀吉はそわそわしながら、先ほどの惨状を思い出しては、信じられない、この世のものとは思えない、悪魔の仕業やと呟き続けている。それらを時々、問い掛けの形に変えて南條にぶつけていたが、南條は医者らしく冷静に、少し見ただけでは何もわからない、警察が調べなければわからないと繰り返すのだった。
MG.translation: Hideyoshi kept on fidgeting, and every time he remembered that horrible scene, he started muttering about how he couldn't believe it, how it couldn't have been something from this world, how it must have been the work of demons. Every now and then, his mutterings produced a question directed at Nanjo, but the latter kept repeating in a calm, doctor-like manner that nothing could be understood by only glancing at the scene, and that until the police arrived, they wouldn't learn anything.

UP.japanese: 秀吉はそわそわしながら、先ほどの惨状を思い出しては、信じられない、この世のものとは思えない、悪魔の仕業やと呟き続けている。それらを時々、問い掛けの形に変えて南條にぶつけていたが、南條は医者らしく冷静に、少し見ただけでは何もわからない、警察が調べなければわからないと繰り返すのだった。
UP.translation: Hideyoshi, fidgeting as he remembered that horrible scene, kept muttering. Unbelievable—That can't be somethin' of this world—It's the work of the devil. Every once in a while, he turned these into questions and bounced them off Nanjo, but Nanjo, in a calm doctorly manner, kept repeating that nothing could be understood by only glancing at the scene, and that until the police arrived, he wouldn't know anything.

findings.sourceReading: Only police investigation can clarify the scene; a brief look is insufficient.
findings.alternative: Investigation is an expected consequence of police arrival, and the earlier brief-look caveat survives. Nevertheless the sentence changes the explicit evidentiary prerequisite. No claim of a different actual police procedure or an unsolvable mystery follows.

findings.description: 気付きもしなかったという方 refers to taking the position that she never even noticed the prank. WH better if she did not notice omits the presentation/pretence, despite her having plainly noticed and ordered it cleaned.

contexts.japanese: むしろ、こんな悪戯がされていたこと自体、気付きもしなかったという方がかえっていいに違いない。
contexts.japanesePC: むしろ、こんな悪戯がされていたこと自体、気付きもしなかったという方がかえっていいに違いない。
contexts.japanesePS3: むしろ、こんな悪戯がされていたこと自体、気付きもしなかったという方がかえっていいに違いない。
contexts.WH: On the contrary, after having such a prank played on her, it would definitely be better if she didn't notice it.
contexts.MG: In fact, it would surely be better to act as though she hadn't even realized that such a prank had been played on her.
contexts.UP: On the contrary, it would definitely be better for her to say she hadn't even noticed that such a prank had been played in the first place.
contexts.note: MG act as though/UP say not noticed preserves feigned ignorance.

MG.japanese: このような幼稚かつ不愉快な悪戯を一体誰が！夏妃は大体の想像がついていたが、どうせ証拠などないし、詰め寄ってものらりくらりで独り相撲になるだろうと思った。むしろ、こんな悪戯がされていたこと自体、気付きもしなかったという方がかえっていいに違いない。夏妃は、綺麗に汚れを落としておくようにと改めて命じると、踵を鳴らしながら客間へ向かうのだった。
MG.translation: Who in the world would pull such a childish and disgusting prank?! Natsuhi had a pretty good idea, but of course there was no proof, so even if she pushed the issue, it would just seem as though she was making a fuss about nothing. In fact, it would surely be better to act as though she hadn't even realized that such a prank had been played on her. Natsuhi gave the order to have it cleaned and headed off to the parlor with a squeak of her heels.

UP.japanese: このような幼稚かつ不愉快な悪戯を一体誰が！夏妃は大体の想像がついていたが、どうせ証拠などないし、詰め寄ってものらりくらりで独り相撲になるだろうと思った。むしろ、こんな悪戯がされていたこと自体、気付きもしなかったという方がかえっていいに違いない。夏妃は、綺麗に汚れを落としておくようにと改めて命じると、踵を鳴らしながら客間へ向かうのだった。
UP.translation: Who in the world would pull such a childish and disgusting prank! Natsuhi had a pretty good idea, but of course there was no proof, so even if she pushed the issue, it would just seem as though she was making a fuss about nothing. On the contrary, it would definitely be better for her to say she hadn't even noticed that such a prank had been played in the first place. Natsuhi gave the order to have it cleaned, and headed off to the parlor with clacking heels.

findings.sourceReading: It would be better to act as though she had never noticed it.
findings.alternative: The reader can infer deliberate ignoring from her cleanup order and avoidance of confrontation. That mitigates the loss, but does not convey her chosen public response in the disputed sentence.

findings.alternative: Across the entire body can loosely describe widespread distribution, and Nanjo immediately disclaims forensic expertise. Still, the explicit near-total qualifier is lost; the broader caveat does not restore that extent qualifier.

UP.japanese: 「探偵権限。……探偵は全ての現場を検証する権利を持つ。そこを退きなさい、右代宮戦人。これはニンゲン側に認められた、ゲームの正当な権利よ」
UP.translation: "Detective's authority. ......The detective has the right to investigate all crime scenes. Move out of the way, Ushiromiya Battler. This is my legitimate right within the game, as granted to the Humanhuman side."

findings.sourceReading: This is a legitimate right of the game granted to the human side.
findings.alternative: に can mark the agent of a passive, but the detective’s asserted entitlement and the higher-plane enforcement immediately following make the granted-to reading coherent. Human-side acknowledgment adds a source of recognition absent from this entitlement formulation. The preceding unqualified detective inspection right limits the practical impact.
findings.sourceNote: Original Witch Hunt is compared with the original-PC Japanese embedded in the historical patches. MangaGamer uses the accepted MangaGamer-based Witch Hunt backport, and Umineko Project uses its repository English; both are compared with maintained PS3-derived Japanese. The MangaGamer and PS3 witnesses are not independently certified retail extractions.

findings.description: Japanese makes Erika and her sympathizers the people Battler cannot forgive. English places those who sympathized with her after cornering Natsuhi, making them additional targets of Erika’s harassment, with her naturally referring to Natsuhi. The accomplice group disappears from the object of Battler’s anger.

UP.translation: He wasn't feeling compassion for Natsuhi because her lie was about to be exposed. However, he couldn't forgive Erika, who was simply enjoying the "intellectual rape" of cornering Natsuhi, or any of the people going along with her. Then, he whispered softly.

findings.sourceReading: He cannot forgive Erika, who enjoys cornering Natsuhi, or those who side with Erika.
findings.alternative: A reader familiar with the scene could infer Erika’s allies, but the English syntax joins Natsuhi and those who sympathized with her as objects of cornering. The preceding sentence explicitly places Eva and others alongside Erika; it mitigates but does not repair the coordination in the anger explanation.

contexts.japanese:
その時、楼座の脳裏に昨日の出来事が蘇る…。
……そうだ、
……あの魔女は薔薇庭園で出会った時、
…真里亞に、封筒を渡していなかったっけ。
そうだ、間違いない、渡していた。
開けようとする真里亞に、まだ開けるなと言ってから、
“それを開ける時はすぐ訪れる”と、確かに言っていた…。
楼座は確信する。
……間違いない。
……真里亞に渡された、あの封筒…………。
楼座はゲストハウスへ駆けて戻ると、足音を忍ばせながらいとこ部屋に近付き、
そっと扉を開け、中をうかがう…。
中からは、若者らしい元気のいいいびきが聞こえてきた。
子どもたちは４人いる。
真里亞もいる。
…すやすやと眠っていた。
ほっと胸を撫で下ろしてから、忍び足で室内に入る。
……目指すのは、ソファーの上に置かれている真里亞の手提げだった。
真里亞は、自分の宝物をいつも持ち歩きたがる。
…母親が常に化粧道具を肌身離さず持ち歩いていることの模倣だろう。
もちろん、単なる物真似だから、その中身はがらくたばかりだ。
真里亞の場合は、オカルトを想起させる不気味な小物や、それが記された自由帳などだ。
……こんな女の子らしくないものを、楼座は持ち歩いて欲しいなどと思ったことは一度もない。
しかし、無理にやめさせようとして、ものすごい大喧嘩をして以来、それには触れないようにしていた。
「………………………、…あった。
………これね………」
黄金の鷲の紋章の入った洋形封筒…。
取り出してみると、中に重たい棒状の物が入っているのがわかった。
…重さと手触りでわかる。
……間違いない。
これは、……鍵だ。
楼座は、一度振り返り、真里亞が熟睡しているのを確認した後、
一息に封筒を破き、中身を手の平の上に零した。
……それは、古く凝った意匠の施された鍵だった…。

contexts.WH: ......That letter which had been handed to Maria............
contexts.MG:
At that time, the events of the previous day swirled around in the back of Rosa's mind...
......That's right,
...when I met that witch in the rose garden,
...didn't she hand Maria an envelope?
Yeah, there's no mistake, she did hand it over.
When Maria tried to open it, the witch told her not to do it yet, and then she surely said:
"The time to open that will come soon"...
Rosa was sure.
...There could be no mistake.
...The envelope Maria had received was......
After dashing back to the guesthouse, Rosa approached the cousins' room while hiding her footsteps,
softly opened the door, and peered inside...
From the inside, she could hear the healthy snores typical of young people.
There were four children.
And Maria was there.
...Sleeping soundly.
After breathing a sigh of relief, she entered the room with quiet footsteps.
...She was after Maria's handbag, which was resting on the sofa.
Maria always liked carrying her treasures around with her.
...She was probably emulating how her mother always carried her makeup with her.
Of course, she was just imitating her mother, so everything on the inside was junk.
In Maria's case, it was full of small, creepy, occult items, notebooks describing things of that nature, and so on.
...Rosa had never been happy to see her daughter walking around with things like that, which weren't girlish at all.
However, trying to force Maria to stop had resulted in a big fight, so she'd decided to let it be.
".........Here.
......This is it......"
A Western envelope with the crest of the gold eagle...
When she took it out of the bag, she realized there was a heavy, vaguely cylindrical object inside.
...She could tell by its feel and its weight.
...There was no doubt.
This was...a key.
After turning around and checking that Maria was still sound asleep,
Rosa tore open the envelope, and the contents spilled out into her palm.
...It was a key with an old and intricate design...
contexts.UP:
Then the events of the previous day swirled around in the back of Rosa's mind...
......That's right,
......when I met that witch in the rose garden,
...didn't she hand Maria an envelope?
Yes, I'm positive, she did.
When Maria had tried to open it, that witch had told her not to do that yet, and then she had definitely said,
"The time will come soon to open it"...
Rosa became convinced.
......There could be no doubt.
......That letter which had been handed to Maria............
After dashing back to the guesthouse, Rosa approached the cousins' room while hiding her footsteps,
softly opened the door, and peered inside...
From the inside, she could hear the healthy snores of young people.
The four children were all there.
Maria was there.
...Sleeping soundly.
After heaving a sigh of relief, she entered the room with quiet footsteps.
......She was after Maria's handbag, which was resting on the sofa.
Maria always liked walking around with her treasures.
...She was probably imitating how her mother always carried her makeup with her.
Of course, she was just copying her, so on the inside, it was full of junk.
In Maria's case, it was full of small, creepy, occult‐like items, and a notebook with things like that written in it.
......Rosa hadn't once been happy to see her daughter walking around with those kinds of ungirlish things.
However, after she had tried to force Maria to stop, they had gotten into a big fight, and she had decided to let it be.
"........................... ...Here it is.
.........This is it........."
A Western envelope with the crest of the gold eagle...
When she took it out, she could tell that there was a heavy, cylindrical object inside.
...She could tell by its feel and its weight.
......There was no doubt.
This was......a key.
After turning around and checking that Maria was still sound asleep,
Rosa tore open the envelope, and tipped out the contents into her palm.
......It was a key with an old and intricate design...

MG.translation: "...It seems everyone is tired after all that has happened. ...In times like this, I think the best thing is to heat yourself with some warm black tea."

UP.japanese: 「…皆さんもいろいろあってお疲れでしょう。……こういう時は温かい紅茶で体を温めるのが一番ですよ」
UP.translation: "...I imagine you all must be tired after all that has happened. ......In times like this, I think the best thing is to heat yourself with some warm black tea."

findings.sourceReading: At a time like this, warming yourselves up with some hot tea would be best.
findings.alternative: Heat and warm overlap semantically, and the drink remains explicit. The English collocation is conspicuously mechanical for ordinary hospitality and for Kumasawa's voice.

findings.description: 私だけが知ってたって意味がない becomes If only I know the truth, that’s pointless, replacing the concessive ‘even if I alone know’ with a wish-like conditional. 死んでわかった then becomes present I know after dying rather than a realization reached upon death.

contexts.japanese:
「……………いいんです。
…お嬢様だけは、真実を知っています」
「私だけが知ってたって意味がないんだよ！！
死んでわかった。
真実ってのは生きてる人間のものだ！！
真実が残らなかったら、死者は報われない！！
何のために嘉音くんが命を懸けたのか、わかんなくなっちゃうッ！！」
contexts.japanesePC: 「私だけが知ってたって意味がないんだよ！！　死んでわかった。真実ってのは生きてる人間のものだ！！　真実が残らなかったら、死者は報われない！！　何のために嘉音くんが命を懸けたのか、わかんなくなっちゃうッ！！」
contexts.japanesePS3:
「……………いいんです。
…お嬢様だけは、真実を知っています」
「私だけが知ってたって意味がないんだよ！！
死んでわかった。
真実ってのは生きてる人間のものだ！！
真実が残らなかったら、死者は報われない！！
何のために嘉音くんが命を懸けたのか、わかんなくなっちゃうッ！！」
contexts.WH: "If only I know the truth, that's pointless!!  I know after dying.  Truth belongs to living humans!!  If the truth doesn't remain, the dead won't be rewarded!!  They won't know why Kanon-kun risked his life!!"
contexts.MG:
"......It's okay.
...At least you know the truth."
"If only I know the truth, that's pointless!!
I know it after dying.
Truth belongs to living humans!!
If the truth doesn't remain, the dead won't be rewarded!!
They won't know what Kanon-kun risked his life for!!"
contexts.UP:
"...............It's alright.
...At least you know the truth, Milady."
"If only I know the truth, that's pointless!!
I found out by dying.
Truth belongs to living humans!!
If the truth doesn't remain, the dead won't be rewarded!!
They won't know why you risked your life!!"
contexts.note: MG retains both If only I know and present I know it after dying. UP retains If only I know but changes the second clause to found out by dying, restoring a completed realization though expressing its trigger freely.

MG.japanese: 「私だけが知ってたって意味がないんだよ！！　死んでわかった。真実ってのは生きてる人間のものだ！！　真実が残らなかったら、死者は報われない！！　何のために嘉音くんが命を懸けたのか、わかんなくなっちゃうッ！！」
MG.translation: "If only I know the truth, that's pointless!! I know it after dying. Truth belongs to living humans!! If the truth doesn't remain, the dead won't be rewarded!! They won't know what Kanon-kun risked his life for!!"

UP.japanese: 「私だけが知ってたって意味がないんだよ！！　死んでわかった。真実ってのは生きてる人間のものだ！！　真実が残らなかったら、死者は報われない！！　何のために嘉音くんが命を懸けたのか、わかんなくなっちゃうッ！！」
UP.translation: "If only I know the truth, that's pointless!! I found out by dying. Truth belongs to living humans!! If the truth doesn't remain, the dead won't be rewarded!! They won't know why you risked your life!!"

findings.sourceReading: Even if Jessica alone knows the truth, that has no value; dying made her understand that truth belongs to the living.
findings.alternative: Context makes Jessica's frustration and post-death realization recoverable. ‘If only’ ordinarily introduces a wish, however, while the source dismisses knowledge confined to herself; present know also weakens the moment of realization expressed by わかった.

findings.description: 魔女は否定する and 何も失う覚悟がない become I denied the witch and I wasn’t prepared to lose anything. Battler’s present self-assessment and continuing commitments are recast as past states.

contexts.japanese:
叔母さんのその眼光は鋭い。
……魔女を否定するためなら、誰だって生贄にする。
…目がそう言っている。
俺は…？
魔女は否定する。
……でも、何も失う覚悟がない。
多分俺は、一番戦っているようなつもりでいて、……一番真実から遠い場所にいる。
contexts.japanesePC:
俺は…？
魔女は否定する。
……でも、何も失う覚悟がない。
contexts.japanesePS3:
叔母さんのその眼光は鋭い。
……魔女を否定するためなら、誰だって生贄にする。
…目がそう言っている。
俺は…？
魔女は否定する。
……でも、何も失う覚悟がない。
多分俺は、一番戦っているようなつもりでいて、……一番真実から遠い場所にいる。
contexts.WH:
And me...?
I denied the witch.
......But I wasn't prepared to lose anything.
contexts.MG:
Aunt Rosa's gaze was sharp.
...In order to deny the witch, she would sacrifice anyone.
...That's what her eyes told me.
And me...?
I denied the witch.
...But I wasn't prepared to lose anything.
I was probably the one who seemed to be fighting the most, ...and yet, the one who was most separated from reality.
contexts.UP:

......In order to deny the witch, she would make anyone a sacrifice.
...That's what her eyes told me.
And me...?
I denied the witch.
......But I wasn't prepared to lose anything.
I was probably the one who thought himself most ready to fight, ......and the one standing furthest from the truth.
contexts.note: Both editions retain past denied and wasn't prepared, recasting Battler's present denial and lack of resolve as retrospective states.

MG.japanese:
俺は…？
魔女は否定する。
……でも、何も失う覚悟がない。多分俺は、一番戦っているようなつもりでいて、……一番真実から遠い場所にいる。
MG.translation: And me...? I denied the witch. ...But I wasn't prepared to lose anything. I was probably the one who seemed to be fighting the most, ...and yet, the one who was most separated from reality.

UP.japanese:
俺は…？
魔女は否定する。
……でも、何も失う覚悟がない。多分俺は、一番戦っているようなつもりでいて、……一番真実から遠い場所にいる。
UP.translation:
And me...?
I denied the witch.
......But I wasn't prepared to lose anything. I was probably the one who thought himself most ready to fight, ......and the one standing furthest from the truth.

findings.sourceReading: Battler still denies the witch, but recognizes that he is not prepared to sacrifice or lose anything in order to sustain that denial.
findings.alternative: The preceding contest can motivate retrospective wording, and the following sentence remains reflective. The Japanese deliberately states his current denial and current lack of resolve before locating him far from the truth.

findings.description: 夜なべをして、チクチクやった becomes worked all night and did it all. Battler’s darkly comic image of Beatrice staying up late stitching away is reduced to unspecified work.

contexts.japanese:
「……兄さんたちが殺されていた最初の殺人。
とても残酷な仕打ちがされていたわよね？
あれがひとりで出来る真似に見える？」
「…………謎の来客、ベアトリーチェさまが夜なべをして、チクチクやったのかもしれねぇぜ」
contexts.japanesePC: 「…………謎の来客、ベアトリーチェさまが夜なべをして、チクチクやったのかもしれねぇぜ。」
contexts.japanesePS3:
「……兄さんたちが殺されていた最初の殺人。
とても残酷な仕打ちがされていたわよね？
あれがひとりで出来る真似に見える？」
「…………謎の来客、ベアトリーチェさまが夜なべをして、チクチクやったのかもしれねぇぜ」
contexts.WH: "............Maybe the mystery guest, Beatrice-sama worked all night, and did it all."
contexts.MG:
...In the first murder, where Nii-san and the others were killed,
they were treated very brutally, right?
Did that look like something that could've been done alone?"
"......Maybe the mystery guest, Beatrice-sama, worked all night and did it all."
contexts.UP:
"......In the first murder, where Nii‐san and the others were killed,
they'd been given a very brutal treatment, right?
Did that look like something that could be done alone?"
"............Maybe our mystery guest Beatrice‐sama worked all night and did it all."
contexts.note: Both editions retain worked all night and did it all, omitting Battler's concrete stitching-away joke.

MG.japanese: 「…………謎の来客、ベアトリーチェさまが夜なべをして、チクチクやったのかもしれねぇぜ」
MG.translation: "......Maybe the mystery guest, Beatrice-sama, worked all night and did it all."

UP.japanese: 「…………謎の来客、ベアトリーチェさまが夜なべをして、チクチクやったのかもしれねぇぜ」
UP.translation: "............Maybe our mystery guest Beatrice‐sama worked all night and did it all."

findings.sourceReading: Battler sarcastically suggests that Beatrice may have stayed up all night painstakingly stitching the elaborate first crime scene together.
findings.alternative: Did it all preserves that she supposedly performed the elaborate work alone, and the surrounding bodies supply context. It removes the needlework wording that gives Battler's retort its concrete macabre joke.

findings.description: 年季の入った粗末なチェスセット becomes a crude chess set which had many years of experience. 年季の入った describes the set as old or well-worn; the translation unnaturally assigns personal experience to the object.

contexts.japanese: 源次と南條は、年季の入った粗末なチェスセットで向かい合っている。
contexts.japanesePC: 源次と南條は、年季の入った粗末なチェスセットで向かい合っている。
contexts.japanesePS3: 源次と南條は、年季の入った粗末なチェスセットで向かい合っている。
contexts.WH: Genji and Nanjo were facing each other across a crude chess set which had many years of experience.
contexts.MG: Genji and Nanjo were facing each other across a crude chess set that had many years of experience.
contexts.UP: Genji and Nanjo were facing each other across a crude chess set which had seen many years.
contexts.note: MG changes which to that but still gives the chess set years of experience. UP says the set had seen many years, restoring an idiomatic age description.

MG.japanese: 源次と南條は、年季の入った粗末なチェスセットで向かい合っている。…まだまだ始まったばかり。そして年季の入ったプレイヤーの序盤は限りなく洗練されているため、互いが決まった順序で決められた駒を動かすだけの儀式のように見えた。
MG.translation: Genji and Nanjo were facing each other across a crude chess set that had many years of experience. ...The game had still only just begun. And, because the opening game of these experienced players had been honed to perfection, it looked like a ceremony where they just moved specified pieces in a specified order.

UP.japanese: 源次と南條は、年季の入った粗末なチェスセットで向かい合っている。…まだまだ始まったばかり。そして年季の入ったプレイヤーの序盤は限りなく洗練されているため、互いが決まった順序で決められた駒を動かすだけの儀式のように見えた。
UP.translation: Genji and Nanjo were facing each other across a crude chess set which had seen many years. ...It had still only just begun. And because the opening game of the experienced players had been endlessly refined, it looked like a ritual where they just moved specified pieces in a specified order.

findings.sourceReading: Genji and Nanjo face each other across an old, well-worn, unpretentious chess set.
findings.alternative: The surrounding chess scene makes the intended age and familiarity recoverable, and English sometimes personifies old objects. Had many years of experience remains an unidiomatic rendering of the set's accumulated age and wear.

findings.description: その可能性はありえない becomes that possibility wasn't possible, an avoidable tautology rather than that possibility was inconceivable or could not be true.

contexts.japanese: しかし、その可能性はありえない…。
contexts.japanesePC: しかし、その可能性はありえない…。
contexts.japanesePS3: しかし、その可能性はありえない…。
contexts.WH: However, that possibility wasn't possible...
contexts.MG: However, that possibility was impossible...
contexts.UP: However, that possibility wasn't possible...
contexts.note: MG revises wasn't possible to was impossible but preserves the possibility/impossible tautology. UP retains the original wording exactly.

MG.japanese:
郷田は恐る恐る勝手口に近付きながら声を掛ける。
……そして、近くの流しに置いてある肉切り包丁の位置を目で確認する。……まだ手には取らない。
家人の誰かの可能性もあるから。
しかし、その可能性はありえない…。
MG.translation: As Gohda fearfully approached the back door, he called out. ...And his eyes flashed towards the butcher's knife that sat in a nearby sink. ...He didn't pick it up yet. Because there was still a possibility that this was a member of the family. However, that possibility was impossible...

UP.japanese:
郷田は恐る恐る勝手口に近付きながら声を掛ける。
……そして、近くの流しに置いてある肉切り包丁の位置を目で確認する。……まだ手には取らない。
家人の誰かの可能性もあるから。
しかし、その可能性はありえない…。
UP.translation:
As Gohda fearfully approached the back door, he called out.
......And he checked with his eyes the location of a butcher's knife set on a nearby sink. ......He didn't pick it up yet.
Because there was still a possibility that this was a member of the family.
However, that possibility wasn't possible...

findings.sourceReading: The narration considers a member of the household as a possible visitor, then rejects that possibility as inconceivable under the circumstances.
findings.alternative: The intended rejection is still completely clear, so this is an English-expression defect rather than a change in the reasoning.

findings.description: 納品書 becomes statements of delivery. The documents are delivery slips or delivery notes whose envelopes are opened with the knife, not statements about delivery.

contexts.japanese: …それは、納品書や請求書の封筒を開けるのに、ペーパーナイフ代わりにしていたものだった。
contexts.japanesePC: …それは、納品書や請求書の封筒を開けるのに、ペーパーナイフ代わりにしていたものだった。
contexts.japanesePS3: …それは、納品書や請求書の封筒を開けるのに、ペーパーナイフ代わりにしていたものだった。
contexts.WH: ...It was something to be used instead of a paper knife to open envelopes for statements of delivery and bills.
contexts.MG: ...It was something to be used instead of a paper knife to open envelopes for statements of delivery and bills.
contexts.UP: ...It was something to be used instead of a paper knife to open envelopes for invoices and bills.
contexts.note: MG retains statements of delivery. UP substitutes invoices, which is idiomatic English but still changes the delivery note into a billing document alongside the separately named bills.

MG.japanese:
源次はチェスの脇に置かれていた文房具箱の中にあったクラシックなデザインのナイフを取る。…それは、納品書や請求書の封筒を開けるのに、ペーパーナイフ代わりにしていたものだった。しかし本来はナイフ。
だからそれには人を傷付ける刃が付けられている…。
MG.translation: Genji took a knife with a classical design from a stationary box placed near the chess set. ...It was something to be used instead of a paper knife to open envelopes for statements of delivery and bills. But it was still a knife. So the blade on it could injure someone...

UP.japanese:
源次はチェスの脇に置かれていた文房具箱の中にあったクラシックなデザインのナイフを取る。…それは、納品書や請求書の封筒を開けるのに、ペーパーナイフ代わりにしていたものだった。しかし本来はナイフ。

UP.translation:

So the blade on it could injure someone...

findings.sourceReading: The knife serves as a letter opener for envelopes containing delivery slips and invoices.
findings.alternative: Statements of delivery points generally toward delivery paperwork and does not disrupt the action, but it is not the ordinary document named by 納品書.

findings.description: だからそれは誰のことなの becomes Like I said, who are you talking about? The connective means then or so in her demand for the person's identity; Like I said invents a callback to wording Rosa did not previously use.

何か恐ろしいものを見て、それが受け容れられなくて混乱しているのか、…見当もつかなかった。

findings.alternative: Holding his head and scratching still communicates agitation, and the following narration explains his profound confusion. The physical intensity is reduced.

そして使用人室に運び手当てした。

...And after that, something terrifying had happened.

MG.japanese:
厨房の勝手口に大怪我をした嘉音くんが現れた。
そして使用人室に運び手当てした。……そして、恐ろしい何かが起こった。嘉音くんがそんなことをしてのけるとは想像できなくて、あれが本当に嘉音くんだったのか疑わしくなった。というところなのか。

Then, he had been taken to the servant room and cared for. ...And after that, something terrifying had happened. UP.japanese:
厨房の勝手口に大怪我をした嘉音くんが現れた。

UP.translation:
Kanon‐kun had appeared from the back door in the kitchen with a serious injury.
Then he had been taken to the servant room and cared for. ......Then, something terrifying had happened. Since these people couldn't imagine that Kanon‐kun could have pulled that off, they had started to suspect whether that really had been Kanon‐kun. Is that how things are?

findings.sourceReading: The charitable reconstruction is that the seriously wounded Kanon appeared at the kitchen's back door and was then carried to the servant room.
findings.alternative: The prior detailed testimony says someone came to the door and Gohda opened it, making emergence through the doorway a natural reconstruction. This summary itself uses a locative に rather than a route marker.

findings.description: 南條先生の遺体が安置された becomes Doctor Nanjo's body had been enshrined. In this practical crime-scene account 安置 means that the body was laid or left at rest in the room; enshrined introduces religious or commemorative treatment.

contexts.japanese:
二人目は、……多分、所在不明の１９人目、ベアトリーチェだ。
ヤツは、予め使用人室のベッドの下に隠れ、ここに南條先生の遺体が安置されたまま、源次さんたちが立ち去るのを待っていた。
そしてその後に這い出て、南條先生のポケットからマスターキーを取り返し、何かの理由で二人の遺体を運び去った。
そしてマスターキーで施錠すれば、この密室の出来上がりってわけだ。
contexts.japanesePC: ヤツは、予め使用人室のベッドの下に隠れ、ここに南條先生の遺体が安置されたまま、源次さんたちが立ち去るのを待っていた。
contexts.japanesePS3:
二人目は、……多分、所在不明の１９人目、ベアトリーチェだ。
ヤツは、予め使用人室のベッドの下に隠れ、ここに南條先生の遺体が安置されたまま、源次さんたちが立ち去るのを待っていた。
そしてその後に這い出て、南條先生のポケットからマスターキーを取り返し、何かの理由で二人の遺体を運び去った。
そしてマスターキーで施錠すれば、この密室の出来上がりってわけだ。
contexts.WH: That person had hidden under the bed in the servant room beforehand, and while Doctor Nanjo's body had been enshrined here, that person had waited for Genji-san and the rest to leave.
contexts.MG:
The second person was...probably the 19th person, Beatrice, whose location was unknown.
That person hid under the bed in the servant room beforehand, and while Doctor Nanjo's body was enshrined here, they waited for Genji-san and the rest to leave.
Then later, they crawled out, took the master key back from Doctor Nanjo's pocket, and carried the two corpses away for some reason.
If they then locked the door with the master key, you'd end up with this closed room.
contexts.UP:
The second person was......probably the 19th person, Beatrice, whose location was unknown.
She had hidden under the bed in the servant room beforehand, and with Doctor Nanjo's body still enshrined here, she had waited for Genji‐san and the rest to leave.
Then after that, she had crawled out, taken the master key back from Doctor Nanjo's pocket, and carried the two bodies away for some reason.
If she had then locked the door with the master key, this locked room would be created.
contexts.note: Both retain enshrined for the body lying in the room; MG changes the surrounding tense and pronouns.

MG.japanese: ヤツは、予め使用人室のベッドの下に隠れ、ここに南條先生の遺体が安置されたまま、源次さんたちが立ち去るのを待っていた。そしてその後に這い出て、南條先生のポケットからマスターキーを取り返し、何かの理由で二人の遺体を運び去った。そしてマスターキーで施錠すれば、この密室の出来上がりってわけだ。
MG.translation: That person hid under the bed in the servant room beforehand, and while Doctor Nanjo's body was enshrined here, they waited for Genji-san and the rest to leave. findings.description: 嘉音の面影 describes Kanon's likeness or recognizable image in the transformed goat attendant. Kanon's face narrows the resemblance to one body part.

contexts.japanese:
魔女が指を弾くと、……６人いた山羊の従者の１人の姿が、……金色の輝きと共に嘉音に変わる。
それは間違いなく目を疑う光景。
…間違いなくそれは嘉音の面影。
……しかし、その瞳には、嘉音が浮かべていた誠実な輝きはまるでない。
…魔女の命令に従うだけの家具の、濁った目があるだけだ。
contexts.japanesePC: …間違いなくそれは嘉音の面影。
contexts.japanesePS3:
魔女が指を弾くと、……６人いた山羊の従者の１人の姿が、……金色の輝きと共に嘉音に変わる。
それは間違いなく目を疑う光景。
…間違いなくそれは嘉音の面影。
……しかし、その瞳には、嘉音が浮かべていた誠実な輝きはまるでない。
…魔女の命令に従うだけの家具の、濁った目があるだけだ。
contexts.WH: ...It was definitely Kanon's face.
contexts.MG:
When the witch snapped her fingers, ...one of the six goat attendants...glittered gold and changed into Kanon.
It was definitely a sight to make one doubt their eyes.
...It was definitely Kanon's face.
...However, in those eyes, the glint of Kanon's integrity was nowhere to be seen.
...They were the hazy eyes of furniture that only obeyed the orders of the witch.
contexts.UP:
When the witch snapped her fingers, ......one of the six goat attendants......glittered gold and changed into Kanon.
It was definitely a sight to make one doubt their eyes.
...It was definitely Kanon's face.
......However, in those eyes, there was none of that sincere glint of Kanon's.
...They were only the clouded eyes of furniture that did nothing but obey the orders of the witch.
contexts.note: Both editions retain It was definitely Kanon's face, narrowing the transformed attendant's recognizable likeness to his face.

MG.japanese:
魔女が指を弾くと、……６人いた山羊の従者の１人の姿が、……金色の輝きと共に嘉音に変わる。それは間違いなく目を疑う光景。
…間違いなくそれは嘉音の面影。……しかし、その瞳には、嘉音が浮かべていた誠実な輝きはまるでない。…魔女の命令に従うだけの家具の、濁った目があるだけだ。
MG.translation: When the witch snapped her fingers, ...one of the six goat attendants...glittered gold and changed into Kanon. UP.japanese:
魔女が指を弾くと、……６人いた山羊の従者の１人の姿が、……金色の輝きと共に嘉音に変わる。それは間違いなく目を疑う光景。
…間違いなくそれは嘉音の面影。……しかし、その瞳には、嘉音が浮かべていた誠実な輝きはまるでない。…魔女の命令に従うだけの家具の、濁った目があるだけだ。
UP.translation:
When the witch snapped her fingers, ......one of the six goat attendants......glittered gold and changed into Kanon. It was definitely a sight to make one doubt their eyes.
...It was definitely Kanon's face. ......However, in those eyes, there was none of that sincere glint of Kanon's. ...They were only the clouded eyes of furniture that did nothing but obey the orders of the witch.

findings.sourceReading: The transformed attendant unmistakably bears Kanon's likeness, although the narration and Shannon continue to identify it as an impostor.
findings.alternative: Face can stand metonymically for a person's recognizable appearance, and the surrounding transformation remains clear. The English nevertheless localizes the resemblance more narrowly than 面影.

findings.description: 螺旋状に刻まれた溝 is a groove carved in a spiral into the small stake. Ditch denotes a much larger channel in the ground and misdescribes the object's surface detail.

contexts.japanese:
全長は多分、３０ｃｍあるかないか。
青銅とか鉄とか、そういう類のもので出来ているのだろう。
手に触れずとも重みのあるものであることがわかる。
握りと、円錐部分で構成されていて、明らかに刺すための武器として作られたものだとわかる。
例えるなら、西洋騎士が使う騎乗槍をミニチュアにしたような感じなのか。
螺旋状に刻まれた溝は、あるいは小さなドリルのようにも見えた。
……しかし、握りの部分には、オカルト染みた、悪魔か何かの意匠が施されていて、

几帳面な夏妃伯母さんの部屋とは思えない荒らされようだった。

findings.description: それを尻目に means Battler enters the parlor on his own while disregarding Rosa's continuing inspection or watching it sidelong. Entered the parlor behind her turns the idiom into a spatial relation.

contexts.japanese:
…楼座叔母さんは、自分が全てのマスターキーを持っているにもかかわらず、再び念入りに客間内の確認を始めた。
カーテンを開け、窓の施錠を再び確認している。
それを見る俺は、……何というのか、もうどうでもいい気分だった。
余計なことを言えばまた喧嘩になる。
俺はしばらくの間、その様子を廊下で眺め、もうそろそろいいかなと思い、それを尻目に勝手に客間に入る。
……死者以外は誰も信用できないというなら、その手に持っている銃で、みんなを殺して回ればいいんだ。
そしたら最後には自分が狼であることに気付く。
…そして最後の狼の頭を、自分でブチ抜いて、このおかしな殺人劇に幕を下ろせばいい…。

contexts.WH: For a while, I gazed at her from the corridor, figured I had waited just about long enough, and entered the parlor behind her.
contexts.MG:
...Even though Aunt Rosa still held all of the master keys herself, she thoroughly checked the inside of the parlor again.
She opened the curtains and checked again to make sure the windows were locked.
As I watched...how should I say it, I felt like it didn't really matter anymore.
If I said anything careless, it would turn into another fight.
For a while, I gazed at her from the corridor, figured I'd waited just about long enough, and entered the parlor behind her.
...If she doesn't trust anyone but the dead, why doesn't she just go around killing everyone with the gun she's got in her hand?
And then, in the end, she'll realize that she herself is the wolf.
...Then she can just blast through the head of the final wolf and close the curtain on this insane murder drama...

If I said anything unnecessary, it would turn into another fight.

findings.description: 巨漢の山羊頭 is one giant goat-headed pursuer. Giant goat heads and they pluralize that attacker, and the plural continues through the four gunshots and charge.

contexts.japanese:
だが追っ手はまだ来る！
薔薇の茂みの向こうから、ニンゲンのふりをするのにも飽きた巨漢の山羊頭が走り来るのが見えた。
楼座は上着のポケットの中に入っていた予備の銃弾を何発かバラバラと零し、真里亞に拾うように命じる。
「う、うん…！
拾う、拾う…！！」
「真里亞。
ママがもし倒れたら。
あなたは走りなさい。
海岸へ行くの。
そして泳いで泳いで泳ぎなさい！
この島のどこにも、生き延びることのできる場所はないッ！！」
「や、やだッ！！
ママと一緒ッ！！
うーーッ！！」
楼座の銃が四度咆哮した。
迫り来る巨漢の山羊の胸板に確かに四発を着弾させたが、相手はまったくそれに怯んでいない！！
その巨体で押し潰すつもりかのように猛烈な勢いで駆けてくる！！

contexts.WH: But the pursuers were still coming!  They could see the giant goat heads, who had given up pretending to be human, running towards them from across the rose bushes.
contexts.MG:
But the pursuers were still coming!
They could see the giant goat heads, who had given up pretending to be Human, running towards them from across the rose bushes.
Rosa spilled several extra bullets, which had been in the pocket of her coat, all over the place, and told Maria to pick them up.
"Y-Yes...!
Pick up, pick up...!!"
"Maria,
if Mama falls down,
run.
Go to the shore.
And swim, and swim, and swim!
There's nowhere for us to survive on this island!!"
"N-No!!
I'll stay with Mama!!
Uuu--!!"
Rosa's gun roared four times.
But even though four shots really did hit the massive, approaching goats in the chest, they didn't even flinch!!
The goats ran with a violent vigor, as though they planned to crush Rosa and Maria with those massive bodies!!
contexts.UP:

They could see the giant goat‐heads, who had given up even pretending to be Humanhuman, running towards them from across the rose bushes.

"Y‐yes...!
Pick up, pick up...!!"
"Maria.
If Mama falls down,
run.
Go to the shore.
And swim, and swim, and swim!
There's no place on this island where we can survive!!"
"N‐no!!
Together with Mama!!
Uuu!!"
Rosa's gun roared four times.
But even though she really did land four shots in the chest of the massive, approaching goat, it didn't even flinch!!
The goat ran with a violent vigor, as though it planned to crush Rosa and Maria with its massive body!!
contexts.note: MG pluralizes the single giant pursuer throughout its charge and the four hits. UP consistently uses one goat-headed attacker.

findings.sourceReading: A single huge goat-headed pursuer runs from beyond the rose bushes; Rosa lands four shots in its chest, but it continues charging.
findings.alternative: Other pursuers are present before and after this encounter, so the plural does not invent the existence of a group overall.

findings.description: 頭部をつんのめらせた describes the goat-headed figure with its head pitched or knocked forward. As it fell over makes the whole figure fall before the later line where it finally crashes to the ground.

contexts.japanese:
楼座は懐より万年筆を抜く。
でも持ち方が歪だった。
手の平で押さえ込み、
握り拳の中指と薬指の間から突き出す様はまるで拳から生えた毒針。
その毒針が、頭部をつんのめらせた山羊頭の左目に突き刺さる。
山羊頭の咆哮は悲鳴か。
しかし楼座の咆哮は違う。
続いて繰り出される掌が目に突き刺さったままの万年筆を打ち抜くのだ。
その先端が頭部の深奥を確かにえぐり破壊する…！
「ママッ、弾が入った！！」
「上出来！！」
真里亞が投げる銃を受け取った時、ようやく巨漢が大地に伏せる轟音がする。

contexts.WH: That stinger sliced into the left eye of the goat head as it fell over.  Was the goat head's roar a scream?
contexts.MG:
Rosa pulled a fountain pen from her pocket.
But she held it crooked.
She placed it in her palm,
in the gap between her middle finger and her ring finger so that it stuck out when she made a fist, almost like a stinger was growing out of it.
That stinger sliced into the left eye of the goat head as it fell over.
Was the goat head's roar a scream?
But Rosa's roar was different.
She pulled back her fist and slammed it into the fountain pen that was still sticking into the goat head's eye.
The pointed tip was gouged into the depths of its head...!
"Mama, the bullet went in!!"
"Good job!!"
As I grabbed the gun Maria had thrown, I finally heard the thunderous crash of the giant tumbling to earth.
contexts.UP:
Rosa pulled a fountain pen from her pocket.
But she held it crooked.
She placed it in her palm,
in the gap between her middle finger and her ring finger, so that it stuck out when she made a fist, almost like it was a stinger growing out.
She jabbed that stinger into the left eye of the goat‐head as its head toppled forward.
Was the goat‐head's roar a scream?
But Rosa's roar was different.
She pulled back her fist and slammed it into the fountain pen that was still sticking into the goat‐head's eye.
The pointed tip was gouged destructively into the depths of its head...!
"Mama, bullets in!!"
"Good job!!"
As I grabbed the gun Maria had thrown, I finally heard the thunderous crash of the giant tumbling to earth.
contexts.note: MG makes the whole goat fall while the pen first enters its eye. UP limits the motion to its head toppling forward before the later bodily crash.

MG.japanese:
楼座は懐より万年筆を抜く。でも持ち方が歪だった。手の平で押さえ込み、握り拳の中指と薬指の間から突き出す様はまるで拳から生えた毒針。その毒針が、頭部をつんのめらせた山羊頭の左目に突き刺さる。
山羊頭の咆哮は悲鳴か。しかし楼座の咆哮は違う。続いて繰り出される掌が目に突き刺さったままの万年筆を打ち抜くのだ。その先端が頭部の深奥を確かにえぐり破壊する…！
MG.translation:
Rosa pulled a fountain pen from her pocket. But she held it crooked. She placed it in her palm, in the gap between her middle finger and her ring finger so that it stuck out when she made a fist, almost like a stinger was growing out of it. That stinger sliced into the left eye of the goat head as it fell over. 
Was the goat head's roar a scream? But Rosa's roar was different. She pulled back her fist and slammed it into the fountain pen that was still sticking into the goat head's eye. The pointed tip was gouged into the depths of its head...!

山羊頭の咆哮は悲鳴か。しかし楼座の咆哮は違う。続いて繰り出される掌が目に突き刺さったままの万年筆を打ち抜くのだ。その先端が頭部の深奥を確かにえぐり破壊する…！

Rosa pulled a fountain pen from her pocket. But she held it crooked. She placed it in her palm, in the gap between her middle finger and her ring finger, so that it stuck out when she made a fist, almost like it was a stinger growing out. She jabbed that stinger into the left eye of the goat‐head as its head toppled forward.
 Was the goat‐head's roar a scream? But Rosa's roar was different. She pulled back her fist and slammed it into the fountain pen that was still sticking into the goat‐head's eye. The pointed tip was gouged destructively into the depths of its head...!

findings.sourceReading: Rosa drives the pen into the left eye while the pursuer’s head pitches forward; only after the follow-up strike does the giant fall to earth.
findings.alternative: The forward pitch may be read as the beginning of the body’s eventual fall.

findings.description: わざわざ曲がりくねらせて距離感を出している says the grove path was deliberately made winding to create a sense of distance. Turned and twisted many times, and only seemed long drops that design or purpose.

しかし楼座は知っている。
この木立の道は、わざわざ曲がりくねらせて距離感を出しているだけなのだ。
まっすぐ突き抜ける！
子どもの頃からずっと遊んでた。
だから知っている！

findings.sourceReading: Rosa knows the path was intentionally made to wind so it would feel longer, allowing her to cut straight through the grove.
findings.alternative: The contrast between its many turns and merely seeming long lets readers infer why the path can be bypassed.

findings.description: 数千万円 means tens of millions of yen. Several ten million is not an idiomatic or grammatical English numeral expression for that value.

contexts.japanese:

すると、客間の中は、…いつの間にか積み上げた黄金のインゴットでいっぱいになっていました。
それは眩い黄金色の壁のようにも見えます。
…インゴットひとつで数千万円の価値があるのだとしたら、
ここにある全てで一体いくらくらいになるというのでしょう。
その数字を知ることすら罪深く感じられるのでした。

findings.description: 蔵臼兄さんと絵羽姉さんが揃っていないと means when Krauss and Eva were not both together or present as a pair. When Krauss and Eva weren’t around narrows this to both being absent.

絵羽姉さんがいない時には絵羽姉さんのようにズルでした。
そして、普段は自分も虐められているくせに、
蔵臼兄さんと絵羽姉さんが揃っていないと、二人分をまとめるかのように私を同じく虐めました。
……だから留弗夫兄さんのこともすごく嫌いでした。

findings.description: それをいつまでも引き摺る means continuing to dwell on, carry, or remain affected by those painful childhood memories. Dragged out forever suggests prolonging a process or story and does not idiomatically express their lingering hold.

contexts.japanese:
……あぁ、でもこれは子どもの頃の記憶のはず。
子どもの頃には少なからずの理不尽なこともあるものです。
そして、それをいつまでも引き摺っていてはいけない。
時と共に記憶の彼方に葬り、それを少しずつ忘れていくのが成長であり、大人になることだったはず。
だから大人になるということは、それら全ての記憶と決別することだったのです。
contexts.japanesePC: そして、それをいつまでも引き摺っていてはいけない。
contexts.japanesePS3:
……あぁ、でもこれは子どもの頃の記憶のはず。
子どもの頃には少なからずの理不尽なこともあるものです。
そして、それをいつまでも引き摺っていてはいけない。
時と共に記憶の彼方に葬り、それを少しずつ忘れていくのが成長であり、大人になることだったはず。
だから大人になるということは、それら全ての記憶と決別することだったのです。
contexts.WH: A large amount of unreasonable things happened when I was a kid.
contexts.MG:
...Oh, but these were my memories from when I was a kid.
It's common for unfair things to happen between kids.
And you mustn't hold onto grudges for such things forever.
With time, those memories get buried away, and forgetting them bit by bit is supposed to be part of growing up and becoming an adult.
So becoming an adult is the same as separating yourself from all those memories.
contexts.UP:
......Oh, but these are my memories from when I was a kid.
Quite a lot of unfair things happen when you're a kid.
And you can't drag them out forever.
In time, you bury them away in the far reaches of memory, and forget them bit by bit; that is supposed to be what it means to grow up, and become an adult.
So becoming an adult is the same thing as separating yourself from all of those memories.
contexts.note: MG replaces dragging memories out with holding onto grudges, which restores lingering but narrows the burden to resentment. UP retains drag them out forever in an active construction.

findings.description: 褒美であると言われても means even if Rosa were told that the altered world was a reward. While you could call it a gift instead assigns the labeling to Rosa and changes the hypothetical explanatory act.

contexts.japanese:
「しかしそれでは、そなたは“兄と姉に苦しめられた記憶”が残らず、
ゆえにそれを以って褒美であると言われても納得はできまい」

contexts.japanesePS3:
「しかしそれでは、そなたは“兄と姉に苦しめられた記憶”が残らず、
ゆえにそれを以って褒美であると言われても納得はできまい」
contexts.WH: "But that way, your 'memories of being hurt by your older siblings' wouldn't remain, and in that sense, while you could call it a gift, you wouldn't be able to accept it."
contexts.MG:
"But that way, your "memories of being hurt by your older siblings" wouldn't remain,
and in that sense, while you might call it a gift, you wouldn't be able to accept it."

"But that way, your "memories of being hurt by your elder siblings" wouldn't remain,
and therefore, you would be unable to acknowledge it as a reward."
contexts.note: MG retains Rosa herself potentially calling the world a gift. UP correctly says she could not acknowledge it as a reward, preserving the externally proposed label.

MG.japanese: 「しかしそれでは、そなたは“兄と姉に苦しめられた記憶”が残らず、ゆえにそれを以って褒美であると言われても納得はできまい」
MG.translation: "But that way, your "memories of being hurt by your older siblings" wouldn't remain, and in that sense, while you might call it a gift, you wouldn't be able to accept it."

UP.japanese: 「しかしそれでは、そなたは“兄と姉に苦しめられた記憶”が残らず、ゆえにそれを以って褒美であると言われても納得はできまい」
UP.translation: "But that way, your "memories of being hurt by your elder siblings" wouldn't remain, and therefore, you would be unable to acknowledge it as a reward."

findings.sourceReading: Without memories of suffering, Rosa would not understand or accept the altered sibling-free world as a reward even if someone described it to her as one.
findings.alternative: English passive accept it leaves room for external persuasion, and the central point that erased suffering cannot be appreciated remains intact.

findings.description: 日々の飽食 refers to an everyday state of plenty or freedom from hunger. Daily gluttony adds culpable overindulgence and changes the young people from beneficiaries of abundance into excessive eaters.

contexts.japanese:
「飢えは癒してこそ満たされる。
飢えそのものをなかったことにしても、誰も感謝しない。
日々の飽食に感謝する若者がいないようにな。
……わかるか？」
contexts.japanesePC: 「飢えは癒してこそ満たされる。飢えそのものをなかったことにしても、誰も感謝しない。日々の飽食に感謝する若者がいないようにな。……わかるか？」
contexts.japanesePS3:
「飢えは癒してこそ満たされる。
飢えそのものをなかったことにしても、誰も感謝しない。
日々の飽食に感謝する若者がいないようにな。
……わかるか？」
contexts.WH: "If starvation is healed, that person is satisfied.  Even if you erase starvation itself, no one will thank you.  Just like how there are no young people who give thanks for their daily gluttony.  ......Understand?"
contexts.MG:
"A person is only satisfied when their starvation is healed.
But if you make it so they never starved in the first place, none of them will thank you.
Just like how there are no young people who give thanks for their daily gluttony.
...Understand?"
contexts.UP:
"It is the relieving of hunger that brings satisfaction.
If you erase hunger itself, no one will thank you.
Just like how there are no young people who give thanks for their daily gluttony.
......Understand?"
contexts.note: Both editions retain daily gluttony and add culpable overindulgence to the analogy about unappreciated abundance.

MG.japanese: 「飢えは癒してこそ満たされる。飢えそのものをなかったことにしても、誰も感謝しない。日々の飽食に感謝する若者がいないようにな。……わかるか？」
MG.translation: "A person is only satisfied when their starvation is healed. But if you make it so they never starved in the first place, none of them will thank you. Just like how there are no young people who give thanks for their daily gluttony. ...Understand?"

UP.japanese: 「飢えは癒してこそ満たされる。飢えそのものをなかったことにしても、誰も感謝しない。日々の飽食に感謝する若者がいないようにな。……わかるか？」
UP.translation: "It is the relieving of hunger that brings satisfaction. If you erase hunger itself, no one will thank you. Just like how there are no young people who give thanks for their daily gluttony. ......Understand?"

findings.sourceReading: Beatrice compares erased hunger to young people failing to feel gratitude for the food abundance they experience every day.
findings.alternative: 飽食 can carry criticism of overconsumption, so gluttony preserves a possible negative edge even though it personalizes the excess.

findings.description: とろける describes the tongue meat becoming meltingly tender in the mouth. Enchanting substitutes emotional charm and loses the food-texture image in both the question and narration.

contexts.japanese:

さぞや柔らかくとろけるであろう？
くっくっくっく！」
それはさぞや口の中で甘く柔らかくとろけるでしょう。
だって、絵羽の嘘はいつも甘く、幼い楼座はいつもそれに耳を貸してしまったのですから。
…だからピリリと胡椒で刺激的に味付けがしてあるのは、その嘘の顛末をよく味で表現していると言えました。

「いいんだよ、嫌々で。

findings.description: 泥を啜ってでも and 泥を啜って literally invoke drinking or slurping mud as the humiliation Battler will endure before rising. Crawling in or through the mud replaces that repeated oral image with movement across the ground.

「だがな、必ず泥を啜って立ち上がる。

何よあれ、あんなの負けでも何でもないんだからぁ！！
あぁ、思い出しただけでもむかむかするわ。
contexts.WH: What's up with that, that wasn't a loss or anything!!  Aaah, just remembering that makes me queasy.
contexts.MG:
...W-Well, last time, right when I felt just a little pity and said she could start with her pieces anywhere she wanted,
that idiot Bern, without taking notice of my compassion, started with all of her pawns on my side of the board!!
What's up with that? That wasn't a loss or anything!!
Aaah, just remembering it makes me queasy.
contexts.UP:
......W‐well, last time, I felt just a little pity and said that she could start her pieces anywhere she wants,
and then that idiot Bern totally didn't pick up on my compassion and started with aaall of her pawns promoted on the eighth rank!!
What's up with that, that wasn't a loss or anything!!
Aaah, just remembering that makes me queasy.
contexts.note: Both editions retain “queasy,” changing Lambdadelta’s anger at the remembered loss into nausea.

MG.japanese: ……ま、まぁ、前回は私がついつい哀れになって好きな場所から駒を進めていいわよって言ったら、ベルンのヤツ、お情けの空気も読めずに手持ちのポーンをぜーんぶ入城させた状態から始めて！！何よあれ、あんなの負けでも何でもないんだからぁ！！　あぁ、思い出しただけでもむかむかするわ。
MG.translation: ...W-Well, last time, right when I felt just a little pity and said she could start with her pieces anywhere she wanted, that idiot Bern, without taking notice of my compassion, started with all of her pawns on my side of the board!! What's up with that? That wasn't a loss or anything!! Aaah, just remembering it makes me queasy.

UP.japanese: ……ま、まぁ、前回は私がついつい哀れになって好きな場所から駒を進めていいわよって言ったら、ベルンのヤツ、お情けの空気も読めずに手持ちのポーンをぜーんぶ入城させた状態から始めて！！何よあれ、あんなの負けでも何でもないんだからぁ！！　あぁ、思い出しただけでもむかむかするわ。
UP.translation: ......W‐well, last time, I felt just a little pity and said that she could start her pieces anywhere she wants, and then that idiot Bern totally didn't pick up on my compassion and started with aaall of her pawns promoted on the eighth rank!! What's up with that, that wasn't a loss or anything!! Aaah, just remembering that makes me queasy.

findings.sourceReading: Lambdadelta insists the prior game did not count as a loss and becomes angry merely remembering Bernkastel’s use of the concession.
findings.alternative: むかむか can literally mean nausea, and queasy can figuratively accompany disgust or indignation.

findings.description: 悪い遊びが過ぎる says Beatrice’s malicious playing around goes too far. She has too much bad fun is unnatural English and turns excessive conduct into possession of a quantity of fun.

contexts.japanese:
手段と目的を時に履き違える。
そして悪い遊びが過ぎる。
その結果、自ら弱点を作り晒してさえいる。
contexts.japanesePC:
手段と目的を時に履き違える。
そして悪い遊びが過ぎる。
その結果、自ら弱点を作り晒してさえいる。
contexts.japanesePS3:
手段と目的を時に履き違える。
そして悪い遊びが過ぎる。
その結果、自ら弱点を作り晒してさえいる。
contexts.WH:
She is sometimes mistaken in her strategy and goals.
And she has too much bad fun.
As a result, she even makes and exposes her own weak points.
contexts.MG:
She sometimes mistakes her means for her ends.
And she has too much dark fun.
Sometimes, that even ends up creating and exposing her own weak points.
contexts.UP:
She sometimes mistakes the means for the end.
And she has too much bad fun.
As a result, she makes and even exposes her own weak points.
contexts.note: Both editions retain the unnatural “too much bad fun,” blurring the claim that Beatrice lets malicious play go too far.

MG.japanese: 手段と目的を時に履き違える。そして悪い遊びが過ぎる。その結果、自ら弱点を作り晒してさえいる。私のような最強の魔女から見れば、何でこんな余裕ぶったことをするのか理解できない。自ら勝率を下げてるなんてね。
MG.translation: She sometimes mistakes her means for her ends. And she has too much dark fun. Sometimes, that even ends up creating and exposing her own weak points. For a super-powerful witch like me, it's hard to understand why she's able to act so tough. Why she lowers her own chances of winning.

UP.japanese: 手段と目的を時に履き違える。そして悪い遊びが過ぎる。その結果、自ら弱点を作り晒してさえいる。私のような最強の魔女から見れば、何でこんな余裕ぶったことをするのか理解できない。自ら勝率を下げてるなんてね。
UP.translation: She sometimes mistakes the means for the end. And she has too much bad fun. As a result, she makes and even exposes her own weak points. It's impossible for a strongest‐ever witch like me to understand why she acts so relaxed. Lowering her own chances of winning.

findings.sourceReading: Lambdadelta says Beatrice confuses means and ends and lets her cruel play go too far, thereby creating and exposing weaknesses.
findings.alternative: Too much fun can idiomatically mean excessive indulgence, and bad identifies the play as malicious.

findings.description: あなたに魔女を認めさせる describes making the addressee acknowledge the witch or witchhood at issue in Beatrice’s game. Making you accept witches plural broadens the condition into accepting witches as a general class.

contexts.japanese:
……あなたに魔女を認めさせること。
これがベアトリーチェの勝利条件のひとつであることはもはや、疑いようもないのだから。
contexts.japanesePC:
……あなたに魔女を認めさせること。
これがベアトリーチェの勝利条件のひとつであることはもはや、疑いようもないのだから。
contexts.japanesePS3:
……あなたに魔女を認めさせること。
これがベアトリーチェの勝利条件のひとつであることはもはや、疑いようもないのだから。
contexts.WH:
......Making you accept witches.
There is no longer any doubt that this is one of Beatrice's victory conditions.
contexts.MG:
...Making you accept witches.
There is no longer any doubt that this is one of Beatrice's victory conditions.
contexts.UP:
......Making you accept witches.
There is no longer any doubt that this is one of Beatrice's victory conditions.
contexts.note: Both editions retain plural “witches,” broadening the stated condition beyond the witch at issue.

MG.japanese: 魔女の戦いは守りが肝心よ？勝とうとするより、負けないようにしなさい。…認めたら負けなら、断じて認めては駄目。……あなたに魔女を認めさせること。これがベアトリーチェの勝利条件のひとつであることはもはや、疑いようもないのだから。
MG.translation: What's the most important element in defense during a witch's battle? Rather than trying to win, try not to lose. ...If accepting her means your defeat, then you definitely mustn't accept her. ...Making you accept witches. There is no longer any doubt that this is one of Beatrice's victory conditions.

UP.japanese: 魔女の戦いは守りが肝心よ？勝とうとするより、負けないようにしなさい。…認めたら負けなら、断じて認めては駄目。……あなたに魔女を認めさせること。これがベアトリーチェの勝利条件のひとつであることはもはや、疑いようもないのだから。
UP.translation: Defense is crucial during a witch's battle, you know? Rather than trying to win, try not to lose. ...If you lose when you accept her, then you definitely must not accept her. ......Making you accept witches. There is no longer any doubt that this is one of Beatrice's victory conditions.

findings.sourceReading: Bernkastel says one of Beatrice’s victory conditions is unquestionably to make the listener acknowledge the witch rather than submit to that recognition.
findings.alternative: Japanese 魔女 lacks an article and can express the category generically; accepting witches conveys recognizing witch existence rather than one individual alone.
findings.sourceNote: Original Witch Hunt is compared with the original-PC Japanese embedded in the historical patches. MangaGamer uses the accepted MangaGamer-based Witch Hunt backport, and Umineko Project uses its repository English; both are compared with maintained PS3-derived Japanese. The MangaGamer and PS3 witnesses are not independently certified retail extractions.

findings.description: しくしくと、仕舞いにはわんわんと泣き出す describes the child first weeping quietly and eventually breaking into loud, unrestrained wailing. Breaking into tears and sobbing flattens that progression and loses the final intensity.

contexts.japanese: それに怯え、私はしくしくと、仕舞いにはわんわんと泣き出すのでした…。
contexts.japanesePC: それに怯え、私はしくしくと、仕舞いにはわんわんと泣き出すのでした…。
contexts.japanesePS3: それに怯え、私はしくしくと、仕舞いにはわんわんと泣き出すのでした…。
contexts.WH: Frightened, I ended up breaking into tears and sobbing...
contexts.MG: I ended up breaking into tears and sobbing, frightened...
contexts.UP: Frightened, I ended up breaking into tears and sobbing...
contexts.note: Both editions use the shared “breaking into tears and sobbing,” flattening the explicit escalation from quiet weeping to loud wailing.

MG.japanese:
私はお祖父さまに叱られるでしょう。
とても厳しく叱られるでしょう。それに怯え、私はしくしくと、仕舞いにはわんわんと泣き出すのでした…。
MG.translation: Grandfather will probably scold me. Probably very harshly. I ended up breaking into tears and sobbing, frightened...

UP.japanese:
私はお祖父さまに叱られるでしょう。
とても厳しく叱られるでしょう。それに怯え、私はしくしくと、仕舞いにはわんわんと泣き出すのでした…。
UP.translation:
I would probably be scolded by Grandfather.
Probably very harshly. Frightened, I ended up breaking into tears and sobbing...

findings.sourceReading: Terrified of Grandfather’s punishment, the child’s crying escalates from quiet weeping until she is bawling loudly.
findings.alternative: Tears and sobbing communicates sustained distress, and English sobbing can be loud, but it does not preserve the explicit quiet-to-loud progression or the eventual wail.

findings.description: The surrounding narration is Beatrice’s first-person interior monologue, marked explicitly by 妾 before and after this sentence. She shook her head lightly abruptly changes the unexpressed Japanese subject into an external third-person narrator.

contexts.japanese: 緩やかに頭を振る。
contexts.japanesePC: 緩やかに頭を振る。
contexts.japanesePS3: 緩やかに頭を振る。
contexts.WH: She shook her head lightly.
contexts.MG: She shook her head lightly.
contexts.UP: I shook my head lightly.
contexts.note: MG retains an external “She” inside Beatrice’s first-person monologue. UP restores “I shook my head.”

MG.japanese:
緩やかに頭を振る。最高の到達点とは曰く、それ以上がないということ。
永遠の行き止まり、永遠の退屈の始まりだ。
MG.translation: She shook her head lightly. If it's the highest possible level, that means there's nothing higher. An eternal dead end, the beginning of eternal boredom.

UP.japanese:
緩やかに頭を振る。最高の到達点とは曰く、それ以上がないということ。
永遠の行き止まり、永遠の退屈の始まりだ。
UP.translation:
I shook my head lightly. If it is called the highest level, that means that there is nothing higher.
An eternal dead end, the beginning of eternal boredom.

findings.sourceReading: While reflecting on the Endless Witch title in her own voice, Beatrice lightly shakes her head and continues her monologue.
findings.alternative: English prose can briefly use external narration inside a focalized passage, and the referent of she is clear.

findings.description: 卿の称号を持つ大魔女とて恐れるほど says boredom is so dangerous that even Great Witches bearing the title Lady fear it. This is frighteningly true instead makes the preceding proposition itself frightening and loses those witches as the experiencers of fear.

contexts.japanese:
退屈は全ての魔女を殺す最悪の毒。
……卿の称号を持つ大魔女とて恐れるほどの。
永遠の至福に辿り着いた故に苛む、永遠の毒…。
contexts.japanesePC: ……卿の称号を持つ大魔女とて恐れるほどの。
contexts.japanesePS3:
退屈は全ての魔女を殺す最悪の毒。
……卿の称号を持つ大魔女とて恐れるほどの。
永遠の至福に辿り着いた故に苛む、永遠の毒…。
contexts.WH: ......To the Great Witches who are given the title 'Lady', this is frighteningly true.
contexts.MG:
Boredom is the worst sort of poison, which kills all witches.
...Even those Great Witches who are given the title "Lady" fear it.
It's the eternal poison that tortures them because of the eternal bliss they've reached...
contexts.UP:
Boredom is the worst poison that kills all witches.
......To the Great Witches who hold the title "Lady", this is frighteningly true.
It is the eternal poison that tortures them because of the eternal bliss that they have reached...
contexts.note: MG explicitly says even titled Great Witches fear boredom. UP retains the original-WH shift by saying the proposition is “frighteningly true.”

MG.japanese:
退屈は全ての魔女を殺す最悪の毒。……卿の称号を持つ大魔女とて恐れるほどの。
永遠の至福に辿り着いた故に苛む、永遠の毒…。
MG.translation: Boredom is the worst sort of poison, which kills all witches. ...Even those Great Witches who are given the title "Lady" fear it. It's the eternal poison that tortures them because of the eternal bliss they've reached...

UP.japanese:
退屈は全ての魔女を殺す最悪の毒。……卿の称号を持つ大魔女とて恐れるほどの。
永遠の至福に辿り着いた故に苛む、永遠の毒…。
UP.translation:
Boredom is the worst poison that kills all witches. ......To the Great Witches who hold the title "Lady", this is frighteningly true.
It is the eternal poison that tortures them because of the eternal bliss that they have reached...

findings.sourceReading: Beatrice calls boredom the worst poison to witches, feared even by the highest titled Great Witches.
findings.alternative: Calling the statement frighteningly true preserves the idea that boredom is gravely dangerous to powerful witches.

findings.description: 静かにせぬか、やかましい is an angry demand that the sisters be quiet because they are noisy. Couldn’t you be silent, shut up combines a question and command with broken punctuation and contradictory conversational force.

contexts.japanese: 「静かにせぬか、やかましいッ！！」
contexts.japanesePC: 「静かにせぬか、やかましいッ！！」
contexts.japanesePS3: 「静かにせぬか、やかましいッ！！」
contexts.MG: "Aaah, must you keep up that infernal racket?!?!"
contexts.UP: "Can you not be silent, shut up!!"
contexts.note: MG replaces the broken construction with a natural complaint about the infernal racket. UP changes “Couldn’t” to “Can you not” but still splices “be silent, shut up” into one malformed command.

MG.japanese: 「静かにせぬか、やかましいッ！！」
MG.translation: "Aaah, must you keep up that infernal racket?!?!"

UP.japanese: 「静かにせぬか、やかましいッ！！」
UP.translation: "Can you not be silent, shut up!!"

findings.sourceReading: Beatrice bellows at the noisy Stakes to be quiet, frightening all seven into hiding.
findings.alternative: Both English fragments demand silence, so the intended outburst remains obvious despite the malformed combination.

findings.description: 告げる here means Beatrice speaks or proclaims before chanting. And I told is incomplete English because tell requires an object or recipient in this use.

contexts.japanese:
妾は黄金の煙管を振り上げる。
そして告げる。
詠う。
思い出させる。
contexts.japanesePC: そして告げる。詠う。思い出させる。
contexts.japanesePS3:
妾は黄金の煙管を振り上げる。
そして告げる。
詠う。
思い出させる。
contexts.WH: And I told.  I chanted.  I made it remember.
contexts.MG:
I waved my golden pipe.
Then I spoke.
I chanted.
I made it remember.
contexts.UP:
I waved my golden pipe.
And I told.
I chanted.
I made it remember.
contexts.note: MG uses the grammatical “Then I spoke.” UP retains the intransitive “And I told.”

MG.japanese: 妾は黄金の煙管を振り上げる。そして告げる。詠う。思い出させる。
MG.translation: I waved my golden pipe. Then I spoke. I chanted. I made it remember.

UP.japanese: 妾は黄金の煙管を振り上げる。そして告げる。詠う。思い出させる。
UP.translation: I waved my golden pipe. And I told. I chanted. I made it remember.

findings.sourceReading: Beatrice raises her golden pipe, speaks, chants, and makes the ruined body remember its form.
findings.alternative: The following chant supplies what she says, so the intended action is recoverable from context.

findings.description: 誰が誰と connects the scattered pieces as who belonged with whom, continuing their grotesque personification as they remember themselves. Which part should go with which part flattens them into ordinary parts, while where should join with where is also missing a grammatical subject.

contexts.japanese:
哀れな肉片が、魔法の力によって、自分たちがどのような姿をしていたのか、思い出し始める。
誰が誰と繋がっていたのか。
どことどこがどう組みあがっていたのか。
contexts.japanesePC: 誰が誰と繋がっていたのか。どことどこがどう組みあがっていたのか。
contexts.japanesePS3:
哀れな肉片が、魔法の力によって、自分たちがどのような姿をしていたのか、思い出し始める。
誰が誰と繋がっていたのか。
どことどこがどう組みあがっていたのか。
contexts.WH: Which part should go with which part, and where should join with where?
contexts.MG:
By the power of magic, the pitiful pieces of meat began to remember what their form had been.
Which part should go with which part,
and where should join with where?
contexts.UP:
By the power of the magic, the pitiful pieces of meat began to remember what their form had been.
Who was connected to who.
Where was joined up with where.
contexts.note: MG retains generic parts and the subjectless “where should join.” UP restores “who was connected to who” and a deliberate fragment parallel to the Japanese sequence.

MG.japanese: 哀れな肉片が、魔法の力によって、自分たちがどのような姿をしていたのか、思い出し始める。誰が誰と繋がっていたのか。どことどこがどう組みあがっていたのか。
MG.translation: By the power of magic, the pitiful pieces of meat began to remember what their form had been. Which part should go with which part, and where should join with where?

UP.japanese: 哀れな肉片が、魔法の力によって、自分たちがどのような姿をしていたのか、思い出し始める。誰が誰と繋がっていたのか。どことどこがどう組みあがっていたのか。
UP.translation: By the power of the magic, the pitiful pieces of meat began to remember what their form had been. Who was connected to who. Where was joined up with where.

findings.sourceReading: The pitiful meat pieces remember who was connected to whom and how their locations fit together as Beatrice mockingly coaches them.
findings.alternative: The referents are plainly body parts, and the surrounding English still depicts the pieces remembering their arrangement.

findings.description: 駄目だな and 全然駄目だぜ repeat Battler’s characteristic evaluation that the alleged hell is no good or fails to measure up. That’s just useless and it’s all useless instead judge utility and lose the recurring verbal motif.

contexts.japanese:
「へ、…へへへへ。
この程度で地獄かよ、駄目だな。
あぁ、全然駄目だぜ」
contexts.japanesePC: 「へ、…へへへへ。この程度で地獄かよ、駄目だな。あぁ、全然駄目だぜ。」
contexts.japanesePS3:
「へ、…へへへへ。
この程度で地獄かよ、駄目だな。
あぁ、全然駄目だぜ」
contexts.WH: "Heh, ...hehehehe.  You call this hell?  That's just useless.  Aah, it's all useless."
contexts.MG:
"Heh, ...hehehehe.
You call this hell? That's just useless.
Aah, it's all useless."
contexts.UP:
"Heh, ...heheheheh.
You call this hell? That's no good.
Yeah, that's no goddamn good at all."
contexts.note: MG retains “useless” twice. UP restores Battler’s recurring “no good” formulation, including its emphatic second use.

MG.japanese: 「へ、…へへへへ。この程度で地獄かよ、駄目だな。あぁ、全然駄目だぜ」
MG.translation: "Heh, ...hehehehe. You call this hell? That's just useless. Aah, it's all useless."

UP.japanese: 「へ、…へへへへ。この程度で地獄かよ、駄目だな。あぁ、全然駄目だぜ」
UP.translation: "Heh, ...heheheheh. You call this hell? That's no good. Yeah, that's no goddamn good at all."

findings.sourceReading: Battler defiantly dismisses Beatrice’s torture as nowhere near good enough to count as hell, repeating his familiar “no good” phrasing.
findings.alternative: Useless remains a blunt negative judgment and can imply Beatrice’s attempt is ineffective against him.

findings.description: 虚勢など張らずに素直になれば tells Battler to stop bluffing or putting on a brave front and be honest with himself. Stayed obedient changes candor about his suffering into compliance or submission to the torturers.

contexts.japanese: 「虚勢など張らずに素直になれば、もっと楽になれるのに」
contexts.japanesePC: 「虚勢など張らずに素直になれば、もっと楽になれるのに。」
contexts.japanesePS3: 「虚勢など張らずに素直になれば、もっと楽になれるのに」
contexts.MG: "If you just stayed obedient instead of acting tough, this would go much easier."
contexts.UP: "If you stopped acting all tough and started being honest with yourself, this would be much easier on you."
contexts.note: MG retains “stayed obedient,” turning honesty into compliance. UP restores the contrast between acting tough and being honest with himself.

MG.japanese: 「虚勢など張らずに素直になれば、もっと楽になれるのに」
MG.translation: "If you just stayed obedient instead of acting tough, this would go much easier."

UP.japanese: 「虚勢など張らずに素直になれば、もっと楽になれるのに」

findings.sourceReading: A Stake says Battler would suffer less if he stopped acting tough and admitted his true feelings.

findings.description: 無限の蘇生は、無限の死をも自在にする states that endless resurrection also makes endless death freely controllable. Giving eternal rebirth and eternal death at will is a sentence fragment and loses the causal relation from resurrection to repeated death.

contexts.japanese: 無限の蘇生は、無限の死をも自在にする。
contexts.japanesePC: 無限の蘇生は、無限の死をも自在にする。
contexts.japanesePS3: 無限の蘇生は、無限の死をも自在にする。
contexts.WH: Giving eternal rebirth and eternal death at will.
contexts.MG: Giving eternal rebirth and eternal death at will.
contexts.UP: Endless rebirths give me free reign over endless deaths, too.
contexts.note: MG retains the fragment and lost causal relation. UP restores endless rebirths as what grants control over endless deaths.

MG.japanese: 無限の蘇生は、無限の死をも自在にする。無限の魔女ベアトリーチェの前には、全ての生き死には意味をなさない。死すらも、妾の檻から逃れる鍵にはなり得ないのだ。
MG.translation: Giving eternal rebirth and eternal death at will. Before the Endless Witch Beatrice, all death and life has no meaning. Even death can't become the key to escape from my cage.

UP.japanese: 無限の蘇生は、無限の死をも自在にする。無限の魔女ベアトリーチェの前には、全ての生き死には意味をなさない。死すらも、妾の檻から逃れる鍵にはなり得ないのだ。
UP.translation: Endless rebirths give me free reign over endless deaths, too. Before the Endless Witch Beatrice, all death and life has no meaning. Even death can't serve as the key to escape from my cage.

findings.sourceReading: Because Beatrice can resurrect Battler endlessly, she can also subject him to death endlessly at will.
findings.alternative: The gerund phrase places eternal rebirth and death together under voluntary control, so the paired concepts remain visible.

findings.description: All death and life has no meaning gives the coordinated subject death and life a singular verb. Standard English requires have, and the reversed fixed pairing further roughens Beatrice’s declarative narration.

contexts.japanesePS3:

findings.alternative: Life and death can be conceptualized collectively as one cycle, making the intended assertion entirely clear.

findings.description: それを突く事で蔵臼からカネを引き出そう says Eva plans to press or attack the suspected private appropriation as leverage to draw money from Krauss. Schemed to take that money away from Krauss omits the leverage mechanism and ambiguously makes the target Kinzo’s already-embezzled wealth.

contexts.japanese:
蔵臼が、金蔵が財産に関心を失ったのをいい事に、
それを私物化し摘み食いをしていることは、ずいぶん前から薄々と感付いていた。
自分たちが軌道に乗っている時は、憎々しく思いながらも、見て見ぬふりをしていたが、
…自分たちにもカネがいる今の状況では、それはとても黙認できるものではない。
絵羽は、留弗夫と楼座に連帯を呼び掛け、それを突く事で蔵臼からカネを引き出そうと企んでいる…。
contexts.japanesePC: 絵羽は、留弗夫と楼座に連帯を呼び掛け、それを突く事で蔵臼からカネを引き出そうと企んでいる…。
contexts.japanesePS3:
蔵臼が、金蔵が財産に関心を失ったのをいい事に、
それを私物化し摘み食いをしていることは、ずいぶん前から薄々と感付いていた。
自分たちが軌道に乗っている時は、憎々しく思いながらも、見て見ぬふりをしていたが、
…自分たちにもカネがいる今の状況では、それはとても黙認できるものではない。
絵羽は、留弗夫と楼座に連帯を呼び掛け、それを突く事で蔵臼からカネを引き出そうと企んでいる…。
contexts.WH: Eva had called Rudolf and Rosa into an alliance, and they had schemed to take that money away from Krauss.
contexts.MG:
For a long time now, they'd vaguely sensed that Krauss was taking advantage of the fact that Kinzo had lost interest in his own wealth,
and they suspected that he'd started embezzling that wealth to suit his own purposes.
Despite being disgusted by this, they'd turned a blind eye to it while everything was still going smoothly for them,
...but now that they needed money, they really couldn't afford to let it slide.
Eva had asked Rudolf and Rosa to form an alliance, and they were now scheming to take that money away from Krauss.
contexts.UP:
They had long felt that Krauss had started taking advantage of Kinzo's loss of interest in his own wealth,
and was embezzling that wealth for his own use.
When everything had been going well for the siblings, even though they had found it detestable, they had pretended not to notice,
...but now that they needed money, they couldn't just quietly accept that.
Eva had called Rudolf and Rosa into an alliance, and they were planning to exploit that knowledge in order to draw money out of Krauss...
contexts.note: MG retains the generic scheme to take money away. UP restores exploiting the suspected embezzlement as leverage to draw money from Krauss.

MG.japanese: 絵羽は、留弗夫と楼座に連帯を呼び掛け、それを突く事で蔵臼からカネを引き出そうと企んでいる…。
MG.translation: Eva had asked Rudolf and Rosa to form an alliance, and they were now scheming to take that money away from Krauss.

UP.japanese: 絵羽は、留弗夫と楼座に連帯を呼び掛け、それを突く事で蔵臼からカネを引き出そうと企んでいる…。
UP.translation: Eva had called Rudolf and Rosa into an alliance, and they were planning to exploit that knowledge in order to draw money out of Krauss...

findings.sourceReading: Eva recruits Rudolf and Rosa so they can confront Krauss with his suspected misuse of the family fortune and force him to pay them.
findings.alternative: The preceding English explains the suspected embezzlement, and scheming to take money from Krauss still conveys hostile extraction rather than a voluntary loan.

findings.description: 父には到底及ばなくても concedes that Eva is nowhere near or cannot possibly equal Kinzo. Even if I couldn’t quite reach Father’s level softens that acknowledged gulf into a narrow shortfall.

contexts.japanese: 父には到底及ばなくても、金融や経済に学識を深め、いつでもその手伝いができるよう自分を研磨してきたはずだった。
contexts.japanesePC: 父には到底及ばなくても、金融や経済に学識を深め、いつでもその手伝いができるよう自分を研磨してきたはずだった。
contexts.japanesePS3: 父には到底及ばなくても、金融や経済に学識を深め、いつでもその手伝いができるよう自分を研磨してきたはずだった。
contexts.WH: Even if I couldn't quite reach Father's level, I deepened my knowledge in economics and finance, and tried to improve myself so that I could help out with that at any time.
contexts.MG: Even if I couldn't quite reach Father's level, I deepened my knowledge in economics and finance, trying to improve myself so I could be of use to him at any time.
contexts.UP: Even if I was far from reaching Father's level, I deepened my knowledge in economics and finance, and tried to improve myself so that I could help out with that at any time.
contexts.note: MG retains “couldn’t quite reach,” softening Eva’s admitted distance from Kinzo. UP says she was far from reaching his level.

MG.japanese: 父には到底及ばなくても、金融や経済に学識を深め、いつでもその手伝いができるよう自分を研磨してきたはずだった。……しかし、それが父に認められることはついになかった。父にとって、女は男を支えるものでしかなく、それ以上であることを許さなかったからだ。
MG.translation: Even if I couldn't quite reach Father's level, I deepened my knowledge in economics and finance, trying to improve myself so I could be of use to him at any time. ...However, in the end, Father never acknowledged my efforts. To Father, a woman was only meant to support a man, and nothing further than that was permissable.

UP.japanese: 父には到底及ばなくても、金融や経済に学識を深め、いつでもその手伝いができるよう自分を研磨してきたはずだった。……しかし、それが父に認められることはついになかった。父にとって、女は男を支えるものでしかなく、それ以上であることを許さなかったからだ。
UP.translation: Even if I was far from reaching Father's level, I deepened my knowledge in economics and finance, and tried to improve myself so that I could help out with that at any time. ......However, in the end, there never came a time when Father acknowledged that. To Father, a woman was only meant to support a man, and nothing further than that was permissible.

findings.sourceReading: Eva says that although she could not remotely match her father, she deepened her financial and economic knowledge so she could assist him.
findings.alternative: Both phrasings preserve Kinzo as the higher standard and Eva as falling short of it.
