findings.description: 百億 is ten billion, not a billion. The English reduces Eva’s hyperbolic count of grievances by a factor of ten at the peak of her inability to voice them.

contexts.japanese:
何が不満か、だって…？
百億の不満、恨み辛み、忘れえぬ屈辱がいくらでも脳裏を過ぎる。
そしてそれらが一度にせり上がって来るものだから、喉の奥から出てくるのは情けない呻き声だけだった。
contexts.japanesePC: 百億の不満、恨み辛み、忘れえぬ屈辱がいくらでも脳裏を過ぎる。
contexts.japanesePS3:
何が不満か、だって…？
百億の不満、恨み辛み、忘れえぬ屈辱がいくらでも脳裏を過ぎる。
そしてそれらが一度にせり上がって来るものだから、喉の奥から出てくるのは情けない呻き声だけだった。
contexts.WH: A billion things are.  Grudges, hard feelings, humiliations that I'll never forget kept floating through the back of my mind.
contexts.MG:
What's my complaint, you say...?
I've got a billion of them. Grudges, hard feelings, humiliations that I'll never forget kept floating through the back of my mind.
They all built up at the same time, coming out of my throat as a shameful moan.
contexts.UP:
What's so unsatisfying, he says...?
A billion grudges, hard feelings, humiliations that I'll never forget crossed through the back of my mind.
And all of them built up at the same time, coming out of my throat as nothing more than a shameful moan.
contexts.note: Both editions retain one billion instead of ten billion, reducing Eva’s emotional hyperbole.

MG.japanese: 何が不満か、だって…？百億の不満、恨み辛み、忘れえぬ屈辱がいくらでも脳裏を過ぎる。そしてそれらが一度にせり上がって来るものだから、喉の奥から出てくるのは情けない呻き声だけだった。
MG.translation: What's my complaint, you say...? I've got a billion of them. Grudges, hard feelings, humiliations that I'll never forget kept floating through the back of my mind. They all built up at the same time, coming out of my throat as a shameful moan.

UP.japanese: 何が不満か、だって…？百億の不満、恨み辛み、忘れえぬ屈辱がいくらでも脳裏を過ぎる。そしてそれらが一度にせり上がって来るものだから、喉の奥から出てくるのは情けない呻き声だけだった。
UP.translation: What's so unsatisfying, he says...? A billion grudges, hard feelings, humiliations that I'll never forget crossed through the back of my mind. And all of them built up at the same time, coming out of my throat as nothing more than a shameful moan.

findings.sourceReading: Eva says ten billion complaints, grudges, resentments, and unforgettable humiliations race through her mind at once.
findings.alternative: Both numbers function as obvious hyperbole for an overwhelming quantity and do not change the underlying history.

contexts.japanese:
「お前に、男を喜ばせる何ができるというのか？

「お前に、男を喜ばせる何ができるというのか？

findings.description: 何でもなさそうな顔をしてる says Krauss wears a face as though nothing is wrong or acts unaffected. Acts like we’re nothing instead makes Eva and her younger self the object of his dismissal, changing concealed distress into contempt for them.

contexts.japanese:
「大学院に進んで、もっといっぱい勉強して、優れた成績を出して、蔵臼を追い詰めてやりましょう」
「あいつ、何でもなさそうな顔をしてるけど、きっと心は相当追い詰められてるわ。
早く身の程を思い知って死んじゃえばいいのに。
そうすれば、私たちが当主になれる。
contexts.japanesePC: あいつ、何でもなさそうな顔をしてるけど、きっと心は相当追い詰められてるわ。早く身の程を思い知って死んじゃえばいいのに。そうすれば、私たちが当主になれる。留弗夫は辞退してくれるわ。あの子は私には逆らえないもの。」
contexts.japanesePS3:
「大学院に進んで、もっといっぱい勉強して、優れた成績を出して、蔵臼を追い詰めてやりましょう」

早く身の程を思い知って死んじゃえばいいのに。
そうすれば、私たちが当主になれる。
contexts.WH: That guy makes a face as though we're nothing, but I'm sure he feels pretty well cornered in his heart.  If only he would just learn his place and die.  If he did, we could become the head.  Rudolf would just refuse.  That kid can't go against us."
contexts.MG:
"Let's go to college, study more and more, get excellent grades, and drive Krauss into a corner.
That guy acts like we're nothing, but I'm sure he feels pretty well cornered in the inside.
If only he'd just learn his place and die.
If he did, we could become the Head.
contexts.UP:
"Let's go to college, study more and more, get excellent grades, and drive Krauss into a corner."
"That guy makes a face as though we're nothing, but I'm sure he feels pretty well cornered in his heart.
If only he would just learn his place and die.

findings.sourceReading: Young Eva says Krauss outwardly looks untroubled but must already feel severely cornered inside.

findings.description: 泣き寝入りする is an idiom for giving up and suffering an injustice or defeat without obtaining redress. Cry yourself to sleep literalizes its components and invents sleep as the response to Eva’s failed plan.

…何しろ、兄さんがお父様の資産を摘み食いしているのは確かなんだから…」
「…つまんない計画。
そんなのさっさとやめて、泣き寝入りでもしちゃえば…？」

findings.description: ケツが痒くなってきた gives Battler a deliberately crude, bodily image—his ass is starting to itch—from realizing Shannon suppressed romantic lines from his childhood crush. I can’t take it replaces that specific comic embarrassment with generic distress.

contexts.japanese:
実は６年前、ちょっぴり彼女を意識していたことを思い出す。
そっかー、譲治の兄貴とじゃお似合いだよな、仕方ねぇよなぁ。
…さらば、俺の６年前の淡い初恋…。
………ってことは、さっき紗音ちゃんが自重してくれた、俺の６年前の恥ずかしいセリフ集は、
……それ関係って可能性が高いな…。
うぉおおおおぉおぉおぉ、ケツが痒くなってきたぜ…。

findings.description: ズルイ calls women unfair, sneaky, or underhanded for asking questions while refusing to answer them. Cruel assigns callous harmfulness rather than the conversational double standard Battler is complaining about.

contexts.japanese:
「話を振ってきたのはそっちのくせに、何で俺が逆ギレされなきゃならねぇんだ。
女って生き物は質問ばかりで、そのくせ、自分が質問に答えることは決してないんだよな。
ズルイ生き物だぜ、まったく」
contexts.japanesePC: 「話を振ってきたのはそっちのくせに、何で俺が逆ギレされなきゃならねぇんだ。女って生き物は質問ばかりで、そのくせ、自分が質問に答えることは決してないんだよな。ズルイ生き物だぜ、まったく。」
contexts.japanesePS3:
「話を振ってきたのはそっちのくせに、何で俺が逆ギレされなきゃならねぇんだ。
女って生き物は質問ばかりで、そのくせ、自分が質問に答えることは決してないんだよな。
ズルイ生き物だぜ、まったく」
contexts.MG:
"If you're the one who brought up this subject, why are you yelling at me now?
Women are creatures who always ask questions, and yet almost never answer them.
What cruel creatures, seriously."
contexts.UP:
"You're the one who brought up this subject, why do you have to go and get mad at me?
Women are creatures who always ask questions, and yet, they almost never answer them.
What cruel creatures, seriously."
contexts.note: Both editions retain “cruel” for Battler’s accusation that women are unfair or sly about asking and answering questions.

MG.translation: "If you're the one who brought up this subject, why are you yelling at me now? Women are creatures who always ask questions, and yet almost never answer them. What cruel creatures, seriously."

findings.sourceReading: After Jessica angrily evades the same romantic question she asked him, Battler jokes that women are unfair creatures who ask but never answer.
findings.alternative: Cruel can colloquially describe the unfair treatment Battler feels he has received, retaining his exaggerated grievance.

findings.description: 青春時代 means youth or adolescence as a life period. Six years of puberty substitutes the biological maturation process and makes the entire six-year span one of puberty.

contexts.japanese:
６年か。
…青春時代の６年ってのは重く、そして早いもんだ。
台風が近付いているということで、空は灰色の度合いを強めているが、それでもなぜか、とても爽やかに感じられるのだった。
…俺も、たまには異性のことを、おっぱいのデカさ以外で真剣に考えてみることにするか…。
contexts.japanesePC: ６年か。…青春時代の６年ってのは重く、そして早いもんだ。
contexts.japanesePS3:
６年か。
…青春時代の６年ってのは重く、そして早いもんだ。
台風が近付いているということで、空は灰色の度合いを強めているが、それでもなぜか、とても爽やかに感じられるのだった。
…俺も、たまには異性のことを、おっぱいのデカさ以外で真剣に考えてみることにするか…。
contexts.WH: Six years.  ...Six years of puberty are pretty important, and they had gone by pretty fast.
contexts.MG:
Six years.
...Six years of puberty are pretty important, and they went by pretty fast.
As the typhoon approached, the clouds grew steadily grayer, but even so, I had this really refreshing feeling.
...Maybe I'll try thinking more seriously about the opposite sex, more than just the size of their boobs...
contexts.UP:
Six years.
...Those six years of puberty are pretty important, and they go by so fast.
With the typhoon approaching, the clouds had grown steadily grayer, and yet, even so, I had this really refreshing feeling.
...Maybe I'll start thinking more seriously about the opposite sex, more than just the size of their boobs...
contexts.note: Both editions retain “six years of puberty” instead of six years during youth or adolescence.

MG.japanese: ６年か。…青春時代の６年ってのは重く、そして早いもんだ。
MG.translation: Six years. ...Six years of puberty are pretty important, and they went by pretty fast.

UP.japanese: ６年か。…青春時代の６年ってのは重く、そして早いもんだ。
UP.translation: Six years. ...Those six years of puberty are pretty important, and they go by so fast.

findings.sourceReading: Battler reflects that six years during one’s youth carry great weight and pass quickly.
findings.alternative: The cousins have physically and romantically matured during adolescence, so puberty points toward an important component of the same transition.

findings.description: 青春し describes the cousins actively living or enjoying their youth as they renew their friendship. As youthful as we were reduces that activity to possessing the quality of youth.

contexts.japanese:

遺産も旧家とやらの面子も知ったことじゃない。
俺たちはこんなにも青春し、旧交を温めあっているんだ。
そして、みんながみんな、幸せになれると信じ合ってる。
contexts.japanesePC: 俺たちはこんなにも青春し、旧交を温めあっているんだ。
contexts.japanesePS3:

And every one of us believes together that we can all be happy.

findings.sourceReading: Battler insists that the cousins are fully enjoying their youth and renewing their old friendship despite the adults' schemes and the approaching storm.
findings.alternative: Calling them youthful preserves the scene's youth motif and accompanies their renewed friendship, but it does not express their active enjoyment of this period.

Then it suddenly burst open and disappeared, becoming golden lace and marking the rose...

findings.description: のんびり待ってる says Kyrie will wait leisurely or take it easy while waiting for dessert. Wait patiently changes relaxed detachment into tolerance or forbearance and weakens the contrast with the others rushing upstairs.

contexts.japanese:
「決まりだな。
行こう！
霧江はちょっと待っててくれ。
真偽を確かめてすぐ戻る」
「……ありがと。
郷田さんがデザートを持ってくるのを、のんびり待ってるわ」
４兄弟と夏妃と秀吉が、威勢よく席を立つと、どたどたと廊下へ飛び出していく。
後には、あまりのことに呆然として言葉を失っている子どもたちと、居心地の悪そうな南條。
そして肩を竦める霧江が残されるのだった。

contexts.WH: "......Thank you.  I will wait patiently for Gohda-san to bring the dessert."
contexts.MG:
"It's decided.
Let's go!
Kyrie, wait here for a while.
We'll go to check whether it's true or not and come back quickly."
"...Thank you.
I'll wait patiently for Gohda-san to bring in dessert."
The four siblings, Natsuhi, and Hideyoshi all rose from their seats forcefully and flew out into the hallway with a clatter.
Afterwards, only the children, stunned completely speechless, Nanjo, who looked uncomfortable,
and Kyrie, who just shrugged, were left.
contexts.UP:
"It's decided.
Let's go!
Kyrie, wait here for a while.
We'll go to check whether it's true or not and come back quickly."
"......Thank you.
I will wait patiently for Gohda‐san to bring the dessert."
The four siblings, Natsuhi, and Hideyoshi all stood from their seats forcefully and flew out into the hallway with a clatter.
Afterwards, the only ones left were the children, stunned completely speechless; Nanjo, who looked uncomfortable;
and Kyrie, shrugging her shoulders.
contexts.note: Both editions retain “wait patiently,” losing Kyrie’s leisurely, detached wait for dessert while the others rush upstairs.

findings.description: 誤魔化している says the adults apparently felt Maria was evading, fudging, or covering something up. Trying to trick them assigns her a more active intention to deceive the adults.

contexts.japanese:
真里亞は何度聞かれてもベアトリーチェにもらったと繰り返すだけ。
それを大人たちは、誤魔化していると感じたらしく、彼女が泣き出すまで詰問を決して緩めようとはしなかった…。
真里亞は解放された時、泣き疲れてぐったりしていた。

contexts.WH: It seemed that the adults felt that she was trying to trick them, so they didn't hold back and questioned her until she broke out in tears...

Maria kept repeating that she'd gotten it from Beatrice no matter how many times she was asked.
The adults seemed to think she was trying to trick them, so they didn't hold back and questioned her until she broke out in tears...
When Maria was released, she sobbed, all worn out from crying.
contexts.UP:

contexts.note: Both editions retain the adults’ belief that Maria was trying to trick them, strengthening evasion into active deception.

MG.translation: Maria kept repeating that she'd gotten it from Beatrice no matter how many times she was asked. The adults seemed to think she was trying to trick them, so they didn't hold back and questioned her until she broke out in tears... When Maria was released, she sobbed, all worn out from crying.

UP.japanese: 真里亞は何度聞かれてもベアトリーチェにもらったと繰り返すだけ。それを大人たちは、誤魔化していると感じたらしく、彼女が泣き出すまで詰問を決して緩めようとはしなかった…。真里亞は解放された時、泣き疲れてぐったりしていた。
UP.translation: Maria kept repeating that she had gotten it from Beatrice, no matter how many times she was asked. It seemed that the adults felt that she was trying to trick them, so they didn't hold back, and questioned her until she broke out in tears... By the time Maria was released, she had cried herself to the point of exhaustion.

findings.sourceReading: The adults interpret Maria's repeated answer as evasive and continue pressing her until she cries.
findings.alternative: Evasion can itself be meant to mislead questioners, so the adults' suspicion of dishonesty remains recognizable.

findings.description: 摩り替わり says the witch legend was replaced or swapped out for the mistress theory. Refined into instead presents the mistress theory as a more precise development of the witch theory.

何しろ、静寂を好むお人だからな。

contexts.japanesePC: ……しかし、魔女伝説が愛人説に摩り替わり、やがてそれは、こっそり愛人のもとへ通っているのではないかと囁かれるようになった。」

"...However, when the witch theory was slowly refined into the theory about his mistress, people eventually whispered that he was secretly going back and forth to see her."

"......However, after the witch theory began to be refined into the theory about his mistress, it was eventually whispered that he was secretly going back and forth to see her."
contexts.note: Both editions retain “refined into,” presenting the mistress theory as a refinement of the witch theory instead of a theory that replaced it.

MG.japanese: 「……しかし、魔女伝説が愛人説に掏り替わり、やがてそれは、こっそり愛人のもとへ通っているのではないかと囁かれるようになった」

UP.japanese: 「……しかし、魔女伝説が愛人説に掏り替わり、やがてそれは、こっそり愛人のもとへ通っているのではないかと囁かれるようになった」
UP.translation: "......However, after the witch theory began to be refined into the theory about his mistress, it was eventually whispered that he was secretly going back and forth to see her."

findings.sourceReading: The witch legend was supplanted by the mistress theory, which eventually led to rumors that Kinzo secretly visited his mistress.
findings.alternative: Both theories are successive explanations for the same rumors, so readers can still follow the historical progression.

findings.description: 長いこと口にすることをはばかられてきた says everyone had long refrained from voicing the suspicion. They hesitated for a long time without speaking recasts that history as one extended silence.

contexts.japanese:
絵羽のその言葉は、４兄弟がずっと思ってきたこと全てを代弁したようだった。
しばしの間、室内は再び沈黙に支配され、一同は雨と風の音に耳を傾ける…。
……この島には誰も知らない隠し屋敷があり、そこにずっとずっと、金蔵の愛人が隠れ住まっている……？
誰もが勘繰り過ぎだと思い、長いこと口にすることをはばかられてきたが…。
……全員が持つ共通の見解であったのだ。
contexts.japanesePC: 誰もが勘繰り過ぎだと思い、長いこと口にすることをはばかられてきたが…。……全員が持つ共通の見解であったのだ。

誰もが勘繰り過ぎだと思い、長いこと口にすることをはばかられてきたが…。
……全員が持つ共通の見解であったのだ。
contexts.WH: Everyone thought that they were being too suspicious, and they hesitated for a long time without speaking, but.........everyone shared a common opinion.
contexts.MG:
Eva's words spoke for what all of the siblings had come to think.
For a while, the room returned to silence again, and everyone listened to the sound of the wind and rain...
...Was there a hidden mansion on this island, and had Kinzo's mistress been living there in hiding for a long, long time...?
Everyone thought they were being too suspicious, and they hesitated for a long time without speaking,
...but everyone shared a common opinion.
contexts.UP:
Eva's words spoke for what all of the siblings had come to think.
For a while, the room returned to silence again, and everyone listened to the sound of the wind and rain...
......Was there a hidden mansion on this island, and had Kinzo's mistress been living there in hiding for a long, long time......?
Every one of them had thought that they were being too suspicious, and had refrained from saying it for the longest time, but...
......it had been a common opinion that everyone shared.
contexts.note: MG turns years of reluctance to voice the shared theory into a long hesitation without speaking. UP restores the longstanding history.

UP.translation: ......Was there a hidden mansion on this island, and had Kinzo's mistress been living there in hiding for a long, long time......? Every one of them had thought that they were being too suspicious, and had refrained from saying it for the longest time, but... ......it had been a common opinion that everyone shared.

findings.sourceReading: Each sibling had considered the suspicion excessive and had avoided saying it aloud for a long time, despite all sharing it.
findings.alternative: The surrounding retrospective context can lead readers to understand the hesitation as longstanding rather than confined to the present pause.

findings.description: 計上しようとしてた says Krauss tried to put or budget a full-island survey into the resort-development plan, and 出来なくなった says the earlier trouble prevented it from being carried out. findings.description: 具体的な証拠 means concrete or specific evidence. Physical proof narrows the possible basis for Krauss's conviction to material evidence.

contexts.japanese:
…蔵臼は間違いなく、隠し屋敷の存在を確信しているのだ。
それで、リゾート開発と称して島を詳しく調べ、黄金の隠し場所の手掛かりを見つけようとしているのだ。
その確信は、単なる思い込みなのか、それとも具体的な証拠があってのことなのかはわからない。
contexts.japanesePC: その確信は、単なる思い込みなのか、それとも具体的な証拠があってのことなのかはわからない。

contexts.WH: They couldn't tell whether that conviction was just him over-thinking things, or whether it was based on some physical proof.
contexts.MG:
...Krauss was definitely sure of the existence of a hidden mansion.
And under the pretense of opening a resort, he had been closely investigating the island, searching for a clue as to the location of the hidden gold.
They couldn't tell whether that conviction was just him overthinking things, or whether it was based on some physical proof.
contexts.UP:
...Krauss was definitely sure of the existence of a hidden mansion.
And under the pretense of opening a resort, he had been investigating the island in detail, searching for a clue as to the location of the hidden gold.
They couldn't tell whether that conviction was just him over‐thinking things, or whether it was based on some physical proof.
contexts.note: Both editions narrow unspecified concrete evidence to physical proof.

MG.japanese: その確信は、単なる思い込みなのか、それとも具体的な証拠があってのことなのかはわからない。……しかし、悪知恵の働く蔵臼がそれを確信している以上、それに足る根拠があるに違いないと兄弟たちもまた確信していた…。
MG.translation: They couldn't tell whether that conviction was just him overthinking things, or whether it was based on some physical proof. ...Still, if Krauss, with all his guile, was sure, that was enough proof for the other siblings to be sure too...

UP.japanese: その確信は、単なる思い込みなのか、それとも具体的な証拠があってのことなのかはわからない。……しかし、悪知恵の働く蔵臼がそれを確信している以上、それに足る根拠があるに違いないと兄弟たちもまた確信していた…。
UP.translation: They couldn't tell whether that conviction was just him over‐thinking things, or whether it was based on some physical proof. ......However, if Krauss, with all his guile, was convinced, then the other siblings were similarly convinced that there must be a sufficient basis for it...

findings.sourceReading: The siblings do not know whether Krauss's conviction is mere assumption or rests on concrete evidence.
findings.alternative: In a search for a hidden mansion and gold, the most likely concrete evidence would be physical, so the practical inference remains plausible.

findings.description: 霧江の言い分は揺るぐものではない says Kyrie's argument or position remains unshaken. WH instead says the importance of what she said does not waver, changing validity or force into importance.

contexts.japanese:
“あの”金蔵ならやりかねない。
…この枕詞が付く限り、どんな荒唐無稽な話にも少なからずの信憑性が宿った。
しかし、それでも霧江の言い分は揺るぐものではない。
こっそりと、親に内緒で段ボール箱に猫を飼うのとはわけが違う。
人間ひとりを３０年にもわたって秘密に世話するなんて、その手間は計り知れないくらいに膨大だろう…。

findings.description: WH's the all of the gold is grammatically malformed for 黄金を全て, which means all the gold.

contexts.japanese:
なのに、わざわざこの期に及んで、碑文を解いてみろ、
解けたら家督と黄金を全て引き渡そうと、“新たなゲーム”を仕掛けてくる意味が、どこにあるというのか。

MG.translation: However, Kyrie still thought there might be a catch. If this was a declaration of victory, Beatrice would only have had to display the gold openly and state her intent to buy the inheritance. Why did she set up this "new game", where she agreed to hand over the all of the gold and the inheritance to the epitaph solver?

UP.translation: However, Kyrie still felt something was slightly out of place. findings.description: 彼女以外の人間が暴けたなら means if someone other than Beatrice managed to uncover the hiding place. If it was exposed to someone makes that person a passive recipient and removes the solving or discovery action central to Kyrie's risk analysis.

「つまり、魔女の手紙に書かれている挑発文は、ベアトリーチェにとってリスクにしかならないのよ」

contexts.note: Both editions say the island has no more than eighteen people, loosening Battler’s exact known-population premise into an upper bound.

findings.sourceReading: Battler asks whether it is delusional to deny the witch while believing all eighteen people innocent on an island containing only those eighteen.
findings.alternative: The cast count is already fixed at eighteen, so readers will ordinarily understand no more than eighteen as excluding outsiders rather than reducing the known count.

findings.description: アリバイの証明が終えられない says Beatrice could never finish proving the successive outsiders' alibis. Kept searching for their alibis replaces the impossible proof burden with an indefinite search for alibis.

contexts.japanese:
「ふむ、なるほど。
………妾が１９人目のアリバイを何らかの方法で証明したとしても。
その瞬間にそなたは２０人目を生み出し、犯人だと主張する。
これを無限に繰り返すことによって、妾は永遠に彼らのアリバイの証明が終えられないというわけか」
contexts.japanesePC: 「ふむ、なるほど。………妾が１９人目のアリバイを何らかの方法で証明したとしても。その瞬間にそなたは２０人目を生み出し、犯人だと主張する。これを無限に繰り返すことによって、妾は永遠に彼らのアリバイの証明が終えられないというわけか。……なるほどなるほど、くっくっくっく！　さながら蝗の大群を呼び出す魔王よな。さすがは金蔵の孫よ。召喚術の才能には恵まれていると見える。」
contexts.japanesePS3:
「ふむ、なるほど。
………妾が１９人目のアリバイを何らかの方法で証明したとしても。
その瞬間にそなたは２０人目を生み出し、犯人だと主張する。
これを無限に繰り返すことによって、妾は永遠に彼らのアリバイの証明が終えられないというわけか」
contexts.WH: "Hmm, I see.  .........Even if I somehow prove an alibi for the 19th person, as soon as I do, you will think up a 20th person, and claim that they are the culprit.  By repeating this endlessly, you would make it so I kept searching for their alibis for all eternity.  ......I see, I see, *cackle*cackle*!  Just like a demon king summoning a plague of locusts.  I wouldn't expect anything less from Kinzo's grandchild.  It looks like you have been gifted with a talent in summoning."
contexts.MG:
"Hmm, I see.
......Even if I somehow prove an alibi for the 19th person,
as soon as I do, you will think up a 20th person and claim that they are the culprit.
By repeating this endlessly, you would make it so I kept searching for their alibis for all eternity.
contexts.UP:
"Hmm, I see.

as soon as I do, you will think up a 20th person, and claim that they are the culprit.
By repeating this infinitely, you would make it so I kept searching for their alibis for all eternity."
contexts.note: Both editions replace Beatrice’s endless burden of proving successive alibis with endlessly searching for alibis.

findings.sourceReading: Each proved alibi would make Battler posit another outsider, preventing Beatrice from ever completing the chain of alibi proofs.
findings.alternative: Searching for each new alibi is part of the work required to prove it, and the endless-regress burden remains clear.

findings.description: Japanese pictures the sole path Battler finds between two cliffs, with the abyss below if he falls, followed by a single tightrope. My only way across the chasm of Hell compresses the cliffs, abyss, and discovered path into a different generic chasm image.

ヤツが語る赤の情報だけなのだ。
落ちれば奈落という、崖と崖の間に見出す唯一の活路。
たった一本の綱渡り。
ヤツの慈悲無き真っ赤な刃こそが、唯一の生きる道なのだ。
…それは文字通り、綱渡りどころか、刃の上を歩くようなもの…。

findings.sourceReading: Red truth is Battler's only path between cliffs over an abyss, a single tightrope that immediately develops into walking on a blade.
findings.alternative: Crossing a chasm of Hell preserves the mortal danger and connects smoothly to the following tightrope image.

findings.description: 弱点を抱え says Battler was burdened with the weakness of having to deny both the witch and the eighteen. Held on to a weak point makes the vulnerability sound like something he voluntarily maintained.

contexts.japanese:
俺の勝利条件である魔女否定は、ヤツの言う対偶では、＝犯人は人間、となる。
でも俺は、１８人の中に犯人を求めたくない。
…だからこそ、魔女も１８人も同時に否定しなければならないという弱点を抱え、
にもかかわらずそれを理解できず、そこを突かれて前回はボロボロに負けた。
contexts.japanesePC: …だからこそ、魔女も１８人も同時に否定しなければならないという弱点を抱え、にもかかわらずそれを理解できず、そこを突かれて前回はボロボロに負けた。
contexts.japanesePS3:
俺の勝利条件である魔女否定は、ヤツの言う対偶では、＝犯人は人間、となる。
でも俺は、１８人の中に犯人を求めたくない。
…だからこそ、魔女も１８人も同時に否定しなければならないという弱点を抱え、
にもかかわらずそれを理解できず、そこを突かれて前回はボロボロに負けた。
contexts.WH: But I didn't want to search for the culprit amid the 18.
contexts.MG:
Because my victory condition is the denial of witches, then, to use her contrapositive logic, the culprit must be human.
But I didn't want to search for a culprit amid the 18.
...That's what made me stick to a weak position, since I had to claim both that it couldn't be a witch and that it couldn't be one of the 18.
Last time, I was unable to understand that, so that's where she hit me, leaving me tattered and defeated.
contexts.UP:
In terms of her contrapositive, my victory condition—the denial of the witch—meant that the culprit was a human.
But I didn't want to search for the culprit amid the 18.
...Therefore, I held on to a weak point, since I had to deny the witch and the 18 at the same time.
Since I had been unable to understand that last time, that was where she had hit me, leaving me tattered and defeated.
contexts.note: MG says Battler stuck to a weak position and UP says he held onto a weak point. Both make his structural burden sound voluntarily maintained.

MG.japanese: もちろん、俺は恐れている。俺の勝利条件である魔女否定は、ヤツの言う対偶では、＝犯人は人間、となる。でも俺は、１８人の中に犯人を求めたくない。…だからこそ、魔女も１８人も同時に否定しなければならないという弱点を抱え、にもかかわらずそれを理解できず、そこを突かれて前回はボロボロに負けた。
MG.translation: Of course I'm afraid. Because my victory condition is the denial of witches, then, to use her contrapositive logic, the culprit must be human. But I didn't want to search for a culprit amid the 18. ...That's what made me stick to a weak position, since I had to claim both that it couldn't be a witch and that it couldn't be one of the 18. Last time, I was unable to understand that, so that's where she hit me, leaving me tattered and defeated.

UP.japanese: もちろん、俺は恐れている。俺の勝利条件である魔女否定は、ヤツの言う対偶では、＝犯人は人間、となる。でも俺は、１８人の中に犯人を求めたくない。…だからこそ、魔女も１８人も同時に否定しなければならないという弱点を抱え、にもかかわらずそれを理解できず、そこを突かれて前回はボロボロに負けた。
UP.translation: Of course I'm afraid. In terms of her contrapositive, my victory condition—the denial of the witch—meant that the culprit was a human. But I didn't want to search for the culprit amid the 18. ...Therefore, I held on to a weak point, since I had to deny the witch and the 18 at the same time. Since I had been unable to understand that last time, that was where she had hit me, leaving me tattered and defeated.

findings.sourceReading: Battler carried an inherent double-denial weakness without understanding it, allowing Beatrice to exploit it in the previous game.
findings.alternative: Battler did persist in both denials, so holding onto that position describes his continued commitment even if the weakness itself was involuntary.

…続けて復唱要求」
「“この島には、１９人以上がいる”！」
「…………………………」

相当、慎重になっているのだろう。

俺の“悪魔の証明”を打ち破るには、
１８人以外の人間の存在と人数を、
事前に赤で確定する必要があるのだから。
そう。
１９人目の存在は、赤以外では打ち破れない。
俺はベアトを、赤を使う他ないように追い詰めた…！
この魔女とのゲーム…、
………戦い方は、
……確かにあるッ！
「拒否してもいいんだぜ。
…お前が赤で言えないなら、この島の合計人数は１８＋Ｘってことになる」
「……このＸは、初手で許すには相当デカい大駒だぜ？
何しろ、以後、１８人の誰にも不可能だった、という根拠のトリックは、
全て１８人以外の人間Ｘで説明可能になる。
……全員アリバイ系の密室を、全て打ち破れる大駒だ…！」
それはさながら、
敵陣にわずかの隙間があれば鋭く食い込める、チェスのビショップのようなもの。
同じ色のマスにしか効果を発揮しないが、その盤上の支配力は大きい。
「…………………………。
………………く」
ベアトも、現在の窮状をよく理解しているようだった。
これほどの大駒を、これほどの序盤に見捨てられるわけもない…。
赤き宝刀を抜けば、それを救うことは難しくないだろう。
……しかしベアトは、むしろ俺がそれを待ち受けていることも、充分に察している。
迂闊な赤き真実が、自らの首を絞めることになるかもしれないと怯えている…！
なぜなら、…本来、魔女は赤で否定されるべき存在だからだ。
信じろ。
疑うな！
魔女などいない！
この世にそんなもの、存在するわけもない。
それが存在できるのは、現実の狭間だけ。
…その隙間にて、真実の暴風から必死に身を守って縮こまり、
虚偽と幻想で食い繋いでいる時だけ、蜃気楼のように細々と存在できる脆弱な存在なのだ。
つまり、魔女だけが使える赤は、自らを否定しかねない現実そのもの。
……赤を振りかざせば振りかざすほどに。
魔女はわずかずつだが、自らの凌げる現実の隙間を失っていく。
だからこそ、あやふやな情報、
……つまり、幻想の余地ある現実の隙間を、無用心に赤で失いたくないのだ。
それが徐々に自分を追い詰めていくと理解しているから。
もちろん、ヤツはそれを認めないだろう。
それを認めれば、
自分がこの世に存在してはならない虚数的存在であることを認めたも同然になってしまうのだから。
怯えるな。
強気でいろ…！
ヤツが一番骨身に染みてわかってるんだ。
赤き宝刀は、相当の覚悟がなければ容易には使えないのだということを…！
「…どうしたよ。
繰り返すぜ。
……復唱要求！」

contexts.MG:
...Again, repeat it.
"There are 19 people or more on this island"!"
"............"
Beatrice fell silent once again.
She'd probably remain extremely cautious
as long as confirming the number of humans on this
island might give her some large disadvantage,
depending on the situation.
The red has already become a foothold for my counterattacks.
Now that we know this, it makes the red very risky for the witch.

To break my "Devil's Proof",
she would need to settle the existence and number of people outside the 18 in red.

in this witch's game!

can be explained with a human X who isn't in that group.
...This huge piece can break open all the rooms you said were closed because everyone had an alibi...!"

how a chess bishop can cut a thin line through enemy forces as long as there's a slight gap.
It could only be effectively used on squares of the same color, but it was very good at controlling territory on the board.
"............
......Nng."

She was afraid that a careless red truth might end up strangling her own neck...!

Believe.

Witches don't exist!

Don't be afraid.
Stay strong...!
I know that she's the one who's really been pierced to the bone.

findings.description: いつの間にか says Battler feels that, before he knew it, he was being made to swallow the witch story. Suddenly changes his belated recognition of a gradual transition into abrupt onset.

いつの間にか魔女話を鵜呑みにさせられていく気がするぜ」

findings.sourceReading: As he listens, Battler realizes that the purported witch-denial game has imperceptibly shifted into asking him to accept a witch narrative wholesale.
findings.alternative: Suddenly can describe the moment of realization rather than the speed of the underlying change, and the surrounding “more I hear” progression remains intact.

findings.description: とてもわかりやすい modifies Beatrice's emotion: her loneliness is extremely easy to read despite her brazen expression. In that really easy to understand expression instead calls the expression itself readable and conflicts with its continued brazenness.

contexts.japanese:
俺が素っ気無い態度を見せると、ベアトは珍しく気落ちしたような仕草を見せた。
もちろん、表情はふてぶてしいままだが…、
自分の身の上話に興味を持ってもらえなかったのが寂しい、
というとてもわかりやすい感情が垣間見えた気がした。
contexts.japanesePC: もちろん、表情はふてぶてしいままだが…、自分の身の上話に興味を持ってもらえなかったのが寂しい、というとてもわかりやすい感情が垣間見えた気がした。

というとてもわかりやすい感情が垣間見えた気がした。
contexts.WH: Of course, her expression was still shameless..., but I had the feeling that I was able to catch a glimpse of loneliness because I hadn't found the story of her past interesting, in that really easy to understand expression of hers.
contexts.MG:
When I started acting cold, Beato seemed unusually discouraged.
Of course, her expression was still shameless,
but in that really easy-to-understand expression of hers,
I had the feeling I was able to catch a glimpse of loneliness at my failure to find the story of her past interesting.

but I had the feeling that I was able to catch a glimpse of loneliness because I hadn't found the story of her past interesting,

contexts.note: Both editions retain an easy-to-understand expression instead of the plainly readable emotion beneath Beatrice’s brazen expression.

findings.sourceReading: Battler glimpses the plainly legible emotion of loneliness beneath Beatrice's still-brazen outward expression when he rejects her story.
findings.alternative: An emotion is ordinarily read through an expression, so the English still communicates that Battler can see her loneliness despite the preceding description.

findings.sourceReading: Feeling a little sorry for Beatrice, Battler maintains his careless posture but offers a slight conciliatory gesture by inviting her to continue.
findings.alternative: Cover for can broadly mean support or help someone out, and the following invitation shows exactly what Battler does for her.

findings.description: Ronove's honorific narration treats the reincarnated Beatrice as お嬢様, a human girl. It grew and it did not possess call her an inanimate thing across two clauses.

contexts.japanese:
「はい。
そのまさかでございます。
しかし、魂は同じと言えど、人間の魂はその器に強く影響を受けます。
お嬢様は、かつての記憶を全て失われ、ごく普通の人間の少女として成長されました」
「それが、……そこのガーデンチェアに座ってるベアトだってのか？」
「はい。
その通りでございます。
まさに瓜二つに成長なされました。

MG.japanese:
家庭教師が、内緒よと約束したはずなのに、…私が漏らした泣き言を、全てお母様に話してしまったらしい。お母様は、右代宮家に名を連ねる者が情けないと、私をひどく叱ったわ。
……私も、もちろん自分なりには努力していた。でも、蔵臼兄さんのような貫禄は全然なかったし、絵羽姉さんのような立派な成績はとても取れなかったし、留弗夫兄さんのようなリーダーシップがあったわけでもない。…いつも目立たず、特に秀でることもなく、何の為に右代宮家に生まれてきたのか、私自身が聞いてみたいくらいだった。
MG.translation:
Even though my tutor had promised to keep it a secret, ...apparently, they told Mother all about how I had complained. Mother scolded me brutally, saying my name was a disgrace to the Ushiromiya family. 
...Of course, I was doing the best I could. But I had none of Krauss nii-san's dignity, I couldn't get excellent grades like Eva nee-san, and I had no leadership abilities like Rudolf nii-san. ...I never stood out, didn't particularly excel at anything, and I found myself asking why I'd even been born into the Ushiromiya family.

UP.japanese:
家庭教師が、内緒よと約束したはずなのに、…私が漏らした泣き言を、全てお母様に話してしまったらしい。お母様は、右代宮家に名を連ねる者が情けないと、私をひどく叱ったわ。
……私も、もちろん自分なりには努力していた。でも、蔵臼兄さんのような貫禄は全然なかったし、絵羽姉さんのような立派な成績はとても取れなかったし、留弗夫兄さんのようなリーダーシップがあったわけでもない。…いつも目立たず、特に秀でることもなく、何の為に右代宮家に生まれてきたのか、私自身が聞いてみたいくらいだった。
UP.translation:
Even though my tutor had promised to keep it a secret, ...apparently, they told Mother all about how I had complained. Mother scolded me horribly, saying that I was a disgrace to the Ushiromiya family.
......Of course, I was doing the best I could. But I had none of Krauss nii‐san's dignity, I couldn't get excellent grades like Eva nee‐san, and I had no leadership like Rudolf nii‐san. ...I never stood out, didn't particularly excel at anything, and I almost wanted to ask myself why I had even been born into the Ushiromiya family.

findings.sourceReading: Rosa's mother condemns her complaints as unworthy of a member of the Ushiromiya family, intensifying the pressure Rosa feels to meet its standards.
findings.alternative: Calling Rosa's name a disgrace to the family conveys that her conduct reflects badly on the lineage, preserving the mother's harsh judgment.

findings.description: WH renders a warm fireplace gradually making the air stagnant or stale as making it “thicker and thicker,” replacing the ventilation image with unsupported physical density.

findings.sourceReading: Rosa compares Beatrice’s ambiguous life to a warm winter fireplace that gradually leaves the air stagnant and gives one a headache, while opening the window means enduring cold wind.
findings.alternative: Thick air can figuratively suggest stuffiness, but “get thicker and thicker” foregrounds density rather than increasingly stale, poorly ventilated air.

…彼女があまりに嬉しそうに笑うものだから、私は調子を合わせて頷いてしまう。
でも、彼女には私のそんな曖昧な笑顔の意味は伝わらないようだった。
ここを出れば、私が本当にそれらへ連れてってくれると、信じたようだった。

findings.sourceReading: Although Rosa wonders how she could possibly take Beatrice to those places without Father finding out, Beatrice’s delighted smile makes her nod along anyway.
findings.alternative: The unresolved problem and fear of Father could naturally make Rosa nervous, but this sentence presents the thought as a question; her emotional hesitation is developed separately.

UP.translation: As she did, she heard the sound of footsteps coming towards her, splashing through puddles. Shannon immediately chased away the emotions welling up inside her.

findings.sourceReading: Hearing someone run toward her through the puddles, Shannon immediately suppresses the elation left by the proposal.
findings.alternative: Her elation is an emotion and may feel as though it is welling up, but the generic wording loses its positive, giddy quality.

findings.description: WH says Kanon stepped in the puddles. 水溜りを踏むことになろうとも is hypothetical: even if he were to step in a puddle, his sound would be quieter than the rain.

contexts.japanese:
嘉音は特に、気配を殺せるように出来ている。
…例えるならば猫。
誰にも気取られることなく、いつの間にかそこにいて、いつの間にか立ち去ることができる。
だからたとえ、水溜りを踏むことになろうとも、
その音は水溜りを叩く雨音よりも遥かに小さい…。
源次もまた、そういう力を持ち合わせていた。
contexts.japanesePC: だから例え、水溜りを踏むことになろうとも、その音は水溜りを叩く雨音よりも遥かに小さい…。

嘉音は特に、気配を殺せるように出来ている。
…例えるならば猫。
誰にも気取られることなく、いつの間にかそこにいて、いつの間にか立ち去ることができる。
だからたとえ、水溜りを踏むことになろうとも、
その音は水溜りを叩く雨音よりも遥かに小さい…。
源次もまた、そういう力を持ち合わせていた。
contexts.WH: For example, even though he stepped in the puddles, the sound he made was far smaller than that of the rain hitting the puddles...
contexts.MG:
Kanon was especially good at hiding his footsteps.
...Just like a cat.
He was able to suddenly be there without anyone noticing and leave in the same way.
For example, even though he stepped in puddles,
the sound he made was far smaller than that of the rain hitting them...
Genji also had abilities of that kind.
contexts.UP:
Kanon was especially good at hiding his presence.
...Like he was a cat.
He was able to suddenly be there without anyone noticing, and leave in the same way.
So, even if he were to step in a puddle,
the sound he would make would be far smaller than that of the rain hitting the puddles...
Genji also had that ability.
contexts.note: MG retains an actual puddle step. UP restores the hypothetical “even if” illustration.

MG.japanese: 嘉音は特に、気配を殺せるように出来ている。…例えるならば猫。誰にも気取られることなく、いつの間にかそこにいて、いつの間にか立ち去ることができる。だからたとえ、水溜りを踏むことになろうとも、その音は水溜りを叩く雨音よりも遥かに小さい…。
MG.translation: Kanon was especially good at hiding his footsteps. ...Just like a cat. He was able to suddenly be there without anyone noticing and leave in the same way. For example, even though he stepped in puddles, the sound he made was far smaller than that of the rain hitting them...

findings.sourceReading: Kanon suppresses his presence so completely that even if he stepped in a puddle, the sound would be far quieter than rain striking it.
findings.alternative: The group has just run through puddles and may in fact have stepped in them, but this sentence uses the possibility to illustrate his ability rather than report an observed step.

findings.description: WH writes “a desecration to the result.” Standard English requires desecration of the result.

それは占いの結果に対する冒涜であり、
タロットを通じて神託を与えてくれる、人より上位の存在への冒涜ともなるのである。

タロット占いでもっとも禁じられている行為は、同じことを二度占うことである。

タロットを通じて神託を与えてくれる、人より上位の存在への冒涜ともなるのである。

To do so ridicules the results of fortune telling...

UP.translation: The most forbidden action in tarot reading is to try predicting the same thing twice. It is a desecration to the result of the fortune telling, and also desecrates the existence higher than humans which delivers signs through the tarot cards.

findings.sourceReading: Repeating a tarot reading desecrates both the divination’s result and the higher being that grants revelation through the cards.
findings.alternative: The intended relationship is transparent and the following clause uses the verb desecrated correctly.

鍵穴にそれを刺し、重い手応えで捻る。

findings.description: WH begins Beatrice’s balloon-of-life explanation with “Even though,” leaving it as a sentence fragment and changing her causal claim into a concession without a main clause.

郷田も上辺は合わせたが、内心は子供だましだと思っていたものだ。

findings.sourceReading: Gohda privately regarded the witch talk as childish, but outwardly respected and followed the island’s custom.
findings.alternative: Slight can mean treat as unimportant, so the intended refusal to dismiss the custom can be reconstructed. The demonstrative that remains vague and the construction does not sound natural in Gohda’s narration.

findings.description: WH calls Beatrice and her teacher’s meeting a “long awaited reunion.” 久し振りの再会 means a reunion after a long absence; it does not say either party desired it, and the teacher has just said she hoped never to be awakened or reunited.

findings.sourceReading: Beatrice mockingly asks what tea she should prepare for their reunion after so long apart; the teacher accepts the hospitality while treating her awakening as regrettable.
findings.alternative: Beatrice herself may relish the opportunity for a contest, and “long-awaited” is a common English collocation for reunion. It nevertheless asserts anticipation contradicted by the teacher’s explicit attitude.

如何なる武器でも打ち砕けない。

findings.sourceReading: Beatrice converts or substitutes a one-use War Tower for herself, letting the hammer strike the tower while she escapes behind it.

findings.description: WH says Lavoisier “abolished” the phlogiston theory and that the caloric theory “was abolished by Joule.” The Japanese 否定した means that their work refuted or disproved those theories, not that they formally abolished them.

findings.sourceReading: Battler says Lavoisier refuted the phlogiston theory and Joule refuted the caloric theory by establishing heat as energy rather than substance.
findings.alternative: Scientific theories can be said loosely to have been abolished when decisive evidence displaces them, and the historical direction remains clear. The verb assigns institutional cancellation rather than evidential refutation.

findings.description: WH calls the epitaph an “unintelligible riddle.” 難解 means difficult or hard to solve; the riddle is comprehensible enough to pose a valid challenge, not meaningless or impossible to understand.

findings.sourceReading: The culprit again demands that the family solve the exceptionally difficult epitaph and threatens to kill everyone if they fail.
findings.alternative: “Unintelligible” can be used loosely for something so difficult that its meaning is opaque, and everyone’s failure remains clear. It suggests incoherence rather than solvable difficulty.

findings.sourceReading: After securing the guesthouse, the adults treat the lobby as their fortress while handling the guns and waiting through the long day.
findings.alternative: Setting up camp conveys establishing a temporary defensive base and the surrounding lock-and-gun context remains. It loses the explicit fortress comparison.

findings.sourceReading: Battler says merely asking about suicide is too weakly worded to force the needed concession, so he demands the stronger proposition that all six deaths were homicides.
findings.alternative: “Naive” can imply a formulation insufficiently wary of loopholes, and the stronger homicide request follows immediately. It mislabels the defect in the wording as innocence rather than insufficient scope.

findings.description: WH renders 達観 as “a far-sighted view.” Here it describes Beatrice’s detached, resigned composure—as though accepting that Battler may laugh—not foresight or long-range judgment.

findings.sourceReading: Beatrice speaks with a detached resignation that seems to say Battler may laugh if he wishes.
findings.alternative: 達観 can denote a broad, dispassionate perspective, which may loosely resemble seeing farther than immediate humiliation. “Far-sighted” normally means prudent anticipation and gives the composure the wrong basis.

findings.description: WH says Battler “accepted it.” 飲み込んでおく means he swallows his objection and lets Beatrice’s cowardly behavior pass in the dignity of victory, not that he accepts or endorses the behavior itself.

findings.sourceReading: Battler thinks her behavior cowardly but decides, as the victor, to swallow the complaint and let it go.
findings.alternative: “Accepted it” can mean tolerating something without approval, and the preceding criticism prevents full endorsement. It remains less precise about suppressing the objection and declining to pursue it.

findings.alternative: Dragging oneself somewhere can loosely intensify the effort involved in returning after extensive redevelopment. The Japanese idiom supplies no such negative physical or emotional state.

findings.description: WH says Eva can create every happiness “by using this money.” She imagines literally melting down the gold to produce every happiness, preserving her fixation on the physical hoard and the extremity of her revelation.

findings.sourceReading: Facing the mountain of gold, Eva declares that every happiness in the world can be produced by melting this gold.
findings.alternative: Melting the gold is ultimately a means of converting it into spendable wealth, so “using this money” conveys the practical claim. It removes the concrete image and reduces her feverish possessiveness to ordinary spending.

findings.description: WH says Eva’s magic itself could not have been “granted” without mutual belief. 叶える takes the unstated wish or dream as its object: her magic could not have made this outcome come true unless the two Evas believed in each other.

findings.alternative: In magical language, a spell or magic may be “granted” through belief, and the surrounding lines still credit both selves. The sentence reverses the relation between the magic and the wish it fulfills.

UP.translation: Rosa slapped Maria's cheek, lifted her up while covering her mouth, and carried her off towards the entrance, trying to at least put some distance between her and Hideyoshi's room.

findings.sourceReading: After slapping Maria, Rosa lifts her while covering her mouth and carries her toward the entrance, away from Hideyoshi’s room.
findings.alternative: English sometimes uses “drag” loosely for compelling a child to go somewhere. Here Maria has explicitly been lifted and is being held, so dragging introduces a conflicting physical action.

findings.description: WH renders なるべく落ち着いた声 as “a properly calm voice.” Rosa is speaking in as calm a voice as she can manage, not being characterized as properly or fully calm.

contexts.japanese:
玄関では、真里亞の口を押さえたまま、楼座は途方に暮れていた。
ロビーでみんなの視線に耐え切れず、
子どもたちには２階へ上がれと怒鳴りつけ、ロビーを飛び出してしまった。
そして廊下に出れば、秀吉たちにうるさいと言われてしまった。
私はどこへ行けばいいというのか。
……この癇癪持ちの娘を連れて、どこへ行けばいいというのか。
悔し涙が溢れそうになった…。
未だ、叫ぼうともがき続ける真里亞の耳元に口を寄せ、
楼座はなるべく落ち着いた声で諭すように言う。
「………真里亞は、そんなにも薔薇が見たいのね…？」
真里亞は、うーうー唸りながら、何度も首を縦に振る。
「…どうしてそんなに薔薇が見たいの？
お母さんが聞いてあげるから、静かに話して？
叫んだら殴るわよ」

contexts.WH: As Maria kept struggling in an attempt to scream, Rosa put her mouth up to Maria's ear, and tried to persuade Maria in a properly calm voice.
contexts.MG:
By the entrance, with her hand still against Maria's mouth, Rosa was at a loss at what to do next.
She hadn't been able to withstand everyone's gazes in the lobby,
and had yelled at the children to go upstairs, dashing out of the lobby.
Then, she had gone out into the corridor, only to have Hideyoshi say that she was too noisy.
Where should I go now?
...Where should I take this child who's having a tantrum?
She felt as though tears of frustration were about to come out...
As Maria kept struggling in an attempt to scream, Rosa put her mouth up to Maria's ear...
and tried to persuade Maria in a properly calm voice.
"......Maria, do you really want to see the rose that much...?"
Maria nodded her head several times, moaning uu-uu-.
"...Why do you want to see it so much?
I'll listen as your mother, so will you tell me quietly?
I'll hit you if you scream."
contexts.UP:
By the entrance, with her hand still against Maria's mouth, Rosa was at a loss at what to do next.
She had been unable to withstand everyone's gaze in the lobby,
and had yelled at the children to go upstairs, before dashing out of the lobby.
And when she went out into the corridor, Hideyoshi had told her that she was being too noisy.
Where should I go now?
......Where should I take this child who's having a tantrum?
She felt as though she was about to cry in frustration...
As Maria kept struggling in an attempt to scream, Rosa put her mouth up to Maria's ear,
and tried to persuade Maria in as calm a voice as she could manage.
".........Maria, you really want to see the rose that much...?"
Maria nodded her head several times, moaning "uu‐uu".
"...Why do you want to see the rose that much?
I'll listen to you, so will you tell me quietly?
I'll hit you if you scream."
contexts.note: MG retains “properly calm”; UP restores that Rosa uses as calm a voice as she can manage.

findings.sourceReading: Rosa brings her mouth to the still-struggling Maria’s ear and speaks admonishingly in as calm a voice as possible.
findings.alternative: “Properly calm” may be read as adequately calm and the verb “tried” supplies some effort. The adverb modifies persuasion, however, while the source directly qualifies the degree of calm Rosa can manage.

findings.description: WH reduces 彼らの自作自演—an act staged by those apparent victims themselves—to the agentless claim that it “had to all be an act.”

…………しかし結局、殺人事件など何も起こっていない。
朝から起きているどたばたは全て、金蔵たちが仕組んだ茶番なのだ。
あの連鎖密室をよく考えれば、彼らの自作自演であることをこれ以上なく物語っている…。
「……本当に、薔薇を見たらもう大人しくする？」

contexts.WH: If you carefully thought about that chain of closed rooms, it clearly had to all be an act...
contexts.MG:
If it would keep Maria quiet for the time being,
Rosa thought that even going out into this wind and rain would be a small price to pay.
She thought it might be a bit reckless.
......But in the end, no murder or anything of the sort had actually occurred.
All of that clamor since this morning had been a farce set up by Kinzo.
If you carefully thought about that chain of closed rooms, it clearly had to all be an act...
"...Will you really listen if you get to see the rose?"
contexts.UP:
If it would keep Maria quiet for the time being,
Rosa thought that even going out into this wind and rain would be a small price to pay.
She did think it might be a bit reckless.
............But in the end, no murder or anything of the sort had actually occurred.
All of that clamor since this morning had been a farce set up by Kinzo.
If you carefully thought about that chain of locked rooms, it communicated more clearly than anything that it was all an act by the victims themselves...
"......Will you really listen if you get to see the rose?"
contexts.note: MG retains the agentless “all an act”; UP restores that Rosa thinks the apparent victims staged it themselves.

findings.sourceReading: In Rosa’s reasoning, the chain of closed rooms most clearly shows that those involved staged the incident themselves.
findings.alternative: The previous sentence calls the whole affair a farce set up by Kinzo, so readers can infer orchestration. The omitted reflexive agent is still the stated evidentiary conclusion Rosa draws from the closed-room chain.

findings.alternative: A future assurance can pragmatically renew an existing promise. The source explicitly asserts current compliance, which is the basis of Rosa’s demand that her sister stop pressing her.

findings.description: WH omits the explicit six from the morning’s doors bearing magic circles.

contexts.japanese: 今朝、魔法陣が描かれた６つの扉の中には、いずれも犠牲者の遺体が横たわっていた。
contexts.japanesePC: 今朝、魔法陣が描かれた６つの扉の中には、いずれも犠牲者の遺体が横たわっていた。
contexts.japanesePS3: 今朝、魔法陣が描かれた６つの扉の中には、いずれも犠牲者の遺体が横たわっていた。
contexts.WH: This morning, behind each of the doors with a magic circle drawn on them had been the body of a victim.
contexts.MG: This morning, behind each of the doors with a magic circle drawn on them...had been the body of a victim.
contexts.UP: This morning, behind each of the doors with a magic circle drawn on them, there had been the body of a victim.
contexts.note: The six victims and earlier investigation allow readers to recover the count, but this recap explicitly links six marked doors to six bodies and WH removes that numeral.

MG.japanese: とにかく、心当たりがない以上、これ以上をここで悩んでも仕方ないだろう。……それよりも重要なのは、この客間の中だ。今朝、魔法陣が描かれた６つの扉の中には、いずれも犠牲者の遺体が横たわっていた。…そして、新しく数字が書き加えられた客間には、何が新しく増えているのか。
MG.translation: Anyway, since we don't have any real clues, it's probably pointless to stand around here worrying about it. ...The inside of the parlor's much more important. This morning, behind each of the doors with a magic circle drawn on them...had been the body of a victim. ...So, if something new has been added to this door, does that mean something new has been added inside the parlor?

UP.japanese: とにかく、心当たりがない以上、これ以上をここで悩んでも仕方ないだろう。……それよりも重要なのは、この客間の中だ。今朝、魔法陣が描かれた６つの扉の中には、いずれも犠牲者の遺体が横たわっていた。…そして、新しく数字が書き加えられた客間には、何が新しく増えているのか。
UP.translation: Anyway, since we don't have any real clue, it's probably pointless to stand around here analyzing it. ......More important was the inside of the parlor. This morning, behind each of the doors with a magic circle drawn on them, there had been the body of a victim. ...And now that a number had been newly added to the door, what new thing had been added inside the parlor?

findings.sourceReading: ６つの扉 expressly counts six doors; each marked door contained a victim.
findings.alternative: The six victims and earlier investigation allow readers to recover the count, but this recap explicitly links six marked doors to six bodies and WH removes that numeral.

findings.description: WH substitutes a large accumulated number of victims for the rapid pace of successive killings.

contexts.japanese: …そりゃあもうすげぇ勢いでだ。
contexts.japanesePC: …そりゃあもうすげぇ勢いでだ。
contexts.japanesePS3: …そりゃあもうすげぇ勢いでだ。
contexts.WH: ...And there's been a hell of a lot of them by now.
contexts.MG: ...And there's been a hell of a lot of them by now.
contexts.UP: ...And at one hell of a pace, too.
contexts.note: A rapid succession also produces many victims, and the next sentence restores discussion of pace, but quantity and speed are distinct propositions.

MG.japanese: 親父も霧江さんも死に、使用人の人たちを皮切りに、次々に殺された。…そりゃあもうすげぇ勢いでだ。最初の殺人が何時の時点で始まったか知らねぇが、…それこそ、時速１人くらいのスピードで殺されてるんじゃねぇだろうか。
MG.translation: Dad and Kyrie-san are dead, and people have been killed off one by one, starting with the servants. ...And there's been a hell of a lot of them by now. I don't know when the first murder happened, ...but they might have been killed at a rate of about one person per hour by now.

UP.japanese: 親父も霧江さんも死に、使用人の人たちを皮切りに、次々に殺された。…そりゃあもうすげぇ勢いでだ。最初の殺人が何時の時点で始まったか知らねぇが、…それこそ、時速１人くらいのスピードで殺されてるんじゃねぇだろうか。
UP.translation: Dad and Kyrie‐san have died, and starting with the servants, people have been killed off one by one. ...And at one hell of a pace, too. I don't know what time the first murders started, ...but I'd say we're probably being killed at a rate of about one person an hour.

findings.sourceReading: すげぇ勢いで describes how rapidly the successive killings are occurring; the following sentence estimates an hourly rate.
findings.alternative: A rapid succession also produces many victims, and the next sentence restores discussion of pace, but quantity and speed are distinct propositions.

findings.description: WH writes a x shape, where the spoken initial vowel sound requires an X shape.

contexts.japanese: ベアトの体を何度か前後から貫いて、その黄金の尾で×字を描く。
contexts.japanesePC: それを命じると、螺旋を巻いて宙に留まっていた黄金の蛇が、文字通り獲物を狙う蛇のように素早く動き、ベアトの体を何度か前後から貫いて、その黄金の尾で×字を描く。
contexts.japanesePS3: ベアトの体を何度か前後から貫いて、その黄金の尾で×字を描く。
contexts.WH: When she ordered that, the gold snake that was curled in a helix and suspended in space, moved as fast as a real snake going after its prey, and pierced Beato's body multiple times from both sides, its gold tail drawing a x shape.
contexts.MG: and pierced Beato's body multiple times from both sides, its gold tail drawing a x shape.
contexts.UP: and pierced Beato's body multiple times from the front and the back, its golden tail drawing a × shape.
contexts.note: The shape remains fully intelligible; this is a local English grammar defect only.

MG.japanese: それを命じると、螺旋を巻いて宙に留まっていた黄金の蛇が、文字通り獲物を狙う蛇のように素早く動き、ベアトの体を何度か前後から貫いて、その黄金の尾で×字を描く。残酷なる魔女の命じたそのままに、ベアトの胸にクロスステッチを描く。
MG.translation: When she ordered that, the gold snake that was curled in a helix and suspended in space... moved as fast as a real snake going after its prey... and pierced Beato's body multiple times from both sides, its gold tail drawing a x shape. As the cruel witch had ordered, it drew a cross-stitch through Beato's chest.

UP.japanese: それを命じると、螺旋を巻いて宙に留まっていた黄金の蛇が、文字通り獲物を狙う蛇のように素早く動き、ベアトの体を何度か前後から貫いて、その黄金の尾で×字を描く。残酷なる魔女の命じたそのままに、ベアトの胸にクロスステッチを描く。
UP.translation: When she ordered that, the gold snake that was curled in a helix and suspended in space... moved as fast as a real snake going after its prey, and pierced Beato's body multiple times from the front and the back, its golden tail drawing a × shape. As the ruthless witch had ordered, it drew a cross‐stitch through Beato's chest.

findings.sourceReading: ×字 describes an X-shaped crossing drawn by the gold tail.
findings.alternative: The shape remains fully intelligible; this is a local English grammar defect only.

findings.description: WH replaces the statement that nobody can crush the heart with the statement that no amount of people could do so.

contexts.japanese: 何人たりとも、あの心臓を打ち砕けはしません。
contexts.japanesePC: 「…………無理でしょう。何人たりとも、あの心臓を打ち砕けはしません。…竜王陛下の兵士風情ではとてもとても。」
contexts.japanesePS3: 何人たりとも、あの心臓を打ち砕けはしません。
contexts.WH: "............It is probably impossible.  No amount of people could crush that heart.  ...Much less the likes of the soldiers who serve under His Highness the Dragon King."
contexts.MG: No number of people could crush that heart.
contexts.UP: No number of people could crush that heart.
contexts.note: No amount of people rhetorically includes one person, but it shifts emphasis from unrestricted personal inability to a numerical or collective measure, just before the successor claims an exception for her power.

MG.japanese: 「…………無理でしょう。何人たりとも、あの心臓を打ち砕けはしません。…竜王陛下の兵士風情ではとてもとても」
MG.translation: "......Indeed, it probably will be impossible. No number of people could crush that heart. ...And certainly not the soldiers who serve under His Highness the Dragon King."

UP.japanese: 「…………無理でしょう。何人たりとも、あの心臓を打ち砕けはしません。…竜王陛下の兵士風情ではとてもとても」
UP.translation: "............It is probably impossible. No number of people could crush that heart. ...Much less the likes of the soldiers who serve under His Highness the Dragon King."

findings.sourceReading: 何人たりとも means any person whatsoever or nobody when paired with the negative, not any number of people.
findings.alternative: No amount of people rhetorically includes one person, but it shifts emphasis from unrestricted personal inability to a numerical or collective measure, just before the successor claims an exception for her power.

findings.description: WH writes a absolute closed room, where an absolute is required.

contexts.japanese: 出口なき絶対の魔法密室にて、永遠に眠るがいいわ。
contexts.japanesePC: 「あんたを。ニンゲンを。……絶対に逃れられぬ赤き結界にて封じて殺す。さらばだニンゲンどもよ。出口なき絶対の魔法密室にて、永遠に眠るがいいわ。……さぁ、心して聞きなさい。赤き真実を。」
contexts.japanesePS3: 出口なき絶対の魔法密室にて、永遠に眠るがいいわ。
contexts.WH: "I'll seal you, and humans as well, ......in a red barrier that most certainly cannot be escaped from.  Farewell, lowly humans.  Sleep for all eternity in a absolute closed room of magic with no exits.  ......Come on, listen carefully.  Listen to the red truth."
contexts.MG: Sleep for all eternity in a absolute closed room of magic with no exits.
contexts.UP: Sleep for all eternity in an absolute locked room of magic with no exits.
contexts.note: Its meaning remains clear; the article error is distinct from the omitted killing already catalogued as finding063.

MG.japanese: 「あんたを。ニンゲンを。……絶対に逃れられぬ赤き結界にて封じて殺す。さらばだニンゲンどもよ。出口なき絶対の魔法密室にて、永遠に眠るがいいわ。……さぁ、心して聞きなさい。赤き真実を」
MG.translation: "I'll seal you, and Humans as well, ...in a red barrier that most certainly cannot be escaped from. Farewell, lowly Humans. Sleep for all eternity in a absolute closed room of magic with no exits. ...Come on, listen carefully. Listen to the red truth."

UP.japanese: 「あんたを。ニンゲンを。……絶対に逃れられぬ赤き結界にて封じて殺す。さらばだニンゲンどもよ。出口なき絶対の魔法密室にて、永遠に眠るがいいわ。……さぁ、心して聞きなさい。赤き真実を」

findings.sourceReading: The clause commands eternal sleep in an absolute magical closed room without an exit.

findings.description: WH replaces the taunt to die bitterly regretting her humiliation with a taunt to give up and die.

contexts.japanese: ヘソ噛んで死んじゃえばぁ？！」
contexts.japanesePC: 下らない下らない馬ッ鹿みたぁい！！　勇ましいことを言って割り込んでおきながら、その体たらくは何なのぉ？！　あぁ情けない恥ずかしい！！　ヘソ噛んで死んじゃえばぁ？！」
contexts.japanesePS3: ヘソ噛んで死んじゃえばぁ？！」
contexts.WH: Worthless, worthless, are you a moron?!!  What's with this predicament, even though you stepped between us saying something brave?!  Aaah, how pathetic, how embarrassing!!  Why don't you just give up and die?!"
contexts.MG: If only you'd just give up and die!"
contexts.UP: Why don't you just give up and die forever?!"
contexts.note: Bitter regret becomes capitulation; distinct from the separately counted UP eternal-duration addition.

MG.japanese: 「下らない下らない馬ッ鹿みたぁい！！　勇ましいことを言って割り込んでおきながら、その体たらくは何なのぉ？！　あぁ情けない恥ずかしい！！　ヘソ噛んで死んじゃえばぁ？！」
MG.translation: Worthless, worthless, are you a moron?!! How can you be so lame, and right after you cut in between us, talking so tough?! Aaah, how pathetic, how embarrassing!! If only you'd just give up and die!"

UP.japanese: 「下らない下らない馬ッ鹿みたぁい！！　勇ましいことを言って割り込んでおきながら、その体たらくは何なのぉ？！　あぁ情けない恥ずかしい！！　ヘソ噛んで死んじゃえばぁ？！」
UP.translation: "Worthless, worthless, you look so duuuumb!! What's with this state of affairs after you butted in sounding all heroic?! Aaah, how pathetic, how embarrassing!! Why don't you just give up and die forever?!"

contexts.japanese: あっははははは、今すぐヘソでも噛んで、死んじゃえばぁッ？！
contexts.japanesePC: 下らない下らない馬ッ鹿みたぁい！！　勇ましいことを言って割り込んでおきながら、その体たらくは何なのぉ？！　あぁ情けない恥ずかしい！！　ヘソ噛んで死んじゃえばぁ？！」
contexts.japanesePS3: あっははははは、今すぐヘソでも噛んで、死んじゃえばぁッ？！
contexts.WH: Worthless, worthless, are you a moron?!!  What's with this predicament, even though you stepped between us saying something brave?!  Aaah, how pathetic, how embarrassing!!  Why don't you just give up and die?!"
contexts.MG: Ahhahahahahaha, if only you'd just give up and die right now!!
contexts.UP: Ahhaha{0ha{0ha{0haha, why don't you just give up and die now and foreverrr?!
contexts.note: Bitter regret becomes capitulation; distinct from the separately counted UP eternal-duration addition.

MG.japanese: 「悔しい？　聞きたければ地獄まで行って、あんたの家族に聞いてみるといい！　なら今すぐ死なないとねぇ？！　あっははははは、今すぐヘソでも噛んで、死んじゃえばぁッ？！　わーっはっはっはっはっはっはっはっはっはっはっはっはっはっはっはっはっはっはッ！！」
MG.translation: "Oh, are you mad? If you want to hear it so much, try going to hell and asking your family there! In that case, you'd better die right now, right?! Ahhahahahahaha, if only you'd just give up and die right now!! Waaahhahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahaha!!"

UP.japanese: 「悔しい？　聞きたければ地獄まで行って、あんたの家族に聞いてみるといい！　なら今すぐ死なないとねぇ？！　あっははははは、今すぐヘソでも噛んで、死んじゃえばぁッ？！　わーっはっはっはっはっはっはっはっはっはっはっはっはっはっはっはっはっはっはッ！！」
UP.translation: "Upset? If you want to hear, try going to hell and asking your family there! In that case, you better die right now, right?! Ahhaha{0ha{0ha{0haha, why don't you just give up and die now and foreverrr?! Waaahhah‐hah‐hah‐hah‐hah‐hah‐hah‐hah‐hah‐hah‐hah‐hah‐hah‐hah‐hah‐hah‐hah‐hah!!"

findings.sourceReading: ヘソ噛んで invokes 臍を噛む, bitter or futile regret, in a speech mocking Beato’s brave intervention and subsequent humiliating failure.
findings.alternative: The taunt also seeks Beato’s capitulation and death, but giving up does not preserve the idiom’s regret and humiliation component.

findings.description: WH changes Lambda’s condition for continued sponsorship from trying to remain the certain victor to repeatedly trying to become the victor.

contexts.japanese: ……あなたが“絶対”の勝者であり続けようとする限り、私は絶対の魔女として、あなたに力を与えるわ。
contexts.japanesePC: 「いいこと？　あんたの役目は、ベルンカステルを屈服させることよ。つまりゲームに、永遠に勝者でいること。……あなたが“絶対”の勝者であり続けようとする限り、私は絶対の魔女として、あなたに力を与えるわ。…………でも。
contexts.japanesePS3: ……あなたが“絶対”の勝者であり続けようとする限り、私は絶対の魔女として、あなたに力を与えるわ。
contexts.WH: "You know what?  Your role is to make Bernkastel surrender.  In other words, that means being the victor in this game for all eternity.  ......As long as you keep trying to become the 'certain' victor, then I will give you my power as the Witch of Certainty.  ............However.
contexts.MG: ...As long as you keep trying to become the victor "with certainty", then I'll give you my power as the Witch of Certainty.
contexts.UP: ......As long as you keep trying to become the certain victor, then I will give you my power as the Witch of Certainty.
contexts.note: The preceding eternal-victory sentence makes the intended requirement recoverable, and keep trying carries persistence, but become describes attaining the position rather than retaining it.

MG.japanese: 「いいこと？　あんたの役目は、ベルンカステルを屈服させることよ。つまりゲームに、永遠に勝者でいること。……あなたが“絶対”の勝者であり続けようとする限り、私は絶対の魔女として、あなたに力を与えるわ。…………でも」
MG.translation: "You know what? Your role is to make Bernkastel surrender. In other words, that means being the victor in this game for all eternity. ...As long as you keep trying to become the victor "with certainty", then I'll give you my power as the Witch of Certainty. ......However."

UP.japanese: 「いいこと？　あんたの役目は、ベルンカステルを屈服させることよ。つまりゲームに、永遠に勝者でいること。……あなたが“絶対”の勝者であり続けようとする限り、私は絶対の魔女として、あなたに力を与えるわ。…………でも」
UP.translation: "Listen close, okay? Your role is to break Bernkastel, force her to yield. In other words, that means being the victor in this game for all eternity. ......As long as you keep trying to become the certain victor, then I will give you my power as the Witch of Certainty. ............However."

findings.sourceReading: “絶対”の勝者であり続けようとする requires Beato to seek to continue being the certain victor, maintaining unbroken victory.
findings.alternative: The preceding eternal-victory sentence makes the intended requirement recoverable, and keep trying carries persistence, but become describes attaining the position rather than retaining it.

findings.description: WH transfers the restriction from where Bernkastel can sing or cry to what she can do, saying she can do nothing except cry in Lambda’s palm.

contexts.japanese: …私の手の平でしか鳴けないように、たっぷりと仕込んであげるんだから」
contexts.japanesePC: ……そしてあなたが屈服したら、…私の手の平でしか鳴けないように、たっぷりと仕込んであげるんだから。
contexts.japanesePS3: …私の手の平でしか鳴けないように、たっぷりと仕込んであげるんだから」
contexts.WH: ......And when you surrender, ...I'll train you so that you can't do anything other than cry in the palm of my hand.
contexts.MG: ...I'll train you so that you can't do anything other than cry in the palm of my hand."
contexts.UP: ...I'll train you so that you can't tweet in anyone's palm but mine."
contexts.note: Both imply coercive captivity, but inability to do anything except cry is a stronger and differently scoped limitation than exclusive dependence on the specified place or person.

MG.japanese: 「……そしてあなたが屈服したら、…私の手の平でしか鳴けないように、たっぷりと仕込んであげるんだから」
MG.translation: "...And when you surrender, ...I'll train you so that you can't do anything other than cry in the palm of my hand."

UP.japanese: 「……そしてあなたが屈服したら、…私の手の平でしか鳴けないように、たっぷりと仕込んであげるんだから」
UP.translation: "......And when you give in, ...I'll train you so that you can't tweet in anyone's palm but mine."

findings.sourceReading: 私の手の平でしか鳴けない means she will be trained so she can sing or cry only in Lambda’s palm, continuing the captive-bird metaphor.

findings.description: WH changes the warning that revenge cannot guarantee the family’s return into a statement that there is no definite proof of their return.

contexts.japanese: 仮に復讐を成し遂げられたとしても、家族が帰ってくる絶対の保証はない。
contexts.japanesePC: 「……徒労になるかもしれない。仮に復讐を成し遂げられたとしても、家族が帰ってくる絶対の保証はない。奇跡的確率で、せいぜい１人を連れ戻せるかどうかよ。」
contexts.japanesePS3: 仮に復讐を成し遂げられたとしても、家族が帰ってくる絶対の保証はない。
contexts.WH: "......It may be a fruitless effort.  Even if you succeed in your revenge, there's no definite proof that your family will return.  Even with a miraculous probability, you may be able to bring only one person back."
contexts.MG: Even if you succeed in your revenge, there's no definite proof that your family will return.
contexts.UP: Even if you succeed in your revenge, there's no definite proof that your family will return.
contexts.note: No proof can colloquially communicate uncertainty, and the adjacent fruitless-effort and miraculous-probability warnings preserve that uncertainty, but lack of evidence and lack of assurance are distinct formulations.

MG.japanese: 「……徒労になるかもしれない。仮に復讐を成し遂げられたとしても、家族が帰ってくる絶対の保証はない。奇跡的確率で、せいぜい１人を連れ戻せるかどうかよ」
MG.translation: "...It may be a fruitless effort. Even if you succeed in your revenge, there's no definite proof that your family will return. Even if you manage to hit a miraculous probability, you may only be able to bring one person back, if that."

UP.japanese: 「……徒労になるかもしれない。仮に復讐を成し遂げられたとしても、家族が帰ってくる絶対の保証はない。奇跡的確率で、せいぜい１人を連れ戻せるかどうかよ」

findings.description: WH changes being allowed to open his mouth into being able to do so.

contexts.japanese: もっとも、口を開くことが許されたとしても、

MG.japanese:
蔵臼の爪先は宙をもがく。金蔵の隆々とした指が喉を締め上げているのだ。
喋るどころか、口をきくことさえ出来はしまい。もっとも、口を開くことが許されたとしても、今の蔵臼に、金蔵を納得させられるような言い訳など、思いつくわけもないのだが…。
MG.translation: Krauss clawed at the air. Kinzo's brawny finger was choking him. He couldn't even open his mouth, much less talk. However, even if he had been able to open his mouth, as he was now, there was no way he'd be able to think up an excuse that Kinzo would accept...

UP.japanese:
蔵臼の爪先は宙をもがく。金蔵の隆々とした指が喉を締め上げているのだ。
喋るどころか、口をきくことさえ出来はしまい。もっとも、口を開くことが許されたとしても、今の蔵臼に、金蔵を納得させられるような言い訳など、思いつくわけもないのだが…。
UP.translation:
Krauss's feet scrabbled at the air. Kinzo's brawny finger was choking him.
He couldn't even open his mouth, much less talk. However, even if he had been allowed to open his mouth, as he was now, there was no way he would be able to think up an excuse that Kinzo would accept...

MG.japanese: 「あのね？　幸せのカケラも、不幸せのカケラも、どちらもいっぱいあって、世界を満たしてるの。だから、身近の幸せが見つけられない人は、どこまで探しに行っても見つけられない。……チルチルとミチルが青い鳥を探したみたいに」
MG.translation: "You know what? There are lots of happy and unhappy Fragments, and they fill the world up. So people who can't find happiness right beside them won't be able to find it no matter how hard they look. ...Like Tyltyl and Mytyl searching for the blue bird."

UP.japanese: 「あのね？　幸せのカケラも、不幸せのカケラも、どちらもいっぱいあって、世界を満たしてるの。だから、身近の幸せが見つけられない人は、どこまで探しに行っても見つけられない。……チルチルとミチルが青い鳥を探したみたいに」
UP.translation: "You know what? There are lots and lots of both happy and unhappy fragments, and the world is full to the brim with both kinds. So people who can't find happiness right beside them won't be able to find it no matter where they go looking. ......Like Tyltyl and Mytyl searching for the blue bird."

MG.japanese: 当時、絵羽は唯一の生き残りとして右代宮家の家督を継承し、全ての財産を独占したかに思われていた。しかし、当時は事故から半年しか経ておらず、危難失踪が成立していなかった。その為、絵羽は家族の生命保険さえ降りず、経済的にかなり困窮していたと思われる。
MG.translation: At the time, it was thought that Eva would succeed the Ushiromiya family and have all the wealth to herself, as the only survivor. However, at that point, not even half a year had passed since the accident, and the others had not been missing long enough to be presumed dead, even under extraordinary circumstances. Because of that, Eva had supposedly been in a very tight spot financially, unable even to collect on her family's life insurance.

UP.japanese: 当時、絵羽は唯一の生き残りとして右代宮家の家督を継承し、全ての財産を独占したかに思われていた。しかし、当時は事故から半年しか経ておらず、危難失踪が成立していなかった。その為、絵羽は家族の生命保険さえ降りず、経済的にかなり困窮していたと思われる。
UP.translation: At the time, everyone thought that Eva had succeeded the Ushiromiya family and obtained all the wealth for herself as the only survivor. However, at that point, barely half a year had passed since the accident, which was not enough for the rest of the family to be legally declared dead in absentia, even given the extraordinary circumstances. Because of that, Eva was thought to have been in a very tight spot financially, unable even to collect from her family's life insurance.

findings.alternative: Retrospective would can express prediction, but the source contemporary appearance concerns completion.

MG.japanese:
その時、廊下から足音が近付いてくるのが聞こえた。
それも複数。夏妃は、はっとして顔を上げる……。しかし、ノックの音だったため、その表情には失望が浮かぶのだった。なぜなら、金蔵だったなら、ノックなどしないだろうからだ。

その時、廊下から足音が近付いてくるのが聞こえた。

Right then, they heard the sound of footsteps approaching from the hall.

MG.japanese:
その丘からの急な下り坂は、１２年間の風雨で土砂が崩れてしまったのかもしれない。緩やかな崖といってもいいような岩だらけの斜面になっており、転げ落ちるのは簡単だが、登るのはかなり難しくなっているようだった。………どうやら、これ以上を進むのは、無理なようだった。これ以上を進めば、戻れなくなる。
つまりは、………ここが、境。
MG.translation: The steep downward slope beyond this hill had probably been caused by earth and rocks collapsing from 12 years of wind and rain. It had become a slant filled with crags that you might even call gentle cliffs, and it would be easy to tumble down, though it looked like climbing back would be pretty difficult. ......In any event, it seemed that proceeding any further would be impossible. If I continued any further, I wouldn't be able to return. In other words, ......this is...the border.

UP.japanese:
その丘からの急な下り坂は、１２年間の風雨で土砂が崩れてしまったのかもしれない。緩やかな崖といってもいいような岩だらけの斜面になっており、転げ落ちるのは簡単だが、登るのはかなり難しくなっているようだった。………どうやら、これ以上を進むのは、無理なようだった。これ以上を進めば、戻れなくなる。
つまりは、………ここが、境。
UP.translation:
The steep downward slope beyond this hill had probably been caused by landslides from twelve years of wind and rain. It had become a slant filled with crags that you might even call gentle cliffs, and though it would be easy to tumble down, it looked like climbing back would be pretty difficult. .........It seemed that proceeding any further would be impossible. If I continued any further, I wouldn't be able to return.
In other words, .........this is...the border.

findings.sourceReading: The existing downward path may have lost earth to twelve years of weather, leaving a rocky descent.
findings.alternative: Landslide damage could produce the present shape, but the English attributes the slope itself to the collapse instead of the damaged existing route.

MG.japanese:
朱志香の部屋には鍵が掛かっていた。
しかし、俺にはマスターキーがあるから何も問題はない。そして室内は、………ひどい有様だった。…でも、食堂でもうお馴染みの死体だから、……多少は免疫もあった。受話器が外れて、ぶら下がっている。
……俺との電話中に、殺されたのだろうか。朱志香はすぐその脇の壁に寄りかかるようにして、……頭部を半分、ブチまけている。
「戦人が来た時には、私は頭を半分ブチまけた死体だよ」
MG.translation:
The door to her room was locked. But that wasn't a problem at all, since I had a master key. Inside the room, ......it was horrible. ...But after the dining hall, I was used to corpses, ...so I'd built up a bit of an immunity. The phone receiver was loose and dangling. ...Had she been killed while still on the phone with me? Jessica was leaning against the wall right next to it, ...with half of her head split open. 
"When you come, Battler, I'll be a corpse with half of its head split open."

findings.sourceReading: ぶちまけられて describes the half-head contents scattered or splattered out, not merely an opening.
findings.alternative: Splitting can accompany the injury, but omits the specified scattering emphasized in the corpse description.

MG.japanese: 床にはしっかりと、くたびれてはいるが貫禄ある絨毯が敷かれている。……どう見ても一枚物だ。落とし穴が開くってんなら、ちゃんとそこだけ切れ目が入れてあるってことになる。……それに、落とし穴なんて細工があったら、あるけばギシギシとか、音を立てるんじゃないか？？いくら歩き回り、絨毯を撫で回してみても、とても落とし穴が隠されているとは思えない。
MG.translation: The room had a solid floor with a carpet that looked dignified, if a bit worn out. ...No matter how you looked at it, it was single piece. If a pitfall had opened up, there would have to be a seam just in that place. ...And, if there had been some trick like a pitfall, wouldn't it creak when you walked on it?? No matter how much I walked around, feeling the carpet, I just couldn't imagine that a pitfall was hidden here.

UP.japanese: 床にはしっかりと、くたびれてはいるが貫禄ある絨毯が敷かれている。……どう見ても一枚物だ。落とし穴が開くってんなら、ちゃんとそこだけ切れ目が入れてあるってことになる。……それに、落とし穴なんて細工があったら、あるけばギシギシとか、音を立てるんじゃないか？？いくら歩き回り、絨毯を撫で回してみても、とても落とし穴が隠されているとは思えない。
UP.translation: The floor was firmly laid with a majestic, if a bit worn‐out, carpet. ......It was clearly a single piece. If pitfalls are meant to open up in it, there would have to be a seam in that one place. ......And anyway, if there was some trick like a pitfall, wouldn't it creak when you walked on it?? No matter how much I walked over or ran my hands over the carpet, I just couldn't imagine that a pitfall was hidden here.

findings.sourceReading: A single countable piece requires a in this declarative sentence.
findings.alternative: No marked dialect or clipped dialogue explains the missing article in ordinary narration.

MG.japanese: 俺も、あのベアトリーチェと名乗った謎の女が現れた時には、ヤツが本当に魔女で、山羊のバケモノを次々に呼び出すのではないかと、かなり信じていた。……しかし、丸一日も放置されて、緊張感がすっかり解けてしまうと。そんなバカなことが絶対にあるわけがないと思えるのだ。命が危険に晒された異常な状況下で、ちょっと頭が混乱して、魔女が魔法で襲ってきたかのような、そんな勘違いをしてしまったのではないか。…………しかし、複数の人間が同じように証言し、その上、全員の意見が食い違わない。……ひとりだけの発言だったなら、何かの見間違いだろうと疑うところなのだが、……それがあまりに、難しい……。
MG.translation: When the mystery woman calling herself Beatrice appeared, even I had pretty much believed that she was a real witch and might start summoning goat monsters right and left. ...However, after being left alone for a whole day, my feeling of tension had faded completely. I was now able to think that something so stupid definitely couldn't be true. Did they lose their heads a little in an extraordinary situation where their lives were exposed to danger......... and mistakenly think that a witch was attacking them with magic? ......But multiple people gave the same kind of testimony, and on top of that, none of their opinions conflicted each other. ...If it had just been a single statement, I'd be able to suspect that they just didn't see what they thought they saw, ...but doing that now is pretty...difficult...

UP.japanese: 俺も、あのベアトリーチェと名乗った謎の女が現れた時には、ヤツが本当に魔女で、山羊のバケモノを次々に呼び出すのではないかと、かなり信じていた。……しかし、丸一日も放置されて、緊張感がすっかり解けてしまうと。そんなバカなことが絶対にあるわけがないと思えるのだ。命が危険に晒された異常な状況下で、ちょっと頭が混乱して、魔女が魔法で襲ってきたかのような、そんな勘違いをしてしまったのではないか。…………しかし、複数の人間が同じように証言し、その上、全員の意見が食い違わない。……ひとりだけの発言だったなら、何かの見間違いだろうと疑うところなのだが、……それがあまりに、難しい……。
UP.translation: When that mysterious woman calling herself Beatrice appeared, even I pretty much believed that she was a real witch and might start summoning goat monsters right and left. ......However, after being left alone for a whole day, once my feeling of tension faded completely, I had a level enough head to think that this was way too stupid to possibly be true. In that extraordinary situation where their lives were exposed to danger, did they just lose their heads a little, and mistakenly think that a witch was attacking them with magic? ............But multiple people testified to the same effect, and on top of that, none of their opinions contradicted one another. ......If it had been a single person's statement, I'd be able to suspect that they just didn't see what they thought they saw, ......but doing that now is pretty...difficult......

findings.sourceReading: Conflict in this sense is intransitive: opinions conflicted with each other.
findings.alternative: The transitive use would require a different sense; ordinary mutual disagreement needs the preposition.

contexts.japanese: そして、床にどっかりと転げ、大地のある安心感を全身で味わった。

MG.japanese: 何度も叩き付け、ようやくガラスに握り拳大の穴が開く。足場が悪いせいで、ずいぶんと手間取ってしまった…。金槌の先を器用に使い、脆くなったガラス片を払って穴を広げ、そこから手を突っ込み、鍵を開けた。そして、苦闘の末、何とか窓を開き、留弗夫の体が書斎に滑り込む。そして、床にどっかりと転げ、大地のある安心感を全身で味わった。
MG.translation: He hit it several times, and eventually, a fist-sized hole opened up in the glass. Because of his unstable footing, this took a lot of effort... Using the end of the hammer skillfully, he brushed aside the now fractured bits of glass and opened the hole further, stuck his hand through it, and unlocked the window. Then, after a hard struggle, Rudolf somehow managed to open the window, and his body slipped through into the study. After that, he flopped onto the floor, using his entire body to enjoy the relief of having a ground under him.

UP.japanese: 何度も叩き付け、ようやくガラスに握り拳大の穴が開く。足場が悪いせいで、ずいぶんと手間取ってしまった…。金槌の先を器用に使い、脆くなったガラス片を払って穴を広げ、そこから手を突っ込み、鍵を開けた。そして、苦闘の末、何とか窓を開き、留弗夫の体が書斎に滑り込む。そして、床にどっかりと転げ、大地のある安心感を全身で味わった。

Using the end of the hammer skillfully, he brushed aside the now fractured bits of glass and opened the hole further, stuck his hand through it, and unlocked the window. After that, he flopped onto the floor, using his entire body to enjoy the relief of having a ground under him.

findings.sourceReading: The physical ground sense is uncountable here; ground under him or solid ground beneath him is idiomatic.
findings.alternative: A ground can refer to a particular terrain or basis in other constructions; this unqualified physical-floor usage does not supply that reading. Meaning remains clear.
