findings.description: MG interprets Jessica’s turning away as not wanting to trouble Shannon. The source presents the gesture as if she did not want attention, followed by Shannon recognizing a desire not to be pressed further. UP preserves attention-seeking denial.

contexts.japanese:
「………しゃ、紗音、もう時間だろ？
早く行かないとまた源次さんや母さんに怒られるぜ。
私は全然平気だから早く行きなよ…！
へへ、悪ぃな、泣いちゃったりなんかしてさ。
……馬鹿みてぇだぜ、私」
朱志香は、構って欲しいわけじゃないというような仕草で背中を向けると、
追い払うような感じで手をひらひらと振る。
紗音は、それ以上しつこくされたくないという朱志香のサインを受け取ると、
ぺこりと頭を下げ、退室していくのだった…。
contexts.japanesePS3:
「………しゃ、紗音、もう時間だろ？
早く行かないとまた源次さんや母さんに怒られるぜ。
私は全然平気だから早く行きなよ…！
へへ、悪ぃな、泣いちゃったりなんかしてさ。
……馬鹿みてぇだぜ、私」
朱志香は、構って欲しいわけじゃないというような仕草で背中を向けると、
追い払うような感じで手をひらひらと振る。
紗音は、それ以上しつこくされたくないという朱志香のサインを受け取ると、
ぺこりと頭を下げ、退室していくのだった…。
contexts.MG:
"......Sh-Shannon, it's about time, right?
If you don't go quickly, Genji-san and Mom will get mad.
I'm just fine, so hurry up...!
Heheh, sorry for crying like this.
......I'm such a moron."
Jessica faced away, acting as though she didn't really want to trouble Shannon,
waving her hand as though chasing Shannon away.
Shannon took that as a sign that Jessica didn't want to be bothered anymore,
bowed her head, and left the room...
contexts.UP:
".........Sha‐Shannon, it's about time for you, right?
If you don't go soon, Genji‐san and Mom are gonna yell at you.
I'm totally fine, so get going...!
Heheh, sorry for crying like this.
......I'm such a moron."
Jessica faced away as if to show she wasn't looking for attention,
and waved her hand as though to drive Shannon away.
Shannon took that as a sign that she didn't want to be badgered any more,
bowed her head, and left the room...

MG.japanese: 朱志香は、構って欲しいわけじゃないというような仕草で背中を向けると、追い払うような感じで手をひらひらと振る。
MG.translation: Jessica faced away, acting as though she didn't really want to trouble Shannon, waving her hand as though chasing Shannon away.

findings.alternative: She turned away as if she was not asking for attention.

findings.description: Both have Beatrice happily blow on her pipe. 煙管をふかす here means smoking or puffing at the pipe; blowing on the object changes the action and leaves the smoking image unexpressed.

contexts.japanese: ベアトリーチェは、薔薇のアーチの上に腰を掛けながら、上機嫌に煙管をふかしていた。
contexts.japanesePS3: ベアトリーチェは、薔薇のアーチの上に腰を掛けながら、上機嫌に煙管をふかしていた。
contexts.MG: As Beatrice sat on the rose arch, she happily blew on her pipe.
contexts.UP: As Beatrice sat on the rose arch, she happily blew on her pipe.

MG.japanese: ベアトリーチェは、薔薇のアーチの上に腰を掛けながら、上機嫌に煙管をふかしていた。そんなところに腰掛けたら、薔薇が潰れてしまうし、アーチが倒れて危ないかもしれないが、…何しろ相手は魔女なのだ。それは余計な心配に違いなかった。
MG.translation: As Beatrice sat on the rose arch, she happily blew on her pipe. Sitting in a place like that would crush the roses, and it might have been dangerous if the arch fell over, ...but this was a witch, after all. Showing concern for her safety was probably a waste of time.

UP.japanese: ベアトリーチェは、薔薇のアーチの上に腰を掛けながら、上機嫌に煙管をふかしていた。そんなところに腰掛けたら、薔薇が潰れてしまうし、アーチが倒れて危ないかもしれないが、…何しろ相手は魔女なのだ。それは余計な心配に違いなかった。
UP.translation: As Beatrice sat on the rose arch, she happily blew on her pipe. Sitting in a place like that would crush the roses, and it might have been dangerous if you fell off the arch, ...but after all, this was a witch. That was surely an unnecessary concern.

findings.alternative: She sat on the rose arch, contentedly puffing at her pipe.

findings.description: MG says Shannon remembered the witch’s words, rather than the witch’s words making her remember the supposed impossibility of her relationship. UP preserves the words as the trigger. The following thought restores the content but the immediate reminder mechanism is changed.

contexts.japanese:
紗音は、ついつい甘い日々に浮かれ、全ての運命が自分を中心に回っていると錯覚してしまいそうになっていた。
…でも、魔女の言葉で思い出す。
譲治との縁は、本来ありえないもので、
………いや、これからもありえないものかもしれない…。
contexts.japanesePS3:
紗音は、ついつい甘い日々に浮かれ、全ての運命が自分を中心に回っていると錯覚してしまいそうになっていた。
…でも、魔女の言葉で思い出す。
譲治との縁は、本来ありえないもので、
………いや、これからもありえないものかもしれない…。
contexts.MG:
Shannon had just gotten wrapped up in those sweet days...and had started believing the illusion that all fate revolved around her.
...But she remembered the witch's words.
Originally, her relationship with George had been impossible...
...no, it might be impossible in the future as well...
contexts.UP:
Shannon had become swept up in these sweet days, and had started to fall under the illusion that all fate was revolving around her.
...But the witch's words made her remember.
Her relationship with George had originally been impossible,
.........no, might also be impossible in the future as well...

MG.japanese: 紗音は、ついつい甘い日々に浮かれ、全ての運命が自分を中心に回っていると錯覚してしまいそうになっていた。…でも、魔女の言葉で思い出す。
MG.translation: Shannon had just gotten wrapped up in those sweet days...and had started believing the illusion that all fate revolved around her. ...But she remembered the witch's words.

findings.alternative: But the witch’s words reminded her.

findings.description: The source says fear outweighed gratitude after reliance on the power. MG substitutes fear rather than gratitude, suppressing coexistence and relative degree; UP substitutes fear more often than gratitude, changing intensity into frequency.

contexts.japanese:
時に、その不思議な力に頼りながらも、その結果は感謝より畏怖の気持ちの方が大きかったに違いない。
………そんな繰り返しがきっと、魔女を深く傷つけていったに違いない。
contexts.japanesePS3:
時に、その不思議な力に頼りながらも、その結果は感謝より畏怖の気持ちの方が大きかったに違いない。
………そんな繰り返しがきっと、魔女を深く傷つけていったに違いない。
contexts.MG:
Surely, even those who had relied on that strange power sometimes felt fear rather than gratitude as a result.
...It must have deeply hurt the witch to have that happen over and over.
contexts.UP:
And even though on occasion they had relied on her strange power, it had undoubtedly resulted in fear more often than gratitude.
.........It must have deeply hurt the witch when that repeated over and over.

MG.japanese: ベアトリーチェは間違いなく魔女であり、不思議な、恐ろしい力を持っている。できることなら付き合いなどしたくないと誰もが思うだろう。時に、その不思議な力に頼りながらも、その結果は感謝より畏怖の気持ちの方が大きかったに違いない。………そんな繰り返しがきっと、魔女を深く傷つけていったに違いない。
MG.translation: Beatrice was definitely a witch, with a strange and terrifying power. Most people probably wouldn't want to stick around her if they could help it. Surely, even those who had relied on that strange power sometimes felt fear rather than gratitude as a result. ...It must have deeply hurt the witch to have that happen over and over.

UP.japanese: ベアトリーチェは間違いなく魔女であり、不思議な、恐ろしい力を持っている。できることなら付き合いなどしたくないと誰もが思うだろう。時に、その不思議な力に頼りながらも、その結果は感謝より畏怖の気持ちの方が大きかったに違いない。………そんな繰り返しがきっと、魔女を深く傷つけていったに違いない。
UP.translation: Beatrice was definitely a witch, with a strange and terrifying power. Most likely, no one would go along with her if they could help it. And even though on occasion they had relied on her strange power, it had undoubtedly resulted in fear more often than gratitude. .........It must have deeply hurt the witch when that repeated over and over.

findings.alternative: Even when they relied on that strange power, their fear must have outweighed their gratitude.

findings.description: MG changes Kinzo having fulfilled all dreams obtainable in the human world into being able to fulfill dreams satisfied by obtainable objects. This replaces completed attainment with capacity and narrows worldly aspirations to objects. UP retains completed satisfaction of worldly dreams.

contexts.japanese:
「そして、莫大な財産を得た金蔵は、人の世で手に入れることのできる全ての夢を叶えきった。
………そして、最後に世界の真理を求めたのだ」
「世界の、…真理？」
「…世界を構成する一なる元素。
人の世で得られる全てを満たした金蔵は、人が求める最後の欲望としてそれを欲したのだ」
contexts.japanesePS3:

"...The single element that makes up the world.
Kinzo, who had gained everything one can obtain in the human world, searched for that, the final desire humans seek."

findings.description: MG changes Beatrice’s reassurance that Shannon need not remember the single element into there being no need to worry. The source’s specific deflection of recollection is lost; UP preserves no need to remember.

contexts.japanese:
一なる元素。
………以前に彼女の口から聞かされた言葉のような気がする。
それが何だったか思い出そうとする紗音の表情を見て、ベアトリーチェは苦笑いしながら、思い出さなくて良い良いと手を振る。
contexts.japanesePS3:
一なる元素。
………以前に彼女の口から聞かされた言葉のような気がする。

contexts.MG:
The single element.
......She seemed to remember the witch using that word before.

contexts.UP:

.........She felt like she had heard the witch say those words before.

MG.translation: The single element. ......She seemed to remember the witch using that word before. When Beatrice saw Shannon trying to remember what that was, she laughed bitterly, waving her hand and saying there was no need to worry.

UP.japanese: 一なる元素。………以前に彼女の口から聞かされた言葉のような気がする。それが何だったか思い出そうとする紗音の表情を見て、ベアトリーチェは苦笑いしながら、思い出さなくて良い良いと手を振る。

findings.description: MG removes Beatrice directing Shannon’s assistance: she had her help regain power becomes Shannon helped, and I had you destroy the dining arrangement becomes you destroyed it. UP preserves the causative direction in both places. This changes the source’s repeated attribution of orchestration.

contexts.MG:
And Shannon had helped the witch regain her power, if only a little bit.
...As a result, it was now possible for the witch to drink tea with Shannon like this...
"...Beatrice-sama, what in the world was that mirror you told me to break?"
"Aaah, that.
......Long ago, it seems various things happened on the islands around this area.
Because of that, malignant forces gathered here and began to draw in an evil distortion.
It seems a traveling eastern magician or something built a shrine for the repose of souls and sealed them in there."
"...That in itself has nothing to do with me, but unfortunately, that magical power rested on a different foundation than mine.
It created a strong interference with my magic and was extremely bothersome."
"Is that how it was...?
And I just assumed it existed only to seal you, Beatrice-sama..."
"I was not its target.
But it was a divine mirror.
As a result, my power was sealed away.
...To use food as an example, maybe it would go something like this.
Let's say the Western food I ordered is being made in the kitchen.
However, when they try to set the table, the area for the guest seating is in the Japanese style with Japanese-style dishes.
So, the kitchen is unable to serve a plate that would be out of place, and no matter how long I wait, my Western food won't arrive. ...Something like that."
"So, you destroyed that Japanese-style guest seating and returned the area to a blank slate for a time.
contexts.UP:
And she had made Shannon help her to regain her power, even if only a little bit of it.
...As a result, she had become able to drink tea with Shannon like this...
"......Beatrice‐sama, what in the world was that mirror you told me to break?"
"Aaah, that topic.
.........It seems that a lot of things happened on the islands around this area, in the distant past.
Bad things gathered due to that, attracting bad distortions.
It seems that a traveling Eastern mage or someone built a shrine for the repose of souls and sealed them in there."
"...That in itself had nothing to do with me, but unfortunately the foundation of that magical power was different.
It created a strong interference with my own magic, and was extremely bothersome."
"Is that how it was...?
I just assumed that it had been sealing you, Beatrice‐sama..."
"I was not its target.
But it was a divine mirror.
As a result, my power was sealed away."
"......If I were to use food as an example, maybe it would go something like this.
Let's say that I have ordered some Western cuisine, which is being made in the kitchen.

「私、……家具じゃないもん。

「いや、人間じゃない。
僕らには愛する資格も、愛される資格も初めからない」

I can't believe myself—it's almost funny.

MG.japanese:
朱志香は、自分が何を不貞腐れてるのだろうと笑う。…さっき、どんな言葉を掛けられれば自分は満足したのかを想像して、笑う。……馬鹿馬鹿しかった。結局、自分がお子様なだけだった。
何だか呆れて、笑いたくなる。
MG.translation: Jessica laughed at what she was sulking over. ...She laughed at what kind of words she could possibly have been expecting. ...That was dumb of me. In the end, I was just acting like an entitled brat. I'm a little exasperated with myself, and it makes me want to laugh.

朱志香は、自分が何を不貞腐れてるのだろうと笑う。…さっき、どんな言葉を掛けられれば自分は満足したのかを想像して、笑う。……馬鹿馬鹿しかった。結局、自分がお子様なだけだった。
何だか呆れて、笑いたくなる。
UP.translation:
Jessica laughed at what she was sulking over. ...Laughed at what kind of words she would have had to receive to be satisfied. ......Ridiculous. In the end, I'm just a spoiled little kid.

findings.description: MG changes the expression Kanon habitually sees on Jessica into the expression Jessica wears when looking at Kanon. This invents a specifically Kanon-directed facial manner instead of the familiar island persona that he now recognizes as concealing her mood. UP retains Kanon as observer.

contexts.japanese:
朱志香の表情は、嘉音がいつも見るそれになっていた。
ついさっきまでの物憂げな朱志香ではない。
それは、右代宮本家跡継ぎの朱志香しか知らなかった昨日までの自分だったなら、
…朱志香はもう吹っ切れて元気を取り戻したと勘違いをするところだろう。
……でも、それは違う。
昨日までは視えなかった彼女を知ってしまったから、今の朱志香が見掛け通りの胸中であるわけがないと理解できた。

contexts.MG:
Jessica's expression became the one she always wore when looking at Kanon.
The listless Jessica from a second ago was gone.
If he had still only known Jessica as the eventual successor to the Ushiromiya family, as he had until yesterday,
...he might have mistakenly thought that Jessica's mood had sprung back to normal.
...But that wasn't right.
He now knew a part of her that he couldn't have "seen""seen" until yesterday, so he understood that there was no way Jessica actually felt the way she appeared.

findings.description: MG saw Jessica trod away uses the past form after saw instead of the bare infinitive tread; UP trodded uses a nonstandard past form instead of trod. Both disrupt the departure sentence, though the action is recoverable.

contexts.japanese:
背を向けた朱志香は、元気なくとぼとぼと歩み去るかに見えた。
だが突然、がむしゃらに駆け出し、屋敷の方へ消えていった…。

contexts.MG:
Kanon saw Jessica trod away with her back to him, looking disheartened.
But then, she suddenly broke into a reckless dash and disappeared in the direction of the mansion...
contexts.UP:
Jessica turned her back to him, and slowly trodded away, looking disheartened.
But suddenly, she started dashing pell‐mell, and disappeared in the direction of the mansion...

findings.description: MG makes the broken brooch evaporate like water. The source compares its disappearance to dissolving into water before it changes into golden butterflies. UP preserves the dissolving image.

contexts.japanese:
嘉音は踏みつけたままのブローチをさらに踏みにじる。
…パキリと割れた感触が足の裏に伝わった。
するとそれはさらりと水に溶けるように消え去り、
黄金に輝く蝶たちに変わって嘉音の足の裏からひらひらと舞い散っていった…。

He felt it break under his foot.

findings.description: 座席で locates Maria in her seat while she kicks her feet. MG makes her stomp her feet on the seat, adding contact with the seat surface. UP keeps the seated kicking motion.

contexts.japanese:
満員とは行かないまでも、車内は座席ほとんどが乗客で埋まる程度には大勢いた。
そんな中、座席で足をばたばたさせながらわがままを騒ぐ真里亞に、楼座は顔をしかめている。
さっきから楼座は声を潜めながら何度も注意しているのだが、真里亞は一向に聞き入れなかった。
contexts.japanesePS3:
満員とは行かないまでも、車内は座席ほとんどが乗客で埋まる程度には大勢いた。
そんな中、座席で足をばたばたさせながらわがままを騒ぐ真里亞に、楼座は顔をしかめている。
さっきから楼座は声を潜めながら何度も注意しているのだが、真里亞は一向に聞き入れなかった。
contexts.MG:
While it wasn't completely full inside the train, it was really packed, with almost all the seats occupied by passengers.
Maria was making a fuss among them, stomping her feet on the seat while Rosa scowled at her.
Rosa had warned her many times to lower her voice, but Maria hadn't obeyed her at all.
contexts.UP:
While it wasn't completely full inside the train, there were enough people here that almost all of the seats were occupied.
Among them, Maria was making a fuss, kicking her feet back and forth in her seat, while Rosa scowled at her.
Rosa had told her many times in a low voice to stop, but Maria was taking no notice whatsoever.

MG.japanese: 満員とは行かないまでも、車内は座席ほとんどが乗客で埋まる程度には大勢いた。そんな中、座席で足をばたばたさせながらわがままを騒ぐ真里亞に、楼座は顔をしかめている。さっきから楼座は声を潜めながら何度も注意しているのだが、真里亞は一向に聞き入れなかった。
MG.translation: While it wasn't completely full inside the train, it was really packed, with almost all the seats occupied by passengers. Maria was making a fuss among them, stomping her feet on the seat while Rosa scowled at her. Rosa had warned her many times to lower her voice, but Maria hadn't obeyed her at all.

UP.japanese: 満員とは行かないまでも、車内は座席ほとんどが乗客で埋まる程度には大勢いた。そんな中、座席で足をばたばたさせながらわがままを騒ぐ真里亞に、楼座は顔をしかめている。さっきから楼座は声を潜めながら何度も注意しているのだが、真里亞は一向に聞き入れなかった。
UP.translation: While it wasn't completely full inside the train, there were enough people here that almost all of the seats were occupied. Among them, Maria was making a fuss, kicking her feet back and forth in her seat, while Rosa scowled at her. Rosa had told her many times in a low voice to stop, but Maria was taking no notice whatsoever.

findings.alternative: The energetic motion permits kicking or flailing, but does not establish standing or striking the upholstery.

findings.description: 隣の座席 places the old woman in the adjacent seat. UP places her across from Maria, then calls her next to them at row 59; MG nearby is less precise initially but preserves adjacency at row 59.

contexts.japanese:
足をばたばたとさせる真里亞の隣の座席に座っていた恰幅のいい老婦人が、ハンドバッグの中からのど飴を取り出し、差し出した。
「うー！　お菓子もらえた、お菓子もらえた！
見て見てママ、
ママ！
ハッピーハロウィン〜！」
「こら真里亞、勝手に人からお菓子をもらっちゃ駄目でしょ？！
返しなさい！！」
「いいんですよ、ホッホッホ。
元気なお嬢さんですこと。
おいくつです？」
老婦人のその言葉に他意はなかったかもしれない。
…でも、楼座には非常に屈辱的に聞こえたようだった。
「真里亞ッ、知らない人からお菓子をもらっちゃいけないっていつも言ってるでしょッ！！」
「うー！
うー！！
これは真里亞がもらったのッ！！
うー
うー！！
いやだッ、真里亞のッ！！」
「離しなさいッ！
ママの言うことを聞けっていっつも言ってるでしょ！！」
「真里亞のー！！
真里亞のぉおおー！！
うー！！
うーーうーー！！」
「そのうーうー言うのを止めなさいって言ってるでしょッ！！」
「うーうーうーうーうーうーうーうー！！！」
楼座は反射的に真里亞の頬を激しく叩く。
…間髪入れずに真里亞は大声で泣き始めた。
すぐにその手から、楼座は飴玉を奪い取り、隣に座り呆然としている老婦人に付き返す。

contexts.MG:
A stout old woman, who was sitting nearby as Maria stomped her feet, picked a candy out of her handbag and held it out to Maria.
"Uu-! I got a sweet, I got a sweet!
Look, look, Mama,
Mama!
<Happy Halloween>!"
"Hey, Maria, you can't just accept sweets from strangers, right?!
Give it back!!"
"Oh, don't worry about it, ho ho ho.
She's such a spirited young lady.
How old is she?"
Maybe there was no malice in the old woman's words.
...However, Rosa seemed to find that remark extremely humiliating.
"Maria, haven't I always told you not to accept sweets from strangers?!!"
"Uu-!
Uu-!!
She gave it to me!!
Uu-
uu-!!
No, it's mine!!"
"Let go of it!
How many times do I have to tell you to do what Mama says?!!"
"It's mine!!
Miiiiine!!
Uu!!
Uuu--uuu--!!"
"Don't I always tell you not to say uu-uu-?!!"
"Uu-uu-uu-uu-uu-uu-uu-uu-!!!"
Rosa reflexively hit Maria violently on her cheek.
...In a flash, Maria started crying loudly.
Rosa immediately took the candy from Maria's hand and pushed it back towards the dumbfounded old woman sitting next to them.
contexts.UP:
As Maria kicked her feet, a stout old woman sitting in the seat across from Maria picked a candy out of her handbag and gave it to her.
"Uu! Got a treat, got a treat!
Look, look, Mama,
Mama!
Happy Hallowee~n!"
"Maria! You can't just accept sweets from strangers, remember?!
Return it!!"
"It's alright, hoh‐hoh‐ho.
She's a lovely young lady.
How old is she?"
There may not have been any malice in those words from the old woman.
...But it seemed that Rosa had taken that in an extremely humiliating way.
"Maria! I'm always telling you not to accept sweets from strangers!!"
"Uu!
Uu!!
This one's mine!!
Uu‐
uu!!
No, it's mine!!"
"Let go of it!
Don't I always tell you to listen to what Mama says?!!"
"It's miiine!!
Miiiine!!
Uu!!
Uuu‐uuu!!"
"I told you, stop making that childish whining noise!!"
"Uu‐uu‐uu‐uu‐uu‐uu‐uu‐uu!!!"
Rosa reflexively hit Maria violently on her cheek.
...In a flash, Maria started crying loudly.
Rosa immediately snatched the candy from Maria's hand and stuck it out towards the dumbfounded old woman sitting next to them.

UP.translation: As Maria kicked her feet, a stout old woman sitting in the seat across from Maria picked a candy out of her handbag and gave it to her.

findings.alternative: Across could describe a facing seat, but that spatial arrangement is not 隣 and conflicts with the later adjacent placement.

findings.description: ほくほくしながら describes Maria walking with delighted satisfaction. MG adds audible chuckling to herself; UP preserves pleased feeling without inventing a vocal action.

contexts.japanese:
二人は見知らぬ町の駅で改札を出る。
真里亞は、母と渡る横断歩道を、まるで遊園地で歩くようにほくほくしながら歩む。
まだ互いの顔は真っ赤だったけど、
……ぎこちなくも笑いあう二人の親子は温かに見えた…。
contexts.japanesePS3:
二人は見知らぬ町の駅で改札を出る。
真里亞は、母と渡る横断歩道を、まるで遊園地で歩くようにほくほくしながら歩む。
まだ互いの顔は真っ赤だったけど、
……ぎこちなくも笑いあう二人の親子は温かに見えた…。
contexts.MG:
They exited through the turnstiles of the station in this unknown town.
Maria walked across the pedestrian crossing together with her mother, chuckling to herself, as though she was walking in an amusement park.
Both faces were still deep red,
...but the two of them, mother and child, smiled warmly at each other without any restraint...
contexts.UP:
The two left the turnstiles of the station in this unknown town.
Maria walked across the pedestrian crossing together with her mother, feeling very pleased, as though she was walking in an amusement park.
Both faces were still deep red,
......but warmth could be seen between the two of them, mother and child, as they smiled at each other awkwardly...

二人は見知らぬ町の駅で改札を出る。
真里亞は、母と渡る横断歩道を、まるで遊園地で歩くようにほくほくしながら歩む。

findings.description: 確信があったからだ explains Krauss’s actual confidence as the reason for increasing investment. MG converts this to a hypothetical rule about what you would only do if confident, weakening attribution of the belief to Krauss. UP retains his confidence as his actual motivation.

contexts.japanese:
時に、そのシーソーが早く良い方へ傾くよう、さらに投資をすることもある。
……もちろん、遠くない将来に、かさんだ投資が全て取り返せるという確信があったからだ。
……しかし、蔵臼が選ぶシーソーは、いつも思い通りにならない。
contexts.japanesePS3:
時に、そのシーソーが早く良い方へ傾くよう、さらに投資をすることもある。
……もちろん、遠くない将来に、かさんだ投資が全て取り返せるという確信があったからだ。
……しかし、蔵臼が選ぶシーソーは、いつも思い通りにならない。
contexts.MG:
At times, it's possible to make further investments, so that the seesaw inclines faster towards the side you want.
...Of course, you'd only do that if you were confident you'd be able to recover all your investments in the not-so-distant future.
...However, the seesaws Krauss chose never turned out as he would have liked them to.
contexts.UP:
At times, he would make more investments so that the seesaw inclined faster towards the good side.
......Naturally, he did that because he had the confidence that, in a not‐so‐distant future, he would be able to recover all the investments made.
......However, the seesaws Krauss chose never turned out as he would have liked them to.

MG.japanese: 時に、そのシーソーが早く良い方へ傾くよう、さらに投資をすることもある。……もちろん、遠くない将来に、かさんだ投資が全て取り返せるという確信があったからだ。
MG.translation: At times, it's possible to make further investments, so that the seesaw inclines faster towards the side you want. ...Of course, you'd only do that if you were confident you'd be able to recover all your investments in the not-so-distant future.

findings.alternative: Generic second person can rhetorically explain an individual case, and surrounding sentences concern Krauss. It nevertheless replaces the explicit asserted reason with a conditional maxim.

findings.description: 賄いも今夜はぜひ期待してください asks the interlocutor to look forward to the servants’ meal too. UP adds an instruction to let the other servants know and an explicit promise not to disappoint them; neither speech act is stated in this line.

contexts.japanese:
「えぇ、ディナーには仔牛のステーキを…！
素晴らしい肉がすでに保冷庫で今夜を待ちわびておりますよ。
賄いも今夜はぜひ期待してください」
郷田が使用人仲間にこれだけ上機嫌なのは珍しい。

findings.description: 子どもには子どものコミュニケーションがある admires children’s own way of communicating. MG substitutes admiration of how good children are at getting along, changing the observation from a distinct mode of communication to proficiency at harmony. UP preserves the source observation.

真里亞は手提げの中から、手に持っていたのと同じジャックオーランタンのお菓子を取り出すと、戦人に差し出す。
それを戦人が受け取ることで、彼らの友情の確認は充分なようだった。
大人たちは、子どもには子どものコミュニケーションがあるのだなぁと感服する。
ハロウィンのお祭りがしたいと駄々をこねていた真里亞にとって、
トリックオアトリートを理解してくれた戦人はきっと仲間のように感じられたに違いない。
contexts.japanesePS3:
真里亞は手提げの中から、手に持っていたのと同じジャックオーランタンのお菓子を取り出すと、戦人に差し出す。
それを戦人が受け取ることで、彼らの友情の確認は充分なようだった。

contexts.MG:
From inside her purse, Maria picked out a jack o'lantern sweet similar to the one she had in her hand and presented it to Battler.
When Battler accepted it, that seemed to be enough to confirm their friendship.
The adults were amazed at how good children can be at getting along with each other.
Maria had been throwing a tantrum because she wanted a Halloween festival,
so Battler, who knew about trick-or-treating, must have felt like an ally.
contexts.UP:
From inside her handbag, Maria picked out a jack‐o'‐lantern sweet identical to the one she had in her hand, and presented it to Battler.

The adults felt admiration at how children have their own ways of communicating.
To Maria, who had been complaining that she wanted to have a Halloween festival,

MG.japanese: 大人たちは、子どもには子どものコミュニケーションがあるのだなぁと感服する。ハロウィンのお祭りがしたいと駄々をこねていた真里亞にとって、トリックオアトリートを理解してくれた戦人はきっと仲間のように感じられたに違いない。
MG.translation: The adults were amazed at how good children can be at getting along with each other. Maria had been throwing a tantrum because she wanted a Halloween festival, so Battler, who knew about trick-or-treating, must have felt like an ally.

findings.description: 感謝の気持ちがあってもいいわけだね allows gratitude for the harvest as a fitting interpretation of giving candy. UP the reason ... must be because ... they should be thanked strengthens this into a necessary causal explanation. MG you might say preserves the tentative allowance.

contexts.japanese:
「ハロウィンの仮装は、向こうから来る客人たちの模倣。
……つまり、彼らにお菓子を施すのは、一年の収穫への感謝の気持ちがあってもいいわけだね」
「うー！
譲治お兄ちゃんの言う通り！」
contexts.japanesePS3:
「ハロウィンの仮装は、向こうから来る客人たちの模倣。
……つまり、彼らにお菓子を施すのは、一年の収穫への感謝の気持ちがあってもいいわけだね」
「うー！
譲治お兄ちゃんの言う通り！」
contexts.MG:
"Halloween costumes imitate the guests that come from the other side.
...In other words, you might say giving out candy is a way to show gratitude for the yearly harvest."
"Uu-!
Just like George onii-chan says!"
contexts.UP:
"Halloween costumes are an imitation of the visitors from the other side.
......So, then, the reason we give candy to them must be because of a feeling that they should be thanked for the yearly harvest."
"Uu!
Just like George onii‐chan says!"

UP.japanese: 「ハロウィンの仮装は、向こうから来る客人たちの模倣。……つまり、彼らにお菓子を施すのは、一年の収穫への感謝の気持ちがあってもいいわけだね」
UP.translation: "Halloween costumes are an imitation of the visitors from the other side. ......So, then, the reason we give candy to them must be because of a feeling that they should be thanked for the yearly harvest."

findings.alternative: George is deriving an interpretation from Maria’s account, and her agreement endorses it. The Japanese still uses permissive あってもいい rather than obligatory necessity or a uniquely established origin.

findings.description: MG changes inventing protective rituals into performing them.

contexts.japanese: そこで彼らは、これらの害を受けないようなおまじないを生み出していった。
contexts.japanesePS3: そこで彼らは、これらの害を受けないようなおまじないを生み出していった。
contexts.MG: So, in order to avoid harm, they performed rituals.
contexts.UP: So in order to avoid harm from them, the people invented protective rituals.

MG.japanese: 現世に戻ってくる霊魂たちが、人々の家に入ってきたり、あるいは取り憑いて悪さをすると当時の人々は信じていた。そこで彼らは、これらの害を受けないようなおまじないを生み出していった。そのひとつが、不気味な怪物の姿を模して、霊魂たちを逆に怖がらせ、取り憑かれないようにしようというものだったらしい。
MG.translation: At the time, people believed that souls returning to the physical world would go into people's houses or possess people and do bad things. So, in order to avoid harm, they performed rituals. One of those was to imitate creepy monsters and scare the souls back, which was apparently a way to avoid being possessed.

UP.japanese: 現世に戻ってくる霊魂たちが、人々の家に入ってきたり、あるいは取り憑いて悪さをすると当時の人々は信じていた。そこで彼らは、これらの害を受けないようなおまじないを生み出していった。そのひとつが、不気味な怪物の姿を模して、霊魂たちを逆に怖がらせ、取り憑かれないようにしようというものだったらしい。
UP.translation: At the time, the people believed that the souls returning to the physical world would go into people's houses or possess people to do bad things. So in order to avoid harm from them, the people invented protective rituals. One of those was to imitate creepy monsters and scare the souls instead, which was apparently a way to avoid being possessed.

findings.sourceReading: 生み出していった narrates the practices being developed; original WH created enchantments and UP invented protective rituals preserve creation.
findings.alternative: Performing practices implies they exist, but does not preserve the narrated origin.

findings.description: 全員顔を揃える means everyone meeting or gathering together. UP gather our faces mechanically translates the idiom into an unnatural physical object for gather; MG meet in person conveys the meeting.

「そうや！
留弗夫くんの言う通りや。
……わしらが全員顔を揃えるのは年に一度しかない。
貴重な時間を大事にし、忌憚ない話し合いをせんといかん」
contexts.japanesePS3:
「そうや！
留弗夫くんの言う通りや。
……わしらが全員顔を揃えるのは年に一度しかない。
貴重な時間を大事にし、忌憚ない話し合いをせんといかん」
contexts.MG:

Just as Rudolf-kun says.
...This is the only time of year we can all meet in person.
We've gotta take this valuable time seriously and be frank with each other."
contexts.UP:
"Yep!
Just as Rudolf‐kun says.
......We can only gather our faces here once a year.
We've gotta value this precious time we've got, and talk together frankly."

findings.description: 鼻の下を伸ばした describes Hideyoshi and Rudolf’s leering or besotted expression as they watch Shannon leave. MG substitutes a general trait, had a soft spot for women, while UP turned heads supplies a neutral movement. Both weaken the immediate lustful reaction.

contexts.japanese:
「それでは、失礼いたします。
御用がありましたら、いつでもお呼び付けください」
紗音が丁寧にお辞儀して退室する。
鼻の下を伸ばした秀吉と留弗夫がそれを見送ると、
…場の空気は紗音が訪れる直前のものに逆戻りし始める。
contexts.japanesePS3:
「それでは、失礼いたします。
御用がありましたら、いつでもお呼び付けください」
紗音が丁寧にお辞儀して退室する。
鼻の下を伸ばした秀吉と留弗夫がそれを見送ると、
…場の空気は紗音が訪れる直前のものに逆戻りし始める。
contexts.MG:
"Then, if you will excuse me.
If there is anything you desire, please call for it at any time."
Shannon bowed politely and left the room.
As Hideyoshi and Rudolf, who had a soft spot for women, watched her go,
...the atmosphere in the room began to revert back to what it had been right before Shannon's visit.
contexts.UP:
"Then, if you will excuse me.
If there is anything you desire, please call for it at any time."
Shannon bowed politely and left the room.
After Hideyoshi and Rudolf watched her go with turned heads,
...the atmosphere in the room began to revert back to what it had been right before Shannon had visited.

MG.japanese: 紗音が丁寧にお辞儀して退室する。鼻の下を伸ばした秀吉と留弗夫がそれを見送ると、…場の空気は紗音が訪れる直前のものに逆戻りし始める。
MG.translation: Shannon bowed politely and left the room. As Hideyoshi and Rudolf, who had a soft spot for women, watched her go, ...the atmosphere in the room began to revert back to what it had been right before Shannon's visit.

UP.japanese: 紗音が丁寧にお辞儀して退室する。鼻の下を伸ばした秀吉と留弗夫がそれを見送ると、…場の空気は紗音が訪れる直前のものに逆戻りし始める。

findings.alternative: MG’s fondness for women and UP’s attention to Shannon can suggest attraction, but neither clearly preserves the depicted leering expression at this moment.

findings.description: 人影に飛びつく describes Maria leaping onto or clinging to the arriving figure. Both translations reduce this to dashing over to the figure, preserving approach but losing the physical contact. The following explanation likewise replaces jumping onto a stranger with dashing over.

「ベアトリーチェー！！」
真里亞がその人影に飛びつく。
……普段の楼座なら、見ず知らずの人に娘が飛びつくようなことがあれば叱る。
…しかし楼座は、それを忘れて、ただただ呆然とするしかできなかった。

「ベアトリーチェー！！」
真里亞がその人影に飛びつく。

findings.description: 留弗夫と絵羽の夫婦 includes Rudolf’s and Eva’s couples in the inheritance-protecting coalition. Both translations narrow the narrated participants to Rudolf and Eva alone, omitting their spouses from this collective action.

contexts.japanese:
「………こんなところでひょっこり現れた謎の女に、遺産のアテをブチ壊されて堪るもんですか…！」
留弗夫と絵羽の夫婦は、自分たちの遺産を余所者に掻っ攫われて堪るかと、
こんな時ばかり兄弟で結束するのだった。
霧江はその逞しい様子を見て、軽く首を横に振り、小さなため息を漏らしながら外を見た。

「………こんなところでひょっこり現れた謎の女に、遺産のアテをブチ壊されて堪るもんですか…！」

こんな時ばかり兄弟で結束するのだった。

contexts.MG:
......As if we'd just stand by and let some suddenly-appearing mystery woman destroy the inheritance we're after...!"
Rudolf and Eva always formed a united front as siblings at times like this,
sickened by the idea that their own inheritance might be snatched away by an outsider.
Kyrie noticed how indomitable they looked, shook her head slightly, and gave a small sigh as she gazed out the window.
contexts.UP:
".........There's no way I'm having my prospects of an inheritance destroyed now by some mystery woman who popped out of nowhere...!"
It was only at a time like this that Rudolf and Eva united as siblings,
sickened by the idea that their own inheritance might be snatched away by an outsider.
Kyrie noticed how indomitable they looked, shook her head slightly, and gave a small sigh as she looked out the window.

MG.japanese: 留弗夫と絵羽の夫婦は、自分たちの遺産を余所者に掻っ攫われて堪るかと、こんな時ばかり兄弟で結束するのだった。
MG.translation: Rudolf and Eva always formed a united front as siblings at times like this, sickened by the idea that their own inheritance might be snatched away by an outsider.

UP.japanese: 留弗夫と絵羽の夫婦は、自分たちの遺産を余所者に掻っ攫われて堪るかと、こんな時ばかり兄弟で結束するのだった。
UP.translation: It was only at a time like this that Rudolf and Eva united as siblings, sickened by the idea that their own inheritance might be snatched away by an outsider.

findings.alternative: The sentence highlights sibling solidarity and the spouses remain present in surrounding dialogue. Nevertheless 夫婦 explicitly includes both couples, not only the two siblings.

findings.description: UP renders Rosa’s 談合 with Eva and Rudolf as consulting, weakening her admission of collusion to extract money from Krauss.

contexts.japanese:
お父様の遺産の分配を、まだ存命の内から議論するなんて、自分は罪深い娘だと思う。
……しかし、綺麗事を言っていられる段階にない。
…そして、蔵臼兄さんからお金を引き出すため、絵羽姉さんや留弗夫兄さんと談合してすらいる。
そんな私にとって、………魔女の出現は、不吉なものを予見させずにはいられないのだ…。
………この中には何と書かれているのだろう。
……きっと、恐ろしいことが書かれているに違いない。
………まずはこっそり読んでみようか？
魔女は全員が揃った晩餐の席でと注文を付けた。
……しかし、そうならば自らの手で晩餐の席上で読み上げればいいだけではないか。
なぜわざわざ私に託すのか。
………つまりそれは、先にこっそり読まれても仕方ないということではないのか…。
……先に中身を読んでおいた方がいい。
…約束違反なのはわかってる。
……でも、そんな綺麗事はもう言っていられない…。
内容次第では、絵羽姉さんや留弗夫兄さんに相談した方がいいだろう…。

contexts.MG:
I feel like such a sinful daughter for discussing Father's inheritance while he's still alive.
......But this is no time to spout off cheap ideals.
...And I've even colluded with Rudolf nii-san and Eva nee-san, in order to get some money out of Krauss nii-san.
Coming from that position, ...I can't help but see the appearance of the witch as a sign of approaching misfortune...
......What could be written in here?
...I'm sure it's something frightening.
......Shall I read it secretly myself first?
The witch requested that it be read at the dinner table, with everyone gathered.
...But if that's what she wanted, why couldn't she just read it aloud herself at dinner?
Why did she go to all the trouble of entrusting it to me?
......Simply put, is it because she doesn't mind if I read it secretly beforehand...?
...It'd be better to secretly read the contents first.
...I understand that'd mean breaking my promise.
...But this is no longer the time for cheap ideals...
Depending on the contents, I should probably discuss it with Eva nee-san and Rudolf nii-san too...
contexts.UP:
I do feel like a sinful daughter for discussing the distribution of Father's inheritance while he's still alive.
......However, I'm no longer at a stage where I can afford to keep everything pretty.
...And I'm even consulting with Rudolf nii‐san and Eva nee‐san in order to get some money out of Krauss nii‐san.
With myself in this situation, .........I can't help but sense something ominous in the appearance of the witch...
.........What could be written in here?
......I'm sure there must be something frightening written.
.........Shall I first read it secretly myself?
The witch had requested it be done at the dinner table, when everyone was gathered.
......However, in that case, couldn't she just read it aloud at the dinner table herself?
Why did she go to all the trouble of entrusting it to me?
.........Did that mean, basically, that it didn't matter whether I secretly read it beforehand...?
......It would be better to secretly read the contents first.
...I understand that it would be breaking my promise.
......But this is no longer the time to keep things pretty...
It would probably be good to discuss it with Eva nee‐san and Rudolf nii‐san, depending on the contents...

UP.japanese: …そして、蔵臼兄さんからお金を引き出すため、絵羽姉さんや留弗夫兄さんと談合してすらいる。そんな私にとって、………魔女の出現は、不吉なものを予見させずにはいられないのだ…。
UP.translation: ...And I'm even consulting with Rudolf nii‐san and Eva nee‐san in order to get some money out of Krauss nii‐san. With myself in this situation, .........I can't help but sense something ominous in the appearance of the witch...

findings.sourceReading: Rosa admits she has even colluded with her siblings to extract money, reinforcing her awareness of improper conduct. Later 相談 at 709 is ordinary consultation about the letter.
findings.alternative: The stated aim of extracting money still suggests coordinated pressure, but consulting loses the explicit impropriety of 談合 and flattens its contrast with later ordinary 相談.

findings.description: UP take back all the hard times we had misstates Kanon’s wish to make up for past suffering as reclaiming the hard times themselves.

contexts.japanese:
「僕は嫌だ。
……これまでの辛かった分を、姉さんと取り戻したい。
生贄なんてごめんだ。
僕と姉さんは生き残る。
そして二人で黄金郷へ辿り着く」
contexts.japanesePS3:
「僕は嫌だ。
……これまでの辛かった分を、姉さんと取り戻したい。
生贄なんてごめんだ。
僕と姉さんは生き残る。
そして二人で黄金郷へ辿り着く」
contexts.MG:
"I don't like it.
...Together with you, I want to make up for all the suffering we've endured.
I won't become a sacrifice.
Nee-san and I will remain alive.
And we'll reach the Golden Land together."

"I don't like it.
......Together with you, I want to take back all the hard times we had.
I won't become a sacrifice.
You and I will remain alive.
And we'll reach the Golden Land together."

MG.translation: "I don't like it. ...Together with you, I want to make up for all the suffering we've endured. I won't become a sacrifice. Nee-san and I will remain alive. And we'll reach the Golden Land together."

UP.japanese: 「僕は嫌だ。……これまでの辛かった分を、姉さんと取り戻したい。生贄なんてごめんだ。僕と姉さんは生き残る。そして二人で黄金郷へ辿り着く」
UP.translation: "I don't like it. ......Together with you, I want to take back all the hard times we had. I won't become a sacrifice. You and I will remain alive. And we'll reach the Golden Land together."

findings.sourceReading: これまでの辛かった分を取り戻したい means recovering what past suffering cost them, living to compensate for it together. MG make up for all the suffering conveys that desire.
findings.alternative: Take back can suggest reclaiming lost life, and survival context helps repair the intention, but its explicit object here is hard times rather than what they lost through them.

findings.description: MG since the early evening shifts Nanjo’s chess visit from starting before evening to starting in the evening.

contexts.japanese:
源次は、蔵臼が階下へ降りていくのを見届けると、扉越しに再び声を掛けた。
「…お館様。
お食事を運ぶ準備はできております。
………南條先生の分はいかがいたしますか」
南條の姿は、書斎の中にあった。
長く続けられてきた二人のチェスの決着を、金蔵が強くせがんだため、夕方前からずっと相手をさせられていたのだ。
南條は医者として、金蔵に余命がないことを宣告している。
…その立場上、命がある内にチェスを決着したいとせがまれれば、断れなかった。
金蔵は普段以上の集中力で一手を熟考する。
……先ほどからずっと金蔵の手番で、待ちくたびれた南條は、読んでもわからぬ魔術書を適当に抜き出しては斜め読みしているのだった。

contexts.MG:
After Genji watched Krauss disappear down the stairs, he called again across the door.
"...Master,
we have finished preparations for your meal to be carried here.
......Shall we bring some for Doctor Nanjo as well?"
Nanjo could be seen in the study.
Because Kinzo had forcefully pestered him into finishing their long-lasting chess game, they had been playing against each other since the early evening.
Nanjo had announced as a doctor that Kinzo's days were numbered.
...So, he couldn't refuse if Kinzo demanded that they finish this game while he still lived.
Kinzo was thinking deeply about his move, concentrating more than usual.
...It had been Kinzo's turn for quite some time, and Nanjo, who was tired of waiting, had randomly pulled out a book on magic that he couldn't understand and was skimming it.
contexts.UP:
After Genji watched Krauss go down the stairs, he called again through the door.
"...My lord.
We have finished preparations for the meal to be carried here.
.........What about the serving for Doctor Nanjo?"
Nanjo was also in the study.
Because Kinzo had strongly pestered him about resolving their long‐lasting chess game, Nanjo had been Kinzo's opponent since before evening.
Nanjo had announced as a doctor that Kinzo's days were numbered.
...In that situation, if Kinzo pestered him about finishing a chess game while he was still alive, Nanjo couldn't refuse.
Kinzo was thinking deeply about his move, concentrating more than usual.
......It had been Kinzo's turn for quite some time, and Nanjo, who was tired of waiting, had started randomly pulling out grimoires that he couldn't understand and skimming through them.

MG.japanese: 南條の姿は、書斎の中にあった。長く続けられてきた二人のチェスの決着を、金蔵が強くせがんだため、夕方前からずっと相手をさせられていたのだ。
MG.translation: Nanjo could be seen in the study. Because Kinzo had forcefully pestered him into finishing their long-lasting chess game, they had been playing against each other since the early evening.

findings.sourceReading: 夕方前からずっと establishes play beginning before evening and continuing; UP preserves before evening.
findings.alternative: Early evening conveys a nearby time and the long session survives, but it crosses the explicit before-evening boundary.

findings.sourceReading: 性急 describes her call becoming a little more hasty or urgent, evidence that Shannon’s departure affected her.
findings.alternative: The witch is hostile throughout, but hostility does not establish the added short temper; this specific change is urgency.

findings.description: MG still had not answered turns Shannon’s decision to give no further replies into an absence of an earlier answer.

contexts.japanese:
「………譲治から指輪をもらうつもりであろう？
受け取れば、妾が嘉音と交わした、そなたを生贄に選ばないという約束を破棄すること、忘れるな」
「まだ御用があるなら、他の者を来させますので。
それでは失礼いたします」
ぴしゃりと遮る。
もう紗音は返事をしなかった。
そして扉が閉じられるその音が、返事の代わりとなるのだった。
その紗音の抵抗は、多分、彼女が思っているよりはるかに深く魔女に刺さったようだった。

contexts.MG:
Ironically, since she was losing her composure,
the more frantically she tried to cling to her claim, the more confused and hazy the thing she was describing became.
Because of that, it only took a single, calmly-spoken sentence to confirm the nature of what she was describing beyond doubt.
"......I also met with her.
I greeted...well, I couldn't really call it that. I exchanged a few words with her.
......It's definitely not something that Rosa-san just saw wrong."
"Kyrie-san, are you serious...?"
"Yes.
......But she didn't tell me her name.
So I can't say for certain that she was Beatrice."
"...However, and sorry if this is subjective,
......but since I met her in the entrance hall, I was able to compare her face with the portrait.
...My first impression was that...this portrait has to be hers.
...This is all just subjective."
contexts.UP:
Ironically, because she had lost her composure when she said that she had definitely met the witch,
the more desperate she became, the more vague the witch's existence seemed.
So, it was a single composed sentence that affirmed her existence for certain.
".........I met her as well.
We exchanged greetings—well, they could hardly be called that—a few words, at least.
.........It's definitely not something that Rosa‐san saw wrong."
"Kyrie‐san, are you serious...?"
"Yes.
.........But she didn't tell me her name.
So I can't conclude that she was Beatrice."
"......However, sorry if this is subjective,
......but since I met her in the entrance hall, I was able to compare her face with the portrait.
...My first impression was that she was undoubtedly the portrait's subject.
.........This is all just subjective, remember."

MG.japanese: だから、冷静な一言が、その存在を間違いなく肯定した。
MG.translation: Because of that, it only took a single, calmly-spoken sentence to confirm the nature of what she was describing beyond doubt.

findings.sourceReading: その存在を肯定した confirms existence through Kyrie’s testimony. Kyrie then explicitly withholds a conclusion that the woman is Beatrice and labels her portrait identification subjective.
findings.alternative: Nature could loosely mean the reality of Rosa’s encounter, and ensuing disclaimers allow repair, but confirming nature beyond doubt states a broader conclusion than confirming that the visitor exists.

findings.description: UP’s ‘the ears’ removes the opening monologue’s first-person possessor and produces nonidiomatic English; the following line explicitly identifies the body and life as Kinzo’s own.

findings.sourceReading: Kinzo admits that not knowing whether luck or his own efforts spared him is frustrating, then says he will refrain from saying more about it.
findings.alternative: Both versions preserve his frustration and self-command, but MG invents triviality and changes what he resolves not to do.

findings.description: MG says this year’s conference might have ‘done the same’ as last year’s pre-dawn session, dropping the escalation to continuing until early morning.

contexts.japanese:
…昨年は、親族会議は未明にまで及んだ。
今年の親族会議は、とうとう早朝にまで及んでも不思議はない。
まだ中で会議が続いている可能性を考え、ノックしたのだった。
contexts.japanesePS3:
…昨年は、親族会議は未明にまで及んだ。

まだ中で会議が続いている可能性を考え、ノックしたのだった。
contexts.MG:
...Last year, the family conference had continued into the early hours of the morning.

MG.translation: ...Last year, the family conference had continued into the early hours of the morning. It wouldn't have been odd if this year's conference had done the same. Considering the possibility that they were still having a discussion inside, she knocked. But there was no response, so she opened the door and said good morning.

UP.japanese: …昨年は、親族会議は未明にまで及んだ。今年の親族会議は、とうとう早朝にまで及んでも不思議はない。まだ中で会議が続いている可能性を考え、ノックしたのだった。だが反応はなかったので、おはようございますと口にしながら扉を開ける。
UP.translation: ...Last year, the family conference had continued into the small hours of the night. It wouldn't have been odd for this year's conference to continue all the way into the next morning. So she had knocked out of consideration for the possibility that they were still having a discussion inside. But there was no response, so she opened the door and said good morning.

findings.sourceReading: Last year’s meeting continued into the hours before dawn; Shannon considers that this year’s might finally have continued all the way into early morning and therefore knocks.
findings.alternative: MG still establishes a very late meeting and motivates the knock, but same erases the explicit contrast between 未明 and 早朝.

findings.sourceReading: Sobbing Maria buries her face in Nanjo’s ample, portly belly while he remains bewildered by the morning’s commotion.
findings.alternative: Well-built can broadly suggest a large solid physique, but applied to a stomach it naturally suggests muscularity and misses the rounded-corpulent nuance of 恰幅の良い.

findings.sourceReading: Retrospective Battler wonders whether Alice, after chasing the watch-bearing rabbit, never regretted the unnecessary curiosity that led her onward.
findings.alternative: Both questions evoke regret and foreshadow the cousins’ discovery, but the source’s negative rhetorical form specifically wonders at an absence of regret.

findings.description: UP combines ‘she’ with the reflexive ‘themselves’ in ‘Is she some unknown person trying to involve themselves,’ producing a mismatched antecedent.

contexts.japanese:
ベアトリーチェというのは何者なんだ。
昨日の晩餐で親父たちが騒いでいたように、遺産相続問題に絡もうとする未知の人物なのか。
……それとも真里亞がのたまうように、黄金伝説の魔女さまが犯人だってのかよ？！
朱志香が短気を起こすまでもなく、この状況下ではその来客が一番怪しいだろう。
しかし、それで決め付けちゃ駄目だ。

contexts.MG:
Who is this person called Beatrice?
Is some unknown person trying to involve themselves with the inheritance problem, just like our parents were freaking out about at dinner last night?
...Or is the culprit this witch from the Legend of the Gold, just like Maria said?!
Even if we set Jessica's temper aside, given the circumstances, it's probably safe to say that this visitor person is the most suspicious.
But we mustn't make up our minds based on that alone.

findings.sourceReading: Battler asks whether Beatrice is an unknown person attempting to involve herself in the inheritance dispute, or the legendary witch Maria describes.
findings.alternative: Singular they and themselves are standard with a gender-neutral antecedent such as person. UP has already fixed the antecedent as she, so the reflexive must agree with it.

MG.japanese: メッセージを読んだ途端、朱志香は激しく怒り、便箋をぐしゃぐしゃに丸めて叩きつける。そして、ベッドサイドにあったインテリアスタンドを掴むと、それを乱暴に振り回して、それを壁や家具にひたすら叩き付けた。…たちまち電球が破裂しその破片を辺りにばら撒いた。
MG.translation: As soon as she read the message, Jessica went into a wild rage, crumpled the paper up, and threw it. Then, she grabbed a light stand by the bedside and violently swung it around, mercilessly hitting the walls and furniture with it. ...The lightbulbs all shattered at once, and the fragments were scattered across the room.

findings.sourceReading: Jessica swings the bedside lamp into walls and furniture; its bulb immediately bursts and scatters fragments around the room.

findings.sourceReading: Gohda sees Jessica as having lost herself to rage and scorching herself in its flames, while Kanon recognizes the grief concealed beneath it.
findings.alternative: Burning with the flames of anger preserves the central metaphor and intensity, but omits 己を焦がす, the reflexive harm that helps motivate the servants’ intervention.

findings.sourceReading: Jessica sometimes forgets to carry her medication, so Kanon normally anticipates this and secretly carries a spare inhaler from the servants’ first-aid kit.

findings.alternative: Fits the plot or fits into the plot can be grammatical in other senses, but fits to is not idiomatic and does not express progression according to a plan.

findings.description: UP changes ‘it is inevitable that the witch will appear’ into ‘it is essential,’ turning a claimed necessary consequence into a requirement or desirable necessity.

「お下がりください。
……お嬢様は、僕が守る…！」
「姫に騎士が揃わば、魔女が現れるのは必然よ。
……どれ、金蔵の家具がどの程度の力を持つか、見せてもらおうではないか」
魔女は指を弾いて鋭い音を立てる。

findings.sourceReading: Beatrice theatrically claims that when princess and knight assemble, the witch’s appearance follows inevitably.
findings.alternative: Both words express necessity, and the theatrical trope remains clear. Essential ordinarily means required or indispensable, while 必然 describes inevitability.

findings.description: UP changes ‘there is no way to reason it out’ into ‘guessing is useless.’ 推理 refers to reasoning or deduction, and しようがない says it cannot be done; the edit recasts an information-limit claim as a judgment about the value of guessing.

findings.sourceReading: Battler argues that insufficient information makes deduction impossible because any explanation or trick could be proposed.
findings.alternative: Guessing can loosely describe attempting a solution without enough information, and the preceding lines explicitly retain the information shortage and impossibility of reasoning.

findings.description: MG renders 根拠否定, rejection of the grounds or basis for a claim, as ‘rejecting the source.’ This narrows the epistemic objection from denying supporting grounds generally to disputing a source’s authority or provenance.

貴様ら無能どもがいつも嘆いてみせる思考停止の理由、“情報不足”！
そして、それに対し情報を与えると今度はその情報の真偽を疑う“根拠否定”！」
「便利よのぅ？
無能を棚上げする実に小気味良い言葉よ。

説明を続けろ！」

findings.alternative: Rejecting a source can be one form of rejecting grounds, especially when Beatrice’s own statements supply the information. UP preserves the broader repeated term as denying the basis.

findings.alternative: Originally can describe an underlying intended condition rather than literal historical time, and the following sentence preserves acquired suspicion. The English past construction nevertheless makes the trusting nature sound like an earlier state.

findings.sourceReading: Battler challenges Beatrice to repeat his positive hidden-culprit premise—‘someone was hiding in the servant room’—in red; she refuses because she says the premise is about to collapse.
findings.alternative: Because Beatrice refuses and immediately announces that Battler's premise will collapse, a reader may infer that the requested proposition concerns the hidden-person theory. contexts.MG:
During the second closed room, I tried applying this theory to Kanon-kun.
...But after hearing "Kanon-kun was killed" in red, I gave it up.
After that, I proposed that a third person might've been in the room, before escaping through a hidden door.
And then, for the first time, I was faced with the red claim that "no hidden doors exist".
Now move from there to what I've just learned.
That term, "hidden door", refers to things that make it possible to enter or leave a room.
...In other words, that category doesn't cover things that don't actually lead in or out of the room, even if these things could never be recognized by people who didn't know about them beforehand.
contexts.UP:
I had used this theory for the second locked room, and reasoned that Kanon‐kun might have done this.
......But I had given up that reasoning when I was told "Kanon‐kun was killed" in red.
And next, I had reasoned that if there had been a third person in the room, it would have been possible for them to escape through a hidden door.
And that was when, for the first time, the claim had been made in red that "no hidden doors exist".
And what I'd learned just now.
These "hidden doors" the witch was talking about referred to things that made it possible to get into or out of the room.
......In other words, things that didn't permit entry or exit to the outside, and also wouldn't be noticed by people who didn't know about them, wouldn't fall under the definition of "hidden door".

MG.japanese: そして今わかったこと。魔女の言っている「隠し扉」は、外部に出入りできるものを指す。……つまり、外部に出入りできず、しかも知らない人には気付けないものは「隠し扉」の定義に入らないことになっている。
MG.translation: Now move from there to what I've just learned. That term, "hidden door", refers to things that make it possible to enter or leave a room. ...In other words, that category doesn't cover things that don't actually lead in or out of the room, even if these things could never be recognized by people who didn't know about them beforehand.

findings.sourceReading: Battler transitions from his previous theories to what he has now realized about Beatrice's definition of a hidden door.
findings.alternative: Move from there can be read as self-directed reasoning rather than speech to another person, and the next sentence states the realization. The imperative framing is absent from the source.

contexts.MG:
That term, "hidden door", refers to things that make it possible to enter or leave a room.
...In other words, that category doesn't cover things that don't actually lead in or out of the room, even if these things could never be recognized by people who didn't know about them beforehand.
So, if we had something like a "hidden shelf" or a "secret closet", for example, that wouldn't count as a "hidden door"!
That means the third person from Jessica's room is hiding here, waiting for us to leave!
Heh, how pathetic, it was all just a bit of wordplay!
Looks like that technique should be enough to handle even this third closed room.
contexts.UP:

In other words, if there were, for example, something like a "hidden shelf" or a "secret closet", they wouldn't be defined as "hidden doors"!
In other words, the third person in Jessica's room was hiding here, waiting for us to pass by!
Heh, how pathetic, just a little playing around with words!

MG.translation: So, if we had something like a "hidden shelf" or a "secret closet", for example, that wouldn't count as a "hidden door"! That means the third person from Jessica's room is hiding here, waiting for us to leave!

findings.sourceReading: Battler first applies the hidden-compartment interpretation retrospectively to the hypothetical third person in Jessica's room, then says the same method may solve the present servant-room mystery.
findings.alternative: The following sentence immediately applies the technique to the third closed room, so the current hiding conclusion is only slightly premature. MG nevertheless collapses the two applications and changes the earlier hypothetical's location and tense.

I don't know how they're hiding in this room.
But if that's a fact, then this also resolves the second locked room, Jessica's room, at the same time!!
I've finally caught her by the tail!
With this, I can explain everything!
Witches don't exist, I don't have to doubt anyone!!
Alright, starting now, I'll flip it over!
The next thing I'll request she repeat is—
"
No one exists in this room except your group.
"Your group" refers to Battler, George, Maria, Rosa, Genji, Gohda, and Shannon."
"......Wha‐............"
"Let's go back to Jessica's room.
At the time of Jessica's corpse discovery,
only Battler, George, Maria, Rosa, Genji, Gohda, Shannon, Kumasawa, and Nanjo were in Jessica's room."
"Whoops, the corpse of Jessica is also included, of course.

contexts.japanese:
「………これで、はっきりしたわ。
もう疑いようもない」
「は…？
……と、言いますと……？」
「あなたたちが死んだ死んだという二人はここにいない。
…そしてベアトリーチェからの手紙があり、親切にも死体は持ち去ったと告白してくれている。
……そういうことよ」
「もう茶番は飽き飽きしたわ！！」
楼座叔母さんはそう叫ぶと、一同を険しい表情でぐるりと見渡す。
「ちゃ、
……茶番って、
……どういう意味ですか…！」
「私は朱志香ちゃんの部屋で言ったわ。
……信用できるのは自分自身と、死体となって見付かった者以外いないってね」
「そして死体が見付からない以上、あの二人が殺されたことを認めるわけにはいかない」
「……ま、待って下さい、楼座叔母さん。
それはどういう意味ですか…！」
「南條先生と熊沢さんは死んでないわ、生きているッ！
殺されたということにして、この屋敷のどこかに隠れているのよ。
私たちを襲うためにね！！」
「何でそんなことがわかるんですか！
郷田さんたちが嘘をついているというんですか？！」
「……楼座さま！！
この郷田、いえ、右代宮家使用人一同！
誓ってそのようなことは致しません！！」
「あなたたちは、南條先生たちは殺されたという。
でも死体がない以上、それを信じるわけにはいかないわ。
あなたたちが口裏を合わせてそういう嘘をついている可能性があるもの！！」
「あなたたちの無実を信じる方法はちゃんとあるわよぅ？
南條先生と熊沢さんの遺体が見付かることよ！！」
「それが見付かったら、私はあなたたちの話を聞いてみようという話にもなるわ。
でも、見付からない限り、あなたたちは狼であることを否定できないッ！！」
「あんたも！
あんたも！！
黄金に目が眩んであの魔女に買収されたんでしょう！！
そんなにカネが欲しい？！
そうなんでしょう？！
一生遊んで暮らしたいの？！
そんな人生に何の価値があるのよッ！！」
「楼座さま…！！
私たちは、……そんなッ！」
「黙りなさい！
そして紗音、それ以上近付かないでッ！！
１０年も恩を受けながらそれを仇で返すなんて！！
容赦なく引き金を引くわよ！！」
「そんな……ッ、
………そんなのって、
………ひどすぎ
……ます……」
「……ろ、楼座叔母さん！！
それは暴言だ！！
この部屋で殺人が起こった！
そして犯人が死体を持ち去った！
彼女たちはそれを正直に申告しているだけだッ！！」
「………う、……ううううぅうぅうううぅぅッ！！！」
紗音はとうとう大粒の涙を零し始める…。
１０年の月日を右代宮家に捧げた。
人生でもっとも輝かしい月日の内の１０年を捧げた。
………そして楼座とも友好な関係を築けていると信じていた。
…その仕打ちが、これッ！！
人は刃物なんか使わなくたって殺せる…。
譲治の兄貴じゃなくたって、
…俺にだって、紗音ちゃんが心を深々と突き刺されて、涙という血を流しているのがわかる…。
「紗音さん、下がって…。
……楼座さま、確かにこの郷田はお勤めして日も浅く、信用を勝ち得ていないのはわかります…」
「…しかしッ、……せめて紗音さんだけでも信じていただくわけには参りませんか…？！
彼女は、１０年間も右代宮家に奉仕を捧げてまいりました…！」
「この郷田を信じろとは申しません…！
せめてッ、紗音さんだけでも信じてやっていただくわけには参りませんか…！！」
…しかし、……もう、俺にもわからないッ！！
わからないんだッ！！
彼らを疑わずして、答えを求めることができないんだ！！！
あぁあぁ、だんだんわかって来たよ…。
……答えなんか求めるから、…どんどんおかしくなっていっちまうんだ…。
答えなんか、いらない。
全ては、１９人目の魔女ベアトリーチェが、不気味な儀式に則り、怪しげな魔法で犯した不思議な殺人。
…………それで、……いいじゃねぇか………。
もう俺は、…誰も、…疑いたくねぇ………。
紗音ちゃんと郷田さんは、半ば涙目で身の潔白を訴えていた。
それを源次さんが静かに止める。
「…………よしなさい。
…楼座さまの言うことはもっともだ。
…死体を見つけない限り、
南條先生と熊沢の無実は証明できない」
そうだ。
……楼座さんの論法によるならば、死体が見付かればその人物の無実だけは証明できる。
でも、死体の人物だけだ。
彼らが屋敷内を探し回り、死体を見つけたとしても、結局、彼らの無実は証明されない。
彼らが南條先生たちを拉致して他所で殺し、密室は彼らのマスターキーで施錠した。

contexts.MG:
".........Now, it's clear.
There's no longer any reason to doubt."
"Huh...?
...What are you saying...?"
"You kept saying those two were dead, but they aren't here.
...And now we have this letter from Beatrice, where she's been kind enough to confess that she carried the corpses off."
"...It's as simple as that.
I've had enough of this farce!!"
As Aunt Rosa yelled this, she looked at all of us with a fierce expression.
'W-
What do you mean...
by farce...?!"
"I said it in Jessica-chan's room.
...You can't trust anyone but yourself and those whose corpses have been found.
And since we can't find the corpses of those two people, we must not accept that they've been killed."
"...P-Please wait, Aunt Rosa.
What do you mean by that...?!"
"Doctor Nanjo and Kumasawa-san aren't dead, they're alive!
We're supposed to believe that they've been killed, but they're definitely hiding somewhere in this mansion.
So that they can attack us!!"
"How could you know that?!
Are you saying that Gohda-san and the rest are lying?!"
"...Rosa-sama!!
I, Gohda...no, all of the Ushiromiya family servants!
We all swear that nothing of the sort happened!!"
"You all say that those two were killed.
But since there are no corpses, we mustn't believe you.
There's a chance that you worked out a story beforehand, that you're lying!!"
"There's a good way to prove your innocence, isn't there?
Find Doctor Nanjo's and Kumasawa-san's bodies!!"
"If you can find them, then maybe I'll start listening to your story.
But until you do, you cannot deny that you are all wolves!!"
"You!
And you!!
I'll bet you were all bought by that witch, that your eyes were blinded by gold!!
Do you really want money that much?!
That's right, isn't it?!
You want to live the easy life for as long as you live?!
What value could a life like that possibly have?!!"
"Rosa-sama...!!
We...couldn't have!"
"Be silent!
And Shannon, don't get any closer!!
To think you'd repay a ten-year-long debt of gratitude with betrayal!!
I'll pull the trigger without mercy!!"
"How......
......how could you...?
...It's too...
cruel..."
"...A-Aunt Rosa!!
That's horrible!!
A murder occurred in this room!
And then the culprit carried the corpses away!
All they're doing is honestly reporting what they saw!!"
"......Aaah, aaaaaaaaaaaaaahhhhhhh!!!"
Shannon had finally broken down in tears...
She had sacrificed 10 years to the Ushiromiya family.
She had sacrificed 10 of the most brilliant years of her life.
......She'd believed that she'd built up a friendly relationship with Rosa.
...And this was what she got in return!!
You can kill a person without using a knife...
I didn't have to be George-aniki...
to realize that Shannon-chan had been stabbed deep in the heart, that she was shedding tears like blood...
"Shannon-san, stay back...
...Rosa-sama, it is true that I, Gohda, have not served for many years, and I understand that I have not earned your trust..."
"...However...could you not believe in Shannon-san at least...?!
She has sacrificed a full 10 years in service to the Ushiromiya family...!
I'm not telling you to believe me...!
At the very least, can't you believe in Shannon-san...?!!"
...But...even I don't understand anymore!!
I don't understand!!
We can't search for an answer without suspecting them!!!
Yeah, bit by bit, I'm starting to understand...
...It's because we've been searching an answer, ...that's why everything keeps going wrong...
We don't need...an answer.
These are all...strange murders, committed with bizarre magic by the 19th person, the witch Beatrice, in accordance with some creepy ceremony.
......Isn't that...enough......?
I don't...want to suspect...anyone anymore......
Shannon-chan and Gohda-san were protesting their innocence, half-crying.
Genji-san quietly put a stop to that.
"......Enough.
...What Rosa-sama says is quite sensible.
...Until we find the corpses,
we cannot prove Doctor Nanjo and Kumasawa's innocence."
That's right.
...By Rosa-san's argument, if their corpses can be found, then the innocence of those people alone can be proven.
But that only counted for the corpses.
Even if the survivors searched the mansion and found the corpses, in the end, their own innocence would never be proven.
"They kidnapped Doctor Nanjo and Kumasawa-san, killed them in another place, and locked the closed room with their own master keys."

"...However, ......could you not at least believe Shannon‐san...?!

"I'm not telling you to believe me...!
At the very least, would you at least believe Shannon‐san...?!!"
...But......I don't understand anymore!!
I don't understand!!
We can't seek an answer without suspecting them!!!
That's it, bit by bit I'm starting to understand...
......It's because we seek an answer; ...that's why everything keeps getting stranger...
We don't need...an answer.
These are all strange murders committed with bizarre magic by the 19th person, the witch Beatrice, as she follows a creepy ritual.
............Isn't that......good enough.........
I don't...want to suspect...anyone anymore.........
Shannon‐chan and Gohda‐san were protesting their innocence, half in tears.
Genji‐san quietly stopped that.
"............Stop.
...What Rosa‐sama says is quite right.
...Until we find the corpses,
we cannot prove that Doctor Nanjo and Kumasawa are innocent."
That's right.
......By Rosa‐san's argument, if the corpses could be found, then the innocence of at least those people could be proved.
But only the people who were corpses.
Even if they searched around the mansion and found the corpses, in the end, their own innocence would not be proved.
They had abducted Doctor Nanjo and Kumasawa‐san, killed them in another place, and locked the room with their own master keys.

彼らが南條先生たちを拉致して他所で殺し、密室は彼らのマスターキーで施錠した。これ以外の方法で密室を打ち破らない限り、……彼らの無実は証明できないのだ…。

findings.description: MG calls Gohda's frying pan ‘thick-feeling,’ an unnatural rendering of 重厚感ある, which describes a solid, weighty, imposing pan.

contexts.japanese:
郷田は、いくつかの重そうな調理道具を吟味している。
…本来なら、誇りある料理人の彼は用途以外に使いたくなどない。
しかし今は、彼が主だと認めた者の命令に応えようと必死だった。
彼は少し悩んだ末、大きめの重厚感あるフライパンを手にする。

findings.description: UP broadens Battler's inability to feel that solving the riddle would save himself into whether it would save ‘us,’ changing the immediate object of his doubt from personal survival to the whole group.

contexts.japanese:
「ベアトリーチェは確か、これを解いたら、どうするって言ってたんだっけ」
確か、魔女の手紙には、利子の回収を諦める、みたいな抽象的なことが書かれていた。
…俺はそれをつまり、一族皆殺しを諦めると好意的に読み取っているのだが、
……本当にそういう意味で書かれているのだろうか。
この謎を解くことで、本当に自分が助かるのか、実感できない。
………仮に解けたとしても、それは犯人の思う壺で、結局は全て無駄な努力なのではないかと思ってしまう…。

「ベアトリーチェは確か、これを解いたら、どうするって言ってたんだっけ」

……本当にそういう意味で書かれているのだろうか。
この謎を解くことで、本当に自分が助かるのか、実感できない。
………仮に解けたとしても、それは犯人の思う壺で、結局は全て無駄な努力なのではないかと思ってしまう…。
contexts.MG:
"What was it again...that Beatrice said she'd do if we solved this?"
I'm sure the witch wrote in her letter that she'd give up on collecting interest, or something abstract like that.
...I optimistically took that to mean she'd give up on killing the whole family,
...but was it really written with that meaning?
For some reason, I couldn't convince myself that solving the riddle would really save me.
......I feel like maybe, even if we do solve it, we'll just be doing what the culprit wants, and it'll all be a wasted effort...
contexts.UP:
"What was it again, that Beatrice said she would do if we solved this?"
I was sure that the witch had written in her letter that she would give up on collecting the interest, or something abstract like that.
...I was optimistically taking that to mean that she would give up on killing the whole family,
......but was it really written with that meaning?
I didn't really feel that solving this riddle would actually save us.
.........I thought that even if we did solve it, that would be doing just what the culprit wanted us to, and it would all be a wasted effort...

UP.japanese: この謎を解くことで、本当に自分が助かるのか、実感できない。………仮に解けたとしても、それは犯人の思う壺で、結局は全て無駄な努力なのではないかと思ってしまう…。
UP.translation: I didn't really feel that solving this riddle would actually save us. .........I thought that even if we did solve it, that would be doing just what the culprit wanted us to, and it would all be a wasted effort...

findings.sourceReading: Battler cannot feel assured that solving the riddle will really save him and suspects that doing so may merely serve the culprit.
findings.alternative: Battler is reasoning in a room with Rosa and Maria and elsewhere discusses saving everyone, so a collective concern is contextually natural.

findings.description: MG replaces Battler's quiz-show image of sounding a buzzer and raising his hand with raising his hand and crying ‘I got it,’ losing the audible answer-buzzer mechanism.

ピンポーンって鳴らして挙手して、解答を魔女に伝えて答えあわせをするのか」
「うー。
それは知らない。
でも、解けばきっと、自動的に儀式は終わる」
contexts.japanesePS3:
「……謎が解けたらどうするんだ。

contexts.MG:
"...What do we do if we solve the riddle?

findings.sourceReading: Battler jokingly imagines buzzing in, raising his hand, submitting the answer to the witch, and having it checked.
findings.alternative: Crying I got it creates the same classroom or quiz-show beat and does not affect how the epitaph actually operates.

findings.description: UP strengthens Battler's qualified claim that magical risk is ‘somewhat’ incompatible with his chessboard theory and that a best move seeks an advantageous development into outright conflict and a move that ‘promises’ one.

contexts.japanese:
リスクを負わなければ、何も得られない、…か。
それは間違いなく世の中の真理だが、……俺が好むチェス盤理論の考えとは少し相容れなかった。
チェスにおける指し手とは、常にリスクのもっとも少なく、有利な展開を期待する最善手の模索だ。
ギャンブルのような運否天賦で手は指さない。
……そう、知的ゲームに博打性の入り込む余地はありえないのだ。
contexts.japanesePS3:
リスクを負わなければ、何も得られない、…か。
それは間違いなく世の中の真理だが、……俺が好むチェス盤理論の考えとは少し相容れなかった。
チェスにおける指し手とは、常にリスクのもっとも少なく、有利な展開を期待する最善手の模索だ。
ギャンブルのような運否天賦で手は指さない。
……そう、知的ゲームに博打性の入り込む余地はありえないのだ。
contexts.MG:
So, ...if you don't bear a risk, nothing can be gained, is that it?
That definitely is the way of the world, ...but it's sort of in conflict with the chessboard thinking I like so much.
At least when making moves in chess, players grope for the best move, always trying to avoid risk and hoping for an advantageous turn of events.
They don't trust to chance, like in gambling.
...That's right, there's no room for gambling in an intellectual game.
contexts.UP:
So, ...if you don't bear a risk, nothing can be gained.
That is doubtlessly the way of the world, ......but it was in conflict with the chessboard theory style of thinking that I liked.
A move in chess is always a search for the best play, that minimizes the risk, and promises an advantageous turn of events.
You don't trust your plays to chance, like in gambling.
......That's right, there's no room for gambling in an intellectual game.

UP.japanese:
リスクを負わなければ、何も得られない、…か。それは間違いなく世の中の真理だが、……俺が好むチェス盤理論の考えとは少し相容れなかった。
チェスにおける指し手とは、常にリスクのもっとも少なく、有利な展開を期待する最善手の模索だ。ギャンブルのような運否天賦で手は指さない。……そう、知的ゲームに博打性の入り込む余地はありえないのだ。
UP.translation:
So, ...if you don't bear a risk, nothing can be gained. That is doubtlessly the way of the world, ......but it was in conflict with the chessboard theory style of thinking that I liked.
A move in chess is always a search for the best play, that minimizes the risk, and promises an advantageous turn of events. You don't trust your plays to chance, like in gambling. ......That's right, there's no room for gambling in an intellectual game.

findings.sourceReading: Battler says risk-taking does not sit entirely comfortably with his preferred theory, under which one searches for the lowest-risk move while expecting a favorable development.
findings.alternative: The following contrast with gambling is categorical, so the stronger wording fits the direction of Battler's argument even though it removes the initial qualification and uncertainty.

findings.description: MG changes Battler's suspicion that the epitaph is a smokescreen meant to mislead him into the claim that Beatrice is misleading him by ‘speaking in riddles,’ shifting the tactic from deliberate distraction to obscure language.

contexts.japanese:
…しかし、ベアトリーチェの指し手は、常に最善手だとは言い切れない。
俺は多分、この碑文に注目させることで何かを誤解させて煙に巻かせようとしているんだろうと思っている。
……しかし真里亞は、そんなことだけは絶対にありえないという。
これは魔女が示した純粋なリスクであり、ゆえに正式な魔法の儀式である証拠だという。

…しかし、ベアトリーチェの指し手は、常に最善手だとは言い切れない。

……しかし真里亞は、そんなことだけは絶対にありえないという。
これは魔女が示した純粋なリスクであり、ゆえに正式な魔法の儀式である証拠だという。
contexts.MG:
...However, we can't be sure that Beatrice's moves are always the best moves possible.
I thought she was probably making us focus on the epitaph to fool us in some way, speaking in riddles.

She said this was a genuine risk that the witch had taken, and therefore proof that this was a formal ceremony for magic.

MG.japanese: 俺は多分、この碑文に注目させることで何かを誤解させて煙に巻かせようとしているんだろうと思っている。……しかし真里亞は、そんなことだけは絶対にありえないという。これは魔女が示した純粋なリスクであり、ゆえに正式な魔法の儀式である証拠だという。
MG.translation: I thought she was probably making us focus on the epitaph to fool us in some way, speaking in riddles. ...But according to Maria, that alone was impossible. She said this was a genuine risk that the witch had taken, and therefore proof that this was a formal ceremony for magic.

findings.sourceReading: Battler suspects that drawing attention to the epitaph is a smokescreen intended to make the survivors misunderstand something.
findings.alternative: The epitaph itself is a riddle and remains the identified focus of possible misdirection, so the general suspicion is preserved.

findings.description: MG recasts Battler's ‘clever advance notice,’ suggestive locked-room staging, and excessive theatrical presentation as a ‘kindhearted’ notice, ‘self-aware’ locked rooms, and ‘over-acting.’

contexts.japanese:
……ベアトリーチェは、何が狙いでこんな事件を引き起こしているんだ。
俺たちを皆殺しにしたいだけなら、大仕掛けなど打たずに、こっそり密かにやればいい。
気の利いた予告状も、思わせぶりな密室演出も何も必要ない。
…全てが過剰演出。
まったく意味がわからない。
contexts.japanesePS3:
……ベアトリーチェは、何が狙いでこんな事件を引き起こしているんだ。
俺たちを皆殺しにしたいだけなら、大仕掛けなど打たずに、こっそり密かにやればいい。
気の利いた予告状も、思わせぶりな密室演出も何も必要ない。
…全てが過剰演出。
まったく意味がわからない。
contexts.MG:
...What is Beatrice after that's making her carry out this crime?
If she just wanted to massacre us all, she could've done it quietly, without this whole crazy setup.
There was no need for that kindhearted advance notice, all this self-aware closed room stuff, or any of the rest.
...It's all over-acting.
I've got no clue what it means.
contexts.UP:
......What is Beatrice after that's making her commit this crime?
If she just wants to massacre us all, she could just do it secretly, without this whole crazy setup.
There was no need for that scrupulous advance notice, dramatic suggestions of locked rooms, or anything.
...It's all over‐dramatized.
I don't get the point at all.

MG.japanese:
俺たちを皆殺しにしたいだけなら、大仕掛けなど打たずに、こっそり密かにやればいい。気の利いた予告状も、思わせぶりな密室演出も何も必要ない。…全てが過剰演出。
まったく意味がわからない。
MG.translation: If she just wanted to massacre us all, she could've done it quietly, without this whole crazy setup. There was no need for that kindhearted advance notice, all this self-aware closed room stuff, or any of the rest. ...It's all over-acting. I've got no clue what it means.

findings.sourceReading: Battler argues that a simple massacre required none of the culprit's clever notices, suggestive locked-room staging, or other excessive theatrics.
findings.alternative: MG preserves that the crimes are needlessly elaborate and theatrical. Kindhearted can describe the apparent chance given to the victims, but it misstates 気の利いた and the staging vocabulary.

findings.alternative: Japanese singular nouns can express a class generically, and Maria's wider beliefs concern witches in general.

findings.sourceReading: Battler counts Grandfather and Beatrice, the nineteenth guest who has not shown even a sign of herself, among those not confirmed dead.
findings.alternative: Battler is the viewpoint speaker, so absence of any displayed sign necessarily includes his failure to sense one.

findings.description: MG translates 余裕ぶった as Beatrice acting “so tough,” changing a display of composure or ease into toughness.

contexts.japanese:
手段と目的を時に履き違える。
そして悪い遊びが過ぎる。
その結果、自ら弱点を作り晒してさえいる。
私のような最強の魔女から見れば、何でこんな余裕ぶったことをするのか理解できない。
自ら勝率を下げてるなんてね。
contexts.japanesePS3:
手段と目的を時に履き違える。
そして悪い遊びが過ぎる。
その結果、自ら弱点を作り晒してさえいる。
私のような最強の魔女から見れば、何でこんな余裕ぶったことをするのか理解できない。
自ら勝率を下げてるなんてね。
contexts.MG:
She sometimes mistakes her means for her ends.
And she has too much dark fun.
Sometimes, that even ends up creating and exposing her own weak points.
For a super-powerful witch like me, it's hard to understand why she's able to act so tough.
Why she lowers her own chances of winning.
contexts.UP:
She sometimes mistakes the means for the end.
And she has too much bad fun.
As a result, she makes and even exposes her own weak points.
It's impossible for a strongest‐ever witch like me to understand why she acts so relaxed.
Lowering her own chances of winning.

MG.japanese: 手段と目的を時に履き違える。そして悪い遊びが過ぎる。その結果、自ら弱点を作り晒してさえいる。私のような最強の魔女から見れば、何でこんな余裕ぶったことをするのか理解できない。自ら勝率を下げてるなんてね。
MG.translation: She sometimes mistakes her means for her ends. And she has too much dark fun. Sometimes, that even ends up creating and exposing her own weak points. For a super-powerful witch like me, it's hard to understand why she's able to act so tough. Why she lowers her own chances of winning.

UP.japanese: 手段と目的を時に履き違える。そして悪い遊びが過ぎる。その結果、自ら弱点を作り晒してさえいる。私のような最強の魔女から見れば、何でこんな余裕ぶったことをするのか理解できない。自ら勝率を下げてるなんてね。
UP.translation: She sometimes mistakes the means for the end. And she has too much bad fun. As a result, she makes and even exposes her own weak points. It's impossible for a strongest‐ever witch like me to understand why she acts so relaxed. Lowering her own chances of winning.

findings.sourceReading: Lambdadelta cannot understand why Beatrice puts on such an air of composure while lowering her own chances of victory.
findings.alternative: Acting tough can imply confident posturing, but toughness does not express the source’s conspicuous ease or composure.

findings.description: UP renders 素直で正直 as “obedient and honest,” replacing straightforward or direct predictability with submissiveness.

contexts.japanese: …ベルンにとっては、私みたいな素直で正直なタイプは、読みやすくてやりやすいんでしょうね。
contexts.japanesePS3: …ベルンにとっては、私みたいな素直で正直なタイプは、読みやすくてやりやすいんでしょうね。
contexts.MG: ...Maybe it's really easy for Bern to read and handle a straightforward and honest type like me.
contexts.UP: ...It's probably really easy for Bern to read and handle an obedient and honest type like me.

MG.japanese: ………でも、ま。そのせいで、ベルンみたいな、相手を読んでかわすタイプの魔女には非常に相性が悪いってわけよ。読みが効かないから。…ベルンにとっては、私みたいな素直で正直なタイプは、読みやすくてやりやすいんでしょうね。ムカつくことに！
MG.translation: ......But, well. Because of that, a witch like Bern, who likes to thoroughly read her opponent, has a really bad affinity with her. Because reading her doesn't work. ...Maybe it's really easy for Bern to read and handle a straightforward and honest type like me. Annoyingly enough!

UP.japanese: ………でも、ま。そのせいで、ベルンみたいな、相手を読んでかわすタイプの魔女には非常に相性が悪いってわけよ。読みが効かないから。…ベルンにとっては、私みたいな素直で正直なタイプは、読みやすくてやりやすいんでしょうね。ムカつくことに！
UP.translation: .........But, well. That's why the type of witch like Bern who reads her opponent and dodges their moves has a really bad matchup with her. 'Cause reading her doesn't work. ...It's probably really easy for Bern to read and handle an obedient and honest type like me. That makes me so mad!

findings.sourceReading: Lambdadelta characterizes herself as straightforward and honest in contrast with Beatrice’s indirect play.
findings.alternative: 素直 can mean obedient in hierarchical contexts, but here it describes her own direct strategic temperament, not compliance with another person.

findings.description: UP renders 趣味の悪い as “nasty hobbies,” literalizing 趣味 and changing Beatrice’s bad taste into a claim about her activities.

contexts.japanesePS3: 一見すると本当に趣味の悪いヤツだと思うでしょ？
contexts.MG: At a glance, you'd think she has really nasty tastes, right?
contexts.UP: At a glance, you'd think she has really nasty hobbies, right?

MG.japanese: 少しは血色が戻ってきたみたいね。ベアトのヤツ、楼座とかいう駒を虐めて遊んでるわ。一見すると本当に趣味の悪いヤツだと思うでしょ？

findings.sourceReading: Lambdadelta calls Beatrice’s taste bad while speculating about why she prolongs the game.
findings.alternative: The surrounding discussion concerns Beatrice’s habitual way of playing, so “hobbies” remains understandable as a loose insult.

findings.description: MG coordinates past “was ... worried” with present “choose” in the same account of selecting lunch, breaking the intended past-tense narration. UP correctly uses chose.

contexts.japanese:
何て言うのかその、…見栄えを気にしてしまい、
トーストにサラダにコーヒーなんて、キザったらしいメニューにしてしまう。
contexts.japanesePS3:
何て言うのかその、…見栄えを気にしてしまい、
トーストにサラダにコーヒーなんて、キザったらしいメニューにしてしまう。
contexts.MG:
I was...how should I put it...worried about my appearance and choose a menu suited for a snob:
toast, salad and coffee.
contexts.UP:
I was—how should I put it—worried about my appearance,
and chose a menu suited for a snob: toast, salad and coffee.

MG.japanese:
でも、紗音と一緒のバイキングは違う。
好きなものだけみっともなく山盛りにできない。何て言うのかその、…見栄えを気にしてしまい、トーストにサラダにコーヒーなんて、キザったらしいメニューにしてしまう。僕ひとりだったなら、焼きそばやマッシュポテトにグラタン等の油っぽいのを山盛りにしてるところだ。
MG.translation: But with Shannon beside me, this buffet felt different. I couldn't shamefully pile on only the things I liked. I was...how should I put it...worried about my appearance and choose a menu suited for a snob: toast, salad and coffee. If I'd been by myself, I would've made a pile of oily stuff like yakisoba, mashed potatoes, gratin, and so on.

UP.japanese:
でも、紗音と一緒のバイキングは違う。
好きなものだけみっともなく山盛りにできない。何て言うのかその、…見栄えを気にしてしまい、トーストにサラダにコーヒーなんて、キザったらしいメニューにしてしまう。僕ひとりだったなら、焼きそばやマッシュポテトにグラタン等の油っぽいのを山盛りにしてるところだ。
UP.translation:
But with Shannon beside me, this buffet felt different.
I couldn't shamefully make a huge pile of nothing but my favorite foods. I was—how should I put it—worried about my appearance, and chose a menu suited for a snob: toast, salad and coffee. findings.description: George says they had only exchanged greetings at infrequent family gatherings. MG reduces this to only meeting at those gatherings, dropping the limited interaction that grounds his surprise at their present intimacy. UP explicitly restores only ever exchange greetings.

contexts.japanese:
