何年も前から面識もある。
でも、年に何度もない親族の会合の席で挨拶をするだけ」
「…そんな君とこうして一緒に過ごせる関係になるなんて、全然想像できなかったよ。
それは紗音もでしょ？」
contexts.japanesePS3:
紗音ちゃんと出会ったのは、昨日今日のことじゃない。
何年も前から面識もある。
でも、年に何度もない親族の会合の席で挨拶をするだけ」

それは紗音もでしょ？」

I didn't just meet you yesterday or today, Shannon-chan.
We've known each other for years now.

It was the same for you too, right?"

さぁ、勇気を。

findings.description: MG makes Krauss say he must correct Eva before she “leave[s] this family,” while 社会に出る means before she enters society or adult public life; marriage out of the family is a separate later claim.

UP.japanese: ……彼女は、私の代わりに悪態を付く。私には滅多なことでは口にできない言葉を、…彼女が私に代わって口にしてくれる。…内なるもうひとりの自分であるとわかっていても、…私にとっては、唯一同情してくれる味方なのだ。
UP.translation: ......She would curse in my place. Words that I couldn't say carelessly, ...she would say for me. ...Even though I understood that she was just another part of myself inside of me, ...I felt like she was the only ally I had who would sympathize with me.

findings.sourceReading: The younger self voices harsh curses on Eva’s behalf that adult Eva could not readily bring herself to say.
findings.alternative: Speaking such words readily could itself be careless, so the translation retains their socially dangerous character.

findings.description: MG says sympathy might do “a lot” to calm Eva’s heart, while 幾分か limits the relief to some degree or somewhat.

contexts.japanese:
…内なるもうひとりの自分であるとわかっていても、
…私にとっては、唯一同情してくれる味方なのだ。
だが、同情は心を幾分か楽にしてくれるかもしれないが、現状を何も改善してはくれない。
……結局、現実に落胆し、それを受け容れるのに必要な時間分だけ、心を慰めてくれるだけなのだ。
contexts.japanesePS3:
…内なるもうひとりの自分であるとわかっていても、
…私にとっては、唯一同情してくれる味方なのだ。
だが、同情は心を幾分か楽にしてくれるかもしれないが、現状を何も改善してはくれない。
……結局、現実に落胆し、それを受け容れるのに必要な時間分だけ、心を慰めてくれるだけなのだ。
contexts.MG:
Even though I understand that she's just another part of myself inside of me,
...I feel like she's the only ally I have who can sympathize with me.
However, while sympathy might do a lot to calm my heart, it won't do anything to improve my current situation.
...In the end, she can only console me for however long it takes me to be dejected by reality...before I finally accept it.
contexts.UP:
...Even though I understood that she was just another part of myself inside of me,
...I felt like she was the only ally I had who would sympathize with me.
However, while sympathy might calm my heart somewhat, it wouldn't do anything to improve my current situation.
......In the end, she could only console me when I was dejected by reality, and for the amount of time I needed to accept it.

MG.japanese: だが、同情は心を幾分か楽にしてくれるかもしれないが、現状を何も改善してはくれない。……結局、現実に落胆し、それを受け容れるのに必要な時間分だけ、心を慰めてくれるだけなのだ。
MG.translation: However, while sympathy might do a lot to calm my heart, it won't do anything to improve my current situation. ...In the end, she can only console me for however long it takes me to be dejected by reality...before I finally accept it.

findings.sourceReading: Eva recognizes that sympathy may ease her heart somewhat but cannot improve the actual situation.
findings.alternative: Even substantial emotional relief would still leave the contrast with no practical improvement intact.

findings.description: UP changes Eva’s goal of becoming a lady who can enter high society proudly into becoming someone Father can take out and boast about, transferring agency and pride from Eva to Kinzo.

その魔法を使えば、……私はきっと永遠に、死ぬまで、自らがいつか当主になれる日が来ることを疑わずに済むだろう。
…しかし、それは右代宮絵羽として、正しいことなのか、わからない…。
お父様の期待するような、社交界に胸を張って出られる淑女を目指すべきなのではないだろうか。
お父様も、生まれ変わった私を見直してくれるかもしれない。

お父様の期待するような、社交界に胸を張って出られる淑女を目指すべきなのではないだろうか。
お父様も、生まれ変わった私を見直してくれるかもしれない。
contexts.MG:
If I use this magic, ...then surely, I'll never have to doubt until the day I die...that I'll eventually become the Head.
...But I don't know if that's the right thing for Ushiromiya Eva...

contexts.UP:
If I can use that magic, ......then surely, until the day I die, I'll never have to doubt that someday I will become the head.
...But I don't know if that is the right thing for Ushiromiya Eva...
Shouldn't I aim to become the kind of lady that Father hoped for, someone he can take out into society and boast about?
Father might take a better view of me if I were reborn.

UP.japanese: お父様の期待するような、社交界に胸を張って出られる淑女を目指すべきなのではないだろうか。お父様も、生まれ変わった私を見直してくれるかもしれない。……兄は兄、私は私で、それぞれの生き方を見つけられるかもしれない。
UP.translation: Shouldn't I aim to become the kind of lady that Father hoped for, someone he can take out into society and boast about? Father might take a better view of me if I were reborn. ......Maybe my brother could find his own lifestyle, and I could find mine.

findings.sourceReading: Eva considers whether she should become the sort of lady Kinzo expects—one able to appear in high society with her own head held high.
findings.alternative: Kinzo’s expected social role for Eva is explicitly tied to family prestige, so his ability to present her proudly is closely related.

findings.sourceReading: Eva imagines that Krauss can be Krauss and she can be herself, with each perhaps finding a distinct way to live.
findings.alternative: Krauss already follows the heir’s prescribed path, so the added assertion is plausible within Eva’s reflection.

findings.description: MG changes Battler’s claim that expecting him to remember six-year-old events is unreasonable into “I’m the one who has it bad, being forced to remember,” reframing impossibility as personal mistreatment or hardship.

"I'm surprised how much everyone remembers about it.
My memory's all hazy."
"Yeah, I'll bet.
Looks like it's taking you a while to remember us.
You know, that hurts a bit."
"Come on, this was six years ago, right?
I'm the one who has it bad, being forced to remember...!"
"...Are you saying that you can't remember well because it was six years ago?
I can remember it as clearly as if it happened yesterday..."

"Not surprised.

It's ridiculous to ask me to remember...!"

I can remember as clearly as if it was yesterday..."

MG.translation: "Come on, this was six years ago, right? I'm the one who has it bad, being forced to remember...!"

findings.sourceReading: Battler protests that after six years it is unreasonable to expect him to remember everyone clearly.
findings.alternative: Being forced to meet an unreasonable expectation is indeed having it bad, so his defensive complaint remains recognizable.

findings.sourceReading: George jokingly teams up with Shannon, and Battler notices that his unusually frank familiarity with a servant may indicate they are dating.
findings.alternative: George and Shannon are in fact secretly dating, and their teamed-up teasing can reasonably look flirtatious to Battler.

findings.sourceReading: Because the other party itself put forward the condition, Kyrie infers that it must believe it has good prospects under those terms.

findings.description: MG says solving the epitaph would cause the gold to be “stolen from her.” Japanese only says the gold would be taken, without establishing that Beatrice currently possesses or owns it; her possession is the disputed premise Kyrie addresses immediately afterward.

ひょっとして、碑文を解くように焚き付けて、
脇から掻っ攫おうと考えているのでは…。
それは極めて妥当な想像だった。

and then planned to steal it away at the last second...?

MG.translation: That certainly was the case. If the epitaph showed the way to the hidden gold, why would she challenge them to try and solve it? If they actually did solve it, wouldn't the gold all be stolen from her...?

findings.sourceReading: The narration questions why the sender would invite the siblings to solve the epitaph if doing so could result in the gold being taken, then considers a plan to exploit their solution.
findings.alternative: The current theory treats Beatrice as the gold’s manager, so “from her” is a natural inference even though the scene has not established possession.

findings.description: MG says Kyrie thought “there might be a catch.” 引っ掛かる says something still bothered her or did not quite sit right; “a catch” prematurely specifies the unease as a hidden drawback or trap.

contexts.japanese: しかし、霧江はまだ少し引っ掛かると考えていた。

contexts.MG: However, Kyrie still thought there might be a catch.
contexts.UP: However, Kyrie still felt something was slightly out of place.

MG.japanese: しかし、霧江はまだ少し引っ掛かると考えていた。もし勝利宣言ならば、勝者らしく、黄金を堂々と示し、家督を買い取ると宣言すればいいだけの話だ。なのに、わざわざこの期に及んで、碑文を解いてみろ、解けたら家督と黄金を全て引き渡そうと、“新たなゲーム”を仕掛けてくる意味が、どこにあるというのか。
MG.translation: However, Kyrie still thought there might be a catch. If this was a declaration of victory, Beatrice would only have had to display the gold openly and state her intent to buy the inheritance. And yet, she had gone to all of this trouble, telling the siblings to try and solve the epitaph. Why did she set up this "new game", where she agreed to hand over the all of the gold and the inheritance to the epitaph solver?

Why had she set up this "new game", where she agreed to hand over the all of the gold and the right to succeed the head to the person who solved the epitaph?

findings.sourceReading: Kyrie still feels a slight unresolved inconsistency in the victory-declaration theory and continues analyzing it.
findings.alternative: A catch is a natural English way to name an unresolved problem in an apparently favorable explanation.

findings.alternative: A provocative challenge can exert strong psychological pressure, and Eva ultimately feels driven to accept it.

findings.description: MG says a nineteenth person “must’ve” visited Maria and delivered the letter. Japanese says the event can be explained by positing that a nineteenth person did so; it presents an available human explanation, not a necessary conclusion.

ゆえに１９人目の人物が訪れて手紙を渡したと、実に簡単に説明できるのだ。

この論法なら例えば、今回のゲームでもすでに問題提起されている、

the problematic case that has already occurred in this game,

Because that's a human move.

findings.description: MG renders “if it is a raven, it is black” as the equation “a raven = black.” That collapses a conditional property relation into identity or equivalence and makes the following contrapositive explanation less precise.

contexts.japanese:
「その通り。
“カラス＝黒い”、を証明すれば良い。
ということは、“黒くない鳥＝カラスではない”、を証明しても、同じ論法になるのがわかるかな？」
「世界中の、カラスでない鳥を全て調べ、それらが黒くないことを証明すれば、
それは結果的に、“ゆえに黒い鳥はカラスである”となるわけだ。
これを対偶論法という。
contexts.japanesePS3:
「その通り。
“カラス＝黒い”、を証明すれば良い。
ということは、“黒くない鳥＝カラスではない”、を証明しても、同じ論法になるのがわかるかな？」
「世界中の、カラスでない鳥を全て調べ、それらが黒くないことを証明すれば、
それは結果的に、“ゆえに黒い鳥はカラスである”となるわけだ。
これを対偶論法という。
contexts.MG:
"That's right.
You must simply prove that "a raven = black".
Do you see that, if you instead prove that "birds that aren't black = not ravens", you would reach the same argument?
If you go throughout the world and examine all birds that are not ravens, and prove that none of them are black,
then as a result, you can claim that "therefore, black birds are ravens".
This is called an argument by the contrapositive.
contexts.UP:
"That is right.
You must simply prove that "if it is a raven, it is black".
And do you see that, if you prove that "if a bird is not black, it is not a raven", you would reach the same argument?"
"If you go throughout the world and examine all birds that are not ravens, and prove that none of them are black,
then as a result, you can claim that "therefore, birds that are black are ravens".
This is called an argument by the contrapositive.

MG.japanese: 「その通り。“カラス＝黒い”、を証明すれば良い。ということは、“黒くない鳥＝カラスではない”、を証明しても、同じ論法になるのがわかるかな？」
MG.translation: "That's right. You must simply prove that "a raven = black". Do you see that, if you instead prove that "birds that aren't black = not ravens", you would reach the same argument?

findings.sourceReading: Beatrice formalizes “if something is a raven, then it is black,” then states its contrapositive: if a bird is not black, it is not a raven.
findings.alternative: The equals sign is informal shorthand, and the next sentence still supplies the intended not-black/not-raven relationship.

UP.translation: "*cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*!! How foolish... Who do you think I am? I am the Endless Witch, the Infinite Witch! For you to challenge me at infinity is absurd. Having control over infinity means also that I am able to kill infinity."

findings.sourceReading: Beatrice mocks Battler for trying to challenge the witch who controls infinity by wielding an infinite regress against her.
findings.alternative: His attack operates by continuing without end, so “challenge me endlessly” describes the mechanism’s temporal form.

findings.description: MG says that when Beatrice speaks in red, it “will contain” no illusions. Japanese states a standing rule in the present: red contains no illusion whenever she speaks it.

妾がこの島には１００人しかいないと一言赤で語れば、
そなたにはもはや１０１人目を生み出すことは叶わぬのだ」
contexts.japanesePS3:
「妾が赤で語る時、そこには一切の幻想がない。
妾がこの島には１００人しかいないと一言赤で語れば、
そなたにはもはや１０１人目を生み出すことは叶わぬのだ」

"When I speak in red, it will contain absolutely no illusions.

findings.sourceReading: Beatrice states the general authority of red truth, then explains how a red population ceiling would stop Battler from creating another outsider.
findings.alternative: The immediately contemplated future red declaration makes future tense natural without denying the general rule.

findings.description: MG writes that Battler can “gleam” information from careless red use. The required verb is “glean”; gleam is a visible shine and is the wrong word.

contexts.japanese:
ベアトリーチェの赤は、まさに伝家の宝刀。
ヤツが赤で語ったことは証拠も反論の余地もなく、それが真実となって確定してしまう。
それらは俺を何度も叩き斬り、わずかな心の拠り所をいつも真っ二つにしてきた。
だが、迂闊に使えばそれは俺に真相を探る情報とされてしまうこともある。
…俺は前回、特に礼拝堂の密室トリックの時、それを逆手に取り、
一度はぎりぎりまで追い詰めたはずだ。

contexts.MG:
Beatrice's red was her true trump card.
When that person speaks in red, it's definitely the truth, and no amount of proof or counterarguments can change that.
Until now, she's used that to severely wound me, and each time, the tiny foundations supporting my heart get split in half.
However, if she uses it carelessly, then I can also gleam a little information about the truth.
...In the last game, I used that to my advantage, especially during the chapel's closed room trick,
and almost completely got her boxed in at one point.
contexts.UP:
Beatrice's red was truly her secret weapon, her treasured blade.
The things she spoke in red would become solidified as the truth, and no amount of evidence or counterarguments could change them.
They had cut me down to size many times now, rending in two any supports my heart had to lean on.
However, if she used it carelessly, then I could also find a little information about the truth.
...In the last game, especially during the chapel's locked room trick, I had taken advantage of that,
and had once closed her in almost completely.

MG.japanese: だが、迂闊に使えばそれは俺に真相を探る情報とされてしまうこともある。…俺は前回、特に礼拝堂の密室トリックの時、それを逆手に取り、一度はぎりぎりまで追い詰めたはずだ。
MG.translation: However, if she uses it carelessly, then I can also gleam a little information about the truth. ...In the last game, I used that to my advantage, especially during the chapel's closed room trick, and almost completely got her boxed in at one point.

findings.sourceReading: Carelessly used red can give Battler information with which to investigate the truth, as in the prior chapel battle.
findings.alternative: The intended verb is obvious from the direct object “information” and the surrounding explanation.

findings.description: MG pluralizes 一縷の望み into “my only rays of hope.” The source uses a single thread or ray of hope, which supports the following single-tightrope image; “only rays” is internally awkward and breaks the singular progression.

contexts.japanese:
煽る。
挑発する。
ヤツに赤で語らせるよう、追い詰めるんだ…。
確かにヤツの赤は、いつも俺の一縷の望みをぶった斬ってきた。
しかし、……それを恐れるな。
この、虚偽と幻想で侵食された島で、たったひとつ信じることができるのが、
ヤツが語る赤の情報だけなのだ。
落ちれば奈落という、崖と崖の間に見出す唯一の活路。
たった一本の綱渡り。
ヤツの慈悲無き真っ赤な刃こそが、唯一の生きる道なのだ。

contexts.MG:
Agitate her.
Challenge her.
Drive her into a corner to make her speak in red...
Of course her red's always wiping out my only rays of hope.
But...don't be afraid of that.
On this island overcome with falsehoods and illusions, the only thing I can trust is...
the information she speaks in red.
It's my only way across the chasm of hell.
Just a single tightrope.
Her merciless blood-red blade is the only way I can survive.
contexts.UP:

Provoke her.
Drive her into a corner to make her speak in red...
Of course her red has always cut right through my only threads of hope.

On this island overcome with falsehoods and illusions, the only thing I can trust...
is the information that she speaks in red.
It is my only way across the chasm of Hell.

MG.japanese: 確かにヤツの赤は、いつも俺の一縷の望みをぶった斬ってきた。しかし、……それを恐れるな。この、虚偽と幻想で侵食された島で、たったひとつ信じることができるのが、ヤツが語る赤の情報だけなのだ。
MG.translation: Of course her red's always wiping out my only rays of hope. But...don't be afraid of that. On this island overcome with falsehoods and illusions, the only thing I can trust is... the information she speaks in red.

findings.sourceReading: Beatrice’s red has repeatedly cut Battler’s single thread of hope, yet red is also the single tightrope and blade-edge path he can trust.
findings.alternative: Rays of hope is a familiar English image, and “only” still marks red as his sole dependable source.

Milady."

UP.translation: Ronove, who was supposed to be her ally, roguishly rushed her next move. Beato smiled back, probably intending to demonstrate that she was still relaxed, ......but she couldn't hide the sweat building up on her forehead. By now she had completely lost that relaxedness which had allowed her to turn her nose up at her worthless opponent.

findings.sourceReading: Ronove mischievously urges his mistress to make her next move despite ostensibly being her ally.
findings.alternative: The intended meaning is readily recoverable from the reference to her next move and the surrounding stalemate.

findings.description: MG says Beatrice would lose a massive piece by declining the repetition request. The source says X is a major piece that she would be allowing Battler to have on his first move; the piece becomes his argumentative resource rather than one of her pieces being captured.

「……このＸは、初手で許すには相当デカい大駒だぜ？
何しろ、以後、１８人の誰にも不可能だった、という根拠のトリックは、
全て１８人以外の人間Ｘで説明可能になる。
……全員アリバイ系の密室を、全て打ち破れる大駒だ…！」

......This is a huge piece that can break open any locked room hinging on everyone having an alibi...!"

MG.japanese: 「……このＸは、初手で許すには相当デカい大駒だぜ？　何しろ、以後、１８人の誰にも不可能だった、という根拠のトリックは、全て１８人以外の人間Ｘで説明可能になる。……全員アリバイ系の密室を、全て打ち破れる大駒だ…！」
MG.translation: "...That X is a pretty massive piece to lose on your first move, right? After all, from now on, all of the tricks that were impossible for the 18... can be explained with a human X who isn't in that group. ...This huge piece can break open all the rooms you said were closed because everyone had an alibi...!"

findings.sourceReading: If Beatrice will not deny at least nineteen people in red, she allows Battler the powerful X piece: arbitrarily many outsiders who can explain crimes impossible for the eighteen.
findings.alternative: Losing a piece still conveys a large tactical concession by Beatrice, and the following lines explain that Battler can use X against the alibi-based rooms.

findings.description: MG says the exchange “proves” Beatrice once had a charming adolescent phase. The source says only that this is a story about her having such a phase; “prove” adds an evidentiary conclusion to Battler’s teasing dismissal.

何の為に生きているのかを理解できなかった」
「ま、誰でも思春期になると、
自分の生きる意味とは何ぞやみたいな、哲学的な悩みに一度は囚われるものさ。
お前にもそんな微笑ましい時期があっただけという話だろ？」

findings.sourceReading: Battler lightly dismisses Beatrice’s identity crisis as the ordinary, almost endearing philosophical anxiety people experience in adolescence.
findings.alternative: The recollection itself is evidence that she had such a period, so “prove” reaches the same practical conclusion while preserving Battler’s teasing tone.

contexts.MG:
Grandfather met Beatrice.
He then fell in love with her and courted her, but she didn't accept him.
Then, he flew into a rage and shut her up inside this hidden mansion.
Beatrice tried to escape, but no matter what she did, she couldn't succeed,
...so she finally chose her own death.
...And then, ......no.
...Maybe there was a girl who looked just like Beatrice...no, a baby.
Grandfather raised this child with care.
But maybe he didn't view this child as his daughter.
"The soul was once again shut up in a cage of flesh."
Those words probably meant that he didn't view this kid as her child,
...but as her reincarnation.
Maybe that's what it meant.
contexts.UP:
Grandfather met Beatrice.
He then fell in love with her and courted her, but she didn't nod her head in agreement.
And so he got angry, and shut her up inside this hidden mansion.
Beatrice tried to escape, but no matter what she did, she couldn't succeed,
......so she finally chose her own death.
......And then, .........hmm.
...Maybe there was a girl that looked just like Beatrice, ...no, a baby.
And Grandfather raised this child with care.
But maybe Grandfather didn't view this child as his daughter.
"Shut my soul up once more into a cage of flesh".
Those words probably meant...
...that he didn't view this kid as her child, but as her reincarnation.
Maybe that's what it meant.

MG.japanese: ……それで、………うーん。…ベアトリーチェには、生き写しの娘、…いや、赤ん坊がいたとか。それで祖父さまはその子を大事に育てたわけだ。
MG.translation: ...And then, ......no. ...Maybe there was a girl who looked just like Beatrice...no, a baby. Grandfather raised this child with care.

findings.sourceReading: Battler hesitates while extending his mundane reconstruction from Beatrice’s death to the possibility that she left an identical daughter or infant.
findings.alternative: “No” can mark self-correction away from the literal soul-transfer story and toward the daughter hypothesis, matching the direction of his reasoning.

とにかく、こちら回りに進めば、必ずお屋敷へ帰れるとわかって、ちょっとだけ安心したわ。

contexts.MG:
Gritting my teeth so that she didn't see me looking troubled,
I pushed my way through the woods, advancing down a path that wasn't a path.
Then, after going through various troubles, I fortunately managed reach the ocean...
At that time, I still didn't even have a clue where I was on the island,
but for the time being, I was just a little reassured, realizing that if I just went around this way, I would surely be able to return to the mansion.

I pushed my way onward through the pathless woods.

but for the time being, I was just a little reassured, realizing that if I just went around this way, I would surely be able to return to the mansion.

findings.description: UP says time “had begun to start counting again.” Begun and start redundantly express the same inception; “had begun counting again” is the grammatical form.

contexts.japanese:
机の上に置かれた、凝った意匠の施されたアンティークの時計は、

２４を数えた時の刻みが０に戻り、再びそれを数え直していた…。
「……時の刻みとは残酷なものよ。
２４を数えるために一日を掛けて辿り着き、そして再び０に戻る。
……２３時５９分までは確かに数えただろう。
しかし、２４時に辿り着くことはできたのだろうか？
……辿り着けず、再び０時に戻ったと考えれば、それは何とも虚しいことよ」

contexts.MG:
On the antique clock with the intricate design that had been sitting on his desk,
the two overlapping hands tilted to the right and began to slide.
The measure of time that counted up to 24...had returned to 0...and had begun to count back again...
"...Measuring time is a brutal thing.
It drags itself all the way to 24 over the course of a day, and then returns back to 0.
...It certainly did count to 23:59.
However, is it ever able to reach 24:00?
...If you conclude that it returns to 0:00 again without reaching 24, how futile it must all be."
contexts.UP:
On the antique clock with an intricate design that was sitting on his desk,
the two overlapping hands had begun to tilt to the right, and separate from one another.
The passage of time that had counted to 24 had returned to 0, and begun to start counting again...
"......The passage of time is a brutal thing.
It drags itself all the way to 24 over the course of a day, and then returns back to 0.
......It surely managed to count to 23:59.
However, was it ever able to reach 24:00?
......If you believe that it returns to 0:00 again without reaching it, how futile it seems."

UP.japanese: 机の上に置かれた、凝った意匠の施されたアンティークの時計は、重なっていた２本の針を右に傾かせ、ずらし始めている。２４を数えた時の刻みが０に戻り、再びそれを数え直していた…。
UP.translation: On the antique clock with an intricate design that was sitting on his desk, the two overlapping hands had begun to tilt to the right, and separate from one another. The passage of time that had counted to 24 had returned to 0, and begun to start counting again...

findings.sourceReading: After the clock passes from twenty-four to zero, it begins counting anew.
findings.alternative: The redundant construction is fully intelligible and still corrects WH’s suggestion of reverse counting.

MG.translation: The most forbidden action in tarot reading is trying to predict the same thing twice. To do so ridicules the results of fortune telling... and also desecrates those beings higher than humans that give revelations through the tarot cards.

findings.sourceReading: Ordinary tarot doctrine treats a repeated reading as desecrating both the first result and the higher being that grants revelation.
findings.alternative: Ridicule is one form of disrespect and preserves Kinzo’s point that repetition insults the reading’s authority.

findings.description: UP says Beatrice sneers “with an absolute superiority.” Superiority is uncountable in this construction; idiomatic English requires “with absolute superiority” or, as MG has it, “with a sense of absolute superiority.”

その高さは１００メルテにも及び、銃眼の数は片方だけで３６０を越える。
それこそが、古代英雄たちが束になっても神域を侵すことを許さなかった、神々の兵団の戦塔。
ベアトリーチェはその巨大な双頭の塔の狭間に優雅に浮かびながら、師匠を見下ろし、絶対の優位に嘲笑う。

まるで大樹の間を舞う蝶のように見えた。

MG.translation: "No, that is not correct. The divine spear avoided her. It is the law of the gods that an absolute spear and an absolute shield must never fight one another. Although, in the end, it means the same thing as defending against it."

findings.sourceReading: The teacher corrects the apparent block: under divine law, the absolute spear itself avoids colliding with the absolute shield, which is functionally equivalent to being blocked.
findings.alternative: The preceding “she defended” supplies the teacher as a salient referent, and avoiding her could loosely mean veering away from her defense. It conflicts with the stated law governing spear versus shield.

findings.description: UP turns two disappearances into acts of erasure: the teacher “began to completely erase her form,” then the spear “erased itself.” The source says her form completely vanishes and the spear also disappears, without assigning either entity an act of erasing itself.

するとベアトリーチェを貫いていた槍も姿を消した。ベアトリーチェはようやく大地に降り立つ。

findings.sourceReading: As the teacher fully remembers that she was already dead, her form vanishes completely; the spear piercing Beatrice disappears with her.
findings.alternative: Reflexive erasure can be used figuratively for vanishing, and the causal sequence remains clear. It nevertheless introduces deliberate self-action absent from 消えていく and 姿を消した.

findings.sourceReading: If Battler listens to Beatrice’s claim, it may consequently sound and appear as though it were true—exactly what he was made to see.
findings.alternative: A claim that sounds true is convincing, so the practical warning remains recognizable. The conditional sequence is reversed by presupposing conviction at the outset.

findings.description: MG says “that set of truths shrinks with observation.” The source’s それ refers to the uncertain wavefunction, which collapses through observation as possible truths are selected down to one; it is not a set of truths literally shrinking.

contexts.japanese:

全ての状態が同時に説明できる。
しかし、真実はひとつです」
「それは観測されることによって収縮し、
無数の真実が淘汰されてたったひとつの真実になる。
法廷で例えるならば、
これは裁判長による判決行為にも似ているでしょう。
検察側、弁護側がそれぞれに主張する２つの真実は、
判決によって収縮し、１つとなるのです」

"At this moment, on Rokkenjima, witches and magic certainly may exist as truth.
...However, until the moment that the cat's box is opened, that world is an uncertain wave function.
The entire situation can be explained by both sides at the same time.
However, there is one truth."
"That set of truths shrinks with observation,
and countless truths are weeded out to become one truth.
It is like when, in court,
the judge hands down his judgement.
The two truths from the prosecutor's and the defense's claims...
are reduced in number by the judgement and become one."

"That is collapsed by observation,
and countless truths are weeded out to become one truth.
It is like when, in court,
the judge makes his judgment.
The two truths from the prosecutor's and the defense's claims...
collapse by the judgment, and become one."

MG.japanese: 「それは観測されることによって収縮し、無数の真実が淘汰されてたったひとつの真実になる。法廷で例えるならば、これは裁判長による判決行為にも似ているでしょう。検察側、弁護側がそれぞれに主張する２つの真実は、判決によって収縮し、１つとなるのです」
MG.translation: "That set of truths shrinks with observation, and countless truths are weeded out to become one truth. It is like when, in court, the judge hands down his judgement. The two truths from the prosecutor's and the defense's claims... are reduced in number by the judgement and become one."

findings.sourceReading: Observation collapses the uncertain wavefunction, eliminating innumerable possible truths until one truth remains, like a judicial verdict.
findings.alternative: A shrinking set is an accessible paraphrase of alternatives being reduced to one. It drops the explicitly invoked wavefunction and misidentifies what undergoes collapse.

「あぁ、見てろよ。
…………もうあいつの寝言には耳を貸さねぇ。
とことん冷静に俺の戦いを貫いてやる。
もうあいつの挑発には絶対に乗らねぇ」

findings.sourceReading: Despite strict locks, an unknown person entered and exited the mansion, making it a permeable danger zone rather than a secure home.
findings.alternative: Entry is the crucial breach and can imply later movement away. Repetition of the source’s two-way movement makes the omission systematic in this passage.

"From now on, it is yours. You may put it on your finger and display it high before your siblings. None should doubt that you have now succeeded the Ushiromiya family inheritance."

findings.sourceReading: Eva confirms that she may inherit all the gold and succeed to the Ushiromiya family headship; the ring proves that she has now succeeded to that headship.
findings.alternative: “Succeed” is repeatedly associated with inheritance and succession throughout the scene, so the intended transfer is recoverable. It produces an ungrammatical transfer of the gold and collapses the institutional headship into generic inheritance.

findings.description: UP changes Bernkastel’s present judgment that Eva’s succession “is not worthy” of her recommendation into the counterfactual “wouldn’t have been worthy,” implying a past disqualification rather than her current refusal to endorse it.

findings.sourceReading: Bernkastel presently judges the succession a coincidence rather than a miracle and says it is not worthy of her recommendation.
findings.alternative: Because Lambdadelta has already supplied the required recommendation, Bernkastel’s hypothetical phrasing can mean she herself would not have recommended Eva. It changes the direct present assessment into a retrospective counterfactual.

findings.sourceReading: For the time being, it is acceptable to understand the young witch as a visualization of a separate entity within Ushiromiya Eva, though Battler should not accept that interpretation uncritically.
findings.alternative: “May not be a hindrance” conveys that the model is usable provisionally. It sounds like an external obstruction assessment rather than Virgilia authorizing a tentative interpretation.

findings.sourceReading: When Battler joins the louder clapping, the assembly responds with great applause as though a ceremony has just ended, making his and Beato’s applause seem like the final recognition required.
findings.alternative: Battler’s applause triggers the concluding response, so he functionally completes the ceremonial sequence. The source leaves the ceremony’s apparent completion impersonal and only then compares his applause to the final requirement.

findings.description: UP says Maria merely “tends to get irritable” at times like this. 癇癪を起こす means throwing a tantrum, which predicts the loud behavioral episode immediately heard upstairs.

contexts.japanese:

するとその時、２階で、どたどたどたっという慌しい足音が聞こえた。
ゲストハウスは安っぽい建物ではないので、普通の足音なら聞こえるわけもない。

真里亞のうーうーうーと連呼する不機嫌そうな声が聞こえてきた。
楼座は髪を振り乱しながら頭を抱え、声なき声で苦悶の唸りをあげる…。

"I wonder if the kids up there are building up stress too.
...I'm worried about Maria.

At that moment, they heard the sound of wild footsteps coming from the second floor.
The guesthouse wasn't a cheap building, so they wouldn't normally have heard the sound of footsteps.

UP.translation: "I wonder if the kids up there have also built up stress. ......I'm worried about Maria. She tends to get irritable in times like this."

findings.sourceReading: Rosa worries because Maria is prone to throwing tantrums under this kind of stress; the adults immediately hear her stomping and crying upstairs.
findings.alternative: Irritability is the emotional state underlying a tantrum and the next actions supply the intensity. It weakens Rosa’s specific behavioral prediction.

findings.description: UP repeatedly uses “decorum” for the instruction to exercise restraint: at the concluding 自重気味 and 自重しろ clauses it shifts curbing excess into polite or dignified conduct. The source already distinguishes dignity from the additional demand for self-restraint.

contexts.japanese:
「…それで良い、それで。
……まぁ、まだ復活の儀式の先は長いぞ。
あと５人も殺さねばならないからな…。
あまり弄ばずに、綺麗に上品に、
…少しあっさり目でいいからな…？」
「ロノウェがそなたに教えた妾のやり方はその、……悪い例だ。
模範にしてはならぬ。
よく心に刻んでおけぃ」
「…………はい、先代さま」
「良い返事だ。
……ロノウェ、煉獄の七姉妹よ、出でよ…！」
「……はい、お嬢様。
ロノウェ、ここに」
「傲慢のルシファー、ここにっ」
「…これまではだな、その、妾も色々派手にやってきたわけだが。
……その、
……まぁ、黄金の魔女としての威厳も大事であり、
まぁ、そのだな…、」
ベアトが、らしくもなくしどろもどろしながら言うのを、
ロノウェはぷっくっくと笑いながら聞き、それを要約した。
「畏まりました。
以後は黄金の魔女の名に相応しい、気品に気をつけるように致します。
……煉獄の七姉妹も、これまでのような悪ふざけは改め、
以後は最短の手順で任務を遂行するように。
……ということで、よろしいですか？　お嬢様？」
「う、うむ。
つまりはそういうことだ。
皆、肝に銘じよ！
良いな…！」
「はいっ。
畏まりましたっ」
「妾が言いたいのは以上だ。
……もう引き上げて良いぞ」
「畏まりました。
それでは失礼いたします」
「失礼いたしますっ」
「……………………………………」
「ま、…妾が言いたいのはそれだけだ。
それでは引き続きしっかりな？
黄金の魔女らしく、貫禄を持って、…その、自重気味にな？
……頑張るが良いぞ。
そなたを見守っておる」
ベアトは最後まで要領悪そうにしながらそれだけを伝え、
黄金の蝶の群れとなって、虚空に姿を消す。
間が持たないので、そそくさと消えたという方が相応しいかもしれない。
後には、雨に打たれながら横たわる真里亞の遺体と、
柵にもたれかかりながら空を見上げている楼座の遺体。
……そして魔女の姿が残るだけだった。
「…………………自重しろ……、………か」
その表情は、少しだけ退屈そうだった。

contexts.MG:
"...Very well, that will do.
...Well, there is still much to do for the resurrection ceremony.
You still have to kill five people...
You should do it without toying with them too much, with beauty and dignity,
...and with at least a little restraint, okay...?
What Ronove told you about how I did it...that was a bad example.
You mustn't use that as a model.
Engrave that into your heart."
"......Yes, Predecessor-sama."
"A good answer.
...Ronove, the Seven Stakes of Purgatory, arise...!"
"...Yes, Milady.
I, Ronove, am here."
"Lucifer of Pride, right here."
"...Up until this point, umm, I've been a little flashy, but...
umm,
...well, the dignity of the Golden Witch is also important,
and about that..."
As Ronove laughed at Beato's uncharacteristically flustered speech,
he summed it up for her.
"Certainly.
From now on, we will be careful to act in a graceful manner, suitable for the name of the Golden Witch.
...Even the Seven Sisters of Purgatory will reform their bad behavior up until now,
and we shall espouse to perform our task in the quickest possible manner.
...Would that be acceptable, Milady?"
"I-Indeed.
That's it, more or less.
Everyone, take it to heart!
Okay...?!"
"Yes.
Certainly."
"That is all I wish to say.
...You may leave now."
"Certainly.
If you would excuse me."
"Excuse us."
"............"
"Well, ...that's all I want to say.
So, take care as you move forward, understand?
Act with dignity, and...umm, restraint, okay?
...Give it your all.
I will be watching over you."
Acting awkwardly until the very end, Beato left that message
and immediately became a cloud of gold butterflies, hiding her form in the empty air.
Maybe it'd be more accurate to say she vanished in a hurry because she couldn't keep up the conversation.
After that, all that remained was Maria's corpse, lying down and pounded by the rain,
Rosa's corpse, propped up by the fence and staring up at the sky...
...And the figure of the witch.
".........Show some restraint, ...you say...?"
Her expression looked just a little bored.

findings.sourceReading: Beato asks the successor to avoid excessive torment, proceed more simply, act with dignity and restrain herself; the successor repeats the restraint instruction resentfully.
findings.alternative: Decorum can imply checking inappropriate behavior and the surrounding instruction not to toy with victims still communicates limits. Repeating the dignity idea loses the distinct emphasis on reducing excess, especially in the final quoted instruction.

UP.translation: "Stop acting like an idiot...! Haven't you played witch enough? We found the gold. And we've even been promised the position of successor to the head. findings.sourceReading: If killing, do it without prolonged suffering; do not toy with lives, and if not killing, do not torment the victim.
findings.alternative: Tease can refer to harassment, but here it underplays physical torment explicitly paired with killing. MG’s bully retains coercive abuse, and the source’s いたぶる requires torment rather than playful provocation.

findings.description: MG writes as though if were absolute truth instead of as though it were.

findings.description: UP uses the past perfect “the vase had been broken” at the exact moment the child broke it, making the vase sound already broken before her act rather than stating the resulting fact that “the vase was broken.”

contexts.japanese: …私が壷を割ってしまった時点で、“壷は割れた”のです。
contexts.japanesePS3: …私が壷を割ってしまった時点で、“壷は割れた”のです。
contexts.MG: ...At the moment I broke the vase, "the vase was broken".
contexts.UP: ...At the time that I broke the vase, "the vase had been broken".

MG.japanese: 私はベアトリーチェが言った意味を理解します。…私が壷を割ってしまった時点で、“壷は割れた”のです。ベアトリーチェは、壷を蘇らせて見せたが、それは仮のもの。“壷は割れた”という運命までも変えたわけではない。
MG.translation: I understood the meaning of Beatrice's words. ...At the moment I broke the vase, "the vase was broken". Beatrice let me see the vase being restored, but that was a temporary thing. It didn't mean she'd changed the fate of "the vase being broken".

UP.japanese: 私はベアトリーチェが言った意味を理解します。…私が壷を割ってしまった時点で、“壷は割れた”のです。ベアトリーチェは、壷を蘇らせて見せたが、それは仮のもの。“壷は割れた”という運命までも変えたわけではない。
UP.translation: I understood the meaning of what Beatrice had said. ...At the time that I broke the vase, "the vase had been broken". Beatrice had shown me that the vase had been restored, but that had been a temporary thing. It didn't mean the fate that "the vase had been broken" had changed.

findings.sourceReading: The narrator says that from the moment she broke the vase, the fact or fate “the vase was broken” had been established.
findings.alternative: Past perfect can locate the broken state before the later retrospective explanation, but its placement after “at the time that I broke” strongly invites an earlier-than-breaking reading.

findings.description: UP duplicates causal conjunctions in because since.

findings.description: UP changes fear of cutting losses into not knowing when to cut them.

contexts.japanese: ……もっとも、損切りを恐れれば、紙切れ同然になるかもしれんがね。
contexts.japanesePS3: ……もっとも、損切りを恐れれば、紙切れ同然になるかもしれんがね。
contexts.MG: ...However, if you're too afraid to cut your losses, you might end up with just a scrap of paper.
contexts.UP: ......However, if you don't know when to cut your losses, what you have might become worthless scraps of paper.

MG.japanese: 「リスクを恐れるなら、事態が好転するまで塩漬けにするのも悪くない。……もっとも、損切りを恐れれば、紙切れ同然になるかもしれんがね。……我々の命がだが」
MG.translation: "When you're afraid of risk, it's all right to bide your time until the price starts to go up. ...However, if you're too afraid to cut your losses, you might end up with just a scrap of paper. ...Though in this case, that represents our lives."

UP.japanese: 「リスクを恐れるなら、事態が好転するまで塩漬けにするのも悪くない。……もっとも、損切りを恐れれば、紙切れ同然になるかもしれんがね。……我々の命がだが」
UP.translation: "If you're risk‐averse, biding your time until the situation improves again is not a bad idea. ......However, if you don't know when to cut your losses, what you have might become worthless scraps of paper. ......And what we have is our lives."

findings.sourceReading: 損切りを恐れれば identifies reluctance or fear concerning accepting a loss.
findings.alternative: Poor timing can follow fear, but inability to judge timing is a different obstacle; MG restores fear.

findings.description: MG changes Jessica personal wish not to die into a general claim about people.

contexts.japanese: 「死にたくないさ。
contexts.japanesePS3: 「死にたくないさ。
contexts.MG: "People don't want to die.
contexts.UP: "I don't want to die.

MG.japanese: 「死にたくないさ。……だから一番なんて、誰だって選びたくない。……人は、幸せに生きたくて、生の限りを足掻いてるんだぜ。だから本当は、まず一番目なんてありえないはずなんだ」
MG.translation: "People don't want to die. ...So no one would want to choose the first option. ...People want to live in happiness...and struggle as much as life will let them. So normally, the first choice should be impossible from the beginning."

UP.japanese: 「死にたくないさ。……だから一番なんて、誰だって選びたくない。……人は、幸せに生きたくて、生の限りを足掻いてるんだぜ。だから本当は、まず一番目なんてありえないはずなんだ」
UP.translation: "I don't want to die. ......So I didn't want to choose the first one—no one would. ......People struggle as much as life will let them, 'cause they want to live in happiness. So normally, the first choice should be impossible from the beginning."

findings.sourceReading: 死にたくないさ expresses her personal reluctance before339 generalizes to anyone.
findings.alternative: General aversion to death includes Jessica, but removes her explicit personal admission. Original WH176229 preserves I.

findings.description: UP introduces the unnatural construction let out a voice for Shannon speaking up.

contexts.japanese: 三面鏡を見ていた紗音が声をあげる。
contexts.japanesePS3: 三面鏡を見ていた紗音が声をあげる。
contexts.MG: Shannon, who had been looking at the three-sided mirror, raised her voice.

MG.japanese:
三面鏡を見ていた紗音が声をあげる。…見れば、ずっと沈黙していた譲治が顔を上げている。
……譲治もどうやら、答えを決めたらしい…。
MG.translation: Shannon, who had been looking at the three-sided mirror, raised her voice. ...When they looked, they could see George, who had been silent the whole time, lift his face. ...It seemed that George had also decided on an answer...

UP.japanese:
三面鏡を見ていた紗音が声をあげる。…見れば、ずっと沈黙していた譲治が顔を上げている。
……譲治もどうやら、答えを決めたらしい…。
UP.translation:
Shannon, who had been looking at the three‐sided mirror, let out a voice. ...They looked to see that George, who had been silent this whole time, had raised his head.
......It seemed that George had also decided on an answer...

findings.sourceReading: 声をあげる means raising her voice or speaking up in response to the scene.
findings.alternative: A voice is audible, but let out a voice is not idiomatic for a person vocalizing. Original WH176669 and MG use raised her voice.

findings.description: UP narrows Gaap claim that the parents were killed all too easily into their being killed without a fight.

contexts.japanese: なら、呆気なく殺されたあんたのお父さんとお母さんからは何をもらったの？
contexts.japanesePS3: なら、呆気なく殺されたあんたのお父さんとお母さんからは何をもらったの？
contexts.MG: "In that case, what did you receive from your parents, who got killed way too easily?
contexts.UP: In that case, what did you receive from your mother and father, who were killed without a fight?

MG.japanese: 「くす、言うわね。……なぁるほど。何度も蹴り倒されて転がされ、それでも立ち上がるのが紗音からもらった強さだと。なら、呆気なく殺されたあんたのお父さんとお母さんからは何をもらったの？　………？」
MG.translation: "*giggle* So you say. ...I get it now. You're saying that the way you can still stand up after being kicked down so many times is the strength you received from Shannon." "In that case, what did you receive from your parents, who got killed way too easily? ......?"

UP.japanese: 「くす、言うわね。……なぁるほど。何度も蹴り倒されて転がされ、それでも立ち上がるのが紗音からもらった強さだと。なら、呆気なく殺されたあんたのお父さんとお母さんからは何をもらったの？　………？」
UP.translation: "*chuckle*, nice words. ......Nowww I get it. So you say that the way you can still stand up after being kicked down so many times is the strength you received from Shannon. In that case, what did you receive from your mother and father, who were killed without a fight? .........?"

findings.sourceReading: 呆気なく殺された describes how unceremoniously or easily they were killed, without specifying whether they resisted.
findings.alternative: Without a fight can colloquially convey an effortless outcome, but also asserts absent resistance; originalWH178690 and MG use too easily.

findings.description: UP combines all and this many ungrammatically in You have killed all this many people.

MG.translation: Then, morning came. ...My tension and fatigue combined with my drowsiness, making for the worst kind of dawn. Basically, I lost patience with them and figured they could do whatever the hell they wanted......

Then, morning came. ......My tension and fatigue, mixed together with my drowsiness, made for the worst kind of dawn. UP.translation: The floor was firmly laid with a majestic, if a bit worn‐out, carpet. ......It was clearly a single piece. その時には、もう部屋は静まり返っていて、……さきほどまでの、取っ組み合うような秀吉の賑やかな気配は、一切消え去っていた。これは、………どういうこと……？！今、私は、……秀吉さんを殺した、殺人者と同じ部屋に一緒にいるということ……？！なら、犯人は早くこの部屋から逃げ出せばいいのに、……どうして息を殺しているの…？！秀吉さんを襲った犯人が、慌しく逃げ出していくらしい音は、……まるで何も聞こえない。……どんなに耳を凝らしても、室内に何かの気配はない。それどころか、今の出来事が全て、幻だったのではないかと思うほどに、……静寂。それはつまり、………まさか犯人が、……息を殺したまま、…このクローゼットの前に立ちはだかり、…私がのこのこと出てくるのを待ち受けているのでは……。もはや私は、何に怯えていいのかわからない。いっそこのクローゼットの暗闇に、溶け込むようにして消えてしまえればいいのに…！これ以上、この部屋に留まってはいけない。
身の危険だけでなく、色々とまずい気がする…。でも、どうすれば？！私には、このクローゼットを出てよいのかさえわからない…！！
MG.translation: By this time, the room had settled back into silence, ...and that earlier sense of Hideyoshi being in a noisy struggle had disappeared completely. What's......going on here...?! So, right now, ...I'm in the same room as the murderer who killed Hideyoshi-san...?! In that case, the culprit should try to escape from the room as soon as possible, ...so why are they hiding in here...?! I haven't heard anything... Nothing that might've been the culprit who attacked Hideyoshi-san rushing away. ...No matter how much I strain my ears, I can't sense anyone in the room. In fact, ...it's so silent that it makes what happened just a second ago feel like an illusion. In other words, ......does this mean...that the culprit is hiding his breath, ...standing just outside this closet, ...waiting for me to stumble out...? I don't even know what I should be scared of anymore. If only I could just melt away into the darkness of this closet...! I mustn't remain in this room any longer. I get the feeling I have more to worry about than just my personal safety... But what should I do?! I don't even know if it's a good idea to leave this closet...!!

UP.translation:

So, right now, ......I'm in the same room as the murderer who killed Hideyoshi‐san......?! findings.sourceReading: のこのこと出てくる here describes walking unsuspectingly into the feared killer waiting outside her closet. PC44070–44071 and MG use stumble out; UP shamelessly supplies a lack-of-shame assessment.
findings.alternative: のこのこ can connote brazenly showing up in other contexts. Here578–585 emphasize concealed danger and fear of leaving, favoring unwary movement over shame; no actual killer presence or emotional diagnosis is certified.

findings.description: MG reverses the resolve to live as a good person forever into a negative prediction.

contexts.japanese: 未来永劫、良き人として生きないと……。
contexts.japanesePS3: 未来永劫、良き人として生きないと……。
contexts.MG: That I won't live as a good person for all eternity....
contexts.UP: I must live as a good person for all eternity......

MG.japanese:
未来に冤罪が証明された時。その時こそ、この物語は遡って書き換えられるだろう……。しかし、その未来は、訪れない。……私は、思う。真実など、儚い。死ぬまで良き人であったとしても。死後に心無い誰かが、私が良き人ではなかったと一言、記録書に書き記し、それを人々が共有すれば。……私が生涯、良心を貫いたことさえ、易々と塗り替えられてしまうのだから。だから、私は思う。
未来永劫、良き人として生きないと……。
MG.translation: In the future, if the accusations against her are proven false. This tale will probably be rewritten... However, that future will never come. ...I think... Truth is a fleeting thing. Even if I am a good person until my death... If some heartless person after my death overwrites the records and says I wasn't a good person, and if that is shared with everyone else... ...Then even all the goodness in which I lived my life could be overwritten easily. And so, I think... That I won't live as a good person for all eternity....

UP.japanese:
未来に冤罪が証明された時。その時こそ、この物語は遡って書き換えられるだろう……。しかし、その未来は、訪れない。……私は、思う。真実など、儚い。死ぬまで良き人であったとしても。死後に心無い誰かが、私が良き人ではなかったと一言、記録書に書き記し、それを人々が共有すれば。……私が生涯、良心を貫いたことさえ、易々と塗り替えられてしまうのだから。だから、私は思う。
未来永劫、良き人として生きないと……。
UP.translation:
If, in the future, the accusations against her were to be proven false, this tale would probably be rewritten...... However, such a future would never come. ......I think... truth is a fleeting thing. Even if I am a good person up until my death... ...if some heartless person after my death writes down that I wasn't a good person, and that is shared with everyone else... ......then even all the goodness in which I lived my life will be overwritten easily. And so, I think...
I must live as a good person for all eternity......

findings.sourceReading: 未来永劫、良き人として生きないと is elliptical necessity, must live as a good person forever. OriginalPC56373–56374 and UP use must. MG says I will not live as a good person for all eternity.
findings.alternative: Prior fear of future reputational rewriting permits fatalistic reflection, but ないと is obligation here, confirmed by original WH affirmative necessity.

findings.description: MG misorders just and a in for a just little bit.

contexts.japanesePS3: 実は私、ほんの少しだけ、交ぜていただきましたので、この時刻に生存していたのをはっきり確認しています」
contexts.MG: I actually joined them for a just little bit, and I clearly witnessed that they were alive at that time."
contexts.UP: I actually joined in for a little bit, and I clearly witnessed that they were alive at that time."

MG.japanese: 「おかしな追求があると面倒なので、先にはっきりさせます。というか、むしろこれは最初にするべきでした。前後したことをお詫びします。２４時の時点での、ゲストハウスの状況です」「………黄金が発見され、緊急の親族会議になり、戦人さんと親族たちは屋敷へ。ゲストハウスには、私と、いとこ３人、南條先生、郷田さん、熊沢さんが残りました」「郷田さん、熊沢さんのアリバイについてはすでにご説明の通り。譲治さん、朱志香さん、真里亞さんの３人は、いとこ部屋でトランプで遊んでいました。実は私、ほんの少しだけ、交ぜていただきましたので、この時刻に生存していたのをはっきり確認しています」「我が主ッ、以上の復唱を要求します！！」
MG.translation: "It'll be a pain to have you try anything funny, so I'll make this clear now. In fact, I should've done this in the beginning. I apologize for being so roundabout. This is the situation around the guesthouse at 24:00." "......The gold was found, an emergency family meeting was called for, and Battler-san went to the mansion with the relatives. I, the three cousins, Doctor Nanjo, Gohda-san, and Kumasawa-san remained in the guesthouse." "I have already explained Gohda-san and Kumasawa-san's alibis. George-san, Jessica-san, and Maria-san were playing cards in the cousin room. I actually joined them for a just little bit, and I clearly witnessed that they were alive at that time." "My master, I ask that you repeat this!!"

UP.japanese: 「おかしな追求があると面倒なので、先にはっきりさせます。というか、むしろこれは最初にするべきでした。前後したことをお詫びします。２４時の時点での、ゲストハウスの状況です」「………黄金が発見され、緊急の親族会議になり、戦人さんと親族たちは屋敷へ。ゲストハウスには、私と、いとこ３人、南條先生、郷田さん、熊沢さんが残りました」「郷田さん、熊沢さんのアリバイについてはすでにご説明の通り。譲治さん、朱志香さん、真里亞さんの３人は、いとこ部屋でトランプで遊んでいました。実は私、ほんの少しだけ、交ぜていただきましたので、この時刻に生存していたのをはっきり確認しています」「我が主ッ、以上の復唱を要求します！！」
UP.translation: "It'll be a pain to have you try anything funny, so I'll make this clear now. In fact, I should have done this in the beginning. I apologize for being so roundabout. This is the state of the guesthouse at midnight." ".........The gold had been found, an emergency family conference called, and Battler‐san had gone to the mansion with the relatives. I, the three cousins, Doctor Nanjo, Gohda‐san, and Kumasawa‐san remained in the guesthouse." "I have already explained Gohda‐san and Kumasawa‐san's alibis. George‐san, Jessica‐san, and Maria‐san were playing cards in the cousins' room. I actually joined in for a little bit, and I clearly witnessed that they were alive at that time." findings.sourceReading: MG joined them for a just little bit misplaces just. OriginalPC47849–47850 and UP retain grammatical for a little bit; Japanese ほんの少しだけ has no disfluency.

contexts.japanese: ゲストハウスの書庫には、小さな図書館と呼べるほどの本が納められている。
contexts.japanesePS3: ゲストハウスの書庫には、小さな図書館と呼べるほどの本が納められている。

MG.japanese: ゲストハウスの書庫には、小さな図書館と呼べるほどの本が納められている。その中には、かつて金蔵が興味を持っていたことのある、海外ミステリーの名作も多数、収められていた。無論、全て原書は英語だが、ヱリカも南條も英語はまったく問題なかった。その際に、もう一度、使用人室の郷田に、書庫の鍵を借りたのだという。ヱリカはそこで、その際に封印は確認し直し、もちろん仕掛け直したと付け加える。くそったれ。都合よく人の出入りは封印しやがるくせに、自分だけは好きに出入りしてやがる。
MG.translation: Cramped though it was, that book storage room in the guesthouse was stocked well enough that it was fair to call it a small library. In it were several famous foreign mystery novels that Kinzo had once taken a liking to. Of course, they were all originals and in English, but English was no problem for either Erika or Nanjo. For this occasion, they had borrowed the key to the library one more time from Gohda in the servant room. At that point, Erika checked the seal again, and, of course, reset it. Damn her. Even though she keeps it sealed for anyone else to enter or leave, she alone enters and leaves whenever she wants.

UP.japanese: ゲストハウスの書庫には、小さな図書館と呼べるほどの本が納められている。その中には、かつて金蔵が興味を持っていたことのある、海外ミステリーの名作も多数、収められていた。無論、全て原書は英語だが、ヱリカも南條も英語はまったく問題なかった。その際に、もう一度、使用人室の郷田に、書庫の鍵を借りたのだという。ヱリカはそこで、その際に封印は確認し直し、もちろん仕掛け直したと付け加える。くそったれ。都合よく人の出入りは封印しやがるくせに、自分だけは好きに出入りしてやがる。
UP.translation: The archive in the guesthouse had enough books in it that you might even call it a small library. In it were several famous foreign mystery novels... that Kinzo had once taken a liking to. Of course, they were all originals and in English, but English was no problem for both Erika and Nanjo. On that occasion, Erika had again borrowed the key to the archive from Gohda in the servant room. She added that she had rechecked the seal at that point and, of course, reset it. Damn her. Even though she keeps it sealed for anyone else to enter or leave, she alone enters and leaves whenever she wants.

findings.sourceReading: JP says the archive holds enough books to be called a small library. PC48447–48448 and UP have no cramped-space condition. MG introduces Cramped though it was.
findings.alternative: Small library describes book collection/library scale, not necessarily crowded room dimensions. No access or mystery-mechanism consequence established.

findings.description: MG and UP change financial subjugation of the birth family into financial ruin.

contexts.japanese:
夏妃は、右代宮家がかつて、実家を経済的に屈服させたことへも復讐するため、
右代宮家の財産の乗っ取りを画策しました。
contexts.japanesePS3:
夏妃は、右代宮家がかつて、実家を経済的に屈服させたことへも復讐するため、
右代宮家の財産の乗っ取りを画策しました。
contexts.MG:
As revenge for financially ruining her birth family,
Natsuhi also plotted to take over the Ushiromiya family's fortune.
contexts.UP:
As revenge for financially ruining her birth family,
Natsuhi also plotted to take over the Ushiromiya family's fortune.

MG.japanese:
望まぬ結婚を強いられた夏妃は、右代宮家に対し恨みを抱き、復讐心を膨らませていきました。
（※裁判概要書：３ページより）夏妃は、右代宮家がかつて、実家を経済的に屈服させたことへも復讐するため、右代宮家の財産の乗っ取りを画策しました。
（※裁判概要書：４ページより）右代宮家の財産が、金蔵個人によって事実上、掌握されていることを知った夏妃は、金蔵に取り入るため、情交によってこれを篭絡しました。
（※裁判概要書：７ページより）
（※ベルンカステル文書：６８２ページより）夏妃は金蔵に取り入るために、金蔵の妄想の魔女である、ベアトリーチェの姿に扮して情交を重ねていました。
金蔵は、その夏妃に、在りし日の愛人の姿を見て、容易に篭絡されたのでした。
また、この姿が偶然、使用人に目撃され、一部の魔女伝説の根拠となりました。
（※裁判概要書：８ページより）
（※提出証拠品：第１７号より）
（※ベルンカステル文書：８０２ページより）
MG.translation:
After being forced into an unwanted marriage, Natsuhi developed a grudge against the Ushiromiya family and was filled with a desire for revenge. 
(*Trial Summary, p.3) As revenge for financially ruining her birth family, Natsuhi also plotted to take over the Ushiromiya family's fortune. 
(*Trial Summary, p.4) When Natsuhi learned that the wealth of the Ushiromiya family was for all intents and purposes controlled by Kinzo himself, she initiated sexual relations to curry favor with him and managed to ensnare him. 
(*Trial Summary, p.7) 
(*Bernkastel Documents, p.682) To curry favor with Kinzo, Natsuhi repeatedly disguised herself as Beatrice, a witch and figment of Kinzo's imagination, and engaged in sexual acts. 
Kinzo saw Natsuhi dressed as the mistress from his past and was easily ensnared. 
Additionally, a servant happened to witness her in this outfit, forming part of the basis for the legend of the witch. 
(*Trial Summary, p.8) 
(*Submitted Evidence #17) 
(*Bernkastel Documents, p.802)

MG.japanese:

findings.description: UP makes reciprocal acknowledgment and shared progress into Battler unilateral admission.

contexts.japanese:
俺たちは“愛し合ってる”と認め合わなきゃ、
……これより先には進めないんだ。

Unless I admit that we're "in love",

MG.japanese: しかし、ならば襲われる疑問は、………公正でない観測者が記した物語が、そもそも推理可能なのかということだ。………これに取り憑かれると、全ての推理はここまでで停滞して、終わる。だから、……俺は信じなければならなかった。ベアトが、………この物語によって、俺と戦おうとしていることを。戦うとは即ち、……俺にも勝つ余地が与えられているということ。それを与えているということは、………推理は可能という、……意味なのではないか。……ここは、……苦しかった。あの残酷な魔女が、自らの敗北を賭して、俺とフェアな勝負をしていると信じなければ、……乗り越えられない。……ワルギリアの言うとおりだぜ、……まるで恋愛だ。ベアトは、俺と全力で、真正面から戦っていると信じられなきゃ、……これ以上の推理には、至れない。………あぁ、…認めるぜ。俺たちは“愛し合ってる”と認め合わなきゃ、……これより先には進めないんだ。
MG.translation: However, that begs the question: ...is it even possible to solve a tale written by an observer who isn't impartial? ...If I get obsessed with this, all my reasoning will end here. However, ...I had to believe. I had to believe... ...that Beato was trying to fight me through this tale. Because it's a fight, ...that means I've been given a chance of winning. By giving me that, ...doesn't that mean... ...that reasoning is possible? ...This part...is tough. Unless I believe that the cruel witch took on the risk of losing to try and have a fair fight with me, ...I can't get past this part. ...Just like Virgilia said, ...it's just like love. If I can't believe that Beato is fighting me head on with everything she's got, ...I won't be able to reason any further than this. ...Sure, ...I'll acknowledge it. Unless we acknowledge that we "love each other", ...we won't be able to get any further.

UP.japanese: しかし、ならば襲われる疑問は、………公正でない観測者が記した物語が、そもそも推理可能なのかということだ。………これに取り憑かれると、全ての推理はここまでで停滞して、終わる。だから、……俺は信じなければならなかった。ベアトが、………この物語によって、俺と戦おうとしていることを。戦うとは即ち、……俺にも勝つ余地が与えられているということ。それを与えているということは、………推理は可能という、……意味なのではないか。……ここは、……苦しかった。あの残酷な魔女が、自らの敗北を賭して、俺とフェアな勝負をしていると信じなければ、……乗り越えられない。……ワルギリアの言うとおりだぜ、……まるで恋愛だ。ベアトは、俺と全力で、真正面から戦っていると信じられなきゃ、……これ以上の推理には、至れない。………あぁ、…認めるぜ。俺たちは“愛し合ってる”と認め合わなきゃ、……これより先には進めないんだ。
UP.translation: However, that raises the question: .........is it even possible to solve a story written by an observer who isn't impartial? .........All reasoning ends here if you get obsessed with this. That's why......it's so important for me to believe. That Beato... ......is trying to fight me through this tale. Because it's a fight, ......that means I've been given a chance of winning. And the fact that I've been given that... ......must mean... ......that reasoning is possible. ......This part......is the hardest. Unless I believe that the cruel witch took on the risk of losing to try and have a fair fight with me, ......I can't get past this part. ......Virgilia's right, ......it's just like love. If I can't believe that Beato is fighting me head‐on with everything she's got, ......I won't be able to reason any further than this. .........Alright, ...I'll admit it. Unless I admit that we're "in love", ......I won't be able to get any further.

"But that wasn't true. Do you know what's needed to fall in love? It's something you can't get from anyone but yourself. Being furniture or not has nothing to do with it. That's why I, overambitious furniture that I am, gave myself what's needed to fall in love. So you have it too, Kanon-kun." 
"You mean, I have what it takes to fall in love?"

findings.sourceReading: JP repeats 恋の資格 as a right one grants oneself. Original WH uses deserve and right; UP retains that entitlement. MG repeatedly uses what it takes and what is needed, shifting moral permission to personal capacity.

findings.description: UP changes failure to solve by the game’s end into permanent inability to solve.

MG.japanese: これほどの謎なら、恐らくヱリカは、戦人消失の謎を最後まで解けないだろう。解けない謎が一つでもあれば、それは魔女側の勝利となる。戦人にとって、……この復唱要求は、………何としても答えたいものなのだ。
MG.translation: With a riddle of that magnitude, Erika probably wouldn't solve the mystery of Battler's disappearance before the end. Each unsolved riddle gives an advantage to the witch side. Battler... wanted to respond to this demand if at all possible.

UP.japanese: これほどの謎なら、恐らくヱリカは、戦人消失の謎を最後まで解けないだろう。解けない謎が一つでもあれば、それは魔女側の勝利となる。戦人にとって、……この復唱要求は、………何としても答えたいものなのだ。

findings.sourceReading: JP 最後まで bounds predicted failure to the end of this contest. PC104637/104639 and MG retain that bound; UP forever unable removes the endpoint. Probability remains qualified.
findings.alternative: Forever can hyperbolically mean never during this game; the wording nevertheless changes an explicit bounded forecast into unbounded incapacity.

findings.description: MG changes the ability to bite one’s tongue into having the courage to do so.

UP.translation: "......I'll defile and humiliate you endlessly, ......and every time I forget the heady taste of victory, ......I'll use your body to remind me. .........Over......and over again...... ......If you're going to bite off your tongue, now's the time... ......Once this goes on your finger, ...you won't even be able to do that."

findings.sourceReading: 舌が噛めるなら expresses ability.1363 expressly denies physical strength, while1364–1365 separately establish refusal to give up. Original PC114163/114165 if you think you can preserves ability. MG adds a courage taunt.
findings.alternative: Guts can encompass resolve to act, but that adds a specific motivational judgment absent from the ability conditional. UP intention paraphrase remains consistent with the invitation.

MG.japanese:
理御は本家に住む、次期当主。
普段から、金蔵の相手をすることが多かった。なので、気難しい相手や、会話が噛み合わない相手とのやり取りには慣れがあったに違いない。瑣末なことは気にするだけ無駄だと割り切り、正体不明の男、ウィルと、まるでずっと前からの友人であるかのように、自然と振舞えてしまうのだった……。

Because of this, Lion must have been used to chatting with people who were moody or hard to follow. UP.japanese:
理御は本家に住む、次期当主。
普段から、金蔵の相手をすることが多かった。なので、気難しい相手や、会話が噛み合わない相手とのやり取りには慣れがあったに違いない。瑣末なことは気にするだけ無駄だと割り切り、正体不明の男、ウィルと、まるでずっと前からの友人であるかのように、自然と振舞えてしまうのだった……。

Lion was the successor to the head and lived with the main family.

findings.description: MG turns not merely a father-daughter relationship into denial of that relationship.

contexts.japanese: ……それは親子としての関係だけでなく。

contexts.MG: ...It was not a father-daughter relationship.
contexts.UP: ......It was not simply a father‐daughter relationship.

MG.japanese: 「お館様は、お時間の許す限り、九羽鳥庵へ通われました。時にはご出張と偽られ、何日も滞在され、ベアトリーチェさまとの生活を大切になさいました。……それは親子としての関係だけでなく。亡きベアトリーチェさまへの深い愛を垣間見れる、心温まるものでございましたとも」

findings.description: MG duplicates auxiliaries in imagine it being been kept safe.

contexts.japanese: ……こんなところに安置され、敬われているということそのものが、生理的に気持ち悪かった。
contexts.japanesePS3: ……こんなところに安置され、敬われているということそのものが、生理的に気持ち悪かった。
contexts.MG: ...viscerally, it was even more unnerving to imagine it being been kept safe and worshiped in a place like this.
contexts.UP: ......psychologically, it was even more unnerving to think about how it must have been kept safe and worshiped in a place like this.

MG.japanese: それはまさに、お供えに見えた。サイドテーブルの上には、一体の小さめのフランス人形が座っている。その人形の髪は、黄金。……服は、黒いドレス。どこから誰がこんな人形を見つけてきたやら。ベアトリーチェを暗示して、誰かがここに置いたのは疑いようもなかった。ということは、この人形こそが、この部屋の主だとでも言うのか…。そして、その主にお供えするように、……小皿が置かれ、クッキーと包み紙で捻ったチョコがいくつか置かれていた。小綺麗に置かれ、人形には埃も積もっていない。……つまり、この人形もお供えも、日々、使用人たちによって手入れされ、部屋同様に維持されているということだ。手入れ？　……いや、これは手入れなんかじゃない。どうか、私たちを祟らないで下さいという、お供え、……いや、まるで崇拝にさえ見える。……だから、人形そのものも充分に不気味だったが、……こんなところに安置され、敬われているということそのものが、生理的に気持ち悪かった。
MG.translation: It really did look like an offering. A small French doll was sitting on the side table. The doll's hair...was gold. ...It was wearing a black dress. Just who managed to find this doll, and where? There's no doubt that someone placed the doll here to symbolize Beatrice. Does that mean...this doll is supposed to be the owner of this room, or something...? And, looking like an offering to that owner, ...there sat a small plate with several cookies and wrapped chocolates. It was all set out neatly, and there was no dust piled up on the doll. ...In other words, both the doll and the offering were taken care of on a regular basis by the servants, kept in good condition along with the rest of the room. Taken care of? ...No, it's more than that. It looked like an offering...no, like some sort of worship, a prayer saying "please don't curse us"... ...So, even though the doll was more than eerie enough by itself, ...viscerally, it was even more unnerving to imagine it being been kept safe and worshiped in a place like this.

UP.japanese: それはまさに、お供えに見えた。サイドテーブルの上には、一体の小さめのフランス人形が座っている。その人形の髪は、黄金。……服は、黒いドレス。どこから誰がこんな人形を見つけてきたやら。ベアトリーチェを暗示して、誰かがここに置いたのは疑いようもなかった。ということは、この人形こそが、この部屋の主だとでも言うのか…。そして、その主にお供えするように、……小皿が置かれ、クッキーと包み紙で捻ったチョコがいくつか置かれていた。小綺麗に置かれ、人形には埃も積もっていない。……つまり、この人形もお供えも、日々、使用人たちによって手入れされ、部屋同様に維持されているということだ。手入れ？　……いや、これは手入れなんかじゃない。どうか、私たちを祟らないで下さいという、お供え、……いや、まるで崇拝にさえ見える。……だから、人形そのものも充分に不気味だったが、……こんなところに安置され、敬われているということそのものが、生理的に気持ち悪かった。
UP.translation: It did look like an offering. A small French doll was sitting on the side table. The doll's hair...was gold. ......It was wearing a black dress. Just who managed to find this doll, and where? There's no doubt that someone placed the doll here to symbolize Beatrice. Does that mean...this doll is supposed to be the owner of this room, or something...? And, as though it was an offering to that owner, ......there sat a small plate with several cookies and wrapped chocolates. It was all set out neatly, and there was no dust piled up on the doll. ......In other words, both the doll and the offering were being taken care of on a regular basis by the servants, and kept in good condition along with the rest of the room. Taken care of? ......No, it was more than that. It looked like an offering...no, like some sort of worship, a prayer saying "please don't curse us"... ......So, while the doll was eerie enough by itself, ......psychologically, it was even more unnerving to think about how it must have been kept safe and worshiped in a place like this.

MG.japanese: 「源次は尊敬する主人のことを、ただ一つだけ信じていないことがあった。それは、ベアトリーチェの孫を、果たして本当に家族として迎え入れられるのか、である」「源次は九羽鳥庵のベアトリーチェにもずっと仕えていた。その胸中についても詳しかった。彼女が金蔵の寵愛を一身に受け、父として敬愛していたことも」「しかしそれは金蔵のそれとは異なった。金蔵は彼女を、ベアトリーチェの生まれ変わりと思い、亡きベアトリーチェへの万感の思いの慰み者にしようとした。その思いを、九羽鳥庵のベアトリーチェが受け入れきれるわけもない。彼女は父と思い、尊敬してきた金蔵自らに、純潔を奪われることになるのである……」
MG.translation: "There was one matter in which Genji did not trust the master he so respected. That matter was whether Kinzo would be capable of accepting Beatrice's grandchild as her grandchild." contexts.japanese:
「第十の晩の、黄金の“郷”に注目した推理だな。
碑文の中には、他に四度も黄金郷という単語が登場するのに、なぜかこれ一つだけが、黄金の郷と記されている」
「なぜ、第十の晩だけ、黄金の郷なのか。
これに気付くのにも、そしてどうしてなのかに気付くのにも、これまた長い時間を掛けました」
「楼座の推理はこうだった。
黄金の“郷”をキョウと読み、京都の“京”と読み解いた。
そして、懐かしき故郷から京都までの十日かかる旅路を十分の一した地点に、何か秘密があると疑った。
………いい推理だったが惜しかった。
“京”は京都以外にも読み解けたんだ」
「……“京”を、京都以外で読み解く……？
ん……」
「難しく考えるな。
そのままだ」
「……京です。
いえ、キョウでなく、ケイと読みましょうか。
数字の単位です。
一十百千万億兆、京」
「数字の、単位……！」
「……私の場合は、この六軒島にいるという地の利がありましたから。
“京”を思い当たるヒントはあったのです。
私の場合は、先に答えがわかってから、逆に問題の意味がわかったという感じでした」
「ややこしいことを言うと理御が混乱する。
話を戻そう。
……第十の晩に１京に至るならば、第一の晩はいくつになる？」
「い、１京の十分の一ですから、
……えっと、………千兆…？」
「正解だ。
千兆から、鍵の選びし６文字を間引くんだ」
「Ｑｉｌｉａｎが英語である以上、千兆も英語であろうとはすぐに察しました」
「千兆は英語では、Ｑｕａｄｒｉｌｌｉｏｎ。

contexts.MG:
"Right, that theory about a ten-day journey ending at the tenth twilight.
"On the tenth twilight, at journey's end, you shall attain to the power of the Golden Land's treasures, once and for the last time." She took that section to be a literal trip that ends when you "attain to", or reach, the treasures of the Golden Land."
"What meaning was there in those words?
Realizing that there was something to be found...and then realizing what that something actually was... took another long stretch of time."
"By Rosa's reasoning,
"attain to" meant reaching some physical location
represented by the four treasures.
...It was a good try, but not quite right.
It's not the treasures we're supposed to reach, but their power."
"...What does it even mean to "reach" the power of something like that...?
Hmm..."
"Don't overthink it.
What else can the word "power" mean?"
"...You reach...
or rather, raise yourself to the power of the "four" treasures.
Starting at twilight number "ten".
And this is done "once and for the last time"."
"Oh, so it's an exponent, like a math problem...!"
"...Here, I had a home-field advantage, since I lived on Rokkenjima.
There was a hint there that made it easier to think of a certain large number.
In fact, you might say that I actually found the answer before I knew what the question was."
"If you keep making it so complicated, Lion's gonna get a headache.
Let's get back to the point.
......10 to the 4th power is ten thousand. If you reach ten thousand on the tenth twilight, how far have you gotten by the first twilight?"
"Well, that's just one tenth of ten thousand.
A thousand, right?"
"Right.
But while that gives us a single word, it has nowhere near enough letters, and it doesn't match the key at all."
"However, the end of the line says "you will attain to the power once and for the last time". If we interpret this as raising 10 to the 4th power once, and then doing the same thing one final time, we end up with ten quadrillion."
"That's ten quadrillion at the tenth twilight, or "quadrillion" at the first twilight.
contexts.UP:
"That theory focused on the tenth twilight's "Home of the Gold".
The epitaph uses the phrase "Golden Land" four separate times, but the phrase "Home of the Gold" is only used that once."
"Why is it written that way only on the tenth twilight?
It took me a long time to notice the significance of this, and just as long to discover the reason."
"Rosa's theory went like this.
She read the "Home" (郷) kanji as "kyou" and interpreted it as {ruby:kyou:京, which she took as short for "Kyoto" ({ruby:kyouto:京都).
Then, she reasoned that if you take a ten‐day trip from the beloved hometown to Kyoto, there might be some secret at the end of the first tenth of that journey.
.........It was a good theory, but she just missed the mark.
京 has another meaning besides Kyoto."
"......京 can mean something other than Kyoto......?
Hmmm......"
"Don't think too hard on it.
You either know it or you don't."
"......There's another meaning of 京.
One where it's not read "kyou", but "kei".
It's the name of a number.
{nobr:10,000 is {ruby:man:万, {nobr:10,000 {ruby:man:万 is {ruby:oku:億, {nobr:10,000 {ruby:oku:億 is {ruby:chou:兆, and {nobr:10,000 {ruby:chou:兆 is {ruby:kei:京."
"So it's a number......!"
"......Here, I had a home‐field advantage, since I lived on Rokkenjima.
There was a hint there that made it easier to think of the number "kei".
In fact, you might say that I actually found the answer before I knew what the question was."
"If you keep making it so complicated, Lion's gonna get a headache.
Let's get back to the point.
......If you reach one kei on the tenth twilight, how far have you gotten by the first twilight?"
"O‐one tenth of one kei, and one kei is ten thousand chou...
......So.........a thousand chou?"
"Exactly.
We remove the key's chosen six letters from a thousand chou."
"Since Qilian was written in English, I immediately guessed that "a thousand chou" would also have to be written in English."
"A thousand chou in English is "quadrillion".
contexts.note: Connected adapted solution replacing Kyoto/kei reasoning

findings.sourceReading: The source concludes by reaching the Golden Land. CH16 explains 郷 read as kyou, then 京 interpreted as kei (10^16), one tenth giving quadrillion. MG adds treasure power and finality to the epitaph and replaces the Kyoto/kei reasoning with repeated exponentiation. Original PC163883/163977/164003 and164983/164985 preserve the Japanese chain and arrival; UP follows them.
findings.alternative: The English adaptation coordinates its altered epitaph with a solvable English mechanism. This explains the editorial choice but does not preserve the source clue, Rosa theory, or narrated arithmetic; it is one connected adaptation rather than multiple independent defects.
findings.sourceNote: Original Witch Hunt is compared with the original-PC Japanese embedded in the historical patches. MangaGamer uses the accepted MangaGamer-based Witch Hunt backport, and Umineko Project uses its repository English; both are compared with maintained PS3-derived Japanese. The MangaGamer and PS3 witnesses are not independently certified retail extractions.

findings.description: MG writes that’ll they need instead of that they need

contexts.japanese: 絵羽たちの言い分を聞く限り、年内に大きなお金を必要としていることはわかる。
contexts.japanesePS3: 絵羽たちの言い分を聞く限り、年内に大きなお金を必要としていることはわかる。
contexts.MG: Going by what Eva and the others said, it's clear that'll they need a lot of money before the end of the year.
contexts.UP: Eva and the others had argued that they needed a lot of money before the end of the year, which was understandable.

MG.japanese:
理御もまた、辛かった。
自分がその場にいたなら、彼らを仲裁してなだめたかった。黄金は逃げない。冷静に時間をゆっくりと掛ければ、解決できる話なのだ。絵羽たちの言い分を聞く限り、年内に大きなお金を必要としていることはわかる。しかし、そのお金は１０億円のキャッシュカードで充分に支払える。火急な支出をそれで満たした上で、ゆっくりと黄金を現金に溶かし、分配すればいいではないか。確かに、換金は蔵臼にしか出来ないかもしれない。その分、兄弟での立場は有利かもしれない。しかし、この黄金は表沙汰に出来ないものだ。世間の好奇の目を引くだけでなく、いろいろ法律上の問題も出てくる。裏金は裏金のままにした方がいい。最も彼らが多くの取り分を得ようと思ったら、彼ら全員が、この黄金の存在を口外すべきではないのだ。即ち、彼らが最大利益を享受するためには、全員で秘密を守るという紳士協定が必要なのだ。確かに換金できる蔵臼の立場はやや有利だ。しかし、他の親族たちには、黄金の存在を公にするという非協力が可能なのだ。それに、……金蔵の死を隠しているという負い目もある。蔵臼は投資家。資金力だけでなく、ある程度の社会信用も重要な立場だ。彼が居丈高になれるほど、立場はそう有利ではないはずなのだ。
MG.translation: It was painful for Lion too. Lion would have tried to intervene and calm them, if that had been possible. The gold isn't going anywhere, right? If you just slow down and think, you'll be able to resolve this. Going by what Eva and the others said, it's clear that'll they need a lot of money before the end of the year. However, the billion yen cash card should be more than enough to pay for that. That would handle their emergency expenses, so they could then convert the gold to cash at their leisure...and just split it amongst themselves. Sure, maybe Krauss was the only one capable of converting the gold. That might give him an advantage over the other siblings. However, this gold couldn't be dealt with by open means. In addition to attracting public attention, it would also lead to various legal problems. It was better for this secret money to remain secret. If they wanted to get the largest portions possible, then they should all agree not to tell anyone about this gold. In other words, to maximize their profits, they would all need to make a gentleman's agreement...to keep this secret. Krauss did have a slight advantage. However, it was possible for the other relatives to refuse to cooperate and tell the world about the gold. And then, ...there was also the concealment of Kinzo's death to consider. Krauss was an investor. He needed not only financial clout, but also a certain degree of public confidence in him. His advantage isn't big enough for him to act so overbearing.

UP.japanese:
理御もまた、辛かった。
自分がその場にいたなら、彼らを仲裁してなだめたかった。黄金は逃げない。冷静に時間をゆっくりと掛ければ、解決できる話なのだ。絵羽たちの言い分を聞く限り、年内に大きなお金を必要としていることはわかる。しかし、そのお金は１０億円のキャッシュカードで充分に支払える。火急な支出をそれで満たした上で、ゆっくりと黄金を現金に溶かし、分配すればいいではないか。確かに、換金は蔵臼にしか出来ないかもしれない。その分、兄弟での立場は有利かもしれない。しかし、この黄金は表沙汰に出来ないものだ。世間の好奇の目を引くだけでなく、いろいろ法律上の問題も出てくる。裏金は裏金のままにした方がいい。最も彼らが多くの取り分を得ようと思ったら、彼ら全員が、この黄金の存在を口外すべきではないのだ。即ち、彼らが最大利益を享受するためには、全員で秘密を守るという紳士協定が必要なのだ。確かに換金できる蔵臼の立場はやや有利だ。しかし、他の親族たちには、黄金の存在を公にするという非協力が可能なのだ。それに、……金蔵の死を隠しているという負い目もある。蔵臼は投資家。資金力だけでなく、ある程度の社会信用も重要な立場だ。彼が居丈高になれるほど、立場はそう有利ではないはずなのだ。
UP.translation:
It was painful for Lion too.
Lion would have tried to intervene and calm them, if that had been possible. The gold wouldn't go anywhere. If they just took their time and thought about it calmly, they would be able to resolve this. Eva and the others had argued that they needed a lot of money before the end of the year, which was understandable. However, the billion yen cash card would be more than enough to pay for that. With their emergency expenses taken care of, they could liquidate the gold at their leisure, then just split it amongst themselves. Sure, maybe Krauss was the only one capable of converting the gold. That might give him an advantage over the other siblings. However, this gold couldn't be dealt with by open means. In addition to attracting public attention, it would also lead to various legal problems. It was better for this secret money to remain secret. If they wanted to get the largest portions possible, then they should all agree not to tell anyone about this gold. In other words, to maximize their profits, they needed a gentleman's agreement that all of them would keep the secret. Krauss did have a slight advantage. However, it was possible for the other relatives to refuse to cooperate and tell the world about the gold. And then, ......there was also the concealment of Kinzo's death to consider. Krauss was an investor. He needed not only financial clout, but also a certain degree of public confidence. His advantage wasn't big enough for him to act so overbearing.

findings.description: MG adds a normality judgment and a Halloween rationale to Maria’s word preference

contexts.japanese:
真里亞はニュアンスの違いにこだわって言ったようだが、
縁寿の方は心の底から、パンプキンとカボチャは別の存在だと思っているようだ。
contexts.japanesePS3:
真里亞はニュアンスの違いにこだわって言ったようだが、
縁寿の方は心の底から、パンプキンとカボチャは別の存在だと思っているようだ。
contexts.MG:
Maria was apparently speaking in English, but Ange, being normal, was not. Maria seemed to think the English word was more fitting for Halloween,
but it looked like Ange thought kabocha and pumpkins were entirely different things.
contexts.UP:
Maria seemed to be complaining about the difference of nuance between the Japanese and English words,
but it looked like Ange thought kabocha and pumpkins were entirely different things.

MG.japanese: 真里亞はニュアンスの違いにこだわって言ったようだが、縁寿の方は心の底から、パンプキンとカボチャは別の存在だと思っているようだ。一同は大笑いするが、縁寿にはなぜ笑われたのかわからず、納得いかない顔で小首を傾げている。
MG.translation: Maria was apparently speaking in English, but Ange, being normal, was not. Maria seemed to think the English word was more fitting for Halloween, but it looked like Ange thought kabocha and pumpkins were entirely different things. Everyone laughed, but Ange, not knowing why she was being laughed at, cocked her head to one side discontentedly.

UP.japanese: 真里亞はニュアンスの違いにこだわって言ったようだが、縁寿の方は心の底から、パンプキンとカボチャは別の存在だと思っているようだ。一同は大笑いするが、縁寿にはなぜ笑われたのかわからず、納得いかない顔で小首を傾げている。
UP.translation: Maria seemed to be complaining about the difference of nuance between the Japanese and English words, but it looked like Ange thought kabocha and pumpkins were entirely different things. Everyone laughed, but Ange cocked her head to one side discontentedly, not understanding what was so funny.

findings.sourceReading: Japanese says Maria insists on a difference in nuance, while Ange treats the words as different things. Active original PC171218/171221 follows that distinction. MG imports obsolete commented English171219 and adds a Halloween rationale.
findings.alternative: The English/Japanese word contrast is a reasonable explanatory adaptation. Being normal and a Halloween motive add judgments not expressed by the source; a discarded English comment is not original-PC Japanese edition material.

findings.description: The maintained PS3-derived Japanese has only 添い遂げる, staying together as partners. MG's sleeping together on their first night and UP's consummate their love both preserve sexual specificity from the fuller original-PC clause 体を重ねることや、初めての夜を添い遂げること. findings.description: MG preserves the longer original-PC drinking exchange: the underage-drinking remark, Battler drinking to cope without tasting the alcohol, Genji asking whether he devotes his final moments to drink, and Kinzo as a heavy drinker drowning his cares. The maintained PS3-derived Japanese rewrites this around idle use of Battler's remaining time, readiness to die, and Kinzo as larger-than-life. "...Just try laying one finger on Maria in front of me. I'll show you just how lukewarm the hell you came from is." 
The blast from the Winchester's 45 caliber Long Colt bullet exploded inside the goat head's throat... and its medulla oblongata was instantly pulverized. The goat head hadn't understood. It had thought women were like pre-opened wine bottles! It had thought that turning them upside down would immediately make their deep-red contents come out!

逆さにすればすぐに真っ赤な中身が出てくるワインボトルだと思ってたッ！

I wonder just how expensive this stuff is.
